News.title: Andy Burnham accused of EU reset deal ‘cover-up’ and told to come clean with public
News.content:
Next

ANDY Burnham was last night accused of a cover-up over his EU reset deal and told to come clean with the public.

The legal text behind the agreement struck at the Brussels summit is still under wraps.



But seven out of eight previous UK-EU treaties had their legal small print published within 48 hours of being agreed, analysis by anti-EU campaign group StayOut found.

Its chairman, Oliver Lewis, said: “People have a right to know what he has handed to Brussels, what it will cost and what rules we have to follow.



“A Prime Minister who wants to take us back into the EU, at a cost of £750million a week, cannot expect the country to take his deals with Brussels on trust.

“If there is nothing to hide, he should publish it today.”

Britain sat on EU legal text when negotiating the Northern Ireland backstop which would have kept the province bound to EU customs rules.

Brexit negotiator Lord Frost said: “When we finalised the revised Withdrawal Agreement in 2019 the text was published the same day.

He added: “If that could be done at the end of the most intense set of trade negotiations this country has ever conducted, then it can certainly be done for this reset.

“The fact that it has not should alarm everyone.



“The Prime Minister must come clean with the British public.

“What is he hiding from us?”

At a press conference on Tuesday, Reform UK leader Nigel Farage said the PM had no mandate for his UK-EU reset deal.

News.title: Burnham is playing a dangerous game by pledging to bring down energy bills when prices are largely outside his control
News.content:
Next

ANDY Burnham said this week he does not want to spend his entire premiership “banging on about Europe” – but is finding it’s now too late to put the toothpaste back in the tube.

The distinctive 2016 feel that now hangs over Westminster will go gangbusters today as the self-proclaimed Bad Boys Of Brexit reform once again.

This is Nigel Farage’s crew, including Arron Banks and Andy Wigmore, who led the Leave.EU movement ten years ago.



At a press conference attended by the Reform leader, they will launch their new pressure group called Keep Britain Out.



A campaign source last night told me they still have a database of hundreds of thousands of supporters ready to mobilise once again.

It comes hot on the heels of the rival Stay Out campaign that has largely been staffed by former Tories.

If you’re a Brexiteer aghast by the PM relitigating the referendum, you might think the more campaign groups the merrier.



During the 2016 referendum, the internal factionalism in the Brexiteer camp did not stop them claiming victory.

But this time the divisions on the right of politics are arguably even more fierce, with the Tories and Reform relentlessly kicking lumps out of each other.

Mr Burnham will be hoping these two rival Leave forces drown each other out, rather than compliment each other by appealing to different parts of the electorate.

The PM will face Kemi Badenoch in the Commons today for their weekly clash, and it could not come at a worse time for the PM as Ofgem announce the next energy price cap.



It is almost inevitable that heating bills are set to rise once again, giving the Tory leader ample ammunition to attack his pledge to reduce the cost of living.

The hike is also a reminder to Burnham that prices are largely outside his control, and so pledging to bring them down – including with his EU reset deal – is to play a dangerous game.

News.title: Horror as driver dies when 18-wheeler crashes and explodes on motorway as wreck left in huge fireball
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment huge 18-wheeler lorry explodes into an enormous fireball on a major highway, leaving the driver dead.

Horror footage showed plumes of jet-black smoke towering into the sky as roaring orange flames engulfed the Texas freeway.



The fiery blast went off as the driver was heading westbound on the Eastex Freeway in Houston when the big rig vehicle flipped, according to cops.

A huge emergency operation was launched as hazmat crews raced to the scene shortly after 2pm on Tuesday.



Houston Fire Department confirmed one death with reports suggesting the driver died inside the cab.

In the shocking footage, large flames rose from the tanker as firefighters desperately sprayed water on the wreckage.



A huge cloud of smoke could be seen drifting across the Houston skyline.

The cause of the fire is not immediately known but fire officials have confirmed the tanker was transporting fuel.



The outbound lanes of the freeway remained closed for hours as crews initiated the cleanup and crash investigators began their work.

Larry Crowson from Houston Police said: “Right now we have to get a crew out here to get that truck tipped over to see if that pavement was impacted or not.”

The fire caused significant congestion and long delays.

Officials say the cause of the blaze remains under investigation.

It comes just weeks after 12 people were injured after a monstrous explosion ripped through a factory in Brazil.



The blast went off at the Pyrozzar factory in Salto, São Paulo with footage showing terrified bystanders running from the inferno.

The factory erupted into an apocalyptic fireball, sending plumes of thick smoke billowing into the sky at breakneck pace.

The 12 injured victims included one of the company owners, military police officers, firefighters and civilians.

Emergency services rushed to the scene near the Prefeito Hélio Steffen Highway and raced wounded people to hospital.

At least 60 firefighters were deployed as well as 22 response vehicles.

News.title: Thomas Markle charged twice for possession of ‘child sex abuse material’ in Los Angeles & could face 40 years in prison
News.content:
Next

THOMAS Markle Snr has been charged twice for possession of child sex abuse material in Los Angeles.

The Duchess of Sussex’s estranged father, 82, could face up to 40 years in prison if convicted, prosecutors said.



Thomas Markle Snr – who remains in custody in Florida – has been charged with two counts of “child pornography” in California.

US attorney Bill Essayli announced on X that a federal grand jury had indicted Markle on Tuesday.



According to the indictment, Thomas Snr is alleged to have “knowingly possessed” 35mm film negatives of “sexually explicit material involving children”.

Essayli said Markle faces “a statutory maximum of 20 years in federal prison on each count if convicted”.

“Federal law enforcement was notified last month that Markle possessed child sexual abuse material (CSAM) in the Philippines and at two storage units in Los Angeles,” he continued.

“A judicially approved search warrant was executed and the materials were seized.



“Markle is expected to be arraigned on the indictment in the coming weeks in U.S. District Court in Los Angeles.

“This is an ongoing investigation. Markle is presumed innocent until proven guilty.”

The Philippine National Police (PNP) filed three charges against the 82-year-old over an alleged stash of child abuse images in the Philippines.

Markle Snr was charged with possessing child sexual abuse material in the US earlier this month after allegations against him were revealed by The Sun.

He was arrested when FBI agents raided his US care home amid a deepening probe into child sex abuse images.



Agents seized approximately 78 items from two storage units rented by Markle in Los Angeles, including slides, film negatives, and books that contained suspected child sexual abuse material.

Following his charge, Markle Snr was ordered by a judge in a Tampa court to be released on bail to the facility with an ankle bracelet.

The 82-year-old was then pictured glaring into the lens in an orange prison jumpsuit after being arrested for allegedly removing the ankle tag.

Thomas Markle Jnr, 60, said he believed his “monster” father deliberately tore off the device so he could get free medical care behind bars.

Markle Snr was taken back into custody in the US after being accused of cutting off the electronic ankle gadget ­while under house arrest.



His jail photo was released by the Pinellas County sheriff’s office following his ­re-arrest, just five days after he was held in an FBI swoop and charged.

According to first assistant US attorney Bill Essayli, Markle Snr appeared in federal court in Tampa, Florida, after authorities learned he had cut off the tag at 1.45am (6.45am UK time).

Last week, the 82-year-old was deemed mentally fit to stand trial by a Florida court.

The Sun revealed how Thomas Jnr reported his father to Philippines cops after finding alleged child sex abuse material.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He had been charged with possessing child sexual abuse material two weeks after the allegations against him were revealed.



Thomas Markle Snr has previously denied all the allegations against him.

News.title: Andy Burnham under fire for letting influencers film TikTok videos inside Downing Street – including offensive clip
News.content:
BURNHAM TIKKED OFF Andy Burnham under fire for letting influencers film TikTok videos inside Downing Street – including offensive clip







Next

ANDY Burnham was last night facing impropriety questions over his embrace of influencers – as he was forced to disown a TikTok star making “disgusting” videos on the steps of No10.

The Tories have written to Cabinet Secretary Dame Antonia Romeo demanding answers over whether public money was used to boost the PM’s personal image.



Downing Street threw a bash for social media creators this month and encouraged them to make content from the event.

Guests were treated to personalised letters from the PM and professional portraits outside the famous black door.



Influencers were also given the Hollywood treatment with a bespoke No10-branded GlamBOT of the kind used at the Oscars.

In the letter seen by The Sun, Tory Mike Wood said: “It is unclear what this event and subsequent digital content were for, if not to promote the Prime Minister’s image.

“In addition, there are clear rules around the vetting of influencers before they are featured in Government Communications.

“Considering some of the content that has materialised in the past 24 hours on social media, it would appear proper vetting did not take place.”



Whitehall rules explicitly ban the use of public resources to build ministers’ personal brands, saying that is a job for their political party instead.

The November 9 event had already landed Mr Burnham in hot water after influencer Max Balegde filmed himself outside the famous No10 black door miming along to a viral song featuring the lyrics “bomboclaat pussywagon chicken nuggets”.

Bomboclaat is a Jamaican profanity referring to a menstrual cloth while pussy is a slang term for female genitals.

Following a national outcry, Downing Street branded the now-deleted clip “clearly not acceptable”, despite the official No10 account “liking” the post initially.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch branded the antics a “disgrace” and demanded the PM disclose every penny spent on courting influencers.



She said: “I find it extraordinary that this government is raising taxes to pay people to tell them what a great job they’re doing.”

Mr Wood is demanding answers over whether any of the influencers have been paid by the Government and whether taxpayer-funded equipment was used to produce their videos.

He also questioned whether No10 was aware of the potential misuse of official government branding in clips posted on influencers’ personal accounts.



He warned: “The Government pledged to cut wasteful spending on communications.

“But spending on influencers is soaring.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Taxpayers have a right to know whether their money is being spent wisely, and whether it is being co-opted for the promotion of political causes.

Analysis by The Sun found Mr Burnham has filmed content with at least 30 influencers since becoming Prime Minister in July.

News.title: What exactly was the point of Labour’s audit into the shambles that is the disability benefits system?
News.content:
THE SUN SAYS What exactly was the point of Labour’s audit into the shambles that is the disability benefits system?

Of no benefit







Next

WHAT exactly was the point of Labour minister Sir Stephen Timms’ audit into the shambles that is the disability benefits system?

It’s obvious the Benefits Street culture nurtured under the Government is bankrupting the country.



But Timms offered NO plan to rein in PIP, projected to surge from £31.6billion to £47billion by 2031.

NO intention to cut handouts, even slightly, to incentivise work. And NO attempt to end the payment of welfare for milder mental and physical problems.



Ministers will instead fast-track claims for the most serious conditions, reduce reassessments and make applications easier — adding to the eyewatering bill.

Andy Burnham shows no sign of having the appetite to face down Left-wing Labour MPs who equate every benefits cut with Dickensian cruelty.



Which is bad news for the taxpayer and does no favours whatsoever to those who remain stuck in the welfare trap.

Criminal waste

ANDY Burnham’s “Number 10 North” vanity project in Manchester isn’t just a colossal waste of public money.

Providing security at the building is also having debilitating real-world consequences for people in the city.

The Police Federation says local cops are being pushed to breaking point by the demands of throwing a ring of steel around this gimmick.



Fighting crime will inevitably be hampered. With police and equipment stretched even thinner, villains will have a field day.

Burnham should be knuckling down to solve the enormous challenges facing the country — reinvigorating our economy, restoring our defences and stopping the boats.

Instead, he seems to be using the trappings of Downing Street primarily to stroke his own ego.

That would explain why Air Miles Andy had no qualms using a taxpayer-funded plane like a VIP taxi — even making it detour to pick him up in Manchester.

PM TikkyTokky

MEANWHILE, Burnham’s toe-curling decision to turn the seat of government into a backdrop for moronic social media stunts has returned to haunt him.



Humiliatingly, the PM had to condemn an “influencer” who, abusing his hospitality, filmed a foul-mouthed video, now deleted, in front of Downing Street.

Leave aside that Burnham faces an uncomfortable propriety probe over No10 using taxpayers’ money in pursuit of online likes.

It’s flabbergasting his aides thought it wise to welcome in YouTubers who make millions from internet pranks.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Our TikTok PM risks turning Britain into a laughing stock.

But is anyone surprised? If you invite clowns into Downing Street, the place is bound to become a circus.

News.title: Our quiet village has been ruined after Traveller site quadrupled in size to 20 caravans – the council has lost control
News.content:
Next

VILLAGE locals have been left furious after a nearby Traveller site reportedly quadrupled in size without permission.

The site in Headcorn, Kent, currently has permission for just three caravans and three mobile homes, but is now believed to hold more than 20.



Aerial photos show Thistlemere Stables in Love Lane with far more caravans than currently permitted.

The local council is now investigating claims that the traveller site has expanded without permission.



The discovery came following complaints from locals over the alleged expansion.

One angry resident, who did not want to be named, said: “It’s a living hell.



“It’s an absolute disgrace they have been able to expand by four times with no permission.

“They can do whatever they want. It’s a joke.



“Residents have been abused verbally while walking by and being sworn at. They think they own the village now.”

An elderly local added: “This should be such a lovely village. They spoil it.

“Whenever a local resident applies for planning permission for anything we have to jump through hoops.

“These people can do whatever they like. It’s so upsetting.”

Another nearby neighbour said: “There is already a disproportionate amount of Gypsy/Traveller sites, south of Maidstone from Headcorn to Paddock Wood, illegally developed on rural land without proper ecological and environmental surveys.



“This being retrospective planning falls into this category. The site will impact on the rural area and devalue neighbouring properties.

“Gypsy/travellers only represent one per cent of the UK population, the area of this site has a greatly disproportionate settlement of GT’s in rural areas.”

Maidstone Borough Council has confirmed their team is looking into claims that the site has more than quadrupled in size.



A MBC spokesperson said: “Maidstone Borough Council is aware of concerns regarding the number of caravans and mobile homes currently on land at Love Lane, Headcorn.

“The council’s Planning Enforcement Team is investigating to establish whether there has been a breach of planning control.

“Planning enforcement is a legal process and each case must be assessed on its individual circumstances and the available evidence.

“It would therefore be inappropriate for the council to speculate on the outcome of any investigation or potential enforcement action at this stage.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Should a breach of planning control be identified, Maidstone Borough Council will consider the available options and take action where it is appropriate, in accordance with planning legislation.”



The plans which had been approved were previously met with concerns from locals over noise and the value of their houses.

News.title: How Putin’s ‘doomsday space nuke’ plot could destroy 16,000 satellites & plunge Western society into chaos
News.content:
Next

AFTER his twitching finger pressed the nuclear button, Vladimir Putin’s space bomb would obliterate the swarm of satellites that are key to our way of life.

Emitting a giant electromagnetic pulse and then creating a vast radiation cloud, the nuke would wipe out spy satellites, Starlink and other space communication we’ve come to rely on.



Agriculture, shipping, weather monitoring, mapping and finance would face severe disruption causing panic and market meltdown in Western societies.

It might sound like something from an excitable sci-fi novel, yet Western intelligence sources believe Russia may be preparing to send a nuke into space in just DAYS.



So, are Britain and its allies ready to meet the doomsday threat?

TikToking Prime Minister Andy Burnham has found time to film with a constellation of at least 30 fame-hungry social media influencers in just four months.



Now, something with a little more gravity has arrived in his in-tray.

According to credible German media reports, Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite in the next 60 days.

Intelligence sources told the outlets that the Sputnik-S satellite has been taken out of storage in Moscow and the Kremlin may be planning to launch it imminently.

The intel has been disseminated to Western allies which would doubtless include Britain. It’s unclear which agency provided the original information.



Head of the European Space Agency Josef Aschbacher said that sending nuclear weapons into space was “the ultimate nightmare scenario”.

While German government spokesperson Stefan Kornelius insisted Berlin was taking the intelligence reports “very seriously”, on Monday, Nato chief Mark Rutte vowed to defend against a space nuke.

The alliance’s Secretary General said: “I can assure ⁠you, we will always make sure we defend every inch‌of Nato territory. “That ‌includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element.”

Speaking alongside Rutte, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz did not confirm or deny the intelligence leaks of a Russian nuclear-primed satellite. However, Merz insisted the reports “reveal the level of escalation Russia is evidently prepared to pursue”.

Russia has been quick to deny it is preparing to blast a nuke into space.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov dismissed stories citing “unknown sources” as “hardly worth taking seriously”.



While the Russian embassy in Berlin said it rejected “unfounded allegations” and said the media reports were part of a “propaganda campaign”. Yet, a declassified report released by the US Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) last month warned of Russia’s space bomb plans.

If detonated, it said the nuke could wipe out “thousands of satellites operated by countries and companies around the world, as well as the vital communications, navigation, scientific, meteorological, commercial and national security services they provide.”

The DIA report added that it would “also leave lingering radiation belts, which could persist for years and damage satellites that initially were only temporarily disrupted”.

So why do the US military know with such certainty the devastation a nuclear bomb in space would unleash?



Well, the Americans have already done it five times. The largest, launched from Johnston Atoll in the middle of the Pacific on July 9, 1962, had a series of unintended consequences.

The Starfish Prime warhead, carried by a Thor missile, was detonated 13 minutes 41 seconds after lift-off at an altitude of 250 miles. In the vacuum of space, it caused an electromagnetic pulse that was so large it sent many of the instruments used to measure the blast off the scale.

Another surprise came when 300 street lights, numerous burglar alarms and telephone calls in Hawaii — 900 miles from the detonation point — were knocked out. Then it caused a blood-red and neon-green twilight to spread above thousands of miles of ocean.

Watching at “Rainbow Bomb” hotel rooftop parties in Hawaiian capital Honolulu, locals witnessed an eerie crimson aurora for several minutes. Up in space came another unintended consequence, Starfish Prime disabled half the world’s satellites.



Back in 1962, that wasn’t disastrous. Today, with the global space economy worth £479billion, it would be catastrophic. Researchers say a space nuke detonated now would destroy most of the 16,000 satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO).

The global economy increasingly relies on the satellites orbiting hundreds of miles above our heads. Western militaries and spy agencies employ satellites for reconnaissance and manoeuvres. And Ukraine expertly uses Elon Musk’s Starlink for battlefield comms, piloting bomber drones and air defence warnings against Russian drones.

It’s why Russia’s war-mongering President Putin is threatening a space nuclear race. But why would Putin detonate a space nuke when it would also take out his own satellites?

Bleddyn Bowen, co-director of the Space Research Centre at Durham University said: “Russia, too, stands to lose the use of very useful military and civilian satellite infrastructures in such a scenario. “This is merely nuclear sabre-rattling.”

Yet, Moscow security analyst Dmitry Stefanovich has pointed out that Russia is far less reliant on space infrastructure for its military and economy than the Western allies. Creating nuclear havoc in space would, in his words, strategically “flip the chessboard”.



In 1967, the Outer Space Treaty signed by Britain, the US and the Soviet Union, banned nukes and other weapons of mass destruction from space.

However, two years ago, Russia vetoed a UN Security Council resolution to reaffirm the ban.

Britain’s then UN Ambassador Barbara Woodward said: “There was nothing in this resolution that any law-abiding state committed to peace and the prevention of an arms race in outer space could reasonably object to. “And yet Russia did.”

When Putin launched his maniacal war on Ukraine in 2022, the first assault wasn’t with tanks and infantry but a cyberattack on a commercial satellite system. Star wars are already here.

Two Russian satellites have been observed approaching ageing European ones to intercept communications. To thwart them, the Europeans then manoeuvre them away.

Analysts have likened the jousts to World War Two-style fighter plane dogfights in space.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Doubtless, Putin is enjoying the frisson of danger the reports of his potential nuclear satellite have sent through Western governments and intelligence agencies.

A man whose scheming evil now extends to the serenity of space.

News.title: Six dead and 14 injured after gas explosion at busy restaurant in Vietnam
News.content:
Six dead and 14 injured after gas explosion at busy restaurant in Vietnam

The explosion damaged nearby houses and shook neighbouring apartment buildings, as debris was scattered 20 metres across the street. Photos of the restaurant captured tables and chairs hurled across the ground.

View 3 Images The scene after an explosion at a hotpot eatery in Hanoi, Vietnam on Tuesday (Image: Nguyá»…n Quang Háº£i/VNA via AP)

Six people have died and more than a dozen have been injured after a restaurant collapsed following a gas explosion.

‌



‌



The horrific blast shattered windows and cracked walls in Vietnam's capital Hanoi on Tuesday, November 24.

‌



The incident occurred at around 8am on Tuesday a busy hot pot restaurant, located on the city's Van Tuyet food street. The tragic incident comes just two weeks after a gas cylinder blast caused a building to collapse in Ho Chi Minh City, killing two people and injuring 12 others.

‌



The Ministry of Public Security believes the incident was related to cooking gas. The restaurant was full at the time and more than 14 people have been hospitalised, including one with a traumatic brain injury.

One victim died in hospital after being struck by flying debris. According to preliminary reports, the victim had been walking past the restaurant when the blast left him injured.

A search is underway for survivors and police have deployed specialised detection equipment and hydraulic machinery to lift concrete slabs.

‌



The explosion damaged nearby houses and shook neighbouring apartment buildings, a preliminary report found. Debris was scattered 20 metres across the street.

Local woman Lan Phuong, 26, said the blast woke her and her younger sister, sending their balcony door flying, news.co.au reports.

News.title: Six people including two children missing after plane crash near Horn Island
News.content:
Six people including two children missing after plane crash near Horn Island

The plane left New Orleans on Tuesday afternoon and was last seen at 3:45pm local time, before descending at 10,000 feet per minute, according to reports

View 2 Images Horn Island is about 10 miles south of Ocean Springs and is 3,014 acres, including 174 acres of private land

A light aircraft has crashed, leaving six people - including two children - missing. The plane reportedly lost contact with authorities at 3:45pm CST on Tuesday, November 24.

‌



‌



It took off from New Orleans Lakefront Airport earlier on Tuesday, WDSU news reported. It crashed near Horn Island in Mississippi, according to the US Coast Guard.

‌



Horn Island is a remote barrier island off the coast of the US, in the Gulf of Mexico, close to New Orleans that can only be accessed by private boat. The wreckage has been spotted around two nautical miles from the island.

‌



The Coast Guard in Mobile, Alabama, told CNN it has found the cabin of the plane, along with three life jackets and a life raft. Reports suggest the single-engine Cessna Centurion 210 was losing 18,000 feet of altitude per minute around the time it crashed.

The plane started rapidly descending around 30 minutes after taking off, when it was at roughly 8,800 feet of altitude, Flightradar24 data added. It was south of Pascagoula, Mississippi when the plane rapidly lost altitude, descending at more than 200 miles per hour in its last few recorded seconds before the data ends.

None of the passengers, four adults and two children, aged eight and 12, have been located. The plane was on its way to Fort Myers in Florida ahead of Thanksgiving, the biggest holiday in the US celebrated on the fourth Thursday in November annually.
