News.title: Solomon Islands names Australia as its primary security partner in a new treaty that excludes China
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The prime ministers of Australia and Solomon Islands signed a bilateral security pact Wednesday following reports that the tiny South Pacific island nation will end its secretive 4-year-old defense deal with China.

The new treaty confirms Australia’s place as the Solomons’ “primary security partner” and states “there will be no foreign military or security base” on the smaller nation 2,000 kilometers (1,200 miles) northeast of Australia, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and his Solomon Islands counterpart Matthew Wale said in a statement.

The deal is the latest bilateral security pact Australia has struck with Pacific neighbors since Beijing inked a treaty with the Solomons’ previous government in 2022 that created fears the Chinese navy would build a base in the South Pacific.

Wale would not confirm or deny news media reports that his government had told Beijing that the security pact with China, which has provided Chinese police trainers to the Solomons’ capital Honiara, would not be renewed when it expires after five years in early 2027.

“Unfortunately there is a non-disclosure clause in the treaty with China,” Wale told reporters in a press conference with Albanese at Australian Parliament House. “So I am unable to talk about that. We have ongoing discussions with China.”

“As you know, Solomon Islands has been, for a number of years, a source of uncertainty and doubt in the region. Those days are done. Gone. We don’t want to be there again,” he added.

In Beijing, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun did not directly answer a journalist’s question about whether the Solomons had said it would end the Chinese security pact.

“China always follows the principle of mutual respect and equality in developing relations with the Solomon Islands,” Guo said Tuesday.

“There is no element of geopolitical rivalry or bloc confrontation in cooperation between China and Pacific island countries, including the Solomon Islands,” he added.

Albanese said the new bilateral treaty elevated bilateral relations to a “level which has never been seen before and has never been stronger.”

The treaty is broader than security. Australia has agreed to also invest in Solomons’ infrastructure, education, renewable energy and sport.

Oliver Nobetau, Pacific Islands program director at the Lowy Institute, a Sydney think tank, described the treaty as significant and fine-tuned to the Solomons’ priorities.

“It demonstrates that Australia is listening to what the Pacific partners want,” Nobetau told Australian Broadcasting Corp.

News.title: New maps issued hours before Iowa detonation show toxic cloud to spread to second state
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The Army has issued new maps hours before it detonates nearly 70 barrels of lead azide in Iowa, showing a toxic cloud spreading toward northern Missouri.

The maps showed lead dust from Wednesday morning’s blast traveling southwest from the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown into northeastern Missouri between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. Central Time. Officials chose Wednesday because they said it had the most favorable weather conditions.

Federal officials also warned Tuesday that vulnerable individuals such as pregnant women and children should evacuate the area.

“If they are women who are pregnant, children under the age of 6, or children in general, and individuals who may have chronic disease, you definitely want to be out of that area,” Sean Kaufman, the principal deputy assistant secretary for preparedness and response at the Department of Health and Human Services, said at a press conference in Iowa, The Washington Sun reported.

“I would evacuate that area that’s signaled in the model. Outside of that area, if you’re close to that proximity and you’re uncomfortable, I think you need to do what you need to do to take care of your family.”

open image in gallery The new maps showed lead dust from Wednesday morning’s blast traveling southwest from the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown into northeastern Missouri between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m. Central Time ( Lori McFate )

Iowa residents have received an alert from federal emergency officials who said some people within five miles southwest of the detonation site may be evacuated before the controlled detonation and that people living five to 20 miles away should stay indoors with windows shut.

Locals are spending their Thanksgiving week taping up windows in their homes and buying supplies like masks and gloves instead of preparing for the holiday on Thursday.

Resident Bob Kemp was supposed to travel down south for Thanksgiving, but was compelled to stay and watch over his and his sister’s homes.

“I’m going to stay here and see how things go,” Kemp told WQAD News 8. “If they would have blown it today, I probably would have went to Texas for Thanksgiving, but since that’s not happening, it’s going to happen on Wednesday, that changed all our plans.”

open image in gallery Federal officials also warned Tuesday that vulnerable individuals such as pregnant women and children should evacuate the area, telling concerned locals, ‘You definitely want to be out of that area’ ( Lori McFate )

The blast was initially scheduled for last Friday, but the Army was held up in court over health and environmental concerns. A federal appeals court ultimately ruled that the Environmental Protection Agency had adequate protections to minimize the spread of lead dust.

But residents are still worried about the potential effects of lead exposure, which is especially harmful for children. Even low levels of lead in a child’s blood can seriously harm their health, including brain damage and slowed growth and development, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

“I’m really angry about this. I feel like we’re guinea pigs,” Krys Plate, a retired second-grade teacher who lives with her husband and their two teenage daughters two miles south of the fence line of the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, told The New York Times.

The Army has advised everyone in the affected areas — but especially pregnant women, children and people with chronic diseases — to avoid outdoor activities until further notice. State health officials in neighboring Illinois have warned residents to stay inside for 24 to 48 hours after the detonation.

People may be exposed to lead, not just from breathing it in but also from surfaces where the dust lands, the Army notes. Once it’s safe to leave their homes, the Army advised people to clean surfaces that may be touched by children, including play equipment, tables and chairs and handrails.

open image in gallery Locals are spending their Thanksgiving week taping up windows in their homes and buying supplies like masks and gloves instead of preparing for the holiday on Thursday ( Getty Images )

As the public becomes more concerned about lead dust filling the air, President Donald Trump has insisted that the detonation is necessary — even calling on Governor-elect Rob Sand to agree to it if he doesn’t want blood on his hands, despite the Democrat not taking office until January.

“The Experts, in particular the United States Military, feel that this approach will be a far safer one than allowing the situation to fester, not knowing when they will detonate by themselves,” Trumpwrote on Truth Social Monday before the appeal court’s decision allowing the detonation to proceed.

“If [Sand] or the Courts do not agree, we will have no choice but to not proceed with the controlled removal of these hazardous materials, and be forced to hold the incoming Governor responsible for any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation,” the president added.

Later Monday, Sand wrote on X that the Trump administration “should make this decision based on the information they have from the people they brought in to do the job months ago and have been on the ground in Middletown for weeks.”

News.title: Coffee shop staff revolt and location is ‘permanently closed’ after accusations of ICE agent’s ownership
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Staff members at a Chicago coffee shop have walked out on the job after accusations that an agent for Immigration and Customs Enforcement was the co-owner of the popular community spot.

A sign that read “permanently closed” hung on the door of Tasa Coffee Roasters in the Humboldt Park neighborhood Tuesday, a photo obtained by CBS News Chicago showed. The storefront had remnants of eggs that were seemingly thrown at the windows and what appeared to be a sign workers had written that was now torn off the glass.

Local nonprofit news site Block Club Chicago had shared a photo of the workers’ sign on Monday before it was taken down. It read, “After finding out from Reddit, that there are allegations Pierre Marquez is an ICE agent, we the baristas and roasters have closed for the day.

“We do not stand beside, condone, support, or accept anyone or any org associated with ICE. As the baristas, we are discussing what steps will be necessary for us. We intend to do our best as employees to be as honest and transparent as we can be.”

open image in gallery A sign that read ‘permanently closed’ hung on the door of Tasa Coffee Roasters in the Humboldt Park neighborhood Tuesday, after workers walked out on the job over accusations that an agent for Immigration and Customs Enforcement was the co-owner of the popular community spot ( Google Earth )

A recent post in a subreddit for the Humboldt Park community claimed that the ICE List, an unofficial database about ICE activity, listed Pierre Marquez as an agent.

“They have their ‘Hands Off Chicago’ sign and act like they're for the community, all while her husband is ripping families apart,” the Reddit user who made the post wrote.

Jackie Marquez opened Tasa Coffee Roasters with her husband Pierre Marquez in 2022, according to local reports.

“We're proud to show that two first-generation Latinos were able to create a space by Latinos, and not just for Latinos, for everyone," Pierre Marquez said in an October 2025 interview with CBS News Chicago.

open image in gallery A recent Reddit post claimed that Pierre Marquez, who reportedly opened Tasa Coffee Roasters with his wife, Jackie Marquez, in 2022, was an ICE agent ( Getty Images )

But Jackie Marquez seemed to distance her husband from the coffee shop in a post on Instagram Stories, calling herself the “sole owner.”

“I personally disagree with current immigration policy, and I believe in civil dialogue and mutual respect, even when we disagree,” the post read. “I ask that my employees not be targeted or held responsible for matters outside their control. My commitment remains firmly with my employees, my customers, and my community.”

The Independent has reached out to Tasa Coffee Roasters for comment.

The accusations against Pierre Marquez outraged the community, with customers and elected officials speaking out.

"I started coming here at 10 a.m. every single morning, Monday through Friday…It's Latina-owned. I'm Latina," former customer Alex Rodriguez told WLS. "It's just really disappointing to see that sometimes your own people will turn their backs on you."

The Northwest Side Progressive Coalition, which includes Democratic Congresswoman Delia C. Ramirez and other local politicians, said it was “no longer supporting, promoting, or partnering” with the coffee shop following the accusations against Pierre Marquez.

“As our immigrant neighbors are living with the fear that someone they love could be taken into detention, we reject any and all businesses that profit from or enable ICE’s terror.”

open image in gallery A spokesperson for ICE declined to confirm whether Pierre Marquez worked for the agency or in another role at the Department of Homeland Security, telling The Independent , ‘We don’t confirm or deny officer identities’ ( Getty Images )

It’s been nearly two years since President Donald Trump took office and kicked off his massive deportation campaign. Stories of federal immigration agents fatally shooting U.S. citizens and detaining a five-year-old boy in Minnesota earlier this year sparked huge public outcry. Many Americans find ICE’s tactics too aggressive and have taken to the streets of major cities, including Chicago, to protest the agency.

The Northwest Side Progressive Coalition mentioned Operation Midway Blitz, an ICE operation targeting illegal immigrants in Chicago that started in September 2025, in Monday’s statement, saying the “terror” created by it “kept families home, and neighborhood businesses lost customers they depended on.”

A spokesperson for ICE declined to confirm whether Pierre Marquez worked for the agency or in another role at the Department of Homeland Security.

“We don’t confirm or deny officer identities. Doxxing our officers puts their lives and their families in serious danger. Our law enforcement officers are on the front lines arresting terrorists, gang members, murderers, pedophiles, and rapists. Now, thanks to the malicious rhetoric of sanctuary politicians, they are under constant threat from violent agitators,” the spokesperson said.

ICE agents are “experiencing coordinated campaigns of violence against them and facing more than a 1,600% increase in assaults against them, a 3,300% increase in vehicular attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats,” the spokesperson said, adding, “Attempting to publicize their identities puts their lives and the lives of their families at serious risk.”

The Independent has not verified the agency’s figures.

News.title: A year after Hong Kong's deadly fire, survivors struggle with loss and lingering sense of injustice
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Yip Ka-kui still sends WhatsApp voice messages to his wife even though they will never be heard. She was one of 168 people killed last November in Hong Kong’s deadliest fire in decades.

Over the past year, the 68-year-old Yip never turned on the television, struggled to step into a supermarket and stopped taking photos outdoors with his camera — all things he used to do with his wife, Pak Shui-lin. He learned to dine alone. Sometimes, he would cry when thoughts of her crept in. The hardest moments came at night, when sleep eluded him hours past midnight.

Now living in his eldest son's place within walking distance of their charred apartment at Wang Fuk Court, Yip has preferred mostly to stay at home in recent months because the familiar streets are full of memories.

“Sometimes, a feeling would suddenly flood in,” he said. “I can't believe she's no longer here."

Residents raised concerns before deadly fire

Like Yip, many residents displaced by the fire that swept through seven apartment buildings were still grieving. Over the past year, they returned to their old homes to collect belongings, learned of improper practices and inadequate oversight that led to the fire, and last month watched officials bow in apology over the tragedy.

But even as life kept pushing them forward, some said justice had yet to be served, and felt pressure from authorities when voicing their concerns. Some residents planned to offer flowers to mark the first anniversary on Thursday, with various religious commemorations to be held in the city.

Before the fire, some residents had already complained to the government about fire hazards during the complex’s building maintenance project. Yip had raised concerns about workers smoking with the main contractor and complained about the project to the Urban Renewal Authority.

But the residents' worst fears came true on Nov. 26, 2025. That day, Pak knocked on her neighbors’ doors to warn them of the fire, saving some, but could not make it out herself. An investigation found the blaze was likely caused by a lit cigarette and spread rapidly through non-fire-retardant scaffolding material.

When the investigation hearings laid bare the facts, Yip was furious.

In May, he returned to their home of over 20 years with flowers. Most of their belongings were burned to ashes, and he could fit all he retrieved into a single ziplock bag. He found his wedding band, but not his wife's.

“You go to a peaceful place, and don't worry about us," he then told her at their home.

Some fire survivors who speak out face pushback

Betty Ho, another survivor, spent 18 years paying the mortgage and only began her retirement last year. When the blaze broke out, she was asleep, and a call from her former colleague checking in on her got her out in time.

The 61-year-old now lives in temporary housing with a view of Wang Fuk Court and can sometimes only fall asleep after sunrise.

When Ho returned to her apartment in May, she found the floor melted and the walls damaged. Her vinyls had warped and her toy cars were ruined, though she retrieved some Doraemon toys.

Ho wished their homes could be rebuilt at the original site, but the government rejected that, saying reconstruction would take about a decade.

She had planned to hang a banner bearing that wish at her old home. But police told her not to do it, she said. Posters making the same demand were also removed in other apartments, local media reported.

In the end, she could only put up posters expressing her love for Wang Fuk Court.

“I'm not doing anything illegal, just sticking them inside my own home. But even that had so many restrictions. I feel the Hong Kong government is no longer the one I knew,” she said.

In a city where national security laws have all but silenced political opposition, the tragedy is a sensitive issue.

The government condemned those it said were “using the disaster to stir up chaos." After people who posted allegedly seditious content online or organized a petition were detained, not everyone felt free to speak. The arrests of an outspoken Wang Fuk Court resident and his wife over fraud allegations unrelated to the fire sent a chill.

Last Friday, Hong Kong Chief Secretary for Administration Eric Chan said the government would not obstruct any lawful commemoration activities but urged residents to carefully choose what to take part in and not to be exploited by people with ulterior motives.

In an emailed response to questions from The Associated Press, the government said Hong Kong is a society governed by the rule of law and any activity that does not violate the law may proceed. But the authorities did not address questions over the posters.

It said the arrests of the former residents had nothing to do with the tragedy, and police declined to comment on the case because it has entered judicial proceedings.

Survivors make hard choices on resettlement

Residents had also been navigating difficult choices about whether to accept the administration's resettlement plan by its Aug. 31 deadline and sell their homeownership rights to the government.

The government deemed that the seven buildings would be difficult to repair cost-effectively and was inclined to demolish them. In September, it said over 99% of the owners of the seven buildings and the remaining one unscathed by the fire agreed to sell.

But Ho refused, saying it was unfair and pointing to a lack of a property inspection report for them to read.

She now faces an uncertain future as the government could later introduce legislation to acquire the remaining apartments. She said the Basic Law, the city's miniconstitution, protects the right of private property ownership.

“I want to see how far it can go,” she said.

Some sold reluctantly. Yip said he had no choice after weighing his family's finances and future — though he deliberately signed just before the deadline.

“The only gesture I could still make was to let you know I would hold on until the very last moment," he said.

Residents question accountability

Prosecution of the companies and individuals involved in the maintenance project is still ongoing.

But an official investigation report in October found faults in the maintenance work and deficiencies in regulatory oversight.

Hong Kong leader John Lee apologized, saying his housing minister had resigned to bear “political accountability." Various reform measures were also announced.

But Ho felt the minister's resignation was not the same as bearing political accountability. She said the government’s apology was not sincere as it came 11 months late.

“Whatever they do now, it will be very hard to accept as satisfactory,” she said.

Yip said he couldn't understand why three other bureaus that oversaw other departments where failings were identified did not have to bear political responsibility.

The authorities, he said, needed to show they were genuinely facing the disaster with a sense of commitment, but their swift rejection of rebuilding at Wang Fuk Court and their strict deadlines for the homeownership buyout plan suggested otherwise.

He said he was not picking a fight, but he just could not let go of how they lost their home and how they were treated afterward.

“It felt as though we were recast from disaster victims to troublemakers. I can't swallow it,” he said.

Yip could not say how long it would take to move on.

“All I can say is that, for now, I will keep going,” he said.

News.title: Under-performing Manchester City are an accident waiting to happen
News.content:
Enzo Maresca had two home games in four days to get Manchester City into decent shape for Sunday’s clash against Arsenal, which now feels like a must-win. On Tuesday, however, they ended up being taunted by Rasmus Hojlund on another evening that raised more questions than answers.

It is now one win in seven for Maresca, who cannot keep a clean sheet and has a £327m midfield that have played well individually, but is yet to form a unit. Worryingly, their reliable source of goals, Erling Haaland, had his quietest game of the season. It required Rayan Cherki to rescue a point against Napoli.

Maresca needs to find a solution in the next five days before heading to the Emirates to face the champions in what could be a defining weekend for the season. Defeat would put them nine points off the pace, with Maresca still trying to find his best combination of players to pick.

Club captain Rúben Dias was on the bench here and Josko Gvardiol was left out of the draw against Fulham at the weekend, which also ended as a draw rather than a morale-boosting win to get City out of their slump.

News.title: Arsenal have 30 shots and still manage to mess it up
News.content:
Mikel Arteta may prefer to imagine his Arsenal team as a remorseless winning machine, although on nights such as these they can still demonstrate a familiar unreliability when it comes to the main purpose of it all.

There were 30 shots over the night from the English champions, only four of which were on target, and in the end their winner never came. Even in the 95th minute, Arteta’s players were still conspiring to foul it up. This Champions League game might have been decided in Arsenal’s favour within 20 minutes. By half-time it should have been a formality. Yet, as chance after chance slipped away, there was always a possibility this would end differently.

The leaders of the Bundesliga were traumatised at times by the ferocity of the Arsenal press, and there were times when Borussia Dortmund will likely have no idea how they survived. Even so, they did just that and, liberated in the second half, Maximilian Beier scored an improbable equaliser in his team’s best period. There were still 40 minutes for Arsenal to put this one to bed and they found many ways not to do so.

It was notable that the man who put Arsenal ahead in the ninth minute with a right-foot thump from space on the edge of the Dortmund box was the same striker who would miss the best chance to win it. That is the Viktor Gyokeres dilemma. In the space of a single game he can look like a potential match-winner and also the last man his manager would wish to see arriving on the end of a perfect Martin Odegaard cross.

So it proved on 75 minutes when Gyokeres thrust himself at an Odegaard ball into the box that just needed guiding inside the post, yet planted it decisively wide of the mark. On the touchline Arteta tried very hard to hide his despair and failed to do so.

News.title: Poor Aston Villa crumble in Turkey to make it six games without a win
News.content:
Aston Villa supporters have happy memories of Istanbul after May’s Europa League final, and they return to face Galatasaray this evening in a fixture which could forecast their Champions League prospects.

It has been par for the course for Unai Emery’s team in Europe so far, with victories over Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Viking and a defeat at Barcelona aligning with the form book.

Nine points from 12 leaves them inside the top eight at the halfway stage of the league phase, but tougher challenges are ahead with PSG and Borussia Dortmund to come after tonight’s game.

Since a statement victory over Manchester City, it has been a frustrating time for Villa either side of the international break. They were dumped out of the League Cup by Bournemouth, were second-best in a home draw with Fulham, threw away a pair of two-goal leads at Old Trafford, and were held by Sunderland at the weekend.

Though Villa put six past Galatasaray’s city rivals Fenerbahce at Villa Park, away games against Turkish opposition can be different beasts, as Liverpool discovered in the last round of Champions League matches.

Galatasaray’s two major attacking threats, Victor Osimhen and Rafael Leão, are both absent with injuries. Davinson Sanchez and Lucas Torreira are former Premier League players in their squad. Galatasaray have won two of four Champions League games, losing to Barcelona and Sporting Lisbon, but they are top of the Turkish Super Lig.

Villa will be without right-back Matty Cash owing to a concussion sustained during the international break with Poland, but will hope to have Victor Lindelof available again after he missed the Sunderland draw with illness.

Emery’s team were unable to train at Rams Park yesterday in order to give a troublesome pitch maximum recovery time after emergency renovation work.

“If we could have trained in the stadium of Galatasaray, maybe we would have decided for the same situation, but it’s not changing our routine,” Emery said. “How the pitch is going to be tomorrow is important, but it’s not an excuse because it’s [the same] for both teams. Hopefully the pitch will be as best as possible.”

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Anthropic falls below stock market listing price
News.content:
Anthropic’s shares dropped below their initial public offering price for the first time, sealing a dramatic reversal of fortunes for the AI giant following its blockbuster stock market debut last week.

The Claude chatbot maker saw its shares fall more than 8pc from their $83 offer price to stand at around $76 as investors appeared to grow sceptical of its valuation.

The slide on the Nasdaq exchange was set to wipe over $200bn from the company’s market value.

Anthropic raised more than $81bn in the biggest IPO on record, with its valuation surging to $2tn as the shares peaked at around $115.

But the company bucked Monday’s huge rally following Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia with the shares slipping from Friday’s close.

Wall Street resumed its slide on Tuesday as underlying fears over the AI trade appear to have outweighed the impact of Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as chief executive.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 was down as much as 3pc, with the benchmark S&P 500 around 1.2 pc lower.

In London, the FTSE 100 closed slightly lower, down 0.1pc, unable to sustain gains made in global markets on Monday.

The ability of AI companies to generate sufficient returns on their massive investment has proved more important than Nvidia’s boardroom drama, according to Goldman Sachs analysts.

Sharon Bell told Bloomberg: “The AI trade really depends on whether companies can make a return on the capex they spend.

“If the answer is yes, then the tech sector should do well over time and if the answer is no, it won’t do so well.”

Ms Bell argued that the management changes at Nvidia would not “make a huge difference either way”.

Glenn Yin at online trading platform ACCM told the Reuters Global Markets Forum: “By the end of ​the day, these businesses need to make enough money to justify investors’ expectations.

“‌My point is: Jensen’s return does not solve this. So, the sentiment is more emotional than sensible, in my opinion.”

Major chipmakers saw their stocks sink on Tuesday as general AI-related optimism faded.

Nvidia, the world’s largest chipmaker, saw its stock fall more than 7pc, while the Philadelphia semiconductor index, which tracks the major US manufacturers of chips, fell 8pc.

Microchip maker AMD’s share price was down as much as 10pc, while shares in Broadcom were down around 3pc.

The dollar eased back from its highest level in almost two years after Jensen ​Huang’s return to Nvidia revived the AI rally and fuelled expectations of more interest rate rises.

The President’s intervention, however, is a “slippery slope”, according to a top Republican senator.

Dave McCormick, the former boss of hedge fund Bridgewater, told Bloomberg: “I am worried about the precedent of the executive branch getting involved in real ownership deals with companies but also in board governance and making these decisions.

“This is a precedent that I don’t think we want to replicate or reinforce.”

Mr McCormick will be one of the politicians grilling the Nvidia boss next week when he testifies before the Senate Banking Committee.

Todd Blanche, the US Attorney General, has labelled Nvidia “a good corporate citizen” despite questions over whether Jensen Huang’s alleged affair could have threatened national security.

Mr Blanche added that if Nvidia was the target of a criminal investigation, “that wouldn’t be the message”.

News.title: Meningitis outbreak triggers epidemic alert in Gaza
News.content:
Cases of meningitis have risen dramatically in Gaza and have triggered an epidemic alert, the territory’s health ministry has said.

At least 272 cases were recorded across the enclave in October, more than eight times the usual monthly rate of 30 to 50 cases, Dr Nidal Ghoneim, a senior health ministry official, told a press conference on Tuesday.

Children under one year old account for 71 per cent of cases, with newborns alone accounting for 13 per cent, World Health Organization (WHO) spokesperson Christian Lindmeier said in a separate briefing.

Dr Ghoneim added that 15 Palestinians had died of meningitis since the start of the year, and that the spread of the disease through the strip threatened the lives of thousands of people, mostly children.

It is thought that most cases are being driven by enterovirus – the leading cause of viral meningitis – which is shed through faeces and can spread rapidly between people in unsanitary environments.

All six wastewater treatment plants in Gaza are currently out of operation, meaning an estimated 150,000 cubic metres of untreated sewage flows into the environment every day, according to the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).

News.title: Trapped Ebola health workers rescued after three days of fighting in Congo
News.content:
Ebola health workers have been rescued after being trapped by fighting for more than three days, in clashes further hampering efforts to curb the virus in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, head of the World Health Organization, said staff had been evacuated from a hospital in Akwe, Ituri province, “under very challenging circumstances”.

The health chief had earlier pleaded for peace, and warned staff had “been sheltering for their lives in a maternity ward of the facility for over 24 hours”.

Staff were caught in a crossfire between the Congolese army, and the People’s Revolutionary Convention (CRP) group led by former International Criminal Court (ICC) convict, Thomas Lubanga, French RFI radio reported.

Local media reported heavy clashes between the army and the CRP in Ituri in recent days. At least 10 people were killed and a stream of refugees fled to the provincial capital, Bunia.

As security worsened, the WHO said it had relocated health teams from Mongbwalu.

News.title: Welsh slogger blasts England to crushing win over Australia
News.content:
It will take more than a few lusty blows to become the cricketing Don in these parts, but an extraordinary display of six-hitting from Aneurin Donald, ably supported by Phil Salt, helped England and Wales to a stunning eight-wicket victory over Australia.

Donald and Salt, the Welsh-born opening pair, put on 151 to help chase down Australia’s 184 with 41 balls to spare. David Gower famously flew a pre-war Tiger Moth between the floodlights, about 200 feet above the ground, on England’s only previous visit to this ground in 1991. It was a good thing he was doing no such thing tonight, with balls flying everywhere off Donald’s blade. He hit nine sixes, one shy of Salt’s England T20 record, in his 85 from 32 balls, before being caught on the fence with the game as good as won.

Donald, who turns 30 next month, has taken the slow road to the big stage. As a teenager, he smashed 234 off 136 balls for Glamorgan against Derbyshire in the County Championship at Colwyn Bay, but at 21 left for Hampshire. Two serious ACL injuries derailed his career, and he moved to Derbyshire in 2023, where he has turned into a formidable T20 opener.

“I am pretty decent at slogging and not too good at batting, so I will keep swinging as hard as I can,” he reflected afterwards. “Luckily there might be a career in it now, not a few years ago.”

Sports.title: Rasmus Hojlund reveals the five words he shouted after scoring against Man City that Utd fans will love
Sports.content:

RASMUS HOJLUND aimed a cheeky dig at Manchester City after scoring against his former club’s bitter rivals in the Champions League.

The Danish striker opened the scoring in Napoli‘s thrilling 2-2 draw with City at the Etihad on Tuesday night.



Hojlund never got going in three years at Manchester United after his £72million transfer from Atalanta.

And, despite impressing on loan at Napoli last season, the Red Devils were more than happy to unceremoniously cut ties with him in the summer.



But he clearly still holds United close to his heart as he could not resist winding up the City supporters as he celebrated his goal.

Hojlund was spotted shouting towards the crowd before being mobbed by his Napoli team-mates.



And after the game, the striker confirmed to TNT Sports that he had shouted: “Only one club in Manchester.”

Asked about his celebration, Hojlund said: “Yeah, it’s good banter.

“There’s a rivalry between Manchester City and United and I have a past with United.

“That’s my club. Nothing against Manchester City. It was good to score here.”

And his comments went down a storm with United supporters on social media.

One wrote: “That’s our Rasmus.”

Another added: “Right buy him back, I need his passion and desire back in my life.”

Hojlund broke the deadlock in the 55th minute after City were caught trying to play out from the back.

Former Chelsea midfielder Billy Gilmour slipped the striker through before he got the better of Marc Guehi and fired a low left-footed effort beyond Gianluigi Donnarumma.



City drew level in the 67th minute when Ayyoub Bouaddi scored his first goal for the club following a short corner involving Jeremy Doku.

But Napoli restored their advantage nine minutes later when Noa Lang smashed home a brilliant volley from Leonardo Spinazzola‘s cross.

Sports.title: Ballon d’Or winner’s son joins non-league Basingstoke Town just weeks after joining previous club
Sports.content:
Next

ANDRIY SHEVCHENKO’S son Kristian Shevchenko has signed with Basingstoke Town just eight weeks after joining fellow non-league club Sholing.

Andriy, 50, will go down in football history having won the Ballon d’Or in 2004 as well as a raft of silverware during a glittering 19-year career playing for AC Milan, Chelsea and Dynamo Kyiv.



The iconic striker led Milan to the Serie A, Coppa Italia and Champions League title during a successful eight-year stint across two spells with the Italian giants.

And although the Ukraine great never managed to live up to expectations at Chelsea between 2006 and 2009, he still picked up an FA Cup and League Cup honour.



Kristian, 20, is hoping to follow into his famous dad’s footsteps but has had to settle for some slightly less exotic climes to kick off his senior career.

The winger joined Sholing last month but never got any minutes with the Southern League Premier Division South outfit.

Now Shevchenko will experience the glitz and glamour of Basingstoke, with the local side also competing in the seventh tier.

Kristian said: “I’m really happy to have signed for Basingstoke Town, it’s a great opportunity for me, and I’m genuinely excited to be part of the club and contribute to what we’re building.

“I’m hungry to work hard, give everything for the badge and, most importantly, help the team achieve its ambitions. I can’t wait to get going and hopefully score plenty of goals along the way!”

Kristian started out at Chelsea, where Andriy registered a total of 22 goals and 13 assists in 77 appearances – a far cry from his 175 goals and 46 assists in 322 games with Milan.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The forward moved to Tottenham in 2022 where he spent about a year before moving to Watford.

The wideman played across the Hornets’ Under-18s and Under-21s until he signed his first ever professional contract in 2025.

However, Kristian never managed to play for the first team and was released by the Championship club in May.

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham scores ‘pure filth’ volley after juggling ball as fans brand Real Madrid star ‘alien’ for goal vs PSV
Sports.content:

JUDE BELLINGHAM left football fans speechless after scoring a sensational volley in Real Madrid’s 5-1 Champions League thrashing of PSV Eindhoven.

The English superstar produced a moment of magic at the Santiago Bernabeu, juggling the ball before unleashing a stunning effort into the top corner from 20 yards out.



Bellingham’s outrageous strike came on the hour mark to put Madrid 2-1 ahead after the Spanish giants had fallen behind in the first half.

And fans wasted little time in taking to social media to wax lyrical about the midfielder’s incredible technique.



One wrote: “Speechless. Pure filth of a goal.”

Another compared the England international to Real Madrid legend Zinedine Zidane, writing: “Zidane with hair.”



A third said: “Jude Bellingham, the next Ballon d’Or winner.”

And a fourth added: “Outrageous goal.”

Remarkably, Bellingham had started the game on the bench before being introduced at half-time by Jose Mourinho when they needed him the most.

Madrid had fallen behind in the 32nd minute when former Tottenham star Ivan Perisic converted from the penalty spot following an Aurelien Tchouameni‘s foul on Sven Mijnans.

Federico Valverde restored parity in the 50th minute before Bellingham produced his moment of brilliance and Kylian Mbappe added a third four minutes later.

Mbappe grabbed his second in the 84th minute before Vinicius Jr completed the rout three minutes later as Mourinho’s men secured their fifth successive Champions League victory of the season.

Sports.title: Arsenal were ‘fortunate’ not to concede penalty against Dortmund as Shearer slams referee decision in 1-1 draw
Sports.content:
Next

ALAN SHEARER says Arsenal were lucky not to concede a penalty against Borussia Dortmund.

The Gunners dropped points in the Champions League as they played out a 1-1 draw at the Emirates.



The North Londoners opened the scoring with a stunning rocket by Victor Gyokeres after just ten minutes.

But the Germans turned the tide in the second half with a host of chances as Maximilian Beier pulled them level on 55 minutes.



And Niko Kovac’s side will count themselves unlucky not to have had a golden chance of a winner.

That’s after the ball struck Gyokeres‘ arm inside Arsenal’s box from a Dortmund corner-kick.

The Gunners striker’s arm was slightly raised and, given the competition’s stricter interpretation on handballs, it would have been no surprise had a penalty been awarded.

However, referee Maurizio Mariani waved play on and VAR didn’t intervene.

And Shearer, 56, – who was providing punditry for Amazon Prime – is adamant Mikel Arteta‘s side were lucky to “get away” with it.

Shearer said: “I think Arsenal were fortunate to have gotten away with that one.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

However, Roberto Martinez and Arsenal hero Theo Walcott – who were also on punditry duty – disagreed with the Premier League’s record goalscorer and backed the referee’s decision.

Dortmund thought they turned the game on its head with a goal by Jobe Bellingham on 68 minutes.

However, Arsenal‘s blushes were saved as Jude Bellingham’s brother was caught offside in the build-up.

The Gunners are fifth in the Champions League table with only four points separating them from leaders Real Madrid.

Sports.title: Emery explains brutal Garnacho snub after naming bizarre Villa bench including TWO keepers vs Galatasaray
Sports.content:
Next

UNAI EMERY has explained why he brutally dumped Alejandro Garnacho from Aston Villa’s squad against Galatasaray.

The Argentine winger, on loan from Chelsea with an option to buy at the end of the season, did not even make the bench as Villa lost 1-0 in Turkey.



Incredibly, Emery only picked 11 substitutes of a possible 12, including two goalkeepers.

That led observers to assume Garnacho had suffered a late injury issue.



But, when asked about the winger’s fitness, Emery seemed to confirm it was simply a selection decision.

In a brief press conference: “Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us.”



Emery may well have wished he had Garnacho as an option as he watched his side fall to a second Champions League defeat.

A late goal from Deniz Gul saw the home side walk away with a 1-0 victory in Istanbul, with the Turkish striker poking a header home and taking a boot to the face from Nicolas Jackson in the process.

Emery’s side didn’t manage to muster up a single shot on target in the game.

And Villa fans were left frustrated at Garnacho’s treatment.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

One on X said: “To do this a second time, having lived through the Harvey Elliot debacle last season, is dare I say it, inexcusable on behalf of the club and the full management structure, Emery included.”

Another added: “It’s an embarrassment. Two seasons in a row. How much is he on per week? But the club don’t mind putting prices up. Shambolic.”

And a third said: “I’m sorry no excuses here. To do this a 2nd season in a row is a disgrace. Does this recruitment learn anything?”

Garnacho’s struggles are no secret since he moved to Villa Park on loan in the summer.

In October he underwent a “mini pre-season” following his Manchester United and Chelsea struggles, in a bid to kickstart his career as a Premier League player once again.



He played 155 minutes across six appearances that month, but hasn’t featured at all for Emery in November.

Going by his post-match press conference, he might not be coming back any time soon either – which could prove to be a problem for Chelsea.

The Blues viewed Garnacho’s appearance-based clause to sell the winger to Villa as easy to achieve, with Villa telling staff he was effectively a permanent signing at the time.

But now Chelsea fans are concerned over whether or not he will make the grade and will wait to see if he is included against Ipswich up next.

Sports.title: Arsenal 1 Borussia Dortmund 1: Gyokeres scores screamer but wastes number of chances as Gunners slip up in Europe
Sports.content:
Next

MIKEL ARTETA must have felt like he was watching a repeat of Saturday’s Premier League draw at Newcastle.

And once again, he will surely have been LIVID with his team.



Like their trip to the north-east, which they ended up drawing, Arsenal were in complete command, should have been out of sight by half-time and ended up regretting being so wasteful.

To prove how sloppy they were in the final third, Arsenal had 29 SHOTS but still scored just ONCE.



That goal came through Viktor Gyokeres, who grabbed his third of the season – but he could have scored a first-half hat-trick.

Dortmund equalised through German international Maxi Beier and it could have been even worse.



Jobe Bellingham, although having an otherwise quiet game, thought he had made it 2-1, but his celebrations were cut short by the linesman’s flag.

Yet at least Arsenal did not lose. And that is why you still have to give them so much credit.

The last time Arteta’s team were beaten in a Champions League game in normal time was the 2-1 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the semi-finals in May 2025.

Arsenal were, obviously, beaten by PSG on penalties in last season’s final and it would hardly be a huge surprise if they end up facing each other again deep into the competition.



Only PSG and Barcelona are ahead of them in the betting while the fourth team, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, arrive here at the Emirates next month.

So a draw was hardly a disaster with Arsenal still likely to finish in the top eight.

They should still have won with Gyokeres and Declan Rice wasting good chances in the end.



And while critics of Gyokeres, and he has many, will point to his wasted chances, at least he actually scored.

Although he will be back on the bench for Sunday’s home game with Manchester City.

The Swede had already tried one long-range effort, from 30 yards, although it lacked power and was straight at the keeper Gregor Kobel.

So at least he had the confidence and belief to have a crack from outside the area when he next got the ball.

He was fed the ball by Noni Madueke, following a sensational crossfield pass by Gabriel Magalhaes, and took a couple of touches before unleashing a swerving, dipping effort over Kobel.



It would be easy to point a finger at the Swiss keeper, as the shot looked to be going straight at him.

But Kobel was off his line because the play was outside the area and at 6ft 5ins, he is not exactly short, but the movement of the ball made it difficult to save.

Arsenal should have scored a few more before half-time. Christos Tzolis had a shot saved by Kobel, with Madueke’s follow-up blocked by Daniel Svensson.



Rice fired over from distance and then should have scored when clean through but was denied by a cracking block by Dortmund skipper Nico Schlotterbeck.

Gyokeres had a couple more chances, but one was blocked and the other was a ridiculously wild finish.

Kepa, playing instead of David Raya, has not always covered himself in glory in an Arsenal shirt.

He had to wait until first-half stoppage time to be tested, saving at his near post from Joane Gadou.

Dortmund forward Beier wasted a brilliant chance at the start of the second half but completely missed the ball.



But he more than made up for that ten minutes into the second half when he received a pass from Gadou, who was given far too much room to bring the ball forward from deep inside his own half, having skipped past a lame tackle by Tzolis.

Beier sidestepped Gabriel and tucked the ball into the corner from around the penalty spot right in front of the Dortmund fans who had made a real noise for every second of the game.

Arteta made a triple substitution of Bruno Guimaraes, Jurrien Timber and Eberechi Eze and it added some energy to the team.

Yet Bellingham still gave Arsenal a scare with the strike that was disallowed; the midfielder was later replaced.



And even Arteta then ran outside his technical area to celebrate what he thought was a winner, but Gyokeres agonisingly headed wide from close range.

There was a bizarre moment when the ball hit the woodwork twice as it deflected off Dortmund bodies while Rice also smacked a shot against the post.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And despite a string of chances at the end, Arsenal failed to score – and Arteta went down the tunnel shaking his head in disbelief.

It should have been 7-1.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Madueke steps up in Saka’s absence against Dortmund but Tzolis must work on end product
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL were unable to muster more than a draw for the second time in the space of four days as Borussia Dortmund made them pay for a slew of missed chances.

The Gunners could have been out of sight in the first half but only led by one going in at the break.



Viktor Gyokeres‘ stunning long-range effort gave Arsenal the advantage, but it wasn’t enough to bag all three points.

Dortmund hit back early in the second half when Maximilian Beier tucked away a tidy finish past Kepa Arrizabalaga.



Mikel Arteta cut a frustrated figure as his side were unable to bounce back in the second half.

Here’s how SunSport Arsenal reporter Joshua Hall rates each individual Arsenal performance…

KEPA ARRIZABALAGA – 6

A big night for the Spaniard who was stepping in for the injured David Raya after some shaky performances during his time at Arsenal.

An overall positive performance, but there were still one or two flappy moments that don’t fill anyone with confidence.

BEN WHITE – 7

Took up some really good positions in the attacking third and combined well with Noni Madueke.

Could have had an assist if someone had got on the end of his wicked cross in the first half.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

EZRI KONSA – 7

Some important interventions and blocks to help keep Arsenal solid at the back, particularly with their full-backs playing so high up the pitch.

William Saliba looks like he will have to wait even longer to get a chance to displace Konsa.

GABRIEL MAGALHAES – 6

Another physically dominant performance from the Brazilian, who thrives when given a fight with a centre-forward.



But he was brushed aside far too easily by Maximilian Beier’s quick feet for Dortmund’s equaliser.

PIERO HINCAPIE – 7

Like White, Hincapie was pushing so far up the pitch to stretch Dortmund and occupy the visitor’s back five.

Some important defensive actions kept Arsenal alive at points too.

DECLAN RICE – 7

Handled Felix Nmecha and Jobe Bellingham well in a physical midfield battle, while still offering plenty going the other way.

Could have had a goal on another night with a few long range efforts and a one-on-one that needed a spectacular Nico Schlotterbeck block to deny a certain goal.



MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 6

Did well up against Bellingham in the middle of the park, managing to keep his England teammate at arm’s length despite their notable disparity in size.

Replaced by Bruno Guimaraes when Arteta wanted something different in the middle of the park.

MARTIN ODEGAARD – 8

Sometimes Odegaard goes unnoticed because he doesn’t pop up with the game-winning goal or a magic assist.



This was a match where the Arsenal captain was constantly making the right pass, choosing the best moment to press and orchestrating Arsenal’s midfield.

He may not have shone, but it was another top performance from the in-form Norse.

NONI MADUEKE – 8

Another really positive performance from the winger, who has stepped up in a big way in Bukayo Saka‘s absence.

His aggressive runs constantly stretched the Dortmund defence and he even picked up an assist for his troubles.

CHRISTOS TZOLIS – 5

A nuisance down the left flank, always causing problems for Dortmund’s back five, but it never amounted to anything of value.



His end product needs work with a few snatched chances ending up miles away from the goal.

He also lost Joane Gadou too easily to allow Dortmund to break forward for the equaliser.

VIKTOR GYOKERES – 7

Not many people inside the Emirates Stadium knew Gyokeres was even capable of his first-half screamer, which was probably his best goal in an Arsenal shirt.



He was pushing for more in the second half and came close on a number of occasions, but ultimately missed too many opportunities.

The Swede looks a different player when he is confident and playing in the Champions League, but he showed both sides here.

SUBSTITUTES

JURRIEN TIMBER (for White, 65mins) – 6

Helped offer more defensive security at the back.
