BRUNO GUIMARAES (for Lewis-Skelly, 65mins) – 6

Combative display and more dynamic going forward than Lewis-Skelly

EBERECHI EZE (for Tzolis, 65mins) – 6

Involved a lot in the attacking phase after he came on.

MIKEL MERINO (for Gyokeres, 87mins) – N/A

Sports.title: Man City 2 Napoli 2: Champions League clash ends in huge controversy as City stars rage at ref for ‘ending game early’
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER CITY’S Champions League clash with Napoli ended in controversy after the hosts thought the ref ended the game early.

Enzo Maresca’s men rescued a 2-2 draw against the Italians at the Etihad on Tuesday night thanks to Rayan Cherki’s strike.



But City players and fans were furious after the whistle went with time still left on the clock – as they started pointing at the clock.

Goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma led the City fury and was booked over his protests by official Istvan Kovacs.



The clock on the big screen showed there were still 25 seconds left to play when Kovacs blew up.

But the broadcaster clock said the two minutes added on had already elapsed.



It was a night to forget on the whole for City, whose special edition ‘Tango’ kit did not bring them any luck as their miserable recent run continued.

It is just one win in seven games now for Enzo Maresca’s stuttering team – who now have to go to face their old rivals Arsenal on Sunday.

An out of form Napoli team looked a decent opportunity for Enzo Maresca’s men to get back into their stride.

The Serie A side had some familiar names in their line-up including former United pair Scott McTominay and Rasmus Hojlund – as well as Scotland international Billy Gilmour.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But the man the home fans really wanted to see was one of their all-time greats in De Bruyne, who was loved here throughout his 10 year stay.

It was the Belgian’s second return to his spiritual home since he left in May 2025 – but the first one in September last year did not go to plan.



Back then he was given an emotional welcome back from the crowd but his night lasted just 25 minutes – as he was subbed as part of a reshuffle following a red card for the visitors.

Napoli lost the game without him so here the 35-year-old had a chance to remind the City faithful of his quality.

They have struggled this season too and KDB has had issues with current coach Max Allegri – leading to talk he could be on the move in January.

They have slipped down to eighth in their domestic league and had lost three of their four Champions League games.

Yet Napoli looked comfortable here while City were struggling to get any kind of foothold in the game.



Elliot Anderson – who spared their blushes with an equaliser against Fulham on Saturday – tried his luck early on but his effort was pushed away by Varja Milinkovic Savic.

Star striker Erling Haaland has looked out of sorts in recent games for City and he appealed for a penalty after being sandwiched by two defenders – but to no avail.

But the better chances were coming at the other end with McTominay causing the home side a few headaches.



He twisted and turned past a couple of defenders but then saw his effort deflected wide and then he teed up Hojlund who shot straight at Donnarumma.

Matteo Politano sent over a corner that Sam Beukema met with a thumping header that was pushed away superbly by Donnarumma.

That was the best chance of the first half and Allegri would have been disappointed his team were not ahead at the interval.

It was no surprise when the visitors took the lead early in the second half though as the hosts got in a mess trying to play out from the back.

Gilmour threaded a pass through to Hojlund who turned Guehi before sending an angled drive beyond Donnaruma.



The Danish forward loved that moment – having a bit of fun with the home fans and appearing to tell them there is only one team in Manchester.

But his joy was short-lived as City hit back 12 minutes later as a short corner routine saw sub Jeremy Doku find space on the right.

He picked out Bouaddi who did not look like a player who has never scored before as he lashed a shot beyond Milinkovic–Savic.



It has taken the Morocco international 108 matches to find the net – so it was a sweet moment for him.

You expected City to go on and win it from there, but this isn’t the City of old.

Nico O’Reilly was caught out down the left and Leonardo Spinazzola’s cross was volleyed in expertly by the arriving Lang.

The Dutch forward suffered a gruesome thumb injury when he was last in the North West – but this was a perfect way to banish that memory.

Josko Gvardiol could have grabbed another equaliser but his low shot bounced back off the post.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

But there was still time for Cherki to take a pass from sub Iliman Ndaiye and wriggled past a couple of defenders before firing past Milinkovic Savic.

A point is better than nothing but there are still plenty of issues for Maresca to solve.

Sports.title: Arsenal showing bluntless in attack - but Man City have problems too
Sports.content:
Arsenal face Manchester City in a blockbuster Premier League contest this weekend, but in recent days and months, both teams have issues to overcome.

Arsenal have drawn back-to-back games against Newcastle and Borussia Dortmund, with Mikel Arteta's side throwing away comfortable half-time leads in both matches.

City, meanwhile, come into the game on a run of just one win in their last six Premier League and Champions League matches.

The game could have a huge impact on the Premier League title race, with Arsenal hoping to open up a nine-point lead over Enzo Maresca's side, who in turn could close the gap to the reigning champions to just three points with a win.

Arsenal

Manchester City Sunday 29th November 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

Sky Sports reporters Sam Blitz and Adam Bate were at Arsenal and City's draws in midweek and analyse their respective issues...

Arsenal showing bluntness in attack again

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz at the Emirates Stadium:

Arsenal have the most 1-0 wins out of any Premier League team since Mikel Arteta took over the club in December 2019. It's all well and good - until teams start making it 1-1.

And in the last two games, they have. And Arsenal only have themselves to blame.

After the Gunners' 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund, Arteta was convinced that their recent draws against Newcastle and the Bundesliga leaders are not comparable.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following his side's 1-1 Champions League draw against Borussia Dortmund, Mikel Arteta, says Arsenal should be pleased with their performance, but admits that The Gunners' finishing could be better

He claims Arsenal played well in this Champions League stalemate - and repeated on several occasions that Dortmund benefited from an "element of luck". There's an element of truth to that - the woodwork was struck three times in the second half.

But Arsenal had thirty shots against Dortmund - the most they've ever had in a Champions League game. Just four of those shots were on target. Seven shots came from within the six-yard box, no goals came from them.

And it's costing them points. Because there has been a pattern in Arsenal's last two matches. Dominate the first half, only take a 1-0 lead, start the second half slowly and then end up drawing the game.

Out of the 2.2 worth of Expected Goals Arsenal missed in the game, 0.96 of that tally came in the first half. From their 13 shots that didn't lead to a goal, they should have taken a bigger advantage.

Image: Arsenal had 30 shots against Borussia Dortmund but only scored once

It invited Dortmund back into the contest when there shouldn't have been one in the first place. Like Newcastle did at the weekend, the Bundesliga leaders sorted their game plan out in the half-time break and came out firing.

Arteta is right that the Newcastle and Dortmund games are different because Arsenal rallied to seize dominance of the game right after the German side's equaliser.

But once again, the conversation sits around the holes in Arsenal's attacking quality, particularly at left wing and up front. After Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus left the club this summer without being replaced, Arsenal are still searching for attacking inspiration at left wing, with neither centre-forward in a goalscoring run of form.

Christos Tzolis is still waiting for his first Arsenal goal, Eberechi Eze is lacking consistency and Viktor Gyokeres backed up his early strike and impressive all-round display by creating doubts again by missing a late sitter.

At the start of the season, Gary Neville questioned whether Arsenal had the attacking player capable of delivering the Champions League. The draw to Dortmund backed that claim up.

Image: Arsenal players show their disappointment after conceding a second-half equaliser to Borussia Dortmund

Arteta struck a calm and positive tone after the Dortmund draw. It was a figure who knows his team have a six-point lead at the top of the Premier League, and will go on to qualify for the knockout stages of the Champions League.

But if these traits continue, it can all slip away quickly in this busy part of the season. If Arsenal don't beat Real Madrid, their top eight spot will be under threat.

Last season, they also benefited hugely from getting a top two spot that meant the second legs of their entire knockout stages were at the Emirates. PSG and Real can open up a bit of a gap on Arsenal in the coming weeks.

And up next, it's Manchester City at the Emirates. Enzo Maresca's side tend to score in most games. A 1-0 lead may not be enough.

Maresca still searching for the Man City solutions

Sky Sports' Adam Bate at the Etihad Stadium:

Move the ball quicker, yelled one fan from behind the press box. Press them, screamed a youngster in front. They were not wrong. Manchester City still have the individual quality to entertain the Etihad Stadium but they are also a frustrating watch at present.

City have picked up just one point from their last four Premier League games and while they did defeat RB Leipzig 3-2 in their previous Champions League outing, they let in two more in this draw with Napoli. It is 10 games now without keeping a clean sheet.

"Off the ball, the team was good from my point of view," said Enzo Maresca in the press conference afterwards, presenting a positive spin. "We did not concede a lot. The problem is that they were clinical. We created many chances." Not everyone agreed.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following his side's chaotic 2-2 draw against Napoli, Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca says the point is a 'good result'

"It is not good enough," City captain Erling Haaland had told TNT Sports just before. "We let them in too easily and were unable to control or attack the game as we want." Tellingly, the striker then added: "When you do not win you start to question everything."

Maresca is being questioned. He has stressed that he is months into his time here not years and it is evident that he is still searching for the solutions. Finding the best role for new signings Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez is something that he is still tweaking.

Against Napoli, it was Jeremy Doku's spark off the bench that helped to bring the first equaliser and Rayan Cherki's class that delivered the second. But it was all the bits in between, with and without the ball, that will concern the Manchester City supporters.

Rasmus Hojlund got the better of Marc Guehi and Gianluigi Donnarumma as Napoli were rewarded for pressing City high up the pitch. Noa Lang converted Leonardo Spinazzola's right-wing cross on the counter-attack - highlighting another weakness.

Maresca turned on his heels and looked to the skies in exasperation at that one because it is a recurring issue for City. They remain susceptible to the breakaways even when he loads the midfield in attempt to prevent it. Losing duels is another theme.

Sluggishness is an easy accusation. Haaland was largely anonymous, unable to get into the game. But that is because City are yet to find a pressing structure that works for them. Even if Haaland does close down, his team-mates are not necessarily following.

Image: City are scrapping around for their identity

As had happened against Fulham at the weekend, Napoli were able to have good possession of the ball, something that was once unheard of for visiting teams at this stadium. That aura was already fading under Pep Guardiola but it is truly absent now.

Maresca is an excellent coach and the structure at Manchester City remains such that he can expect to be given time to figure all this out. But as he himself has previously acknowledged, there is not just one thing that is undermining this team right now.

The loss at Aston Villa was not the same as the home reverse to Brighton. Fulham approached it very differently to Nottingham Forest. Both got results. And now Napoli, in just one game, showed two different ways to undo Maresca's side. Problems to solve.

Sports.title: Poch fumes at Yoro red and thinks Szoboszlai goal shouldn't have stood
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino has heavily criticised VAR in Manchester United's loss at Liverpool after Leny Yoro's red card was overturned, while the Argentine believes Dominik Szoboszlai’s opener should not have stood.

Yoro's one-match suspension for the red card he was shown in the 4-0 defeat at Anfield has been removed, despite referees' chief Howard Webb supporting the decision to send him off.

Man Utd will contact ProRef and the Premier League directly over what they believe to be a 'totally wrong' interpretation of Yoro's red card against Liverpool.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Match Officials Mic'd Up, Howard Webb and Michael Owen take a look at the VAR process from Anfield after Leny Yoro was given a red card in the eighth minute.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Following Leny Yoro's overturned red card for Manchester United during their 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, Mauricio Pochettino questioned VAR's involvement in the Frenchman's dismissal.

It is the second time this season VAR has wrongly gone against Man Utd after ProRef admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford in September.

United received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision to award Erling Haaland's winner, which was initially ruled offside before VAR overturned the decision.

Pochettino mentioned the Haaland call in a passionate outburst over VAR as he questioned why the VAR did not intervene to overturn the on-field decision.

Speaking at a press conference ahead of his team's Champions League match against Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday, Pochettino said: "Very disappointed because I think this type of thing never can happen.

"My question was always the same - we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotional relationship with the game.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News’ Kaveh Solhekol explains Manchester United's appeal successful appeal process for Leny Yoro's red card, that the defender had picked up against Liverpool.

"But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? No, because now we are going to repeat the game? We're going to have the possibility to play with the similar tools, 11 against 11?

"The problem is that when we were there, I think they need to take their time to review the situation.

"We have an unbelievable car but we need to be in the level to drive, we need to drive in the best way.

"We love and accept the technology, but what are they doing? But it's not only this mistake or the mistake for Haaland against Manchester City, it's how after it affects everything."

Poch explains why Szoboszlai goal shouldn't have stood

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dominik Szoboszlai's free-kick opens the scoring for Liverpool against Manchester United in the Premier League.

Pochettino then insisted that Liverpool's opening goal should not have stood because Bradley Barcola was touching the Manchester United wall as Szoboszlai struck in.

Pochettino referenced a similar call last season, which saw Eberechi Eze's free-kick goal for Crystal Palace at Chelsea disallowed after ex-Palace captain Marc Guehi pushed Moises Caicedo to create a gap for the ball to fly through.

The IFAB Laws of the Game state: "If, when a free-kick is taken, an attacking team player is less than 1 m (1 yd) from a 'wall' formed by three or more defending team players, an indirect free-kick is awarded."

Pochettino believes that the law applied to Szoboszlai's free-kick opener due to Barcola's involvement.

He said: "No one talks about that the goal wasn't legal, it should be disallowed because (Bradley) Barcola was touching our wall. Maybe in the last two years, they've maybe changed the rule because I've been in America, but last season when (Eberechi) Eze scored for Palace (at Chelsea) you can see [it was disallowed].

"But VAR didn't check [Dominik Szoboszlai's goal]; that must be disallowed.

"But this type of situation, I need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce and to say we were right and the decision wasn't good, and now the three points, where are they?

"I think it's a thing we need to think a little bit more deeper and it's not for tomorrow's game.

"It's about to be tough in the way we use the technology. We need to move on. I'm so proud of the players in the way they manage these unfair situations that happen on the field.

"Our focus now is to improve, to start to win games and tomorrow we have a great opportunity here."

What did Webb say about Yoro decision?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The Ref Watch panel debate whether Leny Yoro should have been sent off against Liverpool on Sunday.

In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'd Up, Webb, chief refereeing officer at ProRef, described the on-field decision from referee Samuel Barrott as "decisive" and said the point of contention was around whether Isak would beat United goalkeeper Senne Lammens to the ball.

Audio from the officials reveals that the VAR, John Brooks, who backed Barrott's decision, determined Isak was "likely" to get on the end of the ball before Lammens. His assistant VAR, Paul Howard, agreed.

Webb was non-committal in his verdict but backed the process of the officials by saying "most people would see that as a correct decision".

"There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens," said Webb. "Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would. That was the referee's call made on the field.

"The VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect and formed the opinion that it wasn't. If there was any doubt, then it was doubt.

"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. And I think by and large most people would see that as a correct decision with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong."

Sports.title: Hibernian finally register home win after battling past Dundee
Sports.content:
Hibernian ended their long wait for a Premiership home win after overcoming Dundee 2-1 at Easter Road.

Martin Boyle and Nicky Cadden - who curled home a stunning effort from outside the box - had the hosts in command before the interval.

But Dundee showed plenty of fight after the break and pulled one back through Joe Wright.

Image: Martin Boyle fired Hibs ahead from the penalty spot

The visitors tried in vain to grab an equaliser and it was Hibs who were left satisfied by their first three points at home since beating Kilmarnock on April 4.

Despite being thrashed by Dundee United 4-0 at the weekend, Hibernian head coach Marink Reedijk decided to make only two alterations to his team, with Cadden and Thibault Klidje coming in.

Dundee manager Steven Pressley changed half of his outfield XI following the 8-0 humiliation to Hearts.

Owen Bevan was suspended and in came on-loan Bournemouth defender Matai Akinmboni for a full debut while Joe Wright, Brad Halliday, Joe Bevan and Ashley Hay started.

Hibs played on the front foot as they looked to start repairing the damage from the weekend's demoralising loss.

Image: Nicky Cadden scored Hibs' second

On a rare start, Togo international Klidje was lively and saw a header crash into the side-netting before hitting a harmless snap-shot straight at Dundee goalkeeper Owen Goodman.

From a short corner routine Hibs worked space for Cadden on the edge of the box from Josh Mulligan's lay-off and his driving effort whistled just past a post.

Dundee were desperate to keep it tight at the back but offered little going forward. Just when it looked like they were beginning to settle Hibs hit them two goals in three minutes before the break.

The first came in the 40th minute when Boyle fired a penalty past Goodman after being tripped by Ryan Finnigan.

Cadden then found the top corner with a sublime curling effort from his left foot just outside the box. It was another short corner routine that saw Miguel Chaiwa set up the wing-back.

Image: Dundee have conceded 10 goals over their last two games

Despite the hammer blow of losing two goals in quick succession before the break, Dundee demonstrated at the start of the second half that they were not going to roll over.

Pressley's side upped their intensity as they searched for a goal to get themselves back in the game and that arrived in the 67th minute courtesy of Wright.

Substitute Callum Jones' free-kick should have been put away by Ryan Astley but the ball broke back to Wright and he slammed the ball high into the net from six yards.

That set up a tense finish but Hibs desperately held on for a rare home victory.

What the managers said...

Hibernian head coach Marink Reedijk:

"It's always nice to win, it's a good one again in order to make sure we get confirmation that if we show our identity about intensity, aggression and proactivity and are brave, that anything can happen here.

"I hope we get another three points next match and that we go again in a way that we do the things we are good at and what our identity and what we stand for is.

"The next match against Motherwell is not at home, I know, but there will be a match at home against Rangers, where this can also come to life again. But that is far away.

"First things first, Saturday lies another challenge."

Dundee boss Steven Pressley:

"Both teams are a bit fragile and there was a lot of trepidation in the game but the one thing about us we got a degree of pride back. It's not the result but a little bit of stability and we showed a lot of courage.

"We wanted to give ourselves a foundation to build from and we gave ourselves that.

"We were much more cohesive in the second half and when you suffer the defeat we suffered on Saturday and you come here and you find yourself 2-0 down at half-time, it asks a lot of questions of you as a group and I thought they responded brilliantly.

"They showed courage and spirit and it's not been easy because there's a fragility about us. We responded in the proper manner."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Sheehan to miss Ireland's Nations Championship finale after two-game ban
Sports.content:
Ireland captain Dan Sheehan will miss Friday's Nations Championship fifth-place play-off against Australia after being handed a two-game ban for his red card against South Africa.

The forward was initially shown a yellow card by referee Christophe Ridley for a croc roll on Springbok replacement Marco van Staden in the 72nd minute of his country's 20-17 victory in Dublin.

The offence was subsequently upgraded to a red card by the foul play review officer.

World Rugby law 9.20d states "a player may remove the jackler from the tackle area by pushing/driving them backwards (including by grabbing the knee/leg), but must not roll, pull or twist an opponent".

Sheehan faced a disciplinary hearing on Monday evening where the panel ruled the incident was a "low entry point" offence and merited a two-week suspension.

The 28-year-old has accepted the sanction and will also miss Leinster's United Rugby Championship meeting with the Ospreys on Friday, December 4.

Typically a hooker, Sheehan started at number eight for the first time at Test level against the world champions.

With Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Sean Jansen all injured, head coach Andy Farrell now faces another reshuffle at the base of the scrum for the meeting with the Wallabies at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.

Ronan Kelleher and Tom Stewart are set to continue as the two hookers in Ireland's matchday 23.

Sports.title: Cherki salvages draw with Napoli but Man City frustrate
Sports.content:
Rayan Cherki’s late strike salvaged a 2-2 draw for Manchester City at home to Napoli in the Champions League but Enzo Maresca’s side again struggled to find their fluency.

Former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund opened the scoring for the Italian side and though Ayyoub Bouaddi equalised, Noa Lang's volley stunned the Etihad Stadium as Napoli restored their lead late on. Cherki's goal at least secured a point.

The draw leaves City in sixth spot in the Champions League table but they are likely to drop out of the top eight by Wednesday evening and have now gone 10 games without a clean sheet. Maresca's men look vulnerable ahead of the trip to Arsenal on Sunday.

How it played out at the Etihad

With little to cheer in the first half, the home crowd took most pleasure in serenading Kevin De Bruyne on his return - King Kev declared one banner - and he gave glimpses of his quality, twice cutting City's defence apart. But the sluggish tempo suited a veteran.

Image: Kevin De Bruyne in action for Napoli against former club Man City in the Champions League

It was all a little too slow from City. Maresca was trying to tighten up in midfield, picking Bouaddi as well as Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez for only the second time. But it left this City side short of thrust in the last third despite Allan's impressive endeavour.

It needed a strong save from Gianluigi Donnarumma to ensure City went in level at the break. Sam Beukema made firm contact with a free header inside the box but the Napoli defender placed it too close to the goalkeeper. The home side did not heed the warning.

Billy Gilmour fed Hojlund inside the box on the angle and he got the shot away under pressure from Marc Guehi to beat Donnarumma low to his left. It was a sweet moment for the Danish striker, 23, whose United links had seen him booed by the City fans.

Image: Rasmus Hojlund celebrates scoring for Napoli against Man City in the Champions League

But Napoli's lead did not last long thanks to Bouaddi. The elegant Moroccan midfielder had yet to score a goal at senior level in his career but his left-footed effort found its way through Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. Substitute Jeremy Doku provided the spark required.

City were pushing for a winner at that stage, but Lang's exquisite volley on the counter-attack was a reminder that Maresca is having trouble controlling counter-attacks. At least he had kept the mercurial Cherki on the pitch to help avoid a damaging defeat.

But after that seven-game winning run in the Premier League, it is one point from four domestically and now this unconvincing effort in front of their own supporters. City are still a work in progress under Maresca. They will need to improve plenty at Arsenal.

Confusion over added time The game ended amid confusion when the referee blew the final whistle with the big screen showing around 20 seconds of the two minutes of added time still to play. City were in possession and moving the ball up the pitch.



Donnarumma was among those incensed at the decision as City players surrounded the official who responded by pointing to his watch. The problem is that this watch must have been telling a different time to the one everyone else was seeing.

Key moments at the Etihad Stadium

55 - GOAL! Hojlund fired in the opener for Napoli

67 - GOAL! Bouaddi's strike levelled it for Man City

76 - GOAL! Lang volleyed in to restore Napoli's lead

86 - GOAL! Cherki's low strike salvaged a point

Haaland: It is not good enough

Man City captain Erling Haaland speaking to TNT Sports:

"We tried to push but we couldn't. It's not good enough. We let them in too easily and were unable to control or attack the game as we want.

"Football can be so difficult and easy. When you win games everything is easy and you know exactly what to do, when you don't win you start to question everything. The perfect thing would be to don't think but it's difficult in these moments.

"We have so much quality. It's about getting that quality out of every single player. We have to regroup to stay positive and bring the energy on the pitch.

"We go to the champions next. The most difficult game of the season. We need a top, top performance."

What's next?

Sports.title: Norwich hit back to hold QPR
Sports.content:
Norwich's impressive run of victories came to an end as QPR held them to a 1-1 draw at Carrow Road.

The Canaries had won their previous five Championship fixtures but had to come from behind to pick up a point this time around after Harvey Vale had fired the visitors in front just before the break.

Philippe Clement's side were quickly back on level terms in the second half through a well-taken Anthony Musaba effort, but were well contained after that as Rangers registered a well-deserved point.

After a slow start, the match burst into life with a flurry of activity around the mid-point of the first half.

Norwich thought they had taken the lead on 19 minutes when Harry Darling got a touch on an in-swinging Jacob Wright free-kick but the effort was ruled out for offside.

Andre Brooks then saw a low shot from the edge of the area come back off the upright, while at the other end Dan Grimshaw did well to palm away a goal-bound effort from Vale.

Rangers were giving the hosts plenty to think about and took the lead four minutes before the break when Vale made another opportunity count.

The Republic of Ireland international had plenty to do after latching on to Kealey Adamson's pass but despite having Ruairi McConville and Darling in close attendance, he worked himself some space in the area before firing a powerful shot past Grimshaw.

Norwich were back on level terms within three minutes of the restart after a poor clearance by goalkeeper Pierce Charles was punished. It went straight to Musaba, who played a quick one-two with Mathias Kvistgaarden before confidently finding the roof of the net.

Vale fired inches wide as Rangers sought a quick response while substitute Oscar Schwartau was foiled by a good save from Charles as the game entered its final 10 minutes.

Norwich continued to press for a winner but could find no way through as they drew a game for the first time this season.

The managers

Norwich's Philippe Clement:

"This team will never settle for a draw - they will always keep going for the win but in football it doesn't always happen.

"After going behind we showed the right mentality, got our goal and kept pushing them back, with the fans playing their part, but unfortunately we couldn't get the second goal we deserved.

"We were up against a well-organised side and knew it was going to be tough but I thought the momentum was with us in the first half too and we just needed a bit of luck.

"We had a goal ruled out through a very tight offside decision and then Andre (Brooks) hit the post.

"When we went behind it became an even tougher task because we know how difficult they are to break down but our response was really good with everyone playing their part, including the lads who came off the bench."

QPR's Julien Stephan:

"That's four points from two very tough away games, Millwall and Norwich, which is a very positive outcome and all credit to the players for that.

"We were up against a side who had won their previous five games, scoring 17 goals, and it was a very good performance, with a draw a fair result I feel.

"We started very well, both with and without the ball, playing with a good tempo, and scored a very good goal.

"Obviously we were disappointed to concede so early in the second half but the lads showed great character to stick to the game plan. They defended properly as a team and we also had some chances.

"I am lucky to have a special group of players here and although they are a young group I thought they showed great maturity out there to come away with a deserved point."

What the result means and next fixtures...
