Sports.title: Man City are too easy to play through and Enzo Maresca must solve these three huge problems before Arsenal clash
Sports.content:
Man City are too easy to play through and Enzo Maresca must solve these three huge problems before Arsenal clash

Manchester City look vulnerable and Enzo Maresca must fix their defensive issues in time for Sunday's clash with Arsenal.

That's according to former City boss Stuart Pearce, who has voiced his concerns after their winless streak extended to three games in all competitions with a 2-2 draw to Napoli in the Champions League.



5 Man City's defensive woes have seen them drop points domestically and in Europe Credit: Getty

Rayan Cherki rescued a point for City with an 86th-minute equaliser, but their shortcomings were once again laid bare at the Etihad Stadium.

Enzo Maresca's side twice came from behind, with Ayyoub Bouaddi equalising first after ex-Manchester United man Rasmus Hojlund gave Napoli the lead.

But City were completely exposed defensively soon after, as Nico O'Reilly was first caught out before Noa Lang was completely unmarked in the box to volley the Italians back in front.



While some individual brilliance from Cherki saw the Premier League giants avoid defeat, their display highlighted their frailties.

The 2-2 draw means City have now conceded in their last ten matches across all competitions.



They last went on such a run in December 2019, while they are now without a clean sheet since their 3-0 win at Liverpool on October 11.

This has coincided with a loss of form for City, who are now winless in four Premier League games and six points adrift of leaders Arsenal as they prepare to face off at the Emirates Stadium on Sunday.



Following the Napoli draw, Maresca admitted his side's defensive weakness is proving costly for them.

Asked to name City’s biggest problem, he told TNT Sports: “It is quite clear that we are conceding too many goals and it’s something that we need to adjust and we are able to do that.”

Pearce lists Man City's problems

Maresca's comments were echoed by Stuart Pearce on commentary, who admitted teams are easily pouncing on City's frailty at the back.

5 Enzo Maresca has just five days to turn things around in time for Sunday's trip to Arsenal Credit: Getty



5 By drawing to Napoli City missed the chance to move into the top four of the Champions League league phase table Credit: Getty

Reacting to the result live on talkSPORT, Pearce began: “There is a vulnerability about City.

"They're easy to play against on occasion. You can play through them and that is a problem.

“They don't look as though they're a side that can actually keep a clean sheet and that is probably their biggest problem, and the biggest damning stat of this recent run.”



He added: “They're almost too easy to play through at the moment.

“Teams draw City onto them and then play through them - either on the floor, or sometimes go beyond them and hit 50, 60-yard balls that defenders should not let bounce [which they do]."

With a crunch clash at Arsenal just days away, Pearce outlined three key areas Maresca must improve to give his side a fighting chance.

5 Enzo Fernandez is a guaranteed starter against Arsenal, but the rest of City's midfield unit is less clear Credit: Getty

Pointing first to City's midfield, he insisted their manager faces a dilemma over who to start alongside Enzo Fernandez, where a potential double pivot of Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi risks moving Cherki out wide.



Pearce said: "I think there's a formula that he's thumbing for at the moment. What is the best midfield combination in there with Enzo Fernandez?"

Continuing to highlight City's flaws, Pearce pointed to their disjointed press and struggles with dealing with balls over the top.

He went on: “How do we press from the front effectively? I don't think they do that particularly well, and if you don't do that, the opposition can set up to play through you.

“And obviously defensively. I'll give you a direct comparison - if you play a ball over 30 yards into Arsenal's back line, Gabriel will be climbing all over you to get first contact.



"If you do exactly the same into Manchester City's central defenders, chances are you're gonna be out of secure possession or the ball will bounce.

5 Marc Guehi's performances have come in for scrutiny this term, with Man City unconvincing at the back Credit: Getty

“That is the difference between both sides at this moment in time so there's a lot of questions to be resolved."

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham tipped for greatness after Puskas contender wondergoal – despite Premier League ‘travesty’
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham is going to become England's greatest ever player - but unfortunately, he will never play in the Premier League.

That's according to Jamie O'Hara and Jason Cundy, who have gushed over the Real Madrid superstar after his stunning goal.

3 Bellingham scored a stunning Puskas contender for Real Madrid on Tuesday night as his side thrashed PSV in the Champions League Credit: Getty

On Tuesday night, Bellingham scored a goal that talkSPORT's Adrian Durham believes will be a Puskas Award contender.

He took a quick touch with his left foot as the ball ricocheted back to him on the edge of the box against PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League.

The ball then flicked into the air in front of him and he took another touch to juggle it with his right boot and set himself up for an incredible strike that looped past the goalkeeper and in.

Real went on to win 5-1 against their Dutch opponents at the Bernabeu but Bellingham's effort, which he described post-match as the best of his life so far, has taken all the headlines.

However, as the England international continues to take the world by storm, O'Hara and Cundy admitted that they don't think he will ever play his club football in the Premier League.

Bellingham won't ever play in the Premier League

On talkSPORT's The Sports Bar, co-host O'Hara began: "I wanted to put on Real Madrid tonight just to watch him play football, he's so much better to watch than Arsenal."

Cundy then added: "It's just one of those goals that you just make up, it comes to you and you have to improvise.

"He brings it down, touch, another touch, outside of his foot to guide it away from the goalkeeper... he's just becoming one of the very best players in the world, we know that anyway."

"He's the best midfielder in the world," O'Hara went on to claim before pointing a sad reality Premier League fans face.

"We're so lucky he's English... but you know what's a travesty? He's not playing in the Premier League.

3 Bellingham found the back of the next after juggling the ball in his feet and firing a volley perfectly into the back of the net Credit: Getty

"The fact that he's not playing in the Premier League and we don't get to watch him every game..."

Cundy agreed that Bellingham will probably 'never' play his club football in England as he's been so successful abroad.

"Maybe that's part of his success," he said. "He had to go to Borrusia ortmund and did what he did there... he's ripping up trees, he's a super talent."

Bellingham will be England's greatest

Bellingham may not play in the Premier League during the rest of his career, but he will always be playing for England.

And the 23-year-old, who is already a superstar for the Three Lions, is already on the path to being his country's best ever.

Cundy said: "This is what you want to see, going into the Euros, going into the next 18 months, this boy to continue to rise and shine."

3 Bellingham has been tipped to become England's greatest ever player as he continues to show he is already one of the best in world football Credit: Getty

O'Hara then stated: "He's going to be England's greatest ever player. Ever. He's better than Harry Kane, a better player than Kane."

Captain Kane is sure to be a contender for being one of the best ever players to wear the England shirt.

He is the nation's all time top scorer and appearance maker, but Bellingham has age on his side and at the moment, there isn't anything that appears to be stopping him.

Sports.title: Unai Emery explains brutal Alejandro Garnacho snub after naming one less substitute in squad
Sports.content:
Unai Emery explains brutal Alejandro Garnacho snub after naming one less substitute in squad

Unai Emery has explained why he left Alejandro Garnacho out of his Aston Villa squad against Galatasaray on Tuesday night.

Garnacho was not part of the Villa set-up in the Champions League despite Emery having the choice to select 12 substitutes.



2 Garnacho was left out of Aston Villa's squad despite Emery picking one less player than he was allowed and two goalkeepers Credit: Getty

In fact, the manager opted to only pick 11 subs in the end for the game which his side lost 1-0 to a late goal from Deniz Gul, with two of those players on his bench being goalkeepers.

It makes the decision to leave Garnacho out even more brutal, amid his nightmare beginning to life at the club.

And the Villa boss explained post-match why he opted not to pick the former Manchester United star.



Rubbing salt in Garnacho's wounds, Emery said in his post-match press conference in Istanbul: "Today the players were here who I think are the best players to be here with us."

Garnacho's nightmare Villa career

Emery had admitted at the start of the season that Garnacho was 'behind' his teammates in the pecking order.



And that is clearly still the case, with the winger not making the Villa squad in any of their last three games.

His last appearance for the club came on October 31 as he appeared for three minutes off the bench against Fulham.



Before that, he had only picked up another three Premier League appearances, totalling just 31 minutes of gametime.

Garnacho hasn't started a single game in any competition, playing just seven times since his summer move.

He left Chelsea to join Villa on a loan with a conditional obligation to buy which is believed to be worth around £42million.

2 Emery explained that he picked his best players for the Champions League game against Galatasaray which his side lost 1-0 Credit: Getty



What else did Emery say post-match?

After the defeat that meant Aston Villa are now winless in six in all competitions, Emery said: "It was a tough match.

“How we played the first half, I was very proud of the players and how they were responding on the field, trying to control of the game like we planned and to stop them here with their supporters.

“Their supporters were pushing them and helping them, and the atmosphere was really fantastic. Our supporters as well were helping us and I’m thankful of how they were here with us, and we felt them.

"We were trying to do our way together in this Champions League."

He added: “I think we deserved, minimum, to draw this match because we competed well.



"This is the level in the Champions League, especially when you are playing away against a team like Galatasaray with a fantastic atmosphere.

“There are things to learn, to have experiences and get better for the next challenges we will face.”

Sports.title: Plans on Newcastle’s proposed £1.3billion oval-shaped new stadium revealed
Sports.content:
Newcastle are edging towards building a new stadium with a potential 72,000 capacity which would see St James Park knocked down.

St James' Park has been the Magpies' home since 1892 and boasts a capacity of 52,719, but there has been speculation over the club's long-term future at the historic venue.



3 St James' Park is one of English football's most iconic venues Credit: Getty

Talks have recently taken place over building a new £1.3billion stadium, rather than redeveloping their current ground - with the two options both being weighed up.

In May, the club announced the purchase of the adjacent Leazes Terrace, although it wasn't specified which purpose this would serve.

St James' Park move?

According to the Daily Telegraph, Newcastle are now leaning towards building a new 'oval-shaped' stadium on Leazes Park instead of expanding their current home.



The Premier League giants are yet to make a final decision but plans are still being drawn up.

Among them, this includes a proposed new stadium built directly adjacent to the Leazes End stand at St James' Park.



It is reported that the venue would have an increased capacity of 65-72,000, with the lower end of the scale more likely.

This would spell the end of St James' Park though, which would be demolished and redeveloped.



In its place, a new leisure, office, retail and accommodation space is proposed to be built on the east of the current plot, with the remainder of the land turning into green space.

However, the club hasn't completely given up hope of redeveloping their existing home.

The report adds that designs have also been drawn up for an expanded St James' Park, which would add an extra tier to the iconic Gallowgate End.

3 Newcastle's proposed new stadium could look like the Allianz Arena Credit: Getty



With a final decision still yet to be reached, the same source revealed that impressions of Newcastle's proposed new stadium have teased a design which includes an oval-shaped ground with a 'wave effect'.

That means there would be two slightly smaller stands around the side of the pitch rising upwards, flanked by larger tiers behind both goals.

It has previously been reported that Newcastle planned to model a new stadium on the style of Bayern Munich’s Allianz Arena.

While the club deny this is what the exterior will look like, the Telegraph report revealed that a more recent artist impression showed the proposed venue as having black and white illuminated cladding similar to Bayern's home.



New stadium 'going to be expensive'

The report adds that Newcastle's owners, Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), will not finance the proposed new stadium on their own and instead will seek a loan which will be repaid.

The club has reportedly spoken to three different lenders about potentially borrowing money to pay for the £1.3bn new stadium.

3 Newcastle could still expand St James' Park, but recent reports suggest a new home could be on the horizon Credit: Getty

According to The Sun, Magpies chiefs have met representatives from US bank Goldman Sachs this month to discuss funding.



Newcastle chief executive, David Hopkinson, said at a recent fan event that a larger ground will be essential from a revenue perspective.

He said on Monday: “We need it [a larger ground] for the revenue a new stadium would unlock.

“Whatever we do here, it’s a generational decision which will define the next era of the club. It’s going to be expensive."

Newcastle are set make a final decision on whether to build a new stadium or expand their current one in 2027.



Should they choose to build a new ground, construction would begin in 2029, after St James’ Park hosts its scheduled Euro 2028 games, with the project expected to take at least four years to complete.

Sports.title: Aston Villa lose as blood pours from nose of match-winner after nasty boot to face
Sports.content:
Aston Villa lose as blood pours from nose of match-winner after nasty boot to face

Galatasaray striker Deniz Gul was left covered in blood immediately after scoring his side's winning goal against Aston Villa.

Gul headed in the crucial goal after 77 minutes, but in the process, Villa's Nicolas Jackson planted his boot directly into his face.

4 Gul was kicked directly in the face by Aston Villa's Jackson as he headed in a late winner for the Turkish giants in the Champions League Credit: TNT Sports

4 The striker celebrated his winning goal with a knee slide before his wound started gushing blood and he lay on the pitch in pain Credit: AFP

The Galatasaray forward reacted to the kick at the time but as he saw the ball bounce into the net, he wheeled away celebrating.

He rushed towards the corner flag and did a knee slide before quickly registering the pain from the kick he took to the head.

Gul covered his face as he was swamped by his teammates, with ex-Spurs defender Davinson Sanchez waving medics on.

As Gul looked down at his hands, which were covered in blood, the Galatasaray players backed away from him, also waving at the medics.

The 22-year-old then lay down on the pitch and received treatment from the Turkish giants' medical staff for a few minutes.

Eventually, he returned with a bandage covering his nose.

And he went on to play the rest of the game, with Galatasaray holding on to their 1-0 lead until the full-time whistle.

Gul only played 35 minutes of the match, coming on in the second half as he replaced Eren Elmali for the hosts.

But his header got the job done for his side, who extended their winning run to eight straight games in all competitions.

They have also now won their last three in the Champions League, rising up the league phase table on Tuesday night.

4 Gul's wound on his face poured with blood and he had to receive treatment from Galatasaray's medical staff after realising his injury Credit: AFP

4 Gul returned to the game with a big bandage over his nose as Galatasaray held on to beat Aston Villa and maintain their winning streak Credit: Getty

Aston Villa beaten in Istanbul

As for Aston Villa, they have now lost two consecutive games in Europe, having been beaten by Barcelona in their previous game.

Unai Emery's side are also on a six-game winless streak.

Their last win in any competition came on October 24 against Manchester City in the Premier League.

Villa only had four shots in the entire match in Istanbul, struggling to breakthrough the Turkish side's back line.

They face back-to-back winners Paris Saint-Germain in their next Champions League fixture on December 8.

Meanwhile, Galatasaray will hope to keep up their impressive form with a win over AEK Athens on the same night.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes says ‘rabbit in the headlights’ £52m Man United man is not Premier League level
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes says ‘rabbit in the headlights’ £52m Man United man is not Premier League level

Paul Scholes has claimed the Premier League looks too much for Leny Yoro after Manchester United’s 4-0 defeat to Liverpool.

Yoro was sent off less than eight minutes into United's embarrassing loss at Anfield as the Mauricio Pochettino era got off to a nightmare start.



3 Yoro has come in for added scrutiny after his sending off against Liverpool Credit: AFP

The Frenchman clumsily ran into the back of Alexander Isak as the Reds striker ran in on goal and cut across his path.

Yoro was controversially shown a straight red card, as Liverpool went on to run riot against the ten-man Red Devils after Dominik Szoboszlai opened the scoring from the subsequent free-kick.

While the defender was set to serve a one-match suspension for his dismissal, this has since been overturned after an appeal.



The FA confirmed on Tuesday that the ban had been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal.

However, the circumstances surrounding Yoro's red gave him little defence in the eyes of Man United great Paul Scholes, who has criticised him in the aftermath of the Liverpool defeat.



Scholes raises questions

Since arriving at Old Trafford as a highly-rated 18-year-old in a deal worth £60million in 2024, Yoro has endured a rollercoaster ride in his 78 United appearances so far.

His most difficult period yet has come this term, forming part of leaky Red Devils defence that has conceded 23 goals in 11 Premier League matches – with only Crystal Palace conceding more.



And while none of United's defenders earned praise for Sunday's display, club icon Scholes took aim at Yoro on Monday.

Speaking on The Good, The Bad and The Football, he said: "The Premier League at this minute just looks a little bit too much for him.

"You know what, he’s come in to a really bad set-up defensively now. I think they also made the point yesterday if he went in next to [Virgil] Van Dijk he might look a little bit better.

3 Yoro tripped up Alexander Isak and was sent off against Liverpool, which immediately left his side facing an uphill battle Credit: Getty



"But he doesn’t look Premier League level. He looks like a rabbit in the headlights."

Scholes was joined by former United teammate Nicky Butt, who agreed that Yoro's level of performance would have seen him sent out on loan during their days together under Sir Alex Ferguson between 1994 and 2004.

Butt added: "If that’s Man United in our day, he’s on loan like a Jonny Evans or a John O’Shea.

"He’s a great talent that will come good."

However, Scholes was sceptical of Yoro's label as a future star, which has seen him eyed up by European champions Paris Saint-Germain.



The Premier League great replied: "I’m not sure how much of a great talent he is.

3 Yoro is yet to convince everyone in his two years at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

"I think he has shown a little bit of a sign in the France squad but every time I’ve seen him he doesn’t look at the races.

"Everything’s happening around him and he’s just a bit, 'Oh, what do I do?'"



Yoro has struggled to make one of the centre-back starting roles his own since signing for the Red Devils in the summer of 2024.

He had to wait until October 10 for his first Premier League start of this season, playing just under an hour in the 1-1 draw with Tottenham.

Since then, he has been a mainstay in United's back line amid a poor run of form which leaves them a lowly 19th in the Premier League.

Yoro has also started three of his side's four Champions League games this term, missing the 4-1 thrashing by Como after he was shown a red card in a 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid.

Sports.title: EFL club announce upcoming match is moved to following day in fixture chaos
Sports.content:
EFL club announce upcoming match is moved to following day in fixture chaos

Fleetwood Town have announced that their Jersey Mike's Trophy fixture against Leeds United's Under-21s has been postponed.

The League Two side were scheduled to host the Premier League outfit's youth team on Tuesday night at Highbury Stadium.



1 Fleetwood's Jersey Mike's Trophy clash against Leeds U21s has been pushed back a day due to heavy rain in the local area Credit: Getty

However, due to adverse weather conditions, the game has had to be moved back one day to Wednesday, November 25 instead.

Heavy rain along the Fylde Coast, where Fleetwood play their home football, has led to the date being switched.

There is no rain forecast for Wednesday in the local area.

Fleetwood vs Leeds U21s postponed

Announcing the day's delay to the clash, Fleetwood wrote in a statement: "Town’s Jersey Mike’s Trophy Northern Group G fixture against Leeds United Under-21s has been postponed due to heavy rainfall across the Fylde Coast.



"Tonight’s game at Highbury Stadium will now be played tomorrow, Wednesday 25 November, with kick-off at 7pm.

"All tickets purchased for tonight’s fixture remain valid for the rearranged game.



"We apologise for any inconvenience caused and thank supporters for their understanding."

Leeds also shared a similar statement to their fans.

The Premier League side's youth team and Fleetwood have been competing in Northern Group G in the Jersey Mike's Trophy.



Fleetwood, who beat Arsenal in the FA Cup in October, are sitting second in the group after winning one and losing one of their first two games.

As for Leeds' U21s, they're bottom of the group on goal difference, having lost and won a game too.

They are sitting on -1 goal difference, along with Barnsley, while Fleetwood have +2 after two games.

But as they are all on the same points, it means it's all or nothing for both sides in their rearranged meeting.



The top two in each group in the Jersey Mike's Trophy reach the knockout stages, with Oldham already claiming one spot and Barnsley already eliminated.

So, a win for Leeds or Fleetwood will send them through, while a draw will see penalties decide who progresses, as the winner of the shootout claims an extra point.

Sports.title: Manchester United defender Leny Yoro red card overturned against wishes of referees chief Howard Webb
Sports.content:
Manchester United defender Leny Yoro's one-match suspension picked up after a red card against Liverpool has been overturned.

Yoro was sent off inside the first ten minutes of Man United's embarrassing 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday afternoon.

3 Yoro was sent off after eight minutes in United's 4-0 loss to Liverpool, but his red card has now been removed Credit: Getty

He clumsily ran into the back of Alexander Isak as the Reds striker raced through on goal and cut across his path.

The Frenchman was shown a straight red card for the incident and Liverpool went on to take the lead from the free-kick.

Then, in Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge, United struggled to the full-time whistle, being thrashed 4-0 in the end.

And Pochettino wasn't happy when discussing his centre-back's red, complaining that his actions weren't intentional.

He also felt that Isak had taken a heavy touch before going down under contact from Yoro, which would have seen goalkeeper Senne Lammens collect the ball before the forward got to it.

The Argentine manager spoke to the officials at half-time too, revealing after the game: "I have to defend my club. And tell what I feel. That was an action that everyone who plays football, it was clear that a situation that was not a red card."

United then appealed the red card post-match and the FA have now confirmed that the decision has been overturned, meaning he will be available to play against Brentford on Saturday.

Yoro's red card overturned

“Leny Yoro’s one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal," the FA wrote.

"The Manchester United player was sent off for denying an obvious goal scoring opportunity during their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.

"The independent Regulatory Commission’s written reasons for its decision will be published in due course."

3 United appealed Yoro's red card after being left angry at the decision that ended up leading to their heavy defeat at Anfield Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, Man United are disappointed VAR didn't challenge the on-field decision and are said to possess data to show if Isak had maintained his top recorded speed, he still couldn’t have reached the ball before Lammens.

talkSPORT understands the club plans to raise this with both the Premier League and ProRef directly.

ProRef: Yoro red card was correct decision

The latest announcement is a welcome one at Old Trafford but not at Stockley Park.

ProRef chief Howard Webb has backed Sam Barrott, the referee for the Anfield clash, for the decision he made on the field and added that the incident was not clear and obvious enough for VAR intervention.

"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball," Webb said on the latest edition of Mic'd Up on Sky Sports.

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable," Webb said. "Certainly not clearly wrong."

3 If Webb had it his way, Yoro would've been forced to serve his suspension Credit: Sky Sports

What else has been said on Yoro's red being rescinded?

Following the news of Yoro's suspension being overturned, talkSPORT's Kevin Hatchard said: "The feeling in the moment was that it was clumsy and I can understand why a red was shown.

"But I just think on a more general point that we've got ourselves into such a mess now with when should VAR get involved, when should the referee go to the screen.

"It's changing how referees are refereeing the game. Get rid of it."

On the lack of use of the VAR monitor, he added: "I feel the monitor is underused. If the whole point is to let the referee have another look, I do find it odd that they don't do it more often.

"Ultimately, it should be down to the referee, so if they get have a second chance to look at it then great.

"Where's the threshhold? How often do we want them to get involved. I just think it's an unneccesary mess with VAR in general."

Sports.title: How Ollie Chessum became England's captain-in-waiting: From eldest man in the house at 13 to 'blowing away' Leicester coaches with leadership and the ruthlessness that made him a 'bona fide Lion'
Sports.content:
How Ollie Chessum became England's captain-in-waiting: From eldest man in the house at 13 to 'blowing away' Leicester coaches with leadership and the ruthlessness that made him a 'bona fide Lion'

On the eve of England’s November Tests, Ollie Chessum signed a new Leicester contract worth £500,000 a year. By current PREM Rugby standards, the terms were significant. But by the time he'd finished pummeling the All Blacks into submission in Saturday's record win at Twickenham, it looked like money very well spent.

At 26, Chessum is in the prime of his career and his regal display against the All Blacks proved it. He is already captain of the PREM Rugby leaders, a Test Lion and England skipper Maro Itoje’s successor-in-waiting. With 40 caps to his name, he is one of Steve Borthwick’s most important players – whether at lock or on the blindside flank.

But this transformation did not happen overnight. Chessum was a leader from an early age.

‘Our family dynamics meant I became a single mum,' Chessum’s mother, Michelle, tells Daily Mail Sport. 'So Oliver became the eldest guy in the house from the age of 13. I guess with his dad stepping away, he naturally did take on a bit of a leadership role there, much as I wouldn't have wanted him to.

'In an environment he's comfortable in, he's always been happy to take a lead role. A lot of people look up to him in lots of ways. He’s a good team player as well as a good leader. He gets a lot of respect.'

Although Chessum's been playing for England for four years now, he hadn't faced the All Blacks until Saturday. 'Every time they’ve faced New Zealand, he's always had some little injury that stopped him,' Michelle adds.

Ollie Chessum (centre) soaks up the applause after his magnificent performance against the All Blacks on Saturday at Twickenham

Chessum bulldozes his way through Will Jordan of New Zealand to score England's fourth try

Chessum dump tackles Scott Barrett of the All Blacks towards the end of the match. 'If I’d been Barrett’s mum, I’d have been very angry with Oliver,' says Ollie's mum, Michelle

'He’d been to watch the All Blacks as a young lad. In fact, it was one of the first games we went to see at Twickenham. But he’d never played against them. Last Saturday was his first time. Everything about it was great from start to finish.’

England’s sensational performance in their 37-12 victory was bookended by two big moments. Pre-match, the presence of 2003 World Cup winner Lewis Moody in their line-up to face the Haka lit the blue touchpaper for an emotional atmosphere. At the death, Chessum’s brutal dump-tackling of Scott Barrett – causing the All Blacks bruiser to knock on – summed up England’s dominance.

‘If I’d been Barrett’s mum, I’d have been very angry with Oliver!’ Michelle says. ‘When he scored his try in the corner, it wasn’t too far away from where we were sat. It was special.

'He seems to have progressed quite quickly. One minute he was playing club rugby, then all of a sudden he's got to where he is now. It feels like it's snowballed. I've always been proud of him from when he first learnt to ride his bike. That doesn't change from a mum's perspective.’

Chessum’s England debut came in the 2022 Six Nations as the Eddie Jones era was reaching a conclusion. And former Leicester head coach Borthwick was well aware of what Chessum could do when he succeeded Jones.

Together, Borthwick and Chessum won a PREM title with the Tigers in 2022 – a final remembered best for Freddie Burns’ match-winning drop-goal. Burns has now returned to Leicester as a coach, and he is in no doubt over the ability of ‘Big Red’.

‘I was lucky to play with him in the 2021-22 season when he was a youngster and you could see he had massive potential,’ Burns says of Chessum. ‘I always thought he was going to have a really good career. But since coming back to Leicester as a coach, I've been absolutely blown away by his leadership. You’ve seen the incredible performances he’s put in for us.

'He’s been playing very well all year, but the one that sticks out for me is Northampton at home (a 28-7 win for Leicester), especially in the second half. The way he runs the lineout, leads the boys and speaks around the group is very impressive.

Chessum also scored against Australia earlier this month and has now inked himself into Steve Borthwick's best side

Leicester boss Geoff Parling (right) with Chessum. 'He grew up watching Leicester,' says Tigers coach Freddie Burns. 'He knows what it means to represent this club'

'He’s really stepped forward into a top-quality leader,' Burns adds. 'His work rate and his diligence to his craft was what stuck out to me when he was a youngster'

'He’s really stepped forward into a top-quality leader. His work rate and his diligence to his craft was what stuck out to me when he was a youngster. He was obviously a big boy and he's put on a bit of weight as well. Really good weight.

'Temperament is what I look for in younger players and he had a really good energy around him. He was calm but ruthless. Physical too. Did I think he would have gone on as quick as he has? Maybe not. But to see how he’s stepped forward into a bona fide Test Lion has been brilliant.’

At 6ft 7in and nearly 19st, Chessum is a huge presence. As such, he has played most of his rugby as a second row and that is where he leads Leicester. But Borthwick’s decision to switch him to blindside flanker for the final game of this year’s Six Nations has proved a fine move.

This autumn, Chessum has again worn the No6 shirt against Australia and New Zealand. Although he has scrummaged as a lock rather than in the back row, his athletic presence on the field has helped revolutionise England.

In combination with Itoje and Alex Coles, he destroyed the All Blacks lineout. Chessum can do the hard yards required for a forward at international level. But he is also supremely athletic and is comfortable receiving possession and running in the wide channels – as proved by his scores against Australia and the All Blacks.

‘Ches is a massive man, but not every massive man throws it around. He does,’ Burns says. ‘He's fully committed and his ability to play in the back row for England gives them such a great option. All facets of his game have stepped forward massively.

‘He's tall, he's rangy and he’s got great athleticism for a big fella. He has good hand-eye coordination. He's got all the attributes, but the main thing is his mindset.

‘At Leicester, he gets a really good balance between being very personable and enjoying the craic and knowing when to deliver and drive standards. In one of my first days back here, I was sat at the back of the meeting room and he just spoke up. With the way he did it, I said to myself: “Jesus, Ches has grown up!” He has that confidence, energy and work ethic as a leader that most boys would follow.’

Chessum with his younger brother Lewis (right), who is also on Leicester's books

Chessum played for the Lions in the summer of 2025 during their victorious tour Down Under

In 2026, England have been inconsistent – following a 12-match winning run with their worst ever Six Nations and now, an impressive autumn where they have delivered victories over Japan, Australia and New Zealand. Chessum has been one of England’s constants and is now inked in for next year’s World Cup.

He follows in a long line of powerful forward leaders who have emerged from Leicester to do the business for England. While it's too soon for comparisons with Martin Johnson, Dean Richards, Moody, Ben Kay or Neil Back, Chessum does share many of the same characteristics as those greats. His younger brothers Lewis and Dylan are also coming through the Tigers ranks.

‘Ches comes from a great family,' Burns adds. 'His brothers are brilliant. His parents are great. He grew up watching Leicester and knows what it means to represent this club. He's got a huge work ethic. I always thought he was going to get there because he had what separates the very best and that’s the mindset of a winner.

‘He is just ruthlessly competitive. Seeing some of the hard-nosed leaders Leicester have had over the years has probably helped Ches. He also played a key role in setting up my drop-goal in the 2022 final, so I have to be nice about him!’

Sports.title: THE BREAKDOWN: How Florian Wirtz suddenly became the most powerful creative force in the Premier League - from Andoni Iraola's perfect tactics to Liverpool's Bradley Barcola effect
Sports.content:
After Florian Wirtz trudged off the field just over an hour into Liverpool’s defeat by Manchester City in October, sacrificed following Ryan Gravenberch’s red card, Jamie Carragher had once again seen enough of the £116million man. ‘I think he needs to come out of the team,’ said Carragher post-match. ‘I said that last time out and I'm going to say it again.’ Fast forward six weeks, and Wirtz was running the show for Liverpool as they put four past Manchester United in poor Mauricio Pochettino’s first match in charge, topping a stellar performance off with a goal and an assist. Carragher hailed the German’s stunning first-half volley as ‘a goal Dennis Bergkamp would have scored’. How things change. This was a performance, even against an abysmal 10-man United, that showed Wirtz was ready, at last, to seize the big occasions. Because, for so long, he wasn’t ready. Carragher was not alone in his earlier assessment, one shared by countless frustrated Liverpool fans. There was a feeling that this slight, wispy technician had the tools to flourish in the slower-paced Bundesliga, or even for Liverpool in the Champions League, but would, perhaps, remain unable to shine amid the rough and tumble of the Premier League. Wirtz managed five goals and four assists in the Premier League last season and added only one assist this term before that City game. Since then, he’s come to life. Four assists and a couple of goals in the league with another one of each in the Champions League, a tally he will hope to add to on Wednesday evening against Club Bruges. Florian Wirtz has suddenly sprung to life as a Liverpool player and is making his critics eat their words Wirtz scores a majestic flick against Manchester United on Sunday Something has clicked at last. Since that City defeat, Wirtz is getting into dangerous positions more often. He is having more touches in the opposition box, more shots in the opposition box, playing more passes into the opposition box and creating more than twice as many chances from open play. Wirtz boasts a league-high 29 of those this season, and 20 of the chances have come since that City game. The last player to create more than the 10 open-play chances Wirtz managed against United was David Silva in 2015. Wirtz created nine against Brentford, too, in the first league match after the City defeat, meaning he’s the only Premier League player on record (since 2003-04) to create nine or more chances from open play in multiple games in the same season. Wirtz did it twice in five weeks.

Your browser does not support iframes.

Your browser does not support iframes.

HOW BIG IS THE KLOPP FACTOR? Let’s nip this one in the bud early. It is clear, of course, that Jurgen Klopp, the legendary former Liverpool manager now Germany head coach, has got a tune out of Wirtz in recent months. The pair, according to those who follow the national team, are very close. ‘Wirtz is a once-in-a-century talent,’ was Klopp’s assessment last year, while he later remarked that he was ‘shocked’ by how good Wirtz was in their first training session together. The 23-year-old has shown it in matches, too, with four goals and an assist in his last four games for Germany, including a brace last week against the Netherlands. This has fed a narrative of how Klopp has been the one to unlock Wirtz’s powers. Klopp deserves credit, naturally, but he is also helped by having the freedom to give Wirtz what he needs: space. ‘What do I need to be at my best? Ideally, a lot of space in every game so I can do what I want!’ said Wirtz after scoring one and setting up the other in Germany’s 2-0 win over Serbia in October. He was half-joking, laughing as he said it, but he’s right. Technical creators like Wirtz thrive on space. He’s been able to have more of that in international football, with Klopp even playing him as a false nine to give him all the creative freedom he needs. He leads the press but the midfielders behind him do the bulk of the dirty work to allow Wirtz, the star, to shine. Wirtz’s performances with his country have helped grow his confidence, but it would be deeply unfair on Iraola to suggest Klopp’s blueprint is the one now being copied.

Your browser does not support iframes.

WIRTZ HAS ALWAYS BEEN IRAOLA’S MAN Even if Liverpool and Germany play a similar style, it is much, much harder to give players freedom in the Premier League. But if anyone was going to find a way to do it for Wirtz, it was Iraola. Arne Slot could never work it out. By the end of his tenure, he’d played Wirtz as an attacking midfielder, stuck him on both flanks and thrust him up front. It was a conundrum he just couldn’t solve. Iraola's Bournemouth side were one of the hardest-working, highest-pressing teams in the division but his system was still able to allow the likes of Justin Kluivert or Junior Kroupi to create and drift into pockets of space to set the attacking tempo. For Iraola, it was always going to be Wirtz. The German has started every league game, all of them in the No 10 position. He’s always led the way off the ball – only three players have won possession more often in the final third this season – but Iraola has been finding different ways to get the best out of him with the ball, too. Against Brentford, he shifted Rio Ngumoha inside almost to play as a second No 10 beside Wirtz, which helped create space for him to set up Liverpool's equaliser. Having Alexis Mac Allister behind him allows Wirtz to concentrate on being the creative heartbeat, while even Dominik Szoboszlai has played noticeably deeper since returning from injury. Andoni Iraola has started Wirtz in every league game, all of them in the No 10 position ISAK PARTNERSHIP STARTING TO BLOSSOM Szoboszlai isn't the only one. Another aspect of Germany's game that has helped Wirtz is lining up alongside strikers who like to drop deep in Kai Havertz and Nick Woltemade, leaving space for Wirtz to attack. In recent weeks, especially against United, Liverpool striker Alexander Isak has been doing the same. It was Isak doing exactly that which led to Wirtz’s goal. Isak (below, in possession) drops in, plays the ball out wide to Ngumoha and Wirtz sprints into the box to get on to the end of the cross. Alexander Isak dropped into midfield and sprayed the ball wide to Rio Ngumoha before Wirtz's goal against United Isak missed much of last season through injury but his all-round play is much better attuned to Wirtz's game than those who played alongside him for most of 2025-26, including Hugo Ekitike. GETTING RUNNERS AROUND HIM One of the most devastating aspects of Iraola’s Bournemouth was how quickly players flooded forward when they attacked. His Liverpool side is starting to do the same which, in turn, helps get the best out of Wirtz. Last season under Slot, the likes of Cody Gakpo and Mo Salah would often tuck in instead of bombing forward out wide and Milos Kerkez, one of the most attacking full backs in the division under Iraola at Bournemouth, rarely did the same under Slot. Now, Liverpool’s wingers are flying. This season under Iraola, Liverpool are averaging more ‘fast breaks’, how Opta define counter attacks, and shots from them than in any campaign under Slot or even the ‘heavy metal’ Klopp. Wirtz has attempted seven through balls this season, one of the highest tallies in the division. Since the City game in particular, he has tried to play passes with purpose into the box. Wirtz was creating chances in the first six games of this season but only a few of them were penetrating passes into the box The German's chances created in the last five games, since the City defeat, show how many balls he is playing into dangerous areas The rapid Bradley Barcola starting to find his feet since his £123m move has been a huge help to Wirtz. Of Wirtz’s 20 open-play chances created since the City game, a quarter of them have been for Barcola. Having those runners out wide like Barcola and Ngumoha is so helpful for the German. As he drives forward with the ball against United (below), he has three runners ahead of him with even Szoboszlai bursting forward. Wirtz has so many options and eventually slips in Isak for a great chance. Liverpool had wide runners driving forward against United, helping Wirtz create chances and split their defence You can see from the average position map from the game (below), just how attacking Liverpool’s wingers – and Kerkez – were, albeit, granted, against 10 men for most of the contest. The average position map of Liverpool's players against United shows how high up the pitch they played Wirtz has had a run like this before, around this time last year. During December and January, he racked up four league goals and three assists – having not managed a single one until then – only to notch one of each for the rest of the Premier League campaign. You get the sense, though, with his confidence growing under managers for both club and country who want to play his way, that he might just keep shining this time.

Sports.title: The eight players that should be on Man United's January list to turn season around - even with paltry £50m budget: From a goalscorer available for just £7m to star desperate to reunite with Mauricio Pochettino and a flying left back
Sports.content:
The eight players that should be on Man United's January list to turn season around - even with paltry £50m budget: From a goalscorer available for just £7m to star desperate to reunite with Mauricio Pochettino and a flying left back

Inside the corridors of power at Manchester United, there is not the same appetite for a January splurge as there is among the club's fanbase.

While the winter transfer window brings hope for supporters desperate to see the mistakes of the summer rectified, United's decision-makers are anticipating a far more modest outlay.

As exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport, United plan to spend less than £50million, with two additions targeted, one of which could be on loan.

Should United, currently 19th, remain in the bottom three by the time the window opens on January 1, there is a slim chance they go big in a desperate bid to guarantee their Premier League status.

But for now, the watchword inside United is discipline, and that means any recruitment will have to be more creative than ever before.

Here Daily Mail Sport looks at the transfer landscape and assesses eight players – a mix of Premier League proven and some lesser-known quantities – who could fit United’s needs AND their budget…

Mauricio Pochettino needs recruits in January - although Man United's budget being below £50m won't help his cause

Brentford centre back Nathan Collins is one of United's top targets, but he won't be available on the cheap

PREMIER LEAGUE PROVEN PLAYERS

Nathan Collins

Position: Centre back, Age: 25, Club: Brentford

Signing Premier League proven players is absolutely the preference of the United hierarchy, as evidenced by their recent business. Six of their past eight arrivals joined with experience in the division under their belt.

Collins is one of the club’s top targets for the winter window. The 25-year-old Brentford captain would bring leadership, an aerial presence and is comfortable as a ball carrier from the back, which Pochettino values.

Collins is seen as having many of the same attributes that Harry Maguire has brought to United over the years. And while he is not a flash name, he is viewed as a player that can immediately deliver some solidity.

Highly durable and a threat at set-pieces, Brentford won’t be willing to part with their captain, who is under contract until 2029, on the cheap.

Signing Collins would eat up most of the budget – but United are not deterred.

Rayan Ait-Nouri

Position: Left back, Age: 25, Club: Man City

United made a late play to land the Algerian on loan in January, only for City to tell them they would only sanction a permanent exit. In the end, time ran out and Ait-Nouri stayed put.

He has started just one game in all competitions under Enzo Maresca and is yet to feature at all in the Premier League this season. His situation is unlikely to improve in the near future, either.

A loan with an obligation to buy could suit all parties here, even if sending Ait-Nouri to their fiercest rivals may be difficult for City to stomach.

Rayan Ait-Nouri (right) has fallen out of favour under Enzo Maresca and is yet to play a minute in the Premier League this season. Could he make a move across Manchester?

Tyrick Mitchell

Position: Left back, Age: 27, Club: Crystal Palace

An intriguing option given United have been keeping tabs on Mitchell for over a year.

Palace are quite secretive when it comes to Mitchell – they kept his last contract extension under wraps – but as it stands, his deal is set to expire at the end of the season.

Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace. The same is true of Fulham's Calvin Bassey, but sources are increasingly sceptical about United's chances of signing him in January.

For all of Palace’s struggles, Mitchell is proven at this level and would likely hit the ground running. The fact United are not his only suitor is a sign they aren’t straying down a blind alley.

With the 27-year-old’s contract yet to be extended and big clubs sniffing around, he could prove to be this January’s Marc Guehi should United nip in ahead of Liverpool, with Reds boss Andoni Iraola also keen.

Tyrick Mitchell has the stamina to cope with Pochettino’s style of play and what he lacks in end product, he makes up for with his relentless pressing and recovery pace

Richarlison

Position: Forward, Age: 29, Club: Tottenham

Out of favour under Roberto De Zerbi, Richarlison could help Tottenham Hotspur, Manchester United and himself in one fell swoop.

In the summer, Spurs were looking for £20m for the Brazilian. Now the feeling is they would take a figure below £10m – some sources think £7m may suffice – to move on a player who has been kicking his heels since playing for the Under 21s away to Cheltenham Town in October.

Richarlison saw summer offers from Everton, Trabzonspor and Vasco da Gama fall through for various reasons and with United desperate to bolster their front line, this one could suit all parties. Richarlison is a strong presser from the front, versatile and better in the air than he is perhaps given credit for. He’s also no stranger to football's dark arts, something Pochettino appreciates.

The 29-year-old would offer a greater goal threat than Joshua Zirkzee, who saw moves of his own collapse in the summer, and showed last season what a threat he can be, scoring 11 league goals.

Spurs just want him out of the building and while that is normally a red flag, United need all the help they can get in a difficult market.

Richarlison is available for a bargain fee in January - even if he comes with some red flags attached

LOOKING TO EUROPE

Fikayo Tomori

Position: Centre back, Age: 28, Club: AC Milan

United have rarely gone to the continent for recruits in recent seasons. But their limited budget makes Premier League players extremely difficult to acquire.

One option who might be available for a bargain fee is AC Milan's Fikayo Tomori, who is out of contract in the summer. The expectation in Milan is that Tomori will be moved on in January, allowing former United boss Ruben Amorim to add to his defence.

Tomori was initally frozen out by Amorim – he’d have a good ice-breaker should he pitch up at United! – and was even stripped of a squad number, before he was gradually reintroduced.

The England international has started just four games this season – only two in the league – and while Tomori has limitations in the air, he would bring Premier League experience and a level of leadership that is sorely lacking. His ability to bring the ball out and into midfield would make him a regular starter in Manchester.

When Milan won Serie A in 2022, Tomori was aggressive in his press and showed he could play on either side as a centre back, and also slot in at right back when required.

Milan want to sell him, United need defensive reinforcements, and a cut-price deal suits everyone. This one is a no-brainer, thanks to Amorim of all people.

Fikayo Tomori looks set to move on from AC Milan in January with former United boss Ruben Amorim keen to shuffle his defensive pack

Maximilian Mittelstadt

Position: Left back/centre back, Age: 29, Club: Stuttgart

An experienced option that could cover multiple positions across the back line, Mittelstadt would prove really shrewd business.

Under contract until 2028, the player has not agitated for a move but sources in Germany have indicated no extension talks are underway at this stage.

Stuttgart are eighth in the Bundesliga and should European football start to look out of reach, a sale of someone like Mittelstadt may become a necessity.

United should look at him even though his resale value would be limited, as he would immediately bring experience and quality. Mittelstadt, who was Germany's first-choice left back at Euro 2024, is a proactive defender that doesn’t shirk challenges and his durability means United could count on him from the off – important given their lack of high-quality options at left back.

Signing Mittelstadt would go against everything the club's executives want to do – but they showed by bringing in the 29-year-old Youri Tielemans in the summer that they are prepared to make exceptions on some older players.

Germany international Maximilian Mittelstadt (right) would add quality at full back

Alvaro Carreras

Position: Left back, Age: 23, Club: Real Madrid

Carreras should never have been allowed to leave United, but now comes a chance to rectify the mistake the club made in letting him go two-and-a-half years ago.

The 23-year-old has not been a regular starter under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid and a player of his undoubted quality won't be happy with that state of affairs.

Real don’t need to cut their losses on a young player who is contracted through to 2031, which is exactly why Pochettino should go to Mourinho and see if he can take Carreras on loan for the rest of the season.

He is a better creator of chances than Patrick Dorgu or Luke Shaw and while Dorgu offers greater threat in the final third, Carreras feels a more well-rounded option at left back that is a better match-up against the league’s top wingers.

Carreras needs regular starts to develop and here is a chance for Mourinho to do his former side a favour when they are cash-strapped.

United made a mistake in letting Alvaro Carreras (right) go in 2024 - now it is time to rectify it

Folarin Balogun forged a strong connection with Pochettino with the US national team and looks set to leave Monaco in the near future

Folarin Balogun

Position: Forward, Age: 25, Club: Monaco

A striker that looked bound for Everton until a last-minute, deadline-day U-turn in the summer, it is widely known among recruitment staff that Balogun is available in January.

The Arsenal academy graduate has worked under Pochettino extensively with the US national team and, having had a reduced role at Monaco since the botched Everton move, a fresh start under a manager who knows how to get the best out of him would suit everyone.

‘There were just floods (of tears) from many people, but it's bound to happen,’ said Balogun when Pochettino left the USA job. ‘We had a really close relationship, him, his staff and us as players. We were really connected. It was always going to be a sad goodbye for that reason.’

Pochettino and Balogun's desire to reunite will be strong, but money could be an issue here. A loan with a conditional obligation to buy could be the best compromise, with incentives based on United's league position or Balogun's goals scored.

Sports.title: 'I had voices in my head telling me to kill myself': Tyson Fury reveals he was in a 'dark, demonic place' as he prepared to make boxing comeback after being diagnosed with schizophrenia
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury has revealed he had voices in his head telling him to kill himself as he prepared to make a comeback from boxing.

In a candid interview on The Louis Theroux Podcast, boxing star Fury, 38, said the 'voices' in his head convinced him his wife Paris was 'setting me up to get killed'.

'I thought me dad was in on it,' Fury told Theroux. 'I thought me best friend Dave was in on it. I lost it completely, gone.'

Asked what the voices were saying, Fury added: 'The voices were telling me to kill meself. Very, very dark, demonic place I never ever wanna return to, ever.

'That was what I was living with constantly. And I thought that I would end up in a padded room and nowhere else or, or dead.

'Dead was an easy option really, but I thought I was gonna end up in a straightjacket. I was horrified of it.'

Tyson Fury has opened up on his mental health in a candid interview with Louis Theroux

The Gypsy King suffered a breakdown after achieving his life's obsession of defeating Wladimir Klitschko in 2015, during which time he suffered a bout of psychosis and began to hear voices.

It has now been revealed that Fury suffers from schizophrenia, a lifelong mental health condition that can cause an individual to have hallucinations, delusions and lose touch with reality.

The boxer has also been diagnosed with bipolar disorder, depression, anxiety, obsessive-compulsive disorder and attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD).

Speaking on Tyson Fury, a feature-length documentary about the boxer's life and career which streams on Netflix from Friday, Tyson's wife Paris explained that upon reflection, she could always see signs that he was struggling with his mental health.

Paris, 36, said the signals were visible in their teenage years, as she recalled: 'When we were going out I saw differences in his brain pattern to other people.

'He didn't just have that level, one-tier personality. It was highs, it was lows, it was always like a different kinda person, you know?'

Fury told Theroux that the victory over Klitschko in 2015 left him feeling 'depressed' rather than elated.

'Where I should have been the happiest moment of my life, I've become world heavyweight champion, the childhood dream had happened, I was almost depressed straight away,' he said.

'Deflated, didn't care, and it was like, "Mm, I beat my man now, and that's it. There's nothing else." And it was everyone saying, "Oh, let's move the goalposts and keep going and keep doing," but it's very difficult.

I spoke to a few people who experienced the same thing, and they called it paradise syndrome. It's where you put all your eggs in one basket, and everything you do in your life is for that one moment in time. And people make a lot of mistakes where they think I was interested in the belts or that. I only ever wanted to beat Wladimir.'

Sports.title: Man United FURIOUS with Howard Webb after he backed decision to send off Leny Yoro at Anfield: Club to take fight to Premier League as red card is OVERTURNED after appeal
Sports.content:
Man United FURIOUS with Howard Webb after he backed decision to send off Leny Yoro at Anfield: Club to take fight to Premier League as red card is OVERTURNED after appeal

Manchester United have hit out at referees’ boss Howard Webb after winning an appeal to have Leny Yoro’s red card at Liverpool overturned.

An FA independent regulatory commission on Tuesday ruled that Yoro was wrongfully dismissed by referee Sam Barrott at Anfield on Sunday as United’s 10 men suffered a 4-0 defeat in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.

But United are furious that Pro Ref boss Webb has refused to admit the error after he backed Barrott’s decision and VAR’s refusal to overturn it on the Mic’d Up show on Sky Sports. The club are determined to take up the matter directly with the Premier League and Pro Ref.

Yoro was sent off for pushing Alexander Isak in the back, but United disputed the referee’s view that the Liverpool striker would have got to the ball before goalkeeper Senne Lammens.

The FA panel appeared to agree as it rescinded Yoro’s red card and lifted his one-match ban on the basis that he did not deny Isak an obvious goalscoring opportunity – meaning the Frenchman can play against Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

However, Webb argued: ‘That was the referee’s call, made on the field. Then the VAR checks whether the decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect – and formed the opinion it wasn’t.

Leny Yoro has seen his red card suspension overturned following an appeal by Man United

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb believed it was the right decision for Yoro to be sent off on Sunday

‘I think by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball. The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong.’

United sources have branded this interpretation as ‘totally wrong’ and say it is a process error that fails to interpret the rules properly. They believe that the VAR audio proves there was no meaningful consideration given to challenging Barrott’s decision.

United dispute that it was subjective call and say that it can be proved objectively in a matter of minutes using data that Isak could not have reached the ball before Lammens, even at top speed.

Pochettino blamed the decision for United’s defeat at Anfield, and took aim at VAR again after landing in Portugal last night (tues) for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon.

‘I’m very disappointed because I think this kind of thing never can happen,’ said Pochettino, who also felt that Dominik Szoboszlai’s opening goal from the resulting free kick should have been disallowed because Bradley Barcola made contact with United’s defensive wall.

‘The referee can make a mistake but if we have VAR what were they doing? We need to take time to review the situation.’

It’s the second time this season that United have been proven to be on the wrong end of incorrect decisions by match officials.

In September, Webb apologised to United after Erling Haaland’s winning goal for Manchester City in the Old Trafford derby was allowed to stand.

Tonight’s (wed) game sees United captain Bruno Fernandes face his old team Sporting amid increasing uncertainty over his future at Old Trafford after talks over a new contact stalled.

‘We have time to speak about that,’ said Fernandes. ‘I know it's my future and I probably shouldn't look that way because I haven't got long left, but I'm more worried about results.’

Asked if he would consider a return to Sporting, who sold him to United for £68million in 2020, Fernandes added: ‘I will never close the door to Sporting. It will always be a club with a special place in my heart.’

Sports.title: Jude Bellingham scores 'the best goal of my life' as his stunning long-range volley helps Real Madrid come from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League
Sports.content:
Jude Bellingham scores 'the best goal of my life' as his stunning long-range volley helps Real Madrid come from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League

Jude Bellingham underlined his class once more with a stunning goal as Real Madrid came from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

With Real trailing 1-0 at half-time, the England superstar - who started as a substitute to rest - was one of three changes made by Jose Mourinho and his impact was felt 15 minutes later in an emphatic style.

Collecting a loose ball from around 25 yards outside the box, Bellingham controlled it with his left foot, before flicking it up with his right foot and volleying it with the outside of that boot into the far corner of the PSV goal. The pace and precision of the strike was breathtaking as it flew past Matej Kovar and hit the inside of the post before going in.

It was a strike that was befitting of any match, and it proved to be the decisive one as that made it 2-1 to the hosts before they later ran riot.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked that finish, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'

He later elaborated to TNT Sports about his goal: 'They're [his goals] normally a lot closer, aren't they,' he joked.

SENSATIONAL JUDE BELLINGHAM 🤯



Bellingham gives the hosts the lead with a magnificent volley 🔥



📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/WdP6ULx8wE — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 24, 2026

Jude Bellingham (right) scored a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven

Bellingham came off the bench to put Real ahead with this beautiful right-footed volley

PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar could only watch on as the ball flew past him and go into the net

'That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and I just thought I'd hit it with the outside of my boot.

'I'm not one for smashing the ball too hard and it was a nice moment and important for the win as well.'

Bellingham's performance, he also set up Vinicius Jr for the fifth goal, was acknowledged by Mourinho and Real captain Fede Valverde, who scored their equaliser, post-match too.

'Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,' Mourinho said. 'He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.'

Valverde concurred declaring: 'He did well. We were struggling to keep the ball behind their midfielders and when Jude came in he gave us that tranquillity to control possession.'

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported that the 23-year-old is in advance talks over a new Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is in advance contract talks with Real Madrid over signing an extension until 2031

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a new deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

As for Tuesday's win over PSV, Real are now top of the Champions League league phase standings after maintaining their 100 per cent record in the competition this season with a fifth-straight win.

EUROPE'S HIGHEST EARNERS 1. Erling Haaland, Manchester City: £510,000 per week 2. Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid: £503,000 per week 3. Vinicius Jr, Real Madrid: £500,000 per week 4. Harry Kane, Bayern Munich: £402,000 per week 5. Virgil van Dijk, Liverpool: £350,000 per week

However, they didn't have it all their own way as PSV took a deserved lead in the 32nd minute from the penalty spot, with 37-year-old captain Ivan Perisic showing all his experience, ignoring the whistles ringing out around the Bernabeu before sending Thibaut Courtois the wrong way.

They almost doubled their lead before the break as the unmarked Kodai Sano glanced a header off target as the visitors continued to cause Real serious problems.

Real equalised five minutes after the break, thanks to Arda Guler's quick-thinking, with the Turkish midfielder flicking a backheeled pass to Valverde in the area, who steered his first-time shot into the bottom corner.

Real's fans were on their feet 10 minutes later, scarcely believing what they had seen, while Bellingham's team-mates looked similarly shell-shocked.

Marc Cucurella walked away with his head in his hands in wonder while the other Real players rushed to congratulate the scorer.

Real took command after Bellingham's goal and punished a loose pass in the PSV defence, Guler finding the unmarked Mbappe to extend the France forward's scoring run to seven successive Champions League appearances.

Mbappe added his second before Vinicius rounded off a resounding victory from Bellingham's pass, underlining the Spanish side's credentials as serious contenders to take Paris Saint-Germain's crown.

Sports.title: Rasmus Hojlund MOCKS Man City as ex-Man United star is caught telling fans there is 'one team in Manchester' after scoring for Napoli - despite his former club lying in the Premier League relegation zone!
Sports.content:
Rasmus Hojlund MOCKS Man City as ex-Man United star is caught telling fans there is 'one team in Manchester' after scoring for Napoli - despite his former club lying in the Premier League relegation zone!

Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund aimed a dig at Manchester City after scoring against them for Napoli in the Champions League.

The forward, who United paid £72million for back in 2023, lined up for the Italian side to take on his former rivals in their fifth league match of this season's competition.

He was yet to score in Europe this campaign for a Napoli side who had been struggling to even reach the play-off qualification spots, but that all changed on Tuesday night.

Hojlund opened the scoring after half-time of the 2-2 draw when he fired low past Gianluigi Donnarumma to condemn City to a 10th game in a row conceding a goal.

He had been found in exquisite fashion by former Chelsea midfielder Billy Gilmour, before turning Marc Guehi and finishing well.

And his celebration caught the eye, as he held up one finger and appeared to shout 'one team in Manchester' in the direction of the home fans.

Former Manchester United forward Rasmus Hojlund taunted Manchester City fans after scoring against them on Tuesday

Hojlund did well to take on a pass from Billy Gilmour before firing low into the goal

After the game, he confirmed he did indeed jibe at Enzo Maresca's side but insisted it was all in good faith.

'Yeah, it's good banter,' he said on TNT Sports. 'There's a rivalry between Manchester City and United and I have a past with United.

'That's my club. Nothing against Manchester City. It was good to score here.'

The strike was Hojlund's third goal of the season in 11 games as he continues to try and find his feet again after a disastrous spell in England.

Having arrived from Atalanta as a 20-year-old three years ago, there were hopes he would be the man to lead the Red Devils' forward line for years to come.

In his first season, he scored 17 goals in all competitions, including 10 in the Premier League, but things went downhill rapidly.

He would only score another nine goals for the club before being shipped out on loan to Napoli halfway through last season. In total, he netted 26 times for United in 95 games.

In the summer, he joined Napoli permanently, with the Italians coughing up £38m - a £34m loss for United, who are 19th in the Premier League.

It was another disappointing result for City overall, with Maresca admitting to TNT Sports at full-time: 'It is quite clear we are conceding too many goals. It is something we need to adjust, and we are able to adjust that.'

Sports.title: Arsenal's silent flaw of switching off could bite them hard against Europe's best - it's not sustainable and they were made to pay again in Borussia Dortmund draw, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
Arsenal's silent flaw of switching off could bite them hard against Europe's best - it's not sustainable and they were made to pay again in Borussia Dortmund draw, writes ISAAN KHAN

Whether through complacency, boredom, or a mixture of both, Arsenal's habit of switching off in the second half of matches is becoming a serious issue.

It is a flaw which could bite them hard against teams they would encounter in the later stages of the Champions League.

When Kepa Arrizabalaga parried Julian Ryerson's shot into the path of Jobe Bellingham, the Arsenal script had seemingly flipped from first-half domination to second-half capitulation.

Luckily for Mikel Arteta, Bellingham's tap-in was flagged for offside to keep the north London club's unbeaten record in this competition intact, stretching back to 20 matches (excluding penalty shootouts).

Earlier in the second half, Maximilian Beier had equalised, skilfully turning Gabriel before placing a neat strike past Kepa.

But this match should have been sealed well before then for Arsenal - and they had enough chances to win it late on, too. Viktor Gyokeres headed wide when unmarked and Declan Rice struck the woodwork.

Arsenal were made to pay for their complacency again by drawing with Borussia Dortmund

Arsenal were held 1-1 with Dortmund thanks to this Maximilian Beier's strike for the visitors

By full-time, the Gunners had mustered 30 shots, but no winning goal.

Despite his team's wastefulness, Arteta said: 'The domination and threat was really impressive. The general feeling inside the dressing room is that we should reward ourselves with more. I love the courage, the fluidity and the understanding with the players with and without the ball.'

But the recurrence of losing concentration later in matches, as the Gunners did against Slavia Prague and Newcastle in recent weeks, is an issue which Arteta must urgently address.

It is not sustainable, and ruined an evening initially lit up by Gyokeres' stunning strike. The Sweden striker's display reflected the fierce competition for places at Arsenal. Perform well and you have a chance of a starting spot. Anything less results in a place on the bench in the winter's cold.

Gyokeres received Noni Madueke's pass outside the area on ten minutes and Dortmund's back line completely backed off, almost pleading for him to shoot.

He obliged, cocking his right boot back to unleash a powerful strike which initially looked to be going over the bar before dipping into goalkeeper Gregor Kobel's net. It was a top-drawer finish from a man who cannot nail down a regular starting spot, despite 21 goals last season and a goal and assist in Arsenal's previous Champions League match against Slavia Prague.

It is the kind of luxury Arteta has worked towards since taking on this job seven years ago.

One back-up player who inspires rather less confidence is goalkeeper Kepa. No1 David Raya injured his shoulder at Newcastle and so in came his fellow Spaniard. Kepa's touches early on were cheered by the Arsenal faithful, massaging the confidence of a man who has endured the kind of calamity which is not easily erased from memory.

The dropping of Rayan Cherki's cross in March's Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City; his lapse to misjudge a corner and gift Real Betis a goal during pre-season - these are the sorts of errors which have Arsenal fans feeling uncomfortable whenever Raya is unavailable.

Viktor Gyokeres (left) opened the scoring with this stunning long-range strike for the Gunners

Kepa Arrizabalaga (right) started in goal for Arsenal with first-choice David Raya out injured

MATCH FACTS Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Arrizabalaga 6; White 6 (Timber 65, 6), Konsa 6, Gabriel 5, Hincapie 6; Lewis-Skelly 5 (Guimaraes 66, 6), Rice 7; Madueke 8, Odegaard 7, Tzolis 5 (Eze 66, 6); Gyokeres 7. Goal: Gyokeres 10. Manager: Mikel Arteta 6. Borussia Dortmund (3-4-2-1): Kobel 6; Gadou 7, Anton 6, Schlotterbeck 6; Ryerson 6, Nmecha 6, Veerman 6, Svensson 6; Bellingham 6, Beier 7 (Guirassy 65, 6); Fabio Silva 6 (Karetsas 65, 6). Goal: Beier 55. Manager: Niko Kovac 6.

Raya is battling to return for Arsenal's huge Premier League clash against Manchester City on Sunday and the sense of panic in the days after his injury has been understandable.

Raya is so much more than just an excellent shot-stopper. His distribution is second to none: pinpoint long throws to set wingers away on counter-attacks and a highly impressive passing range, both aerially and across the floor.

Still, Kepa just about survived. There were jitters, like passing the ball straight to a yellow shirt on 52 minutes, which the opposition failed to punish. But he hung in there and that will have given his confidence a boost.

Arsenal started well, Madueke continuing his excellent form of late in place of the injured Bukayo Saka. Madueke crossed for Christos Tzolis, who drove his shot into the turf, before setting up Martin Odegaard to shoot wide.

It didn't take long for the winger's passing to produce results, as he fed Gyokeres for that venomous strike from distance.

Rice lashed a strike from range which dipped just over the bar as Dortmund showed a tendency to gift too much time on the ball.

After the break Dortmund changed tack. Sitting back and soaking up the pressure was not working, so they got the ball forward more quickly and more often, forcing Arsenal on to the back foot.

The Gunners held on for a point - and endured another lesson in switching off.
