Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Threatens to Smack Rayo Valenzuela in Leaked DMs After Walking Away From Zuffa
Sports.content:
Jose “Rayo” Valenzuela posted a screenshot of an Instagram message exchange between him and Shakur Stevenson on Tuesday, showing the bitterness on Rayo’s part after Shakur left Zuffa without accepting an offer to fight him.

Rayo (16-3, 10 KOs) had hoped to fight Shakur (25-0, 11 KOs) while they were briefly teammates, but Shakur rejected Zuffa’s offer.

Posting the exchange on X, Valenzuela captioned the image, “Saying everything but ‘let’s fight!'”

Valenzuela’s post comes after he was interviewed by Ring Magazine and called Shakur “weak” for leaving Zuffa Boxing instead of being a team player and agreeing to fight him in an in-house contest. Stevenson signed with Zuffa on July 9th of this year, but the two mutually parted ways three months later in October, with Stevenson failing to fight once while signed.

The comments from Valenzuela clearly bothered Shakur, causing him to slide into Valenzuela’s DMs.

“Say bh ass n* watch how loose you is with yo words, All that calling me a p*y st watch that.. Ion play them type of games,” said Shakur.

“Shut yo ass up and fight!” said Valenzuela.

“U a b*h, That’s why u clout chasing. I thought u was more solid then that, But look u using them disrespectful ass words stand on that st when u run into me!!” said Stevenson.

“You a b***h and ain’t nobody scared of you. We can fight next and settle it!” said Valenzuela.

“Just know I will smack the holy st out of u if u keep disrespecting me,” said Stevenson.

“I used to look at you and be like I’d beat tf outta dude!” said Valenzuela.

The interaction shows the bad blood between Rayo and Shakur from the brief period when they were both with Zuffa Boxing. It was a logical fight to make, but Shakur was aiming higher, wanting a bigger money fight. Being dismissed as inadequate has likely gotten on Valenzuela’s nerves because this is a fight that could have easily happened. Stevenson turned it down.

Stevenson would have been better off if he had taken it because he’s just been sitting inactive. At least he would have gotten the opportunity to be seen by fans while showing he’s a team player by fighting one of Zuffa’s fighters. Turki Alalshikh owns 60% of Zuffa, and it would have worked well for Stevenson’s career to fight one of his fighters instead of wasting time trying to get a fight with Devin Haney (31-0, 15 KOs) while insisting on a weight handicap.

In Valenzuela’s interview with Ring Magazine, he was critical of Shakur for trying to get a catchweight against Haney and Raymond Muratalla (24-0, 17 KOs), viewing that behavior as showing weakness.

Shakur is now a free agent and has a purse bid scheduled for November 30th for his mandatory defense against Muratalla. No one has signed Stevenson, and it may not be worth it if he’s going to price himself out and waste time trying to get weight advantages for fights.

Valenzuela is still with Zuffa Boxing and is in negotiations for a fight against WBA lightweight champion Floyd Schofield (19-0, 13 KOs). The two have a December 11th deadline before a purse bid is called.

If Stevenson wanted to smack Valenzuela, he had the perfect chance to do that when he was signed with Zuffa. They wanted the fight, but he turned it down and left the company.

Sports.title: Agit Kabayel Has Earned His Shot at Usyk
Sports.content:
Oleksandr Usyk is still the best heavyweight in the world, and Agit Kabayel is the man I’d most like to see him fight next. Usyk has already beaten Tyson Fury, Anthony Joshua, and Daniel Dubois twice apiece. Kabayel brings a different test. He does his best work to the body, and he’s stopped heavyweights who were supposed to make him pay for coming forward.

Kabayel makes his first defense of the WBC title against Nelson Hysa on Saturday in Düsseldorf. He was elevated after Usyk vacated the belt in June, but the wins that make his case came before the promotion. Kabayel stopped Frank Sanchez and Zhilei Zhang, then took out Damian Knyba in three rounds in January. Sanchez has since knocked out unbeaten Richard Torrez Jr. in two rounds, a result that makes Kabayel’s win over him look even better.

What Kabayel would ask of Usyk

Kabayel went downstairs against Frank Sanchez and Zhilei Zhang and stopped them both. Against Usyk, I’d watch what he does after the first body shot. Can he stay close enough to land a second, or does Usyk turn him and make him walk in all over again? I’d pick Usyk, but that’s the exchange I’d want to see in the eighth or ninth round, when Kabayel has had time to slow him down.

Dubois has had the best year of the other champions. He got up twice in May to stop Fabio Wardley in the 11th and take the WBO belt, then finished the rematch in two rounds in October. There’s a better fight for him in a rematch with IBF champion Filip Hrgovic, whom he stopped on cuts in 2024. Hrgovic has since stopped Moses Itauma in nine rounds to win his title. He entered the ring after Dubois beat Wardley and asked him about fighting in March. That rematch would put two belts on the line and give Hrgovic a chance to answer for his only defeat.

Fury and Joshua will get more attention in Cardiff on December 11 than any of those fights. British fans have waited years to see them settle it, and the winner will have a big win to sell. Usyk has already fought both men over 24 rounds each. Kabayel has spent the past two years earning the opportunity to show what he can do with twelve.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Offers to Fight Liam Paro Over Haney VADA Dispute
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia (26-2, 20 KOs, 1 NC) has stepped forward, offering Liam Paro a fight on four weeks’ notice if he pulls out of his December 19th welterweight unification clash against Devin Haney at the Chase Center.

Garcia posted on X today in response to IBF champion Paro (28-1, 16 KOs) talking about pulling out of his fight against Haney in San Francisco because of his stubborn and strange refusal to enroll in VADA testing.

“Liam Paro I will fight you with 4 weeks notice If you decide to pull out This man is up to no good,” Garcia said on X.

Ryan’s noble gesture gives Paro a fallback position if he decides he doesn’t want to take the risk of fighting Haney, whom he’d have no way of knowing is clean or dirty. In terms of money, Paro fighting Ryan would give him a shot at making more cash. The Australian PPV buys would likely be huge for a fight between Paro and Garcia.

If Haney loses his fight with Paro, he should be plenty concerned because it strengthens Ryan’s hand if he captures the IBF belt from the Australian fighter. Winning a second belt would place Ryan in a position where he could pick anyone he pleases and get the lion’s share of the loot. He wouldn’t need Haney.

Thus far, Haney (33-0, 15 KOs, 1 NC) and his dad, Bill, have given no signs of changing their minds about enrolling in VADA. I don’t know what led to this resistance to being tested. You can argue that when some fighters get popular, it changes them.

Bill made it clear that California State Athletic Commission urine testing is plenty and feels that it is too late for VADA testing despite there being almost a month to go before the fight. Ryan posted this in reaction today: “Devin scrambling for the Victor Conte formula as we speak. He needs to be watched asap as he calls all the people he can to figure it out. You are 4 weeks before the fight; there should be no reason you aren’t testing.”

The Testing Reversal Looks Suspicious

A couple of years ago, Garcia tested positive for Ostarine during a VADA test in April 2024 for his fight with Haney in Brooklyn. For years, the Haneys favored strict VADA enrollment from every opponent, including Devin’s last fight a year ago against Brian Norman Jr. in November 2025 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. For Haney to suddenly decide against VADA testing ahead of his bout against the dangerous southpaw, Paro, raises questions. Why now? That’s what Ryan is wondering about.

Paro Won’t Cave on Paperwork

On June 24, Paro won the IBF title with a 12-round unanimous decision over Lewis Crocker (22-1). Now holding the IBF belt, Paro has no reason to want to go into Haney’s hometown of San Francisco for drug testing that doesn’t include blood testing.

One positive for Haney is that if Paro does walk away over the drug testing issue, it enables Haney to hold onto his WBO belt without risk of losing it. So in theory, he can face Ryan while still holding that title and his unbeaten record. The downside is that his negotiating leverage would take a hit, placing him in a position where he would be facing the far more popular Ryan Garcia while holding just one title, and coming off of a 13-month layoff. Whatever status gain he got from his win over Norman Jr., he’ll have lost it due to sitting for ages and whiffing on fights against Paro and Shakur Stevenson.

If Haney stays on the December 19th card without Paro, he’d still need to find a quality opponent because that’s a DAZN PPV event. That network isn’t going to be happy if Haney finds a scrub as his opponent to keep him safe from losing his WBO belt. Bringing in a quality opponent on less than one month’s notice will put the ring-rusty Haney at risk of losing his strap, which is his golden ticket for a second fight against Ryan.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Says He Will Knock Out Roided Devin Haney
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia is going for the throat with Devin Haney, telling fans on X that he wants Haney to be loaded up on steroids, and it will not save him in their rematch.

WBO welterweight champion Haney is getting bashed by fans this week for refusing to enroll with VADA for his December 19th unification clash with IBF champion Liam Paro in San Francisco. Haney’s decision not to enroll for testing has made him a target for Ryan and fans, who see it as suspicious behavior.

With Ryan’s own history of testing positive for minute amounts of the banned PED Ostarine for his fight with Haney in 2024, he sees it as odd that Haney is not on board with testing for his fight with Paro.

It is a crucial fight for Haney, who needs a victory over the heavy-handed southpaw Paro to move ahead for a big-money rematch with Ryan. That is the one that Haney has been pining away for, bitter still over the memory of being dropped repeatedly by Ryan, arguably saved by the referee in round 7.

“I will KO DEVIN TILL HE CANT WALK ANYMORE EVEN IF HE WAS ON STEROIDS,” Garcia posted on X. “I want him to be so roided up, I want him to feel like he has power just so I can take it away. He is nothing.”

Haney Cannot Fix His Chin

From Ryan’s perspective, it does not matter how much work Haney (33-0-1 NC, 15 KOs) puts in with his training; he is still going to lack power at welterweight, and his habit of dropping his right hand when he jabs is going to make him vulnerable. Ryan took advantage of that flaw to drop him three times with his left hook in their fight in April 2024. Even if Haney does develop a little more power with his weight work, he is still going to need to be able to take Ryan’s left hooks when they land cleanly.

A fighter can build muscle by bulking up or improve their stamina, but there is nothing they can do to improve their punch resistance. Haney is not going to beat Ryan by staying on the outside, jabbing all night. That will not be enough to convince the judges he deserves the win if he is playing it safe, afraid to mix it up for fear of being hurt like he repeatedly was the last time he fought Ryan.

The December 19 Unification Hangover

Devin’s decision not to enroll in VADA for his December 19th unification fight at the Chase Center in San Francisco with Paro (28-1, 16 KOs) has put that fight in jeopardy. Paro has already said he will pull out unless Haney agrees to enroll in VADA. Haney’s dad, Bill, argues that the testing for PEDs is pointless due to there not being enough time.

If Paro pulls out, that would leave Haney with no fight and just his WBO belt. Realistically, he needs two titles to strengthen his position during negotiations with the more popular WBC champion Ryan Garcia. Without that extra belt, Haney is in a bad position trying to get a larger purse split. He would be lucky to be on the small end of a 75/25 split with Ryan without a second title. That is why he needs to be enrolling with VADA pronto so that he does not blow his deal with Paro.

Sports.title: Nobody in America Knows Fury vs. Joshua Is Happening
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are closing in on their Battle of Britain fight in 17 days in Cardiff, and the fight has generated next to no interest for their December 11th bout. For a mega-fight, it’s invisible. Chris Mannix and Sergio Mora put the spotlight on the nonexistent promotion. They mentioned that Netflix and the promoters have done nothing to sell the fight.

“This event needs some promotion,” Mannix said on his channel. “Like, have you seen anything promoting Fury vs Joshua?”

Mora echoed Mannix’s view that the fight’s marketing is nowhere to be found. His thoughts are that the fight should be getting a major promotional push, with it being mentioned everywhere.

“No, I have not. It’s not really being promoted the way it should be,” Mora said. “It should be a mega event. It should be everywhere, on every commercial. If it’s on Netflix, everywhere. I haven’t seen [that].”

Mannix pointed out the lack of visibility in the United States, and that the fight is scheduled for 2:00 AM for the ring walk in Wales to accommodate American prime time.

“Where is the AJ-Fury face-off? Where is that to go viral and build with millions of views to get people excited? The US audience has no idea this fight is happening. There’s nothing out there about this fight.”

The question is, would it even make a difference if there were a Fury vs. Joshua face-off? I don’t see this making a difference. Even if ESPN showed video clips of a face-off, how is that going to help if the fans view the fight as one between two past-their-best heavyweights, collecting a large paycheck in an overdue fight?

With the money Turki Alalshikh is paying Joshua and Fury, said to be $100 million each in guaranteed purses, it takes away the incentive to work hard promoting it. They’re already getting the cash from Turki in purses up front. Eddie Hearn, Frank Warren, Fury, and Joshua don’t need to labor through promoting the event because the money is already there. Why would they need to expend energy conducting daily interviews, flying here and there on a press tour when they’re already getting paid?

For Joshua and Fury, the last thing they want is to be placed in the hot seat, forced to answer questions about why they’ve looked poor in their fights over the last 3 to 7 years.

Fury (39-2-1, 25 KOs) being forced to answer why he chose to fight 46-year-old Mariusz Wach and Arslanbek Makhmudov rather than top contenders. In Joshua’s case, he’s being forced to explain why he didn’t try to avenge his loss to Daniel Dubois after being knocked out.

Getting dropped twice in round 1 by his tune-up opponent, Kristian Prenga, before pulling it out in round 2. It looks so bad how Joshua (30-4, 27 KOs) looked in that fight ahead of the Fury clash. That alone makes a clash against Fury a tough sell.

The undercard that is being packaged with the Joshua vs. Fury event looks like it was thrown together on the cheap, hoping fans wouldn’t notice or care to see. They actually do care. Using Martin Bakole as the replacement opponent after Jai Opetaia pulled out to fight 41-year-old Deontay Wilder hasn’t gone over well with fans. Netflix should have put their foot down and insisted on a quality opponent to be brought in to face Wilder. The rest of the undercard is useless fights that don’t belong on this card.

Sports.title: De La Hoya Wants WBA Rules Bent For Ryan Garcia vs Teofimo Lopez
Sports.content:
Oscar De La Hoya is trying to talk a Ryan Garcia vs. Teofimo Lopez unification into existence before the WBA has even cleared the paperwork.

Golden Boy wants the sanctioning body to shove mandatory challenger Jack Catterall aside for February so Lopez can bring his WBA welterweight belt into a bigger money fight. If the WBA refuses to budge, Lopez has to either defend against Catterall or drop the strap.

“A unification supersedes anything,” said De La Hoya on Brian Custer’s The Last Stand. De La Hoya claimed both fighters want the bout and named Las Vegas and Madison Square Garden as possible venues, speaking as though approval was already in the bag. WBA president Gilberto Mendoza poured cold water on that November 20 by confirming no special permit has been granted. Lopez’s manager, Keith Connolly, admitted the process is still dragging on.

Catterall Earned His Title Shot

Lopez (23-2, 13 KOs) inherited the Catterall obligation the second he squeezed past Rolly Romero by majority decision in August to grab the WBA title. Back in May in Giza, Egypt, Catterall dropped and outboxed unbeaten contender Shakhram Giyasov over twelve rounds to lock down the mandatory spot. That claim stayed glued to the belt when Lopez took it from Romero. Lopez tried to get out of the fight, only for the WBA to reaffirm the order on November 11.

Golden Boy is banking on WBA Rule C.39, which allows the organization to consider a special permit for a unification bout. Until the WBA actually signs off, Catterall holds an active order for his shot. Even De La Hoya admitted Catterall deserves the fight.

Why Lopez Needs The Belt

Going into a February 6 bout with Garcia (26-2, 21 KOs) without a title weakens Lopez’s hand at the negotiating table and leaves only Garcia’s WBC belt up for grabs. Garcia is riding high after winning the WBC strap from Mario Barrios in February and blowing away Conor Benn in two rounds in September. Facing Catterall first carries obvious danger for Lopez’s camp. Catterall is a slick southpaw who can stink out a fight and ruin a massive payday before Lopez ever gets near Garcia.

The WBA holding its ground does not kill the February 6 fight. Lopez can drop the belt, walk in as the challenger for Garcia’s WBC title, and let Golden Boy sell the event anyway. Only one belt would be at stake instead of two. If Lopez wants to keep his WBA title, he has to deal with Catterall first because the sanctioning body has already ordered that defense twice.

Sports.title: Andy Hiraoka Is the Right Test for Richardson Hitchins
Sports.content:
Richardson Hitchins says he is returning in February, though he still has no opponent. Zuffa Boxing should give him Andy Hiraoka. More than two years will have passed by then since Hitchins edged Liam Paro by split decision for the IBF light welterweight title. Zuffa paid for an unbeaten former champion. It needs to put him in with someone who can actually beat him.

“FEBUARY I’m Back !!!!” Hitchins posted on X without naming an opponent or a city. Dan Rafael reported in October that Zuffa was mapping out early 2027 dates for Hitchins after talks for a Keyshawn Davis bout stalled. Both Hitchins and Hiraoka used to campaign at light welterweight before moving up to 147 pounds. Hitchins already made his welterweight debut on July 26 against Ricardo Salas, while new Zuffa signee Hiraoka will be fighting at 147 for the first time in his promotional debut.

What Hiraoka Brings at 147

Hitchins stopped George Kambosos Jr. in eight rounds at 140 and swept every round on all three scorecards against Salas in New York. Those shutout scores against Salas show how cleanly Hitchins worked from the outside. They also skip over how frequently he clinched once Salas closed the gap. Hitchins grabbed, waited on the referee to break them, and went right back to his jab without taking much back.

Hiraoka (24-1, 19 KOs) makes those clinches harder to pull off. The southpaw works behind a sharp right jab and digs to the body on the way in. If Hiraoka keeps a hand free when Hitchins reaches to tie him up, Hitchins will spend the night resetting his feet instead of dictating the pace. Hiraoka will have to earn his entry, too. He is coming off a decision loss to Gary Antuanne Russell down at light welterweight in February, so a February 2027 date would show whether his power holds up in his welterweight debut.

Zuffa Needs a Real Answer

If Zuffa wants to book fights the way the UFC does, this matchup is sitting right in front of it. It has two welterweights under contract whose styles clash cleanly. Nobody outside the camp knows how much say Hitchins and his manager, Keith Connolly, have over opponents. If Hitchins has approval rights, passing on Hiraoka makes business sense for him. Keyshawn Davis brings a bigger name and a bigger payday for the risk. Hiraoka offers plenty of trouble inside the ropes without bringing half the attention.

Hitchins (21-0, 8 KOs) and the Salas fight already showed what happens when an opponent lets him stand on the outside and jab all night. Hiraoka won’t give him that kind of space. Putting them together in February is the quickest way for Zuffa to learn what happens when Hitchins gets pushed onto his heels for twelve rounds.

If Zuffa wants to know what Hitchins is really worth at 147, matching him against Hiraoka will give them an answer. Better to get that read now than waste another year protecting him.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Waited Ten Years To Share Schizophrenia Diagnosis
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury says doctors diagnosed him with schizophrenia after he beat Wladimir Klitschko in November 2015. He waited nearly ten years to mention it, saving the reveal for a Netflix documentary timed to his fight with Anthony Joshua. The film drops November 27, two weeks before Netflix streams Fury vs. Joshua live from Cardiff on December 11.

“Words can’t explain the darkness I was in,” said Fury in excerpts published by BBC Sport. Netflix tied the documentary directly to the Joshua bout in its October 29 announcement, putting the fight right in the headline. You don’t need to guess why the film is dropping now. Fury, 38, hasn’t explained publicly why he waited a full decade until the biggest fight and biggest purse of his career to share a diagnosis he skipped in earlier accounts.

What Fury Said About His 2016 Crisis

Fury was talking publicly about his mental health back in October 2016, less than a year after taking the unified heavyweight titles from Klitschko. He told Rolling Stone he was dealing with depression, drinking heavily and using cocaine. He also said he had been told he had a form of bipolar disorder.

He revisited that breakdown in his book Gloves Off. Fury wrote that doctors told him he had bipolar disorder, paranoia and anxiety. Schizophrenia never appeared in that version. In the Netflix film, Fury says he heard voices threatening him and his family, thought the radio was talking to him, and begged his wife Paris to get him out of a hospital in June 2016 because “the Illuminati” wanted him.

Fury went into that hospital with a suspected heart attack, which doctors diagnosed as an anxiety attack. He says a London psychiatrist later confirmed schizophrenia and bipolar disorder. According to the Los Angeles Times, Paris remembers the psychiatrist telling them Fury was “a mild schizophrenic.”

Fury says a 2017 Halloween night out in a skeleton costume served as his turning point before he returned to the ring and stopped Deontay Wilder in 2020. Everything in these excerpts still comes down to what Fury and his wife say happened, with no word from the doctor who saw him.

Netflix gets a fresh promotional hook heading into a December 11 heavyweight main event it is carrying live. The streamer already owns footage of Fury’s comeback and title runs. He left that diagnosis out of Rolling Stone and his own book for ten years, then brought it out right before the biggest payday of his career. None of that helps him with Joshua’s right hand in Cardiff.

Ghana News.title: Mahama to launch 5G network before year-end – Sam George
Ghana News.content:
(ADOBE STOCK)

Ghana is expected to join the league of countries with operational 5G networks before the end of this year, with consumers expected to start accessing the service in early 2027.

The Minister of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, gave the indication in Parliament during the debate on the 2027 Budget, saying President John Dramani Mahama would officially announce the launch of the network before the year ends.

He said the government had revised the 5G policy inherited from the previous administration, opening up the spectrum to wider participation and raising $240 million from its sale.

The revenue, he explained, came from spectrum in the 700 megahertz, 2.3 gigahertz and 3 gigahertz bands, with the proceeds accruing to the state.

Mr George said the revised approach was intended to make 5G access more inclusive while generating revenue for the taxpayer.

“We have sold the 5G spectrum, democratised it. We’ve raised $240 million for the Ghanaian taxpayer,” he told Parliament.

He contrasted the government's progress with the launch of the previous administration's 5G policy in November 2024, arguing that the announcement had not translated into a service available to consumers.

“November, this November, is exactly two years since the Akufo-Addo administration launched 5G. We are yet to see one 5G signal in this country,” he said.

The Minister expressed confidence that the new arrangements would pave the way for the network to become operational, with users expected to begin seeing 5G signals from the start of 2027.

“Before the end of this year, His Excellency President Mahama will announce the launch of 5G in Ghana. And by the start of next year, you will see the 5G signal,” he said.

Ghana News.title: FDA targets WHO Listed Authority status as it marks 30th anniversary
Ghana News.content:
The Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) is working towards attaining World Health Organisation (WHO) Listed Authority status as part of efforts to strengthen Ghana’s position in global health regulation.

Chief Executive Officer of the FDA, Professor Kwabena Frimpong-Manso Opuni, announced the ambition at the launch of the Authority’s 30th anniversary celebrations in Accra on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

He said the Authority was taking steps to secure the recognition, which would further strengthen its standing among regulatory institutions meeting internationally recognised standards.

“Our ambition is not simply to be an effective national regulator, but to be a trusted regulatory partner and a centre of excellence that contributes meaningfully to public health protection across Africa,” he said.

The ambition builds on progress made by the FDA in strengthening its regulatory systems over the past three decades.

The Authority attained WHO Maturity Level Three status in 2020, which was successfully re-benchmarked in January 2025. Its clinical trials and pharmacovigilance functions have also attained WHO Maturity Level Four.

The FDA’s laboratory is accredited for 63 tests, while the Authority has been designated a Regional Centre of Excellence by the African Medicines Regulatory Harmonisation initiative, enabling it to support the training of regulators across the continent.

FDA prepares for changing regulatory environment

Professor Opuni said the next phase of the Authority’s development would require it to respond to an increasingly complex regulatory environment.

He cited advances in medicines and therapies, artificial intelligence, digital health solutions and increasingly complex global supply chains as developments requiring stronger regulatory systems.

“We must therefore ensure that the FDA does not simply preserve its achievements, but builds on them to become a more responsive, innovative, efficient, and globally respected regulatory institution,” he said.

A new strategic plan covering 2026 to 2030 is expected to guide the transition, with priorities including digital regulation, modern infrastructure, staff development and stronger partnerships.

Support for local pharmaceutical manufacturing

The FDA also plans to strengthen its support for local pharmaceutical manufacturing as government pursues a target of producing 70 per cent of the country’s pharmaceutical needs locally.

Professor Opuni said the Authority would provide the regulatory framework needed to support the growth of domestic pharmaceutical production.

As it marks 30 years of operations, the FDA says maintaining public confidence will require cooperation among manufacturers, distributors, importers, health professionals and consumers.

Ghana News.title: Government assures Food and Drugs Authority of technical independence and support
Ghana News.content:
The government has assured the Food and Drugs Authority (FDA) of its commitment to protecting the institution’s technical independence, saying its regulatory decisions must remain free from external interference.

Chief Director of the Ministry of Health, Desmond Boateng, gave the assurance on behalf of Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh at the launch of the FDA’s 30th anniversary celebrations.

He said government would provide the Authority with the support and resources needed to strengthen its regulatory capacity.

Mr Boateng said the FDA’s independence was essential to ensuring that decisions on the safety and quality of regulated products were guided by scientific evidence, public safety and the national interest.

“As a government, we guarantee the FDA absolute technical independence in this endeavour. A trusted regulator is one whose decisions are guided solely by public safety and the national interest, free from external interference,” he said.

The minister’s address also raised concerns about the circulation of illicit, counterfeit, substandard, falsified and unregistered products on the Ghanaian market.

He warned that such products posed a serious threat to public health and could undermine the quality of healthcare.

“The proliferation of illicit and fake products on our markets poses a direct lethal threat to unsuspecting citizens and undermines our clinical care outcomes,” he said.

FDA urged to strengthen surveillance and enforcement

Mr Boateng identified the growing use of social media and e-commerce platforms to market unapproved and expired products as a major regulatory challenge.

He said the trend was creating gaps in oversight and exposing consumers, particularly young people, to potentially unsafe products.

He therefore urged the FDA to intensify market surveillance, strengthen controls at ports and borders, expand laboratory testing and enforce sanctions under the Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851).

He also called for the adoption of modern tracking systems and digital platforms to monitor products across supply chains and help verify their authenticity.

The government’s assurance comes as the FDA marks 30 years of regulating the safety and quality of products under its mandate.

Ghana News.title: Thomas Markle charged in US on second count of possessing child sexual abuse material
Ghana News.content:
Thomas Markle, the estranged father of ‌Britain's Duchess of Sussex, Meghan Markle, and father-in-law of Britain's Prince Harry, was indicted on Tuesday in US federal court on two counts of possessing child sexual abuse material.

The indictment doubles the number of federal charges currently lodged in Los Angeles against the 82-year-old ​Markle in a case that grew out of an investigation initiated last month in the Philippines, where ​he previously resided.

The elder Markle was originally charged on November 5 in a criminal complaint with ⁠a single felony count of possessing child sexual abuse images.

According to an FBI affidavit filed with the complaint, ​the material in question was found in two Los Angeles storage units and included two explicit photos of Markle posed ​with a naked underage girl and other images of him with children in various stages of undress.

One of the photos showed a naked girl in a room that appeared to be part of a motel chain in the Philippines, the affidavit said.

Philippine police said last ​week criminal complaints had been filed against Markle in the country’s Cebu province, where he once lived, accusing him ​of violating local laws against online sexual abuse and exploitation of children.

Markle has denied the allegations, telling the Daily Mail the ‌claims were ⁠untrue and describing them as "sick lies."

He was arrested on November 6 at a Florida assisted-living facility where he has been a patient, and is expected to be transferred to California in the coming weeks to be arraigned in US District Court in Los Angeles on the two-count grand jury indictment returned on Tuesday.

Following a court-ordered psychiatric evaluation of ​Markle, a US magistrate judge ​in Tampa, Florida, last ⁠week ruled that he was mentally competent to stand trial, meaning that he understood the proceedings against him and could assist in his own defence.

Each count of possession of child ​sexual abuse material, an offence referred to in the US criminal code as possession ​of child pornography, ⁠is punishable by up to 20 years in prison if he is convicted, the US attorney's statement said.

Meghan Markle, an American actor, has been estranged from her father since the run-up to her marriage to King Charles' younger son, Harry, ⁠in 2018, ​when the Duchess said she first became aware of allegations ​against her father. She has said she was "deeply distressed" over the matter, which led her to cut off contact between her father and her ​two children, Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5.

Ghana News.title: US House Democrats expand probe into Trump Jr.’s investments
Ghana News.content:
US House Democrats probing Donald Trump Jr.'s business dealings have sought records ‌from prediction market firm Polymarket, vaping company Juul and two other companies tied to 1789 Capital, the venture capital firm where the president's son is a partner.

In letters published on Tuesday, US Representative Jamie Raskin, a Maryland Democrat expected to chair the House Judiciary Committee next year, asked the companies — which also include GrabAGun and Hadrian Automation — for a range of records of communications with 1789 Capital and its executives.

Jumpstart your morning with the latest legal news delivered straight to your inbox from The Daily Docket newsletter. Sign up here.

"The ​probe examines whether the President’s son and his business partners helped steer federal contracts or regulatory decisions to companies in which they had a significant financial ​interest or used advance knowledge of those forthcoming decisions to make investments and profit," Raskin's office wrote in a press release. Raskin opened ⁠the probe in August.

Democrats, who take control of Congress in January, are preparing a flurry of investigations into Republican President Donald Trump and his administration, from contracts and potential conflicts ​of interest, to immigration and the investigation into the late financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

1789 Capital President Omeed Malik and Trump Jr. denied any wrongdoing at an Axios event ​last week.

“We responded to Congressman Raskin back in September, pointing out in detail the many flaws in his understanding of how 1789 has operated and a number of basic factual errors," Bill Burck, an attorney representing 1789 Capital, said in a statement. "These are personal attacks untethered to actual evidence."

Juul said it intended "to cooperate with any Congressional effort to understand our company."

A representative for online gun retailer GrabAGun said: "Congressman Raskin's ​letter is a political document, and its allegations are baseless."

Representatives for Trump Jr., Polymarket and Hadrian Automation did not immediately return requests for comment.

In a move legal experts say will ​likely face challenges, President Donald Trump sought on Friday to curb cooperation between the private sector and Congress, ordering companies with federal contracts to alert the White House before sharing information with lawmakers, and ‌to withhold ⁠material deemed confidential.

Under the US Constitution, Congress has oversight powers and authority to obtain information, including via subpoenas that the administration has sought to limit in scope.

RASKIN HIGHLIGHTS TIMING OF INVESTMENTS

Raskin's expanded investigation focuses on how the four companies "benefited, or stand to benefit," from Trump administration contracts, regulatory decisions or proposed rule changes, which Raskin said could point to conflicts of interest or other misconduct.

In his letter to Polymarket, Raskin said that the company had effectively been banned from the US and was also under federal investigation before Trump returned to office.

In ​July 2025, regulators closed that probe and approved ​Polymarket's acquisition of a US platform ⁠that paved the way for it to re-enter the US market. The following month, Polymarket disclosed that 1789 Capital had made a strategic investment, Raskin wrote. Reuters and other outlets reported at the time that the investment was worth tens of millions of dollars.

Reuters reported last month that ​the Commodity Futures Trading Commission has reopened its probe into Polymarket.

Raskin also said that in July 2025, months after 1789 Capital ​made a $5 million investment in ⁠Juul, authorities eased restrictions on sales of some Juul products, with more authorised earlier this year.

GrabAGun went public in 2025 after merging with a special-purpose acquisition company backed by Malik. In May 2026, the Trump administration proposed rules to make it easier to direct-ship guns to customers, Raskin also said.

The GrabAGun representative said the proposed rule changes were well known across the industry and that ⁠the company ​only provided input through the public comment process.

Raskin also wrote to Hadrian Automation, saying that the manufacturing company ​won US government contracts worth nearly $1 billion shortly after 1789 Capital acquired a stake in the company.

Raskin said that the president himself has publicly acknowledged the business conflicts, telling CNBC in July: "I feel badly in a way ​for my kids ... Almost anything they do ... they have inside information."

Ghana News.title: Years of investment at risk as GTEC freezes PhD programme accreditation – UTAG-UG
Ghana News.content:
Dr Jerry Joe Harrison, President UTAG-UG

The President of the University of Ghana branch of the University Teachers Association of Ghana (UTAG-UG) has warned that years of investment in developing new doctoral programmes could go to waste after the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) issued a directive.

Dr Jerry Joe Harrison argues that suspending accreditation for new PhD programmes could undermine universities' efforts to build local expertise, reduce dependence on foreign training, and address Ghana’s shortage of highly skilled professionals.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, Dr Harrison described the decision as the wrong way to address concerns about the quality of doctoral education in the country.

GTEC’s directive initially raised concerns about a possible suspension of admissions into PhD programmes. The Commission later clarified that the directive applies to accrediting new programmes, not to admissions into existing accredited programmes.

However, Dr Harrison maintains that the clarification does little to address the broader implications for universities that have committed substantial resources to developing new programmes.

“Accreditation is not an instantaneous something; it's a process.”

He explained that some institutions had spent years preparing documentation, undergoing inspections and establishing partnerships with foreign institutions in anticipation of accreditation.

“Sometimes you have foreign partners you are working with and all that. The cost involved. Who bears that? And I think that that's the wrong approach.”

Dr Harrison also raised concerns about programmes awaiting reaccreditation and the potential implications for students already enrolled.

“What happens to the programs that are currently in the process of being accredited? So the program is there, but it's due for reaccreditation. What happens to those? What happens to students who are in those programs?”

He warned that the decision could frustrate efforts to build expertise in critical areas where Ghana still depends on foreign institutions.

“As a country, Ghana doesn't have enough PhD holders. Let's be frank. Look, we spend so much money training people abroad.”

He cited aerospace engineering as an example of a specialised field in which universities could spend three to four years building capacity before seeking accreditation.

Dr Harrison argued that rather than imposing a blanket suspension, GTEC should strengthen its regulatory mechanisms and sanction institutions found to have violated accreditation requirements.

“GTEC has every power to visit there to withdraw the accreditation if they've actually violated the rules.”

He insisted that universities committed to meeting regulatory standards should not bear the consequences of other institutions' violations.

“I think that we can make sure that quality is delivered without unnecessarily burdening, you know, people and creating this kind of inconvenience.

“I think that this is just the wrong approach to trying to address a problem that GTEC has identified.”

Ghana News.title: Government to recruit 10,000 more health workers next week – Akandoh
Ghana News.content:
The government is set to add 10,000 health professionals to the public health workforce within the next week, a move that will take the number of recruits under the current administration to more than 18,000.

Health Minister, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, announced this in Parliament during the debate on the 2027 Budget, saying the latest exercise would cover different professional categories across the health sector.

He said about 8,600 health workers had already been recruited between 2025 and 2026, with the new intake expected to significantly increase the number employed by the government.

Mr Akandoh challenged critics to identify any previous administration that had recruited more than 18,000 health professionals within a period of less than two years.

“In the next one week, we are going to recruit 10,000 health professionals again. I dare any of them to tell me that any government in the history of Ghana has recruited more than 18,000 health professionals in less than two years,” he said.

The Minister also disclosed that the Ministries of Health and Finance had put in place an arrangement to facilitate the immediate employment of medical doctors after their housemanship.

Under the new arrangement, doctors completing their mandatory housemanship would move directly into public-sector employment instead of remaining at home for an extended period while waiting for recruitment.

“You no longer have to wait at home before you are recruited. There is a smooth transition, and that is exactly what we are doing at the moment,” he said.

Mr Akandoh said the government had inherited a backlog of more than 100,000 unemployed health professionals, a situation he said had placed pressure on the country’s healthcare workforce.

Among them were 13,500 nurses and midwives who, although recruited, had not been placed on the government payroll.

He said those workers had since been enrolled on the payroll and their outstanding salary arrears fully paid.

Ghana News.title: Yoro red card overturned, but refs’ chief Webb backs decision
Ghana News.content:
Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card shown to him at Anfield overturned by the Football Association - even though referees' chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send the defender off.

Yoro was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott for bringing down Liverpool forward Alexander Isak just eight minutes into Sunday's match.

Isak had run onto a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch that meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if Yoro had not brought down the Swede.

New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at a decision he felt had changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0.

"The ball wasn't in his control," he said. "Isak, when he saw the control wasn't good, it's normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.

"But all that we play football; you know that wasn't intentional. That is never a foul."

The FA backed that view, meaning Yoro will be clear to face Brentford in the Premier League at Old Trafford on Saturday.

However, in the latest edition of Mic'd Up on Sky Sports, Webb said Barrott got it right.

"I think, by and large, most people would see that as a correct decision, with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball," he said.

How can a decision be both right and wrong

By Dale Johnson, Football issues correspondent

How on earth can the head of referees say a decision was right, but the FA say it was wrong?

"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable," Webb said. "Certainly not clearly wrong."

Not clearly and obviously wrong for a VAR intervention, but clearly and obviously wrong for the FA to rescind the red card.

You wonder how the general fan is supposed to understand it all.

The FA's appeals process is notoriously difficult to predict, especially on highly borderline situations like Yoro.

A commission features three people, usually former players though sometimes there is a retired official is on the panel.

A simple majority is needed, so a club just needs two people to agree with them.

It's why clubs might appeal against red cards when it seems impossible to win, you just never know.

Such was the split of opinion on Yoro, United always stood a chance of at least getting those key two votes.

And this is the crux of appeals process. An FA commission is just the subjective opinion of three people.

Do the appeal again tomorrow with three different panel members, and United might lose.

This is why Pro Ref don't use the outcome of FA appeals to determine how games are officiated.

Two years ago, Brentford's Christian Norgaard won an appeal against a red card at Everton. That was a split 2:1 vote, but enough to say a decision was wrong.

Pro Ref told its referees not to alter their interpretation based on this vote.

Let's throw in another one. The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel.

Earlier this season, Brighton appealed against Pascal Struijk's VAR red card at Sunderland.

An FA commission upheld the appeal, but in contradiction the KMI Panel voted the VAR intervention was correct.

Make it make sense, supporters might ask.

This will forever be the problem with officiating, and indeed any hope of true consistency with VAR.

Was Yoro's red card right or wrong? On which side of the fence will the KMI Panel fall?

Football is just a floating mass of subjectivity. Of referees, of VARs, of panel members and of fans. It just depends whose opinion you ask.

Sporting boss Fonseca dismisses Man Utd fragile talk

Sporting coach Paulo Fonseca speaks to the media ahead of the Champions League clash with Manchester United

United have travelled to Lisbon for their next Champions League match on Wednesday (20:00 GMT).

The early dismissal of Yoro at Anfield meant Sporting had no chance to assess any changes Pochettino might have made after he replaced Michael Carrick during the international break.

But despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Sporting boss refuses to accept United are "fragile".

"I don't following the reasoning," said Fonseca, who was only appointed on 4 November after the Portuguese club bought him out of his contract at Lyon.

"Manchester is a great team," he said. "I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile. In their last Champions League game, they trailed 2-0, then won 3-2 against a very difficult opponent in Roma.

"Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day."

United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their past six games in all competitions.

Yet, such was the nature of the Liverpool game, Fonseca has had to watch analysis of Pochettino's time in charge of the United States to get an idea of what to expect.

"Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," he said.

"I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict."

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Kilmar Abrego Garcia self-deports to Spain after lengthy US legal battle
World.content:
Share Kilmar Abrego Garcia self-deports to Spain after lengthy US legal battle on social media

Kilmar Abrego Garcia, who was wrongfully deported to El Salvador last year as part of United States President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown, has self-deported to Spain.

Abrego Garcia, a Salvadoran national, voluntarily departed on Tuesday after months of legal opposition to a second deportation, this time to one of various African countries proposed by Department of Homeland Security officials.

A judge told Abrego Garcia to self-deport on Tuesday, The Associated Press reported, citing a source familiar with the matter.

US Senator Chris Van Hollen, who met with Abrego Garcia while pressing for his release from Salvadoran mega-prison CECOT, said Abrego Garcia is “traveling to a country of his choice, a free man”.

“I am relieved that he will be safe, in a country of his choosing, and free – including from this Administration’s constant persecution,” Van Hollen, who is vying for Senate majority leader, said in a statement posted on X.

Salvadoran prison

Abrego Garcia, 31, was arrested in Baltimore in March 2025 and deported to a Salvadoran prison notorious for abusive conditions and alleged use of torture.

The Trump administration, at the time, described Abrego Garcia’s deportation as an “administrative error”. However, the administration initially refused to seek his return, arguing that Abrego Garcia was a member of the MS-13 gang despite having no criminal record at the time of his removal.

In June 2025, the Trump administration brought him back after facing public pressure and a court order, but only after securing an indictment charging him with human smuggling in Tennessee.



The Tennessee case was dismissed by a federal judge in May, though the government appealed it in August.

Abrego Garcia had said that if he must be deported, he would prefer to be sent to Costa Rica, but Todd Lyons, the former acting director of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), said that deporting him to Costa Rica would be “prejudicial to the United States” in a March 2026 memo.

Lyons wrote that Abrego Garcia should be sent to Liberia because the US has spent government resources and political capital negotiating for it to accept third-country nationals.

The memo came despite a US agreement with Costa Rica to accept deportees who cannot legally be returned to their home countries.

Abrego Garcia has lived in Maryland for years, but he immigrated to the US illegally as a teenager.

In 2019, an immigration judge issued an order saying that he could not be deported to El Salvador because he faced danger there from a gang that had threatened his family.

The judge allowed him to live and work in the US under ICE supervision, but he was not given residency status.

World.title: WHO chief urges end to US fuel blockade on Cuba
World.content:
Share WHO chief urges end to US fuel blockade on Cuba on social media

World Health ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus has called for the lifting of a US fuel blockade on Cuba, as shortages dent the island’s once vaunted healthcare system.

Tedros warned that the sanctions were endangering the lives of children on Tuesday, during a ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠visit to Cuba that included tours of several healthcare facilities in Havana.

“The intensification ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠of fuel restrictions and sanctions is causing direct harm to the Cuban people, especially the most vulnerable,” Tedros said.

During his three-day visit, the United Nations health agency’s top official said his organisation would contribute $2m to help strengthen Cuba’s ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌national immunisation programme and provide essential medical equipment to healthcare facilities.

The UN has repeatedly warned of a growing humanitarian crisis on the island, calling the US blockade a violation of international law and the human rights of all Cubans.

Cuba’s government says the measures ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠led to daily power outages lasting 20 hours ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠or more, critical shortages of medicines and surgical supplies, and a decline in health indicators, such as infant mortality rates.

Tedros met with Cuba’s President Miguel Diaz-Canel on Tuesday to discuss the country’s health needs.

“We agreed on the need to prioritise essential health services and time-sensitive interventions, particularly for children,” Tedros wrote in a post on X.

“Fuel restrictions and sanctions affecting the purchase of medical products are severely impacting the health system that Cuban doctors have built over decades.”

Falling life expectancy

Tedros said during a news conference that Cuba’s life expectancy had fallen from 78.8 years in 2020 to 74.4 years in 2025, the first decline since records began in 1950.



The 2025 figures predate the imposition by the administration of US President Donald Trump of a fuel blockade and stiff sanctions against a ‌number of Cuban officials and entities in January.

Washington argues the energy blockade is intended to push for ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠political change on the island and says that exports of food and medicine are subject ⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠to legal exemptions.

An annual non-binding resolution calling for an end to a US embargo on the island has ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌passed ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌in favour of Cuba in the UN General Assembly by wide margins every year since 1992.

World.title: Israel’s Eisenkot secures first coalition partner in bid to form government
World.content:
The Yashar party says it agreed to sign a coalition pact with Israel’s Our Home party, led by Avigdor Lieberman.

Share Israel’s Eisenkot secures first coalition partner in bid to form government on social media

Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party has announced an agreement to unite with a right-wing opposition party in a bid to form the next Israeli government following October’s elections.

The Yashar party said on Tuesday that it agreed to sign a coalition pact with Israel’s Our Home party after a meeting with its leader Avigdor Lieberman, the first alliance of its kind since the election.

After no party managed to secure a 61-seat majority, Israel’s parliament was sworn in on November 10 without a new government.

President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming ⁠a government, while Benjamin Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister despite the October 27 election stripping Netanyahu of his majority.

Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government under a 28-day mandate, though he could ask for a 14-day extension. If Eisenkot fails, Netanyahu would have an opportunity to do so. If no one is able to form a government, another election will be held next year.

Arab parties

The agreement between Eisenkot, whose party won 21 parliament seats, and Lieberman, whose party won seven, was unforeseen since Lieberman has been vocal about his opposition to forming a government with support from Arab parties as well as to a unity government with Netanyahu.

Lieberman had once served as foreign minister under a previous Netanyahu government but has since become a strong critic.

Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud’s alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties outperformed election expectations but still lost its majority. It now holds 53 of the Knesset’s 120 seats.



Eisenkot’s centre-right Yashar party and patchwork coalition partners, including Lieberman, hold just 48 seats. But they have potential allies in the parties representing Israel’s Arab minority, which hold 19 seats and ⁠are aligned with Eisenkot in their vehement opposition to Netanyahu.

The path forward

Talks are also ongoing between Eisenkot, some of his “change bloc” partners and Likud on forming a unity government.

The left-wing Democrats party, which won eight parliament seats, separately said it was suspending talks with Eisenkot after the Yashar party leader’s talks with Netanyahu’s Likud on a possible unity government.

Yair Golan, head of the Democrats, said he prefers a government without Netanyahu but with Arab parties.
