Mr Yusuf was elected governor in March 2023 on the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP) platform, defeating Nasiru Gawuna of the APC.

However, the Kano State Governorship Election Petition Tribunal nullified his election, a decision the Court of Appeal later upheld.

On 12 January 2024, the Supreme Court reversed the decisions of the two lower courts and affirmed Mr Yusuf’s election.

The governor remained in the NNPP until January 2026, when he defected to the APC, ending his longstanding political alliance with Mr Kwankwaso.

The latest controversy comes less than two months before the presidential election scheduled for 16 January 2027, in which Mr Tinubu is seeking a second term while Mr Kwankwaso is contesting on the NDC ticket alongside Mr Obi.

World.title: Bellingham beauty in Real Madrid win; Arsenal, Man City held in Champions League
World.content:
Real Madrid’s English midfielder Jude Bellingham shoots during the UEFA Champions League first round day 5 football match between Real Madrid CF and PSV Eindhoven at the Santiago Bernabeu Stadium in Madrid on November 24, 2026. Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP.

Jude Bellingham scored one of the goals of the season as Real Madrid hammered PSV Eindhoven 5-1 on Tuesday to maintain their perfect record in this season’s Champions League, while Arsenal and Manchester City were both held to draws at home.

Elsewhere, debutants Como and Real Betis continued their excellent form since the start of the league phase, but Aston Villa slumped to another defeat on their travels.

Record 15-time European champions Real had to come from behind to beat PSV at the Bernabeu as they made it five wins from five in this season’s league phase to go clear at the top of the standings with 15 points.

Dutch champions PSV led at half-time courtesy of an Ivan Perisic penalty, but Federico Valverde equalised five minutes after the restart.

Bellingham then put Real ahead on the hour with a remarkable strike, as he controlled a Kylian Mbappe lay-off outside the box and then teed himself up for a sweet volley on the outside of his right boot which flew into the corner of the net.

Mbappe then scored twice to move to 19 goals in all competitions this season and 76 career Champions League goals. The France captain now has 105 Real Madrid goals, one more than the Brazilian Ronaldo managed for the club.

Vinicius Junior sealed the win for Jose Mourinho’s side, who have now claimed 10 consecutive victories in all competitions.

“That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and then I just hit it. I thought I would go with the outside of the boot a little bit, stab it a little bit, I am not one for smashing the ball too hard. It was a nice moment,” England star Bellingham told British broadcaster TNT Sports about his goal.

Reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain can join Real at the top of the standings if they beat Roma on Wednesday, but Como and Betis are currently level with the French side on 12 points after they beat AEK Athens and Slovan Bratislava respectively.

Como and Betis flying

Luis Milla scored as Como beat AEK 1-0 in Italy after Lucas Da Cunha earlier squandered a penalty, while Cucho Hernandez grabbed both goals for Betis in their 2-0 victory in Slovakia.

Arsenal had to settle for a point after drawing 1-1 with Borussia Dortmund at the Emirates Stadium, as Viktor Gyokeres put the Gunners ahead but later missed a golden chance to win the game.

Gyokeres opened the scoring with a thunderous strike, but Maximilian Beier equalised for Dortmund and the Arsenal striker headed woefully wide from Martin Odegaard’s cross late on.

It is the second time Arsenal, last season’s beaten finalists, have dropped points to German opposition this season following a 2-2 draw at Bayern Munich.

Manchester City are in the midst of a poor run of form in the Premier League and Enzo Maresca’s side had to come from behind twice in the second half to draw 2-2 against Napoli.

Rasmus Hojlund, formerly of Manchester United, gave the Italians the lead early in the second half only for Ayyoub Bouaddi to equalise.

Kevin De Bruyne was returning to face his former side and he saw his Napoli team retake the lead through Noa Lang in the 76th minute, but Rayan Cherki’s fine late goal earned City a point.

City won 10 of their first 11 games this season under Maresca. But the wheels have come off in the wake of the club being found guilty of widespread breaches of Premier League financial rules.

Aston Villa lose

“We don’t like these moments – we want to win games – but unfortunately this moment is like this,” said Maresca, ahead of a trip to Premier League champions Arsenal on Sunday.

None of the Premier League’s representatives in the competition won on Tuesday, with Villa losing 1-0 to Galatasaray in Istanbul as Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game late on. The two clubs are now level on nine points in the standings.

Portuguese champions Porto won 1-0 at Feyenoord thanks to Oussama Targhalline’s early own-goal, while Antonio Nusa netted twice as RB Leipzig beat Lens 3-1 — that was a fourth straight Champions League loss for the French team.

A stoppage-time own-goal gave Bodo/Glimt a 1-0 victory against Austria’s LASK in Norway.

World.title: Tinubu seeks reduction of 2026 budget to N65.176trn; Senate approves N10.79trn loan
World.content:
President Tinubu

By Henry Umoru

ABUJA—THE Senate has begun a repeal and re-enactment of the 2026 budget, with President Bola Tinubu presenting a proposal to reduce government expenditure and realign the appropriation with available resources and existing obligations.

With the Senate fast-tracking the consideration of the President’s revised 2026 Appropriation Bill, it then scaled second reading in the Senate which approved an additional N10.79 trillion external borrowing to finance the budget deficit.

The revised appropriation proposal reduces the 2026 budget from the N68.3 trillion originally approved by the National Assembly to N66.1 trillion, while retaining the N31.4 trillion deficit and the N29.2 trillion borrowing plan.

The revised proposal, tagged “ Transmission of FGN 2026 Appropriation Repeal and Enactment bill and Revised 2026 Federal Government Fiscal Framework “ was presented by the President of the Senate, Godswill Akpabio.

He said the proposal aligned with the 2026 budget in terms of existing obligations and available resources.

According to Tinubu, under the revised framework, aggregate expenditure is projected at N65.176 trillion, compared with N68.3 trillion in the approved budget.

Other highlights, as stated by the President in the request, include the fact that projected federal government revenue, including revenue from government-owned enterprises, stands at N33.7 trillion, while aggregate capital expenditure is N26.2 trillion.

Tinubu, who noted that the fiscal deficit remained unchanged at N31.4 trillion, equivalent to 5.6 per cent of GDP, said: These adjustments prioritise existing commitments and improve the credibility and execution of the capital budget while maintaining fiscal discipline.

“Planned new borrowing also remains at N29.2 trillion, comprising N18.4 trillion in domestic borrowing and N10.7 trillion in foreign borrowing.

“The proposed $7.7 billion in external borrowing, equivalent to approximately N10.3 trillion at an exchange rate of N1,346.5 to one US dollar, is intended to finance existing foreign borrowing provisions and does not increase the borrowing envelope.’’

He said the adjustments were intended to prioritise existing commitments, strengthen the credibility of the budget and improve capital budget implementation, while maintaining fiscal discipline.

The president’s request read: “The proposal aligns the 2026 budget with existing obligations and available resources. It regularises some NNPCL expenditures incurred on behalf of the federation, addresses under-provided debt service obligations, recognises issued capital warrants and supplementation commitments, and provides for reforms to ministries, departments and agencies and social accounts.’’

To quicken the process, the Upper Chamber temporarily suspended its rules, considered the presidential request and after scaling second reading, it was referred to the Committee on Appropriations, led by Senator Olamilekan Adeola, APC, Ogun West.

The Senate subsequently adjourned plenary until December 1 to enable the committee complete its work and present its report.

In his remarks, the Senate president, Godswill Akpabio, urged senators, particularly members of the appropriations committee, to suspend their campaign activities and concentrate on the urgent legislative assignment.

The decision was sequel to a motion by the Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, APC, Ekiti Central, who sought the cooperation of his colleagues for the accelerated consideration of the presidential request after a closed-door session lasting about 30 minutes.

Bamidele argued that the urgency of the revised budget required expeditious legislative action to enable the federal government address outstanding fiscal obligations and implement the appropriation before the expiration of the 2026 financial year on December 31.

In his lead debate on the revised budget, Bamidele said revision provided an opportunity to strengthen budget credibility by prioritising ongoing projects, setting legitimate outstanding obligations, and avoiding the proliferation of new projects at the expense of existing commitments.

“ I strongly believe that completing existing projects will provide greater economic value than continually commencing new ones without guaranteeing their completion,’’ he said.

Supporting the bill, Chairman of the Senate Committee on Appropriations, Solomon Adeola, said the proposed review was an effort to reposition the budget to make it more effective and efficient.

He assured the Senate that his committee would submit its report within one week, prompting Akpabio to consider suspending plenary to enable the 73-member committee concentrate on the assignment.

Senator Garba Maidoki, who supported the review, appealed for adequate funding of constituency projects and ongoing infrastructure interventions in rural communities.

World.title: 2027 Elections: NUC to shut varsities for 4 weeks, mobilises VCs for INEC
World.content:
By Joseph Erunke

ABUJA — The National Universities Commission, NUC, is considering a three-to-four-week adjustment of academic calendars across Nigerian universities to enable academics participate in the conduct of the 2027 general elections.

The move is part of a broader strategy by the commission to mobilise vice-chancellors and university authorities nationwide to provide credible, non-partisan academic personnel for the elections, particularly as Collation and Returning Officers.

NUC Executive Secretary, Prof. Abdullahi Yusufu Ribadu, disclosed this in Abuja when the Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, led a delegation of national commissioners and senior officials on a courtesy visit to the commission Monday.

Ribadu said the NUC would engage vice-chancellors on the nomination of qualified academics for electoral assignments, adding that an online meeting would be convened to facilitate the process.

He also pledged to issue a formal circular to universities upon receiving an official request from INEC.

While stressing that the credibility of the 2027 elections would depend significantly on the integrity of personnel deployed to conduct them, Ribadu said: “Since we want to have credible elections, we also have to have credible personnel.’’

The NUC boss said the proposed adjustment of academic calendars would provide sufficient room for academics to discharge their electoral responsibilities without compromising students’ academic programmes.

According to him, the proposed break will not exceed four weeks, while the commission will consult university administrators to ensure that the arrangement does not disrupt academic activities or interfere with INEC’s electoral timetable.

“We will discuss with the vice-chancellors and have their calendars tweaked in such a way that it will not affect the elections, nor will it affect the studies of the students,” he sai

Ribadu further insisted that academics and other ad hoc officials engaged in the electoral process must demonstrate absolute neutrality, proposing that they be made to take an oath of neutrality before deployment.

Beyond providing election officials, the NUC executive secretary proposed a broader institutional partnership between universities and INEC, including student internship opportunities at the electoral commission, joint research initiatives and possible academic programmes in electoral studies.

Earlier in his remarks, INEC Chairman, Prof. Amupitan, said the visit was aimed at strengthening the existing partnership between the electoral commission and Nigerian universities, ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He acknowledged the critical role universities had played in previous elections, particularly through the deployment of vice-chancellors and other senior academics as Collation and Returning Officers.

Amupitan, however, said INEC was introducing far-reaching technological, operational and security reforms to strengthen the electoral process and guarantee the safety of academics and other personnel engaged in election duties.

On technological improvements, he disclosed that polling unit results recorded on Form EC8A would undergo automated arithmetic consistency and over-voting checks before transmission to INEC Result Viewing Portal, IReV.

He also announced the procurement of 57,000 additional Bimodal Voter Accreditation System, BVAS, machines, a development he said would reduce the voter-to-device ratio to 850 voters per machine.

On the security of electoral personnel, Amupitan disclosed that the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security, ICCES, had been decentralised to Local Government Areas and Registration Areas to strengthen security coordination at the grassroots.

He said dedicated security cordons and escort arrangements would also be provided around collation centres to protect election officials from intimidation and attacks.

The INEC chairman further cited provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 criminalising violence, abusive rhetoric and threats against electoral personnel, stressing that the commission had the powers to prosecute offenders.

“No Returning Officer or Collation Officer will be left to stand alone against lawlessness,” he assured.

World.title: Dear Bunmi, should I tell him his wife is sleeping with my husband?
World.content:
AI-generated image.

Dear Bunmi, my husband of almost 25 years had been having an affair with a married woman. And he was reluctant to let go, even after years of pleading with him to.

In the end, I decided I’d had enough.

The kids had left home and I didn’t need him any more, as he was a sort of irritant.

As you can imagine, I’m very angry at the other woman. I don’t know whether she’s still sleeping with my ex-husband, but I do know that her husband has no idea.

Dear Bunmi, I feel he should be made aware of what’s going on, as she’s taking her husband for a fool. Besides, why should mine be the only marriage to suffer?

Kemi, by e-mail

Dear Kemi,

What are you hoping to achieve by meddling in someone else’s relationship? Yes, perhaps her husband has a right to know, but if you were honest with yourself, that wouldn’t be why you would do such a thing. The truth is, you don’t want justice, you want revenge. If you really want to move on from the break-up of your marriage, forget about the past. If you truly want to move on from this, be the better person and move on.

Vanguard News

World.title: Trump, NATO chief to meet amid Ukraine security concerns
World.content:
File: US President Donald Trump; Photo by Mandel NGAN / AFP.

United States President Donald Trump is scheduled to meet NATO Secretary-General, Mark Rutte, today, amid growing concerns over European security and the ongoing war between Russia and Ukraine.

The meeting, expected to take place in Palm Beach, Florida, comes as Washington and its European allies continue discussions over the future of Ukraine, military support and security guarantees for the war-torn country.

According to Reuters, the White House announced the planned meeting, while NATO also confirmed Rutte’s visit to the United States.

The discussions are expected to focus on transatlantic security relations, NATO’s defence commitments and efforts to find a diplomatic solution to the conflict between Moscow and Kyiv.

Trump has repeatedly called on European members of NATO to increase their defence spending and take greater responsibility for the security of the continent.

The meeting also comes amid disagreements among Western allies over the terms of a possible peace agreement and the extent of future military assistance to Ukraine.

Rutte has maintained that NATO’s support for Ukraine remains important to European security, as Russia’s invasion continues to shape diplomatic and military calculations across the region.

The outcome of Wednesday’s meeting could provide further indications of Washington’s position on NATO’s future role in the Ukraine conflict.

Vanguard News

World.title: Police declare 9 wanted over parcel of bullets sent to First Bank MD
World.content:
First Bank MD Olusegun Alebiosu

The police have declared nine persons wanted over an alleged threat to the life of First Bank of Nigeria Ltd. Managing Director, Mr. Olusegun Alebiosu.

The Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG), Zone 2, Mr Olohundare Jimoh, disclosed this on Tuesday in Lagos.

Jimoh spoke while briefing journalists at the Zone 2 Police Command headquarters, Onikan.

He said the threat involved a parcel containing two rounds of 7.62mm live ammunition delivered to Alebiosu’s residence.

The parcel, packaged as a fashion-design gift, was delivered by a dispatch rider whose identity remained unknown.

He said the incident was reported to the police on May 7, while the parcel was opened the following morning.

Jimoh described the ammunition as dangerous, noting that the 7.62mm rounds were designed for compatible firearms, including AK-47 rifles.

He said the discovery prompted a discreet investigation to identify those behind the alleged threat.

A joint team of crime detectives, ballistic experts and forensic investigators was subsequently constituted to investigate the incident.

According to him, preliminary investigations revealed that First Bank had undertaken extensive loan recovery activities involving customers allegedly owing several billions of naira.

Some of the customers reportedly confronted bank representatives and issued threats against the managing director during the recovery process.

Jimoh said the investigation was intended to establish the facts and identify those responsible for the alleged threat.

He disclosed that 10 bank customers and other persons considered relevant to the investigation had been invited for questioning.

The AIG said the invitations were issued in accordance with established investigative procedures and relevant legal provisions.

He said the investigation complied with the Judges’ Rules, the 1999 Constitution, the Administration of Criminal Justice Act, 2015, and other applicable laws.

Jimoh said the Firearms Act prohibited unlawful possession or control of ammunition without appropriate legal authorisation.

He disclosed that the 10 persons were invited on Nov. 5 to appear for questioning on Nov. 12.

However, only one person honoured the invitation, while the remaining nine failed to report.

Consequently, the police declared the nine persons wanted to facilitate the investigation into the alleged threat against Alebiosu and his family.

Jimoh urged anyone with useful information about their whereabouts to report to the nearest police station.

He assured the public that the investigation would remain discreet and professional, adding that anyone found culpable would face the full weight of the law.

The AIG stressed that nobody was above the law and that the police would ensure justice was served.

He added that the rights of both the suspects and the complainant would be protected throughout the investigation.

World.title: Governor Lawal shares 2,000 vehicles, tricycles, motorcycles
World.content:
Governor Dauda Lawal said that distributing empowerment assets to beneficiaries shows his administration’s commitment to helping individuals and associations across Zamfara grow their businesses, create jobs, and become self-reliant.

On Saturday, the governor launched the distribution of motorcycles, Keke NAPEP tricycles, Hijet pickups, and three-wheel barrow pickups to Zamfara residents at the Trade Fair Complex in Gusau, the state capital.

The distribution is the second phase of the state government’s empowerment programme targeting various groups, organisations and associations through the Zamfara State Agency for Poverty Alleviation (ZAPA).

The second phase includes 1,000 motorcycles, 1,000 tricycles popularly known as Keke NAPEP, 40 Hijet pickup vehicles, 40 three-wheeled pickup vehicles and 40 vehicles.

In his remarks, Governor Lawal reiterated that the initiative offers another opportunity for prospective beneficiaries to expand their economic opportunities and improve their standard of living.

He said, “This gathering is particularly important as it gives me a unique opportunity to formally distribute these vehicles in recognition of the immense contributions of individuals and various organisations to the overall development of our State.

“I wish to commend the Zamfara State Agency for Poverty Alleviation (ZAPA) for its commitment to implementing this laudable initiative.

“I also urge all beneficiary associations to regard these assets as valuable economic investments, utilise them strictly for their intended purposes and ensure timely repayment in accordance with the agreed loan arrangements. This will ensure the programme’s sustainability and enable other deserving citizens to benefit.

“Let me remind this gathering that humanitarian services save lives, relieve suffering and protect human dignity during conflicts, natural disasters and health emergencies. They bridge immediate survival needs with long-term community recovery when local systems are overwhelmed.

“My administration will continue to provide empowerment opportunities and livelihood support to individuals, groups and communities to expand opportunities and enhance the well-being of citizens of the State.”

World.title: Rivers 2027: ADC targets landslide victory, Ikuru says
World.content:
By Daniel Abia, P/Harcourt

The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has expressed confidence that it will secure a landslide victory in Rivers State in the 2027 general elections.

The Rivers South-East Senatorial candidate of the party, Bertram Ikuru, expressed the confidence during the inauguration of the ADC campaign council in Andoni Local Government Area on Tuesday.

Ikuru said the campaign council, chaired by Gogo Wellington, would strengthen the party’s grassroots mobilisation and help it win elective positions across Andoni LGA.

Congratulating members of the council on their appointments, he urged them to intensify grassroots mobilisation, promote unity and advance the party’s political objectives ahead of the elections.

He expressed optimism that the team would mobilise voters across the 11 wards of Andoni to secure victory for the ADC.

“I am optimistic that this team would deliver a very impactful campaign. It would maximally mobilise voters across the 11 wards of Andoni to secure a total victory for our dear party.

“Andoni is yearning for a positive turnaround which only ADC can offer. This indeed is the reason the party has since been widely accepted across the 11 wards,” he said.

Ikuru urged party members and supporters to rally behind the campaign council to build a formidable political structure capable of delivering victory at the polls.

Responding on behalf of the council, Wellington thanked the party for the confidence reposed in the team and pledged to work towards securing victory for the ADC.

He said the council would ensure peaceful and productive campaign activities across Andoni, adding that it was committed to winning all elective positions in the area.

The campaign council also comprises Mbaba Charles as Vice Chairman, Golden Ekprikpo as Secretary and Zilpah Nehemiah as Director of Women, among others.

World.title: LASU Gets NUC Commendation on Five Programmes, Launches Electric Campus Transport Scheme
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Funmi Ogundare

Lagos State University (LASU) has received commendations from four accreditation teams of the National Universities Commission (NUC) following an assessment of five undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, with the teams expressing satisfaction with the institution’s curriculum, staffing, teaching facilities and learning environment.

The programmes assessed during the exercise, which commenced on November 16, included Christian Religious Studies, Estate Management, Peace Studies and Conflict Resolution, as well as MSc Public Administration and Master of Public Administration (MPA).

At the exit meeting on November 17 at the university’s main campus, Ojo, the teams presented their observations and reports after evaluating the programmes’ academic standards, staffing, teaching and learning facilities, library resources, curriculum implementation and assessment procedures.

The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Ayodeji Badejo, who received the teams alongside members of the university management, expressed delight at the positive reports and commended the assessors for their professionalism and constructive observations.

The Estate Management accreditation team, led by Prof. Victoria Bello of the Federal University of Technology, Akure, hailed the university’s admission requirements and adherence to established standards. The team also applauded the institution’s efforts to promote discipline and prevent examination malpractice, while expressing satisfaction with its service delivery.

Similarly, the Christian Religious Studies accreditation team, led by Professor Olatundun Oderinde, lauded the programme’s curriculum for meeting NUC requirements. It described the marking schemes as satisfactory, the staffing as good and adequate, and the general learning environment as conducive.

Other areas that attracted commendation included the accuracy of the curricula, the quality of course delivery, the adequacy of assessment methods, and the standard of external examination.

Meanwhile, the university recently launched an electric-powered transportation scheme, LASUSU VoltRide, in partnership with Glid Haven Global Resources Limited, to ease movement and address transportation challenges across its Ojo campus. The initiative is designed to provide safe, affordable and environmentally friendly transportation for students and staff.

Speaking through the acting Dean, Student Affairs, Dr Abiodun Fatai-Abatan, the VC described the initiative as a timely intervention to address mobility challenges, particularly among students who often struggle to get to lecture venues on time due to inadequate campus transportation.

“LASU remains committed to exploring innovative and reliable solutions to improve students’ welfare and enhance the overall campus experience,” she said.

Badejo commended Glid Haven Global Resources Limited for introducing the initiative, describing it as a demonstration of commitment to safety, empowerment, innovation and progress.

She noted that the electric-powered vehicles would not only ease movement across the campus but also reduce environmental pollution, dependence on fossil fuels and the impact of rising fuel costs. The VC urged students to use the service responsibly by wearing seat belts, avoiding overloading and protecting the vehicles against vandalism.

Earlier, the Executive Director of Glid Haven Global Resources Limited, Mr Oluwatayo Israel Olowe, said LASUSU VoltRide was designed to introduce smarter, cleaner and more sustainable transportation to the university community.

Olowe, an alumnus of LASU, said the initiative was also an opportunity for the promoters to give back to the institution that shaped their academic and professional journeys.

World.title: Babcock Conference Seeks Inclusive Education for Neurodiverse Children
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Funmi Ogundare

Babcock University’s International Conference on Translational Research in Learning Disabilities (ICTR-LD 2026) has called for a fundamental shift in educational practices, urging schools to abandon one-size-fits-all teaching methods and adopt inclusive approaches that recognise and accommodate the diverse learning needs of children.

The conference urged educators, policy makers, researchers and parents to create learning environments where children with conditions such as dyslexia, dyscalculia and other forms of neurodivergence can access quality education and realise their full potential.

The two-day conference, held recently, themed, ‘Neurodiversity: Helping Different Minds Learn Better’, brought together educators, clinicians, researchers, university leaders, policymakers, technologists, parents and learners to examine how research on learning disabilities could translate into practical interventions in classrooms, campuses and homes.

Speaking at the opening ceremony, President/Vice-Chancellor of Babcock University, Prof. Afolarin Ojewole, challenged participants to reconsider conventional assumptions about intelligence and learning, noting that learning difficulties should not deprive children of educational opportunities.

He called on schools to adapt their facilities, curricula and teaching methods to accommodate diverse learners, while urging educators and researchers to develop practical, evidence-based solutions to address their needs.

Ojewole described the conference as both a moral and pedagogical turning point in the pursuit of inclusive education, noting that learners with dyslexia, dyscalculia and slow learning processes had suffered in silence because their challenges were often misunderstood.

“For too long, learners with dyslexia, dyscalculia, or slow learning processes have suffered in silence. Their struggles have often been mistaken for laziness, while their immense potential has remained buried under rigid and punitive classroom systems,” he stated.

Executive Secretary of the Nigerian Educational Research and Development Council (NERDC), Prof. Salisu Shehu, described the conference as an important platform for strategic partnerships in education, research and development.

He reaffirmed the role of education in sustainable development, particularly in an era increasingly shaped by digital technology and Artificial Intelligence, and expressed the council’s readiness to explore collaborative opportunities with Babcock University and other institutions.

Similarly, the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN), in her remarks delivered by Princess Adaobi Ekwuno on behalf of its Registrar, Dr. Ronke Shoyomo, emphasised the need for research to extend beyond academic publications and translate into improvements in educational quality.

She reaffirmed the council’s every child’s right to quality, inclusive and equitable education, regardless of individual learning needs, while emphasing the responsibility of teachers to acquire the competencies required to support diverse learners.

Several presentations at the conference examined practical approaches to inclusive education.

In its communiqué, the conference called for stronger institutional commitment to inclusive education through practical teacher training, sensory-friendly learning environments, peer support initiatives, clear referral pathways and improved collaboration among educators, families, clinicians and policymakers.

“There is a need to involve learners in shaping policies and services affecting them, while ensuring that technology and interventions are responsibly implemented and guided by evidence and professional judgment,” it said

World.title: Closing Nigeria’s Future Workforce Gender Gap With GirlsGetSET
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Uchechukwu Nnaike

As technology advances and industries rely more on technical expertise, the demand for a skilled, innovative and diverse workforce continues to grow. Yet one challenge persists: women’s underrepresentation in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM).

Experts argue that bridging this gap cannot start at hiring; it must begin earlier by giving young people, especially girls, confidence, exposure and support to envision themselves pursuing technical careers.

This is the thinking behind GirlsGetSET, a STEM-focused initiative that introduces young girls to the possibilities in STEM through hands-on learning, mentorship and career exploration.

GirlsGetSET was created to bridge the divide between classroom education and real-life careers. Through interactive activities, problem-solving exercises, and mentorship sessions with professionals, students gain insight into how STEM skills apply in the energy and technology sectors.

Baker Hughes, one of the global partners leading the GirlsGetSET programme, recently collaborated with Bethesda Secondary School, Lagos, Nigeria, to mentor students. Employees volunteered to carry out practical science-based projects, share personal experiences, inspiring career journeys, and lessons learned, helping students to understand available pathways.

Research shows that role models are key to driving career aspirations (Gibson, 2004; Valero et al., 2019). Young girls considering STEM careers are more likely to view technical roles as attainable when they have direct exposure to professionals in those fields.

Educators at the Bethesda Secondary School also highlighted the programme’s impact on students’ confidence and aspirations. Mr Temidayo Adedeji, Schools Supervisor, said, “The GirlsGetSET mentorship programme has been a deeply transformative experience for our girls at Bethesda Secondary School, Ikota. We particularly appreciated the way the programme introduced the girls to inspiring women in STEM, while providing practical guidance on setting career goals and mapping out achievable pathways.”

According to the organisers, this raises an important question for the Nigerian energy industry: how can organisations help build the future workforce they will rely on? Initiatives such as GirlsGetSET, they said, demonstrate the important role local companies play in developing future talent pipelines.

The first cohort concluded with a graduation ceremony, celebrating the students’ achievements and marking GirlsGetSET’s successful first year in Nigeria.

Feedback from students and teachers highlighted increased awareness of STEM opportunities, greater confidence, and a better understanding of available career pathways.

A participating senior secondary three (SS3) student said, “The GirlsGetSET programme showed us that you don’t need a traditional background to engage with STEM. The experience taught me the discipline to trust my own path, knowing that real achievement takes time to build. It showed us that growth isn’t rushed, but carefully cultivated through consistency and perseverance.”

Another participant said, “Before GirlsGetSet, I didn’t realise how much potential I had to explore new fields. Believing in yourself means having the courage to pursue your vision, even when others doubt you.”

Stakeholders believe that programmes like this will help the country to ensure that the next generation of engineers, scientists, innovators and technology leaders are not just highly skilled, but better reflect the society they serve.

World.title: Ronik Polytechnic Graduates 1,051 Across Five Academic Sessions
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Oluchi Chibuzor

The Ronik Polytechnic, Ejigbo, Lagos, has graduated 1,051 students across five academic sessions, as the institution continues to expand its academic programmes aimed at producing graduates capable of solving societal problems.

Speaking at the convocation programme in Lagos recently, the acting Rector, Dr Abiodun Olafenwa, urged the graduating students to see their certificates as a licence to solve the problems confronting society.

He disclosed that 1,051 graduands who satisfied the institution’s academic and character requirements across five academic sessions, from 2020/2021 to 2025/2026, were awarded National Diploma and Higher National Diploma certificates.

“To our graduating class of excellence: As you step out of the gates of Ronik Polytechnic into a complex, rapidly evolving global economy, remember that your diploma is not merely a piece of paper-it is a licence to solve problems, innovate, and serve,” said Olafenwa. “You have been trained in an institution that values both the head and the hands. Go out and build enterprises like Dangote and Walker, think deeply like Alele-Williams and Freire, act with integrity like Niyi Osundare, and stand undaunted like the masters of Invictus.”

Olafenwa added that the institution was committed to strengthening its infrastructure, expanding degree articulation programmes and developing practical skills hubs to position itself as a leading polytechnic in West Africa.

“As we upgrade our campus infrastructure, launch degree articulation programmes, and roll out modern practical skills hubs, we reaffirm our commitment to becoming West Africa’s foremost practical polytechnic. We call on well-meaning individuals and corporate partners to deepen their collaborative support in funding research, sponsoring skills hubs, and building infrastructure,” he explained.

In his remarks, the Chairman of the Governing Council, Dr Adebola Olubanjo, said polytechnic education has a distinctive role in addressing societal challenges.

“It connects ideas with practice, enabling learners to understand how things work and how they can work better,” Olubanjo noted. “A strong technical education develops both the capacity to perform a task and the judgement to examine evidence, question assumptions, and improve existing methods. This combination is essential to productive enterprise and national development.”

The guest lecturer, Dr. Adewole Usman Rufai lauded the institution’s effort and commitment to knowledge development in the country.

Speaking on the theme, ‘Rise to Excellence: Empowering Minds for Skills and Service’, he stated that the convocation exercise further showcased achievements of the graduates and the dedication of all who have sustained their education.

The polytechnic also conferred its fellowship on Abiodun Jolaoso, Kolawole Akinlayo and Mrs. Mogbonjubola Ejerinde.

World.title: Rivers-born Tech Expert Launches Guide to Careers in Tech for African Students
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

Rivers-born technology expert and United Kingdom-based author, Sobere Opusunju, has launched a new career guide aimed at helping secondary school students across Africa to understand opportunities in the technology industry and make informed career choices.

The book, ‘Start Here: A Secondary School Student’s Guide to Careers in Tech’, was unveiled virtually recently with endorsements from the British Computer Society (BCS), The Chartered Institute for IT, and industry leaders.

Opusunju, Deputy Chair of BCS Hertfordshire branch and founder of Tech2Africa Limited, said the book was inspired by repeated questions from young Africans who wanted to pursue technology careers but did not know where to begin.

He said students from countries including Uganda, Zimbabwe and Rwanda had repeatedly asked him: “If I want to go into tech, where do I start?”

According to him, the book was written to address the gap by giving young people practical exposure to the wide range of careers available in the technology sector.

“A young person cannot choose a path they have not seen,” Opusunju said, adding that the book draws from his personal experiences and conversations with young people across Africa.

The book introduces students to 44 technology career roles spanning data, cloud computing, product design, cybersecurity and artificial intelligence (AI), among other fields.

Opusunju, who hails from Opobo in Rivers State, said his immediate target was to raise funds for 1,000 copies to be distributed to 10 secondary schools in Rivers State before expanding the initiative to schools across Nigeria.

He appealed to individuals and organisations to sponsor copies, noting that many secondary school students could not afford the book.

“The copies will be printed in Nigeria and delivered to the named schools through Tech2Africa Limited,” he said.

His wife, Olive Kyogerera, who delivered the welcome address, said the book reflected Opusunju’s passion for educating young Africans.

She expressed hope that at least 10,000 copies would eventually reach schools, saying it would give students “courage” and encourage them to pursue their aspirations.

In his citation, Dr. Maclean Eneotu Jacob, described Start Here as Opusunju’s third book, noting that his commitment to youth education dates back to 2008, when he founded the Save Opobo Foundation while studying at the Malaysian campus of the University of Wollongong.

The foreword was written by Dr. Paul Moggridge, a Computer Science lecturer at the University of Hertfordshire, who praised the book for being accessible to students without assuming access to expensive laptops or fast broadband.

Students from Uganda, Kenya, Zimbabwe and Nigeria also read excerpts from the book, while guests pledged copies for schools across Nigeria and other African countries.

World.title: New NCE-Degree Framework Will Transform Teacher Education, Boost Professional Opportunities, Says EKSU Chancellor
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Gbenga Sodeinde

The Chancellor of Ekiti State University (EKSU), Dr. Tunji Olowolafe, has stated that the federal government’s newly introduced Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree programme will redefine teacher education in Nigeria, strengthen colleges of education and restore the prestige of the teaching profession.

Olowolafe, who delivered the 2026 convocation lecture of Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State, described the policy as one of the most significant reforms in Nigeria’s education sector, saying that it would expand academic opportunities for prospective teachers while improving the quality of teacher preparation nationwide.

Speaking on the theme, ‘The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria’, he said the policy, which empowers colleges of education to independently award the Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE) and bachelor’s degrees in Education, marks the end of decades of dependence on university affiliations for degree certification.

According to him, the reform has the potential to reposition colleges of education as competitive institutions capable of attracting high-quality candidates and producing professionals equipped for the demands of modern classrooms.

Olowolafe regretted that colleges of education had, over the years, suffered declining patronage because they were widely perceived as institutions for candidates unable to secure admission into universities.

Quoting statistics from the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB), he noted that barely one per cent of admission seekers deliberately chose colleges of education, a trend he described as a serious threat to the future of teacher education in the country.

The EKSU chancellor commended President Bola Tinubu for initiating reforms aimed at reversing the trend through the Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023, which provides the legal framework for qualified colleges of education to award degrees independently.

He explained that the implementation of the Dual-Mandate programme, which commenced in May 2025, represents a landmark policy shift capable of transforming teacher preparation across the country’s 28 federal colleges, 51 state-owned colleges and qualified private institutions.

Looking ahead, Olowolafe warned that Nigeria faces an estimated shortage of one million teachers and urged students graduating from colleges of education to prepare themselves for emerging opportunities within the education sector.

He also stressed the need for institutions to embrace artificial intelligence and other digital technologies to improve teaching, learning and educational access, while insisting that technology should complement, not replace the human qualities of empathy, integrity, sound judgment and mentorship that define effective teachers.

The renowned entrepreneur also advocated the integration of vocational and technical education into mainstream learning, arguing that practical skills should enjoy equal recognition with conventional academic qualifications.

As part of his commitment to advancing education, Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a solar-powered ICT centre with Starlink internet connectivity at SACOETEC.

The facility, to be known as GOMTECH, will be fully funded and equipped by the foundation, which will also collaborate with the institution in its management.

He also unveiled an annual academic excellence award under which the best graduating NCE student, best bachelor’s degree graduate and outstanding lecturers would receive cash prizes.

Earlier, the Provost of SACOETEC, Dr. Modupe Oba-Adenuga, described the convocation lecture as timely, saying that it provided a valuable platform to examine the challenges confronting teacher education and chart a new direction for the profession in line with national and global educational realities.

World.title: Queens College Principal Tasks Graduands on Innovation, Nation Building
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Uchechukwu Nnaike

The Principal, Queen’s College Lagos, Dr. (Mrs) Oyindamola Obabori, has described the school as an incubator for leaders, innovators and change makers, saying that the rigorous academic activities have equipped the students to build, transform and lead.

Obabori, who stated this at the recent speech and prize-giving day of the college, told the prize winners that their discipline, sleepless nights and relentless drive have paid off in full.

“You have set a standard of academic, artistic and athletic brilliance and we salute your magnificent achievements. Stand tall, because today, the spotlight is entirely yours,” she said.

She also commended the students who worked tirelessly, improved their grades, stayed up late at night to master tough concepts, and represented their houses with pride in various competitions.

According to Obabori, champion status was forged in quiet moments when no body was watching; when one chooses integrity over shortcuts, kindness over indifference and resilience over defeat.

She added that the entire QC community had been placed on the pedestal of champions by the performance at the 2025/2026 West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE), winning the second best college position.

She commended teachers and other staff of the institution for their commitment and dedication, describing them as master coaches.

“You see potential long before it manifests. You push, nurture, correct and inspire with selfless dedication. Thank you for doing hard-work so effortlessly and for pouring your hearts into these young minds every single day.

“To our incredible parents and guardians, you are the ultimate ride-or-die investors in these dreams. Look at the harvest of your prayers, your sacrifices, financial commitments and your unwavering belief. Today’s celebration belongs to you, just as much as it belongs to them.

“My dear students, as we celebrate today, remember that winning a prize is a wonderful milestone, but not the finish line. It is a reminder of what you are capable of achieving when you dedicate your heart and mind to a goal,” Obabori stated,

The principal then urged the students to go into the world with their heads held high, carry the values of the school with pride and continue to shine brightly.

The President, Queen’s College Old Girls Association (QCOGA), Temitayo Okunoren-Makindipe said the college has a strong legacy of academic excellence, discipline and sisterhood.

“As old girls, we remain deeply grateful for the foundation our alma mater has given us and are committed to supporting its continuous growth and development.

“As we look forward to the school centenary in 2027, we are reminded of our shared responsibility to preserve this legacy and ensure that future generations continue to benefit from what Queen’s College provides,” she said.

She commended the principal and the entire management of the college for their leadership; the teachers for their dedication to nurturing young minds; and parents/guardians, for their continued support and partnership in the education of the students.

“As we celebrate today’s accomplishments, may we remain mindful that the true measure of education lies not only in academic success, but also in the development of responsible, compassionate and confident individuals who are prepared to contribute positively to the society,” she said.

The guest speaker, Mrs. Valerie Tunde-Obe, Executive Director, Business Development and Innovation, Punch Nigeria Limited, admonished the graduands to do whatever they choose with excellence and integrity.

“There is dignity in every honest profession and honour in work done exceptionally well. Don’t just be successful, be significant. Success is what you achieve, significance is who you impact positively along the way,” she said.

“Talent open doors; character decides what happens when you walk through them. These days, you can become famous overnight; one dance, one video, one hashtag and boom, two million views by breakfast.

“But going viral is not the same as being valuable; being seen is not the same as being respected. Let your ambition be big, but your integrity, bigger,” Tunde-Obe stated.

The high point of the event was the distribution of awards to teaching and non-teaching staff members for their contributions to the development of the college.

Students were also recognised for academic excellence, brilliance in sports and dedication and discipline in other fields.

World.title: Transatlantic University Gets NUC Approval to Admit 700 Students, Begins Academic Activities Dec 1
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

David-Chyddy Eleke in Awka

Transatlantic University of Medicine and Health Sciences, Umuchukwu, in Orumba South Local Government Area of Anambra State, has secured National Universities Commission (NUC) approval for an initial intake of 700 students.

The Vice-Chancellor, Prof. Charles Esimone, disclosed this while briefing journalists at the institution’s administrative block in Umuchukwu, saying the newly approved university will commence academic activities on December 1, 2026.

Esimone told journalists that all arrangements have been concluded for the take-off of the university, describing the institution as unique, given its focus on medicine and health sciences.

The newly licensed university is owned by Umuchukwu-born, US-based medical practitioner, Dr Godwin Maduka, proprietor of Las Vegas Pain Institute, and former governorship candidate in Anambra State.

According to Esimone, considering the proprietor’s calibre as a renowned pain doctor in the US, nothing short of the best is expected, adding that it was established to provide quality education and professional training in the health sector.

“This university had commenced in principle in October following the issuance of our operational licence by the NUC and the completion of the commission’s resource verification exercise. We will commence full academic activities on December 1,” Esimone said.

On tuition fees, he said students in other programmes would pay N3 million, while those studying Medicine and Pharmacy would pay between N5 million and N7 million per session.

Earlier, the Registrar, Rev. Sam Ufoh, led journalists on a guided tour of the institution’s facilities, showcasing the infrastructure put in place ahead of the commencement of academic activities.

World.title: Battle of the memes? Herman Mashaba mocks Helen Zille
World.content:
Forget the battle of the mayoral bids, Action SA’s Herman Mashaba and the DA’s Helen Zille are going tit for tat in the memes department in a public social media spat.

The political party heads are engaging in back and forth over who gets to govern Johannesburg and how power should be shared.

Although the DA received the most votes in the province’s major metros, it did not secure an outright majority and requires the help of smaller parties, like ActionSA as a coalition partner.



Negotiations between the two parties has effectively reached a stalemate as neither is willing to compromise on its offers.

HERMAN MASHABA CLAPS BACK AT HELEN ZILLE

Over the weekend, Helen Zille responded to Herman Mashaba’s ongoing public demands amid coalition negotiations, with a meme that mocked his “arrogance”.

In it, was a spoof SABC news announcement that the ActionSA leader had elected himself as Springboks coach ahead of the Nations Championship final against France this weekend.

The meme claimed that the nw coach had served France with an ultimatum and shocking squad shake-up.

“This sums it up well”, shared Helen.

This sums it up well. I wonder who is "arrogant". pic.twitter.com/VqqIvexVVy  November 23, 2026

On ActionSA’s TikTok page, the party clapped back with a meme of Helen Zille bing forcibly removef from a polling Gqeberha polling station during the 2021 local government eclections.

The party captioned the meme: “Soon to be removed”, hinting at Helen’s mayoral bid.

The account also posted another meme, an AI-generated video of Herman Mashaba dancing with pals from the ANC and MK Party, whom are also engaging in coalition talks.

SABC DISTANCES ITSELF FROM MEME

Meanwhile, the SABC has distanced itself from the meme posted by Helen Zille

It shared on its X platform: “This graphic is not SABC News content. It was not broadcast on any of our platforms and uses our branding without permission”.

The SABC encouraged the public to check news through its official channels.

World.title: ‘We will get that R5 000’: Pensioners float bold plan for older persons grant
World.content:
Black and white photo of elderly hands clasped over a cane. Image: Pexels

Some older persons grant recipients believe taking to the streets is the only way to secure a bigger grant.

The call came in response to The South African’s December 2026 old-age grant payment date reminder on Facebook, where pensioners shared frustration over the size of their monthly payment.

Picket call gains support

Sabata Modise said protest action could deliver a dramatic increase for older South Africans.



“As long we picket we will get that five thousand for senior citizens of SA,” Modise wrote.

The comment drew laughter and likes from other users. It also reflects a growing feeling among pensioners that their concerns are not being heard.

Sphelile Linah shared that frustration.

“Every time they raised food electricity but never raised money for us no bonus for Christmas why because we are struggling,” she wrote.



How far R5 000 older persons GRANT IS from reality

Older persons aged 60 and older currently receive R2 400 a month.

A R5 000 grant would mean an increase of R2 600 a month, more than double the current amount.

The grant rose from R2 315 to R2 400 in April 2026, an increase of R85. At that pace, reaching R5 000 would take decades.



SASSA will pay December’s older persons grants on Wednesday, 2 December. The amount stays the same as in previous months.

What it would take to change the grant

Grant amounts are not set by SASSA. The Minister of Finance announces increases in the national Budget each February, and Parliament must approve them. New amounts usually take effect in April.

This means any push for higher grants would need to be directed at National Treasury and Parliament, not SASSA offices.



Carol Frances Alexander had a more modest request.

“Due to all respect, I don’t need the date I need a R600 added to my R2400,” she wrote.

The next opportunity for an increase will come with the February 2027 Budget speech.

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Airlift rescue: Veteran hiker, 60, saved following rocky mishap
World.content:
A helicopter carrying a rescue team was dispatched to the hiker's location following his fall. Image via Facebook @WSARWesternCape

A 60-year-old veteran hiker is safe following a harrowing hiking ordeal in the Western Cape this past weekend.

On Saturday, 21 November 2026, the hiker and his companions were hiking in the remote Olifants River Dome area near the Cederberg when the ordeal occurred.

LOOSE ROCK DISRUPTS HIKING EXCURSION

According to Wilderness Search And Rescue (WSAR), the group had successfully summited the peak. As they were making their way back to camp, however, a loose rock gave way beneath the veteran hiker’s foot.



This resulted in the hiker tumbling onto a lower ledge. He struck his head, causing him to bleed.

At once, his companions came to his assistance. After applying a dressing to control the bleeding, they promptly called emergency services on 021 937 0300.

WSAR AIRLIFTS HIKER TO SAFETY

Once the alarm was raised, a Western Cape Government Health and Wellness EMS / Air Mercy Service rescue helicopter carrying a team – including an EMS paramedic – was dispatched to the injured hiker’s location.



“The injured hiker was assessed and treated on scene before being flown to a nearby landing zone and transported to hospital by ambulance for further medical care,” said WSAR, per a Facebook post.

The hiker has since been discharged from hospital and is said to be in recovery at home.

‘ELEMENT OF UNPREDICTABILITY’

WSAR commended the hiker’s companions for their actions, as well as the rescue team’s efforts.



The organisation also noted how this situation illustrates that not even Mother Nature shows no mercy to the most experienced hikers.

“No matter how experienced or well-prepared you are, the outdoors will always have an element of unpredictability,” they said. “A loose rock or an unexpected slip can change an adventure in an instant.

“Being safe isn’t about eliminating every risk. It’s about being prepared for the unexpected and looking out for one another when it matters most.”



If you’re planning a hike, read here for the best hiking safety tips.

World.title: Afrikaans is Groot concert under fire over ‘demonic’ performance
World.content:
Afrikaans is Groot and Nataniël have come under fire over a 'demonic' performance. Images via Facebook

The annual Afrikaans Is Groot music festival has come under fire al concert-goer accused organisers, and particularly artist Nataniël, of promoting a “demonic” performance.

The music events takes place from 20 to 29 November 2026 at the SunBet Arena, in Pretoria.

NATANIËL, AFRIKAANS IS GROOT UNDER FIRE OVER ‘DEMONIC’ PERFORMANCE

On Facebook, Afrikaans is Groot concert-goer, JC Lamprecht, who is a well-known MMA fighter, revealed that he had walked out of Friday night’s show over its “wicked” imagery.



Lamprecht was referring to the performance of Afrikaans singer, Nataniël, that featured a backdrop of a red sky, a full moon, an underworld city and dancers wearing long lack coats. On the stage was a giant spider-like prop and and image across the screen of a wing-faced Nataniël.

Accusing the singer of sinister practises, Lamprecht told his 106 000 followers: “I will never publicly worship or glorify the wicked.

“My sincere apologies to all the other artists who performed. But there was a moment where it was clear to me that the wicked is openly honoured and glorified. I will never stand for that!”

He added: “I will not remain silent or participate in anything that directly goes against my faith and my Lord Jesus Christ. I BOW MY KNEE TO ONLY ONE KING – JESUS CHRIST!”

In another comment, he claimed that the Afrikaans Is Groot show appeared to show the “devil taking over the world”

The post quickly went viral, attracting tens of thousands of likes, comments and shares. In the comment action, many Christian followers agreed with his stance, accusing Nataniël of portraying “Lucifer” in a “demonic” and “satanic” performance”.



Devon Hofymer, the son of Steve Hofmeyr, who has previously performed at Afrikaans is Groot, commented that the themes seen during the show had become “normalised” in society.

He shared a Facebook post: “As Christians, we must understand that not everything presented as entertainment is innocent. We can’t continue to water things down, shift our standards and silence our consciences just because something has become popular or acceptable in the world.

“The danger is not only what we see today, but what we will be used to tomorrow.

“We must stay vigilant.

“Because what we normalize today can tomorrow open the door to things we would have earlier stood up to without hesitation”.

FESTIVAL RESPONDS TO BACKLASH

Responding to the backlash Afrikaans is Groot Artistic Director Carien Loubser rubbished claims that Nataniël’s performance was “demonic”.

She shared: “You don’t have to like everything, and you don’t have to understand everything. But it’s unfair to dismiss something you don’t understand as demonic.

Loubser disputed claims that concert-goers had walked out of the show, adding that the response had been positive.

She continued: “Music has many forms. You can dance to it or get deep. It can make you laugh or cry,” she said.

“Music can make you remember or forget. Every person has the right to make their own interpretation. And that’s actually the wonderful thing about music.”

World.title: Number Of The Day | $1 trillion | 24 November 2026
World.content:
The Trillion-Dollar Illusion: What Happens When Markets Invest In Personalities?

There was no revolutionary new chip, technological breakthrough or dramatic improvement in Nvidia's financial results behind the company's extraordinary market recovery on Monday. Instead, investors were responding to the return of a familiar face. Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive sent Nvidia's shares soaring by 31%, restoring nearly $1 trillion in market value and lifting technology stocks across Wall Street. It was a remarkable demonstration of how much financial value can be attached to an individual's reputation, but it also exposed a troubling feature of modern financial markets: the growing difficulty of separating confidence in a business from confidence in the person running it.

The economics of belief

The value of a publicly traded company is not simply determined by what it owns or earns today. Investors are also attempting to establish what that business might achieve tomorrow, making assumptions about future profitability, technological developments, competitive advantages and management decisions. When those expectations change, valuations can move dramatically without an equivalent change in the company's underlying operations. Nvidia's engineers did not become more productive overnight, nor did its manufacturing capacity suddenly expand. What changed most visibly was the market's confidence in the direction of the business.

Behavioural economics offers a useful framework for understanding this phenomenon. Investors do not make decisions in isolation; they respond to the behaviour of other investors, interpret emerging information and frequently act on expectations about how markets will react. A leadership announcement can consequently trigger a self-reinforcing cycle in which rising prices attract further buying, strengthening the impression that confidence has returned. The danger is that the resulting valuation may reflect collective enthusiasm more readily than a measured assessment of the company's long-term prospects.

The concentration problem

The influence of celebrity executives becomes particularly consequential when the companies they lead occupy dominant positions within global financial markets. Nvidia's importance extends beyond its shareholders because of its position within the artificial intelligence ecosystem, where technology developers, cloud computing businesses and infrastructure providers are connected through commercial relationships and expectations about future growth. When confidence in one influential company deteriorates, investors may reassess the prospects of businesses operating throughout that ecosystem, spreading uncertainty well beyond the source of the initial disruption.

For South Africans, this interconnectedness challenges the assumption that events on Wall Street are distant from domestic financial concerns. Retirement funds, global equity portfolios and exchange-traded funds can provide exposure to international technology companies, even when individual investors have never directly purchased shares in those businesses. Furthermore, market-capitalisation-weighted indices give larger companies greater influence over overall portfolio performance. A fund containing hundreds of businesses may therefore remain particularly sensitive to developments affecting a relatively small group of dominant companies.

Why a market recovery does not eliminate risk

Nvidia's decision to reinstate Huang may have reassured shareholders, but a recovering share price cannot independently establish whether the institutional concerns surrounding his departure have been adequately addressed. The company has expressed confidence, following input from the US government, that his reinstatement does not present a national security risk. Nevertheless, the broader governance question remains relevant: can an organisation maintain effective oversight when its financial fortunes appear so closely connected to one executive?

This tension becomes especially important when investors are evaluating businesses through periods of rapid technological change. Strong demand for artificial intelligence, confidence in a founder's vision and expectations of future profitability can collectively support enormous valuations. However, these expectations cannot substitute for sustainable earnings, effective risk management and institutional resilience. The distinction between an exceptional executive and an exceptional business becomes most visible when circumstances force investors to evaluate one without the other.

The $1 trillion figure explored on eNCA's Number of the Day with Gareth Edwards and Francis Herd is therefore significant for reasons that extend beyond Nvidia's recovery. It provides an opportunity to reconsider what financial markets are actually rewarding when they attach extraordinary value to an individual. A business may benefit enormously from a visionary leader, but when confidence in that leader becomes the foundation of its valuation, the market may be placing a price on something considerably more fragile than the company itself.

World.title: Senegal regain Afcon title after appeal to sports court
World.content:
LAUSANNE - Senegal on Tuesday regained its Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January.

"The Court of Arbitration for Sport has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025," CAS said in a statement.

The Swiss-based sports court said Senegal's appeal had been upheld by "a unanimous decision", and their original 1-0 victory after extra time is reinstated.

In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) sensationally overturned the result of the final, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title, after many Senegalese players walked off the pitch in protest at a penalty given to the hosts with the game still goalless.

The CAF Appeals Committee had justified its decision to overturn the result and declare Morocco champions based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations.

Those state that if a team "refuses to play or leaves the ground before the regular end of the match without the authorisation of the referee, it shall be considered (loser) and shall be eliminated for good from the current competition".

However, the Senegal players eventually returned to the pitch and the final carried on.

The CAS panel therefore considered that the referee's decision to restart the final showed that "the conditions for resuming the match had been met", and that articles 82 and 84 were therefore "not applicable in this case".

World.title: Ledama Ole Kina court battle over Sh1.2m dispute takes new turn
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Narok Senator Ledama Ole Kina has been granted a stay of execution in a Sh1.2 million compensation dispute with former Narok County Assembly employee Zakayo Rotiken.

The court has given the senator an opportunity to raise funds and settle the outstanding amount.

The Employment and Labour Relations Court, sitting in Nairobi, issued the orders on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, and scheduled the matter for mention on February 18, 2027.

The development follows a protracted legal dispute arising from Rotiken's dismissal, in which the court awarded him Sh1,220,737.61 in compensation.

During Tuesday's proceedings, Ole Kina sought between 30 and 45 days to raise funds and settle the outstanding amount.

The court subsequently granted a stay of execution pending further proceedings in the matter.

In a statement, Rotiken's lawyer, Tonge Yoya, said the stay of execution did not invalidate, overturn or extinguish the original judgment, insisting that the senator remained legally obligated to settle the award.

The claimant's legal team also told the court that it intended to challenge pending applications by Ole Kina, arguing that some of the issues had already been determined in previous proceedings.

The lawyers said an application dated November 19, 2026, seeking to amend a preliminary objection filed on September 25, 2026, was directed to be served upon them.

Ole Kina was further directed to file and serve written submissions on the preliminary objection within 14 days.

The objection is anchored on the doctrine of res judicata, which bars parties from reopening matters that have already been conclusively determined by a competent court.

Rotiken's lawyers contend that a previous application by the senator seeking a stay of judgment was dismissed on April 24, 2026, and argue that subsequent applications touching on the same issues should not be entertained.

However, the Parliamentary Service Commission (PSC) is considering a request to release funds to settle a court-awarded compensation to Zakayo Rotiken, a former employee of Narok Senator Ledama Ole Kina, in a labour dispute that has resurfaced following a dramatic confrontation between the senator and auctioneers.

In a letter addressed to the parties in Employment and Labour Relations Court Cause E165 of 2021, Rotiken versus Ledama Ole Kina, the Commission confirmed that it had received a request seeking the release of funds to settle the decretal sum and costs awarded by the court.

The letter signed by the Commission's Director of Litigation and Compliance, Anthony Njoroge, states that the request has been placed before the Commission for consideration, with a decision expected once deliberations are concluded.

"The Commission's decision shall be communicated to you as soon as the Commission has concluded its deliberations on the matter," reads part of the letter.

The development comes against the backdrop of a viral video showing Senator Ole Kina threatening to shoot a female auctioneer who had gone to repossess a milk delivery lorry belonging to his Enkanasa Cow Milk Company over an outstanding financial obligation.

The confrontation sparked public outrage, with questions emerging over the circumstances surrounding the attempted repossession and the senator's conduct towards the auctioneers.

The dispute is linked to a labour case filed by Rotiken, who had been employed by Ole Kina before his dismissal. The former employee moved to court seeking redress over his termination, resulting in a monetary award against the senator.

The dispute stems from a court case filed by former Narok County Assembly employee Zakayo Rotiken against Senator Ledama Ole Kina at the Employment and Labour Relations Court in Nairobi. The court awarded Rotiken KSh 1,220,737.61 in compensation following his dismissal.

The latest communication from the Parliamentary Service Commission signals that the institution is considering facilitating settlement of the court award, although it has not yet made a final commitment to release the funds.

World.title: Ruto backs Didmus Barasa for Bungoma governor in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kimilili MP Didmus Barasa with President Ruto at a political rally in Mt Elgon during the President’s development tour in the Western region. [PCS]

President William Ruto has thrown his weight behind Kimilili MP Didmus Barasa in the race to succeed Bungoma Governor Kenneth Lusaka in 2027, setting the stage for a contest over the county's political leadership.

During his ongoing tour of Western Kenya, the President rallied support for Barasa, signalling his preference for the legislator in the battle for control of Bungoma County after the next General Election.

Barasa has expressed confidence in securing the United Democratic Alliance (UDA) party nomination, citing his development record and grassroots mobilisation in Kimilili as the foundation of his gubernatorial bid.

The MP has urged Bungoma leaders aligned with Kenya Kwanza to unite behind his candidature, arguing that a common political front would strengthen the region's bargaining power within the national government.

He said he intends to replicate his development model in Kimilili across the county's 45 wards, prioritising healthcare, education and youth empowerment.

“I want to take the development model we have implemented in Kimilili and extend it to all the 45 wards in Bungoma. Our people deserve better healthcare, improved education infrastructure, functional vocational training centres and quality early childhood education facilities,” he said.

The legislator pledged to strengthen county hospitals, improve the availability of medicines and expand access to healthcare services at the grassroots.

He also promised to invest in vocational training centres to equip young people with practical skills for employment and entrepreneurship, while improving Early Childhood Development and Education (ECDE).

Barasa identified agriculture, trade, infrastructure and youth entrepreneurship as key sectors requiring investment to unlock Bungoma's economic potential. He said his proposed administration would prioritise accountability, efficient use of public resources and improved service delivery.

His bid has received backing from a section of county leaders, including Senator Wafula Wakoli of Ford Kenya and Webuye East MP Martin Pepela.

However, Ruto's apparent preference for Barasa has attracted opposition from Sirisia MP John Waluke, who has questioned the endorsement and instead declared support for Westlands MP Tim Wanyonyi, who is associated with the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM).

Waluke argued that Bungoma residents should determine their next governor without external political influence.

“Bungoma belongs to its people, and the people must decide who will lead them in 2027. We cannot allow the gubernatorial contest to be determined through political endorsements from outside. Residents must be given the freedom to choose a leader who represents their interests,” he said.

The contest is also unfolding amid political differences between Barasa and National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang'ula, adding to the competing interests shaping Bungoma's succession politics.

World.title: Shun leaders inciting you to cause chaos, PS Omollo tells youth
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo. [File,Standard]

Internal Security Principal Secretary Raymond Omollo has warned young people against political violence, saying the destruction of public property costs lives and diverts resources meant for development.

The warning comes amid concerns over political violence in Embu following the September 12 incident at Nembure Stadium, where a meeting attended by Deputy President Kithure Kindiki was disrupted, leaving one person dead, six vehicles torched and three others vandalised.

Speaking during a Mass at St Thomas More Kairuri Parish in Embu County, Omollo challenged young people to question leaders who ask them to disrupt meetings, block roads or destroy property.

“Before you leave home to disrupt a meeting, ask that leader whether they would allow their own child to do what they are asking you to do,” he said.

“Ask them what they are doing to help you access education, training and employment.”

Omollo said young people should also question what political leaders were doing to improve their access to education, technical training and employment.

He said the Government was working to expand opportunities for young people through education, technical training and employment.

The PS welcomed efforts in the technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector to equip young people in Embu with skills to pursue their ambitions.

At the same time, Omollo commended county leadership for working with the national government to combat illicit alcohol and drug abuse.

Omollo said proposed legislative changes targeting the sector had passed the first reading in Parliament and urged residents to participate in the next stages of the legislative process.

On security, the PS acknowledged calls for more police vehicles, saying the Government was investing in personnel, vehicles and equipment.

However, he challenged residents to help protect public investments, citing reports that 10 police vehicles had been burned in Embu.

“We use our taxes to buy police vehicles, build markets and construct roads. We cannot pay for development and then allow a few individuals to destroy what belongs to all of us,” he said.
