World.title: Those Who Really Mistreat You and Don’t Care About You
World.content:
Eggs for 130 pesos each or 3,600 for a carton of 30.

By Lien Estrada

HAVANA TIMES – In his song “La sal no sala” (Salt Doesn’t Make Things Salty), Argentine singer Charly García has a line that goes: “The girl on the corner is treating me badly, she sells me a drug I can’t afford.” When I first heard it, I found it quite amusing. I’ve enjoyed his entire discography thanks to a friend abroad who was kind enough to get it for me.

Back then, we didn’t have Internet access, and Charly García’s music wasn’t heard in Cuba because, as I understand it, like John Lennon, he had made statements unfavorable to the dictator, Fidel Castro. And, of course, he was never forgiven for that.

However, I had seen a television interview with Colombian singer Carlos Vives, who said that Charly Garcia’s music was exceptional, and that was when I asked my friend to do me the favor of getting it for me. And he did. Like Fito Paez’s music, I find it revealing. But the line that has stayed with me the most is this cheeky one about the girl who sells a product at such a high price that it cannot be purchased, and the singer interprets that as mistreatment.

Perhaps this line has resonated so deeply with me because I live in a context where buying anything is a real challenge. When you find that a package of seasoned sausages costs far more than most people’s retirement pensions. A 10-pound package of chicken costs 9,500 pesos when the minimum wage is 3,210 pesos. A piece of candy costs 40 pesos. And to think that I had naively believed that everything would improve once the currencies were unified, supposedly in 2021.

That experience with stores where prices were in US dollars, but salaries and pensions were paid in Cuban pesos was never a good one, not even for those who belonged to the country’s sole political party, which runs everything and controls everything. Therein lies the difference between Cuban reality and the line from Charly’s song “La sal no sala.”

We know that those who mistreat us with these economic measures to “save the Homeland” are certainly not the girl on the corner. Nor is it the young man with the pushcart trying to sell lemons that will eventually rot because most people cannot afford them. Those mistreating us are not the women who resell goods, because there are few other business opportunities in this land. Cuba stopped producing things quite some time ago.

Those who mistreat us are those elderly gentlemen dressed in olive green, whom there seems to be no way of convincing that building an economy is essential to saving that very Homeland they are forever mentioning in their speeches, and that our daily bread cannot be obtained by talking about ideological work among the people.

But we don’t know how to get the message across by force (through sabotage, gunfire, and bombs), and these army officers won’t listen to reason. They see no mistreatment whatsoever in their political and economic management of a country that is increasingly falling apart, but rather “decisions that are not fair, but necessary,” as the tyrant Commander-in-Chief Fidel Castro once put it.

People decide to leave. Even sensing the truth of what the French say: “To leave is to die a little.” It doesn’t matter. More than a million Cubans have decided they will no longer endure mistreatment at the hands of a government that refuses to budge and is utterly convinced that it is right. More and more people are leaving. Every day.

One thing, however, is clearer than ever: it is not the girl on the corner who is mistreating us. And that is an important fact.

Read more from the diary of Lien Estrada here on Havana Times.

World.title: International News Briefs for Tuesday, November 24, 2026
World.content:
HAVANA TIMES – We bring you some of the top international news stories compiled by Democracy Now on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO After Trump Intervenes

Nov 24, 2026

Image Credit: X/@aburducky

Jensen Huang is back as CEO of the chip giant Nvidia, after President Trump personally called into a meeting of the company’s board on Sunday to push for his reinstatement. Huang had resigned less than two weeks ago, after news reports revealed he had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who was allegedly in communication with China’s top spy agency. The woman worked with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company suspected of buying advanced Nvidia chips and then diverting them to China in violation of U.S. export rules. On Monday, the Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist. During an interview on CNBC, President Trump was questioned about his role in reinstating Huang.

Eamon Javers: “Mr. President, did you give the board of directors an assurance that Jensen Huang would not be prosecuted at all for any of these” —

President Donald Trump: “I didn’t use the word ‘prosecuted.’”

Eamon Javers: — “questions around export controls?”

President Donald Trump: “But I said — I said that we believe — and I put out a statement. I think you probably saw that.”

Eamon Javers: “We did, yes.”

President Donald Trump: “That we believe he’s fine, he’s absolutely fine. I gave them enough” —

Carl Quintanilla: “There was a” —

President Donald Trump: — “assurance.”

Meanwhile, President Trump used his Truth Social platform to share a bizarre AI-generated meme that altered a photo taken moments after Trump was shot in Butler, Pennsylvania, in 2024. The doctored photo depicts a bloodied Huang holding a red bra in the air, with an Nvidia flag replacing the U.S. flag behind him.

Trump’s Stake in Nvidia Grows by Up to $15 Million as Stock Price Soars on Jensen Huang’s Return

Nov 24, 2026

Image Credit: Joyce N. Boghosian

News of Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia sent share prices soaring by over 30%, recovering much of the value lost since Huang resigned two weeks ago. Among beneficiaries of the stock surge is President Trump, whose stake in Nvidia grew to as much as $62 million before the scandal broke. Trump’s net worth grew by up to $15 million on Monday. Also benefiting is Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick ran for decades before joining the Trump administration. It’s now controlled by Lutnick’s sons, Brandon and Kyle. Cantor Fitzgerald held shares in Nvidia worth hundreds of millions of dollars, even as Lutnick made key decisions affecting Nvidia’s operations.

Jensen Huang’s reinstatement as CEO comes after Reuters reported Nvidia’s accounting practices have prompted an investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission. Nvidia and Huang also face a class-action shareholder lawsuit in California alleging securities fraud and misleading investors. And Huang is scheduled to testify on Capitol Hill next week, both in private testimony to lawmakers and in a public session of the Senate Banking Committee. We’ll have more on this story after headlines.

Analysis Estimates More Than 700,000 Russian Soldiers Have Died Fighting in Ukraine

Nov 24, 2026

A new report estimates more than 700,000 Russian soldiers have died in combat since President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine nearly five years ago. The finding is based on an analysis of leaked data from Russia’s state statistics agency, published by a pair of Russian-language news outlets operating outside of Russia.

On Monday, the Kremlin warned that Ukraine will face “painful consequences” for drone attacks on Russian ships in Libya and the Baltic Sea. Overnight, Russian drone and missile attacks on Zaporizhzhia left two people dead and more than 40 others injured, after a guided aerial bomb hit an apartment building near a bridge crossing the Dnipro River.

UNICEF Says Russian Attacks Are Killing Three Children, on Average, Each Day in Ukraine

Nov 24, 2026

Russia’s latest deadly strikes came as the U.N. Children’s Fund said the number of children killed or injured in Ukraine is approaching levels not seen since 2022, during the first year of Russia’s full-scale invasion. This is UNICEF’s Louise Wateridge.

Louise Wateridge: “According to the Human Rights Monitoring Mission for Ukraine, at least 1,144 children have been killed or injured in Ukraine in the first 10 months of 2026. This is a higher number of verified child casualties than in any other of the previous three years here in Ukraine, and that is more than three children who have been killed or injured every single day.”

Russia Threatens “Open War” with Estonia, a Former Soviet Republic Turned NATO Member

Nov 24, 2026

Russia has threatened to attack Estonia, after the Kremlin accused the country of allowing Ukraine to launch attacks from Estonian territory. On Monday, Russia’s Foreign Ministry declared Estonia was “on the verge of triggering open war.” The threat came after Estonia announced the closure of its land border with Russia. Estonia is a former Soviet republic, and has been a NATO member since 2004.

Rapid Support Forces Launch Drone Attack on Sudan’s Capital as Electrical Grid Nears Collapse

Nov 24, 2026

Sudan’s military says it intercepted drones launched by the Rapid Support Forces over the capital Khartoum, following a series of attacks that struck the city’s main airport and several buildings, including a U.N. facility. At least four people were reportedly killed in those attacks. They came as Sudan’s power grid is on the brink of collapse following attacks on electricity stations

Yemen’s Houthis Say 41 Civilians Are Killed in Saudi Attacks Using U.S. Arms

Nov 24, 2026

In Yemen, officials with the Ansar Allah movement, also known as the Houthis, say Saudi warplanes killed 41 civilians in a single day, in a series of strikes carried out with U.S.-made ordnance. One Saudi airstrike targeted a telecommunications hub, leaving 17 civilians dead, according to a Houthi spokesperson. Other attacks targeted buses and public transport vehicles in Hodeidah and Lahij, reportedly with GBU-49 and GBU-12 bombs. The U.N. warns over 1,600 people have been killed and 300,000 displaced since the ceasefire in Yemen between the Saudi-backed government and the Houthis collapsed in July.

Oxfam Report Finds Israel’s Military Assault “Has Turned Gaza into a Toxic Wasteland”

Nov 24, 2026

In Gaza, an Israeli airstrike on a security post killed two police officers and another Palestinian in al-Mawasi, a narrow strip of land that Israel has designated as a so-called safe zone. Another strike killed three brothers traveling by donkey cart — one of them, a child. In Gaza City, Palestinians held a funeral for Adel al-Helo, an employee of the U.N. agency for Palestinian refugees, UNRWA, killed in an attack a day earlier. This is his brother, Nizar al-Helo.

Nizar al-Helo: “He was working at the water dam in Jabaliya camp, supplying the water for the people of Jabaliya camp, and have been killed by an airstrike in Jabaliya camp by the Israeli army. They doesn’t make any difference between the civilian people and other people, even the people of the United Nations.”

Meanwhile, Oxfam has published a new report titled “Environmental War Crimes: How Israel’s military assault has turned Gaza into a toxic wasteland, threatening human survival.” It finds contamination from heavy metals, explosive residue, asbestos fibers, dioxins, crystalline silica, persistent organic pollutants and biological contaminants across 99% of Gaza’s territory.

Lebanese Immigrants Are Set to Lose Protected Status in U.S., Despite Ongoing Israeli Assault

Nov 24, 2026

In southern Lebanon, Israeli forces launched a series of airstrikes, artillery and machine-gun attacks earlier today — the latest in a series of violations of a U.S.-mediated ceasefire Israel agreed to earlier this year. The violence has uprooted 1.2 million people from their homes — about one-fifth of Lebanon’s population.

Here in the U.S., a program granting temporary protected status to Lebanese immigrants and refugees is due to expire on Friday. A bill introduced by lawmakers in Michigan, a state home to a large Lebanese diaspora community, would extend TPS. It’s co-sponsored by Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib.

Rep. Rashida Tlaib: “Without temporary protected status, our neighbors are at risk of being deported to Lebanon, where the ongoing Israeli invasion — illegal Israeli invasion — and ethnic cleansing campaign has already killed 4,000 people this year. I introduced the Lebanon TPS Act because the safety of our neighbors cannot be left up to the whims of Trump and Stephen Miller.”

Mexico to Try Alleged Drug Kingpin “El Chapo Isidro” After Denying U.S. Extradition Request

Nov 24, 2026

Mexico’s military says it captured one of the leaders of the Beltrán Leyva cartel and two of his lieutenants during an operation in Sinaloa state on Friday night. The arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores sparked a wave of armed ​clashes between Mexican security forces and cartel members, who set up flaming roadblocks in some areas. Meza Flores is known as “El Chapo Isidro” and is one ​of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives. His arrest reportedly came in coordination with U.S. intelligence agencies. Mexico denied a U.S. request to extradite him, saying he will be tried in a Mexican court. The Trump administration has threatened to take unilateral ⁠military action inside Mexico after accusing the government of failing to halt narcotrafficking.

Alarm Grows over U.S. Army Plan to Explode Lead-Containing Munitions on Wednesday

Nov 24, 2026

The U.S. Army is proceeding with plans to blow up a stockpile of toxic explosives at a munitions plant in southeastern Iowa. The acting Army secretary said late Monday the “extensively mitigated, carefully controlled detonation” would occur on Wednesday morning, based on forecast wind conditions. The statement came hours after a federal court denied a request for an emergency stay from environmental groups who warn the plan could send a plume of toxic lead up to 100 miles away. In response, Senator Tammy Duckworth, an Army veteran whose home state of Illinois is potentially downwind of a lead-release disaster, wrote, “The Army still has failed to explain to the public why this detonation needs to happen this way — and too many people fear for their family’s health and safety. This is an extreme failure of communication, planning and leadership. And they must be held accountable for the harm done.”

Pete Hegseth Faces Call to Resign from His Former Chief of Staff

Nov 24, 2026

A former top aide to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is calling on him to resign, saying he has badly mismanaged both the Pentagon and the ongoing war in Iran and let showmanship get in the way of doing his job well. Joe Kasper, Hegseth’s chief of staff during the first three months of the second Trump administration, told Politico, “Pete’s been belligerent in his stewardship of an office that will outlive him or any memory of his service.”

Jimmy Gomez Quits Congress as Ethics Committee Finds Evidence of “Unwelcome Sexual Conduct”

Nov 24, 2026

In more news from Capitol Hill, outgoing California Democratic Representative Jimmy Gomez announced he’ll resign from Congress next week, after a House Ethics Committee report found substantial evidence that he had engaged in “unwelcome sexual conduct” with a female aide. The report determined Gomez’s behavior might have constituted a “criminal misdemeanor sexual abuse.” Gomez is the third congressman to resign over sexual misconduct allegations this year, following Democrat Eric Swalwell of California and Republican Tony Gonzales of Texas.

JD Vance Faces Senate Scrutiny for Allegedly Helping Campaign Donor Secure Venezuelan Oil Licenses

Nov 24, 2026

Image Credit: Reuters/Juan Carlos Hernandez

A Senate committee is investigating whether JD Vance used his position as vice president to help a major political donor secure lucrative business opportunities involving Venezuelan oil. That’s according to Reuters, which reports Vice President Vance met in December 2025 with John Addison, a trader with the commodities giant Vitol whose company went on to land ⁠special licenses to sell hundreds of millions of dollars’ worth of Venezuelan oil following the January U.S. military operation that abducted President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores. Reuters reports Vance and Addison met at Montana’s Yellowstone Club, an ultra-exclusive ski and golf resort. Both Vance and Addison have denied having the meeting, but in a letter to Vance, New Hampshire Democratic Senator Maggie Hassan writes, “Despite denials from your office and Mr. Addison, flight records place his private jet and ⁠your government plane at the same Montana airport on the day of the reported meeting.” John Addison had been an early backer of Vance, contributing $300,000 to Vance’s successful 2022 campaign for an Ohio Senate seat.

Read more news here on Havana Times.

World.title: CIA and US intelligence office suffer intrusion exposing unclassified information
World.content:
CIA and US intelligence office suffer intrusion exposing unclassified information

25th Wednesday, November 2026 - 01:08 UTC Full article

The CIA headquarters seal in Langley, Virginia

The Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and the US Office of the Director of National Intelligence recently discovered a computer intrusion that exposed unclassified information from an open-source intelligence analysis system, The New York Times reported on Tuesday. Unlike the system outages of recent weeks, attributed to technical failures, this is a security breach.

The Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and the US Office of the Director of National Intelligence recently discovered a computer intrusion that exposed unclassified information from an open-source intelligence analysis system, The New York Times reported on Tuesday. Unlike the system outages of recent weeks, attributed to technical failures, this is a security breach.

The intrusion affected a network analysts use to draw intelligence from public, unclassified material such as social media, satellite imagery and commercial databases, according to US officials and people familiar with the incident cited by the newspaper and by Reuters. It is unclear what information was compromised or how the intrusion occurred, and data from other federal agencies was probably also exposed. Those responsible have not been identified.

The Office of the Director of National Intelligence said there had been “no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems”. The CIA did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

The incident adds to a series of security breaches at federal bodies: according to Reuters, one has recently been reported at the Department of Agriculture and two at the FBI, one of them at its National Crime Information Center, while the Pentagon and the Department of Homeland Security have also been affected by cyber incidents.

It also coincides with a string of technology failures that authorities attributed to technical causes: the global Microsoft outage on November 12; the nationwide ground stop of all US flights for about four and a half hours on November 13, which the government blamed on outdated telecommunications equipment; and the outage of the National Security Agency's classified internal network on November 17, which the agency attributed to routine maintenance.

According to Uruguay's El País, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there is no evidence that the failures are linked or that the country is under a systemic attack.

World.title: Argentina enters technical recession after two quarters of contraction, the first since 2024
World.content:
Argentina enters technical recession after two quarters of contraction, the first since 2024

25th Wednesday, November 2026 - 00:55 UTC Full article

Argentina's economy has entered a technical recession for the first time since 2024

Argentina's economy has entered a technical recession, with two consecutive quarters of contraction, for the first time since the first half of 2024. GDP fell 0.6% in the second quarter, and INDEC's monthly activity indicator points to a contraction of about 1.8% between July and September.

Argentina's economy has entered a technical recession, with two consecutive quarters of contraction, for the first time since the first half of 2024. Gross domestic product fell 0.6% in the second quarter, and the monthly activity indicator of the National Institute of Statistics and Censuses (INDEC) points to a contraction of about 1.8% between July and September.

In September, activity rose 1.1% from August but fell 1.2% year on year, according to INDEC. In the first nine months of the year it has grown by just 1%, and in September it stood 2.4% below December. The institute revised July upwards, from a 2.8% fall to 2.5%, and August, from growth of 0.1% to 0.4%.

Ten of the fifteen sectors posted year-on-year falls in September. Industry fell 1.8%, commerce 2.2% and financial intermediation 11.5%, the largest negative contribution, while mining grew 11.1% and construction 3.5%. According to the consultancy ACM, agriculture and mining account for almost all of this year's growth.

Weak employment and incomes are holding back a recovery in consumption. According to calculations by the consultancy Ficonomics based on official data, 274,300 registered private-sector salaried jobs were lost between November 2023 and August 2026, a fall of 4.3%, more than half of them in industry and construction. Juan Manuel Franco, chief economist at SBS, notes that registered private real wages remain 2.3% below November 2023. Industry used 60.1% of its installed capacity in September, against 67.9% in the same month of 2023.

Analysts expect the economy may exit recession in the fourth quarter, although without a strong recovery. ACM calculates that if activity holds at September's level, the final quarter would grow 0.9%. The consultancy LCG expects a positive close but forecasts growth of at most 0.7% in 2026 and about 1.5% in 2027. “We do not expect a radical change in the short-term dynamic, but some months of growth that allow the last quarter to close positive,” it said. ACM forecasts growth of close to 1% this year and SBS around 0.6%, while Ficonomics does not rule out another quarterly fall.

Analysts warn of an additional risk: that the need to contain pressure on the exchange rate could force interest rates higher, making credit more expensive just when consumption and investment need it to recover. Country risk reached its highest level in a year in early November.

World.title: The flag at waist height: the rules for visiting the Argentine Military Cemetery in the Falklands
World.content:
The flag at waist height: the rules for visiting the Argentine Military Cemetery in the Falklands

24th Tuesday, November 2026 - 22:31 UTC Full article

The rules allow the Argentine flag to be placed on a grave or cross, without inscriptions or political statements, although it may bear the name of the fallen or their unit

Tourism authorities in the Falklands have asked operators to remind visitors of the rules of conduct at the Argentine Military Cemetery at Darwin, while a programme to repair its stonework, which has deteriorated over time, is being drawn up. The rules, set out in a bilingual document, allow the Argentine flag to be placed on graves but consider holding it above waist height a political gesture.

The Falkland Islands Tourist Board circulated a message to tourism operators on Monday on behalf of Stanley Growers Limited, the company that carries out maintenance at the cemetery and liaises with those responsible for the site on its care. According to the text, “some of the stonework has deteriorated over time”, and a programme of repair and refurbishment is being developed “in consultation with the relevant parties responsible for the cemetery”. While that work progresses, the company asks visitors to treat the site and its structures “with appropriate care and respect”.

Operators are asked to have their guides and drivers brief visitors on the rules before arrival or give them a copy of the document, keep copies in vehicles and remind visitors of the rules during the visit. They must also ensure visitors do not touch, climb on, lean on or attach anything to the structures, observe temporary warning signs, barriers or safety tape, and report any damage or safety concerns. “The intention is not to restrict respectful visits to the cemetery,” the message stresses, but to protect the site while the condition of the stonework is assessed.

The attached document, bearing the letterhead of the Commission of Relatives of the Fallen in the Malvinas and South Atlantic Islands, states that its spirit is “to facilitate coexistence between the Islands and the Continent and consolidate the ties of Peace”. “This Cemetery, like all Military Cemeteries, is above national politics,” it says. “When someone dies in a battle wearing the uniform of their country, it does not matter which side or what colour the uniform is, the fallen have the right to due respect.” The text notes that the islanders respect the combatants' resting place and ask, in turn, that their own feelings be respected.

The rules allow the Argentine flag to be placed on a grave or cross, without inscriptions or political statements, although it may bear the name of the fallen or their unit. If held unfurled by hand, for example because of the wind, it must be kept no higher than the waist: holding it above that height “is considered a sample for political purposes and is not allowed”. Plaques may not be fixed to the crosses or to the wall of the cenotaph, which bears the 649 names of those who fell in the conflict, and inscriptions are banned. Visitors may move freely and take photographs. Those who break the rules “are exposed to being removed from the place and even deported”, the document warns.

The cemetery, near the settlement of Darwin on East Falkland, holds more than 230 graves of Argentine soldiers. Relatives inaugurated the cenotaph in 2004, and since 2017 a humanitarian project led by the International Committee of the Red Cross has identified more than a hundred soldiers buried without a name. Next year marks the 45th anniversary of the war, which the British Embassy in Buenos Aires has said will be commemorated “with respect and sensitivity” together with veterans and families from both countries.

Argentine Cemetery - Rules of Conduct by MercoPress

World.title: Princess Anne visits South Georgia and sees British Antarctic Survey science at first hand
World.content:
Princess Anne visits South Georgia and sees British Antarctic Survey science at first hand

24th Tuesday, November 2026 - 13:31 UTC Full article

Photo: Government of South Georgia & the South Sandwich Islands

Princess Anne, the sister of King Charles III, visited South Georgia as part of her South Atlantic tour, meeting British Antarctic Survey scientists and staff stationed on the island, the Government of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands said on Monday. The visit to the islands, which began in the Falklands, was rejected by Argentina as a “provocation”.

The Princess, accompanied by her husband, Vice Admiral Sir Tim Laurence, experienced “firsthand the work of those who live and work on this remarkable Island”, the local government said in a series of posts on X, accompanied by photographs. At King Edward Point she met the British Antarctic Survey team, the UK's national operator in Antarctica, which explained the scientific research taking place on the island. At that station, the groundfish survey marks 40 years this season.

1/5 Her Royal Highness The Princess Royal and Vice Admiral Sir Tim Laurence visited South Georgia, experiencing firsthand the work of those who live and work on this remarkable Island. #SGSSI #RoyalVisit https://t.co/twCuKDGk92 — Government SGSSI (@GovSGSSI) November 23, 2026

The Princess also met Government staff stationed on the island, “whose work is instrumental to South Georgia's operations, heritage and environment”, and visited its post office, which connects this remote territory with the rest of the world. The local government also highlighted the icebergs, landscapes and wildlife that accompanied the journey. The posts do not give the date of the visit or mention the planned programme, which included unveiling a memorial at a former whaling station, opening the restored Stromness Managers' Villa and commemorating the explorer Sir Ernest Shackleton.

The Princess, Patron of the South Georgia Heritage Trust, an organisation dedicated to protecting the island's heritage and environment, arrived in the islands on November 9. The following day she opened Stanley's new National Sports Complex, an investment of about £5 million.

On November 17, the Argentine government rejected the visit, calling it a “provocation” at a time when, according to Buenos Aires, the United Kingdom is advancing hydrocarbon exploitation in waters whose sovereignty Argentina claims. Argentina had also protested against the Princess's previous visit in 2022. The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea will announce on Saturday, November 28, its decision on Argentina's request to halt the Sea Lion oil project.

World.title: Argentina receives two bids for the Ushuaia naval base pier amid Sea Lion tensions
World.content:
Argentina receives two bids for the Ushuaia naval base pier amid Sea Lion tensions

24th Tuesday, November 2026 - 12:39 UTC Full article

The Ushuaia naval base, where the new military pier will be built.

The Argentine government has received two bids to build the military pier at the Ushuaia integrated naval base, a project President Javier Milei relaunched in September, four days before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea rules on Argentina's request to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands.

The Argentine government has received two bids to build the military pier at the Ushuaia integrated naval base, a project President Javier Milei relaunched in September to turn the country into a “central logistics hub of the South Atlantic”, four days before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea rules on Argentina's request to halt the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands.

Of the 15 companies that had expressed interest, only two submitted proposals, both above the official budget of about 189.3 billion pesos set by the Navy, according to Infobae. Concret Nor bid about 192 billion pesos, 1.4% more, and Lemiro Pablo Pietroboni about 210.3 billion, 11.1% above. Both companies have already won sections of the privatisation of the national road network. The process now moves to technical and economic evaluation.

The first phase envisages building, over 18 months from early 2027, the first 240 metres of the pier, to be used by boats of the Navy's Southern Patrol Division. The full project, with a 585-metre main pier and the involvement of the state shipyard Tandanor, is due to be completed in 2029 at an estimated cost of US$450 million to US$500 million, and aims to turn Ushuaia into a logistics hub for operations in Antarctica. Its second stage depends on funds included in the 2027 budget, still under debate in Congress.

The base is not a new initiative. It stems from a 1990 plan that formally began in 2022 under Alberto Fernández's government and was virtually halted in December 2023 at 9% completion. Milei relaunched it on September 4 through a decree reallocating Defence Ministry funds, on the same day he announced sanctions against companies linked to Sea Lion.

Those sanctions have already had an effect. Britain's Rockhopper Exploration reported on November 20 that its partner and the project's operator, Israel's Navitas Petroleum, is at an advanced stage of replacing two contractors that declined to fulfil their contracts for fear of Argentine sanctions, although it said it does not expect a significant adverse impact on the timetable. According to Argentina's Foreign Ministry, the Singapore shipyard Seatrium is also considering cancelling the upgrade of the project's production vessel.

The International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea will announce on Saturday, November 28, its decision on the provisional measures requested by Argentina, while the arbitral tribunal that will rule on the merits of the dispute is constituted.

World.title: Colombia's peace deal turns ten with 36% of its commitments fulfilled
World.content:
Colombia's peace deal turns ten with 36% of its commitments fulfilled

24th Tuesday, November 2026 - 12:35 UTC Full article

Juan Manuel Santos (L) and FARC leader Rodrigo Londoño, known as Timochenko, shake hands next to Cuban leader Raúl Castro, after the peace agreement.

The peace agreement between the Colombian state and the former FARC guerrillas turns ten on Tuesday with only 36% of its commitments fulfilled, according to the Kroc Institute, more than 500 former fighters killed and a government that considers it a mistake.

The peace agreement between the Colombian state and the former FARC guerrillas turns ten on Tuesday with only 36% of its commitments fulfilled, according to the Kroc Institute, more than 500 former fighters killed and a government, that of President Abelardo de la Espriella, which has cut back the institutions created by the deal and considers it a mistake.

The agreement was signed on November 24, 2016, at the Teatro Colón in Bogotá, after Colombians narrowly rejected a first text in a referendum and Juan Manuel Santos's government renegotiated it. More than 13,600 fighters handed over their weapons, and in 2017 the country recorded its lowest homicide rate in more than three decades.

Implementation, however, has been slow and uneven under three governments. Rural reform, the first point of the agreement, promised to hand three million hectares to landless farmers within 12 years; at the current pace, the Comptroller's Office estimates it would take about 400 years. According to the Ombudsman's Office, 521 signatories of the agreement have been killed over the past decade. The UN Verification Mission confirmed 13 killings of former fighters in 2026 up to September, and attempted murders rose from five in 2025 to 15.

In his three months in office, De la Espriella has cut the budget of the Special Jurisdiction for Peace, the court that tries former guerrillas and soldiers, broken off talks with armed groups, which he declared terrorists, and stepped up military offensives. “The false peace has cost Colombia dearly!” he said on the eve of the anniversary, calling the agreement a “mess”. At his government's request, the UN mission, renewed for a year, will no longer monitor rural reform, a decision backed by the United States.

Santos, who received the Nobel Peace Prize for the agreement, argues that the problem is not the deal but the failure to implement it. “The lack of implementation is what has caused many of the problems,” he said.

The state never filled the territories left by the FARC. The National Liberation Army, dissidents who rejected the agreement and the Clan del Golfo now fight over cocaine routes, gold mines and border crossings. According to the armed forces, these groups have some 29,000 members in 165 structures, compared with about 13,000 in 2022.

“We did not sign a peace agreement to die for it,” Osvaldo Mendoza, a former fighter who organised disarmament in a village in Cauca department, told El País.

World.title: Pneumonia complicates Jair Bolsonaro's hospital stay in Brasília
World.content:
Pneumonia complicates Jair Bolsonaro's hospital stay in Brasília

23rd Monday, November 2026 - 22:09 UTC Full article

Jair Bolsonaro, 71, remains in intensive care at the DF Star hospital.

Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro has been diagnosed with pneumonia at the Brasília hospital where he has been admitted since Friday with an intestinal obstruction, his doctors said on Monday, although they ruled out surgery after his intestinal condition improved.

Former Brazilian President Jair Bolsonaro has been diagnosed with pneumonia at the Brasília hospital where he has been admitted since Friday with an intestinal obstruction, his doctors said on Monday, although they ruled out surgery after his intestinal condition improved.

Cardiologist Brasil Caiado told a press conference that Bolsonaro's health had improved since his admission, but that on Sunday afternoon he suffered chills, pain and vomiting. Tests detected bilateral aspiration pneumonia, although less serious than the one diagnosed during another hospital stay in March, according to the doctors.

Surgeon Cláudio Birolini said the intestinal obstruction, the reason for his admission, had improved, so doctors opted to continue clinical treatment rather than operate. The 71-year-old former president will remain in the intensive care unit of the DF Star hospital, and there is no forecast for his discharge.

Bolsonaro, who governed from 2019 to 2022, has had numerous hospital stays and operations since he was stabbed in the abdomen at a campaign event in September 2018. His fragile health was one of the arguments the Supreme Federal Court considered in allowing him to serve under house arrest the 27-year sentence imposed on him for plotting a coup. The court will vote between December 4 and 15 on the constitutionality of a law that reduces the sentences of those convicted in the coup plot.

World.title: UK expresses support for Pedro Alliana's government in Paraguay
World.content:
UK expresses support for Pedro Alliana's government in Paraguay

23rd Monday, November 2026 - 22:05 UTC Full article

Pedro Alliana is sworn in as president of Paraguay, next to his wife.

The United Kingdom has expressed its support for the government of Paraguayan President Pedro Alliana, who took office just over two weeks ago after the removal of Santiago Peña over the collapse of Ueno Bank, Paraguay's Foreign Ministry said on Monday.

The United Kingdom has expressed its support for the government of Paraguayan President Pedro Alliana, who took office just over two weeks ago after the removal of Santiago Peña over the collapse of Ueno Bank, Paraguay's Foreign Ministry said on Monday.

Paraguayan Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez received a call from Chris Elmore, Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State at the UK Foreign Office, “who conveyed his country's support” for Alliana's administration, the ministry said in a statement. The two reviewed the main issues on the bilateral agenda and agreed on a round of political consultations for early 2027.

Since taking office, Alliana has received calls from Argentine President Javier Milei, Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

Alliana, previously vice-president, was sworn in on November 6 amid the crisis over the takeover of Ueno Bank, a bank linked to Peña that received large deposits from public bodies during his term, including five pension funds. Peña remains in pre-trial detention at a military facility, charged with breach of trust, self-serving administration and criminal association. Former Central Bank president Carlos Carvallo, also in pre-trial detention, is charged in the same case.

World.title: In Beijing, Ebrard pushes for more Mexican exports to China
World.content:
Remaining in China after last week’s close of the APEC summit, Economy Minister Marcelo Ebrard took advantage of the 11th Mexico-China High-Level Group Meeting to arrange for a working group to be formed to address Mexico’s gaping trade deficit with the Asian giant.

Ebrard met with his Chinese counterpart, Commerce Minister Wentao Wang, in Beijing — a 2,000-kilometer flight from Shenzhen, the site of the APEC summit — to urge the establishment of new mechanisms to boost Mexican exports to China.

Resultados de la reunión del Grupo de Alto Nivel México-China https://t.co/YUgHILOlH0 — Marcelo Ebrard C. (@m_ebrard) November 23, 2026

He emphasized the need to change the “persistent and growing” trade imbalance between Mexico and China. While China is projected to export more than uS $130 billion worth of goods to Mexico this year, Mexico will likely export only around $10 billion to China.

The hope is that the new bilateral working group will create the necessary protocols to allow the export of certain Mexican products, such as avocados, lemons, beef, pork, sorghum and processed seafood, some of which have been in the works for a decade.

“Our ability to export more to China depends on the authorization of all these protocols, so that the balance between imports and exports improves in Mexico’s favor,” Ebrard said. “That is fair and reasonable.”

Several Mexican companies are prepared to export their products if a favorable business environment can be established. For example, the Mexican state-owned company Exportadora de Sal (Salt Exporter) hopes to increase its market share in China, having provided a proposal to supply up to 10 million tonnes of salt over four years.

After attending the APEC meeting, President Sheinbaum stressed that deepening trade ties with China would not impede Mexico’s bilateral relationship with the United States.

“The economic integration between Mexico and the U.S. is very significant,” Sheinbaum said during a press conference. “What we want is greater cooperation with China on various issues, from scientific research to tourism, and everything related to this collaboration.”

At the same time, Sheinbaum ruled out for now the negotiation of a free-trade agreement with China.

With reports from La Jornada, Líder Empresarial and El Financiero

World.title: Nescafé coffee producers protest in southern Mexico over low pay
World.content:
Coffee producers from the Costa, Sierra and Frontera regions of Chiapas – Mexico’s largest coffee-producing state – marched on Monday to protest against the low prices that the multinational food company Nestlé pays them to produce coffee beans for Nescafé.

The demonstration moved through the main streets of Tapachula and concluded with a rally in front of the municipal government building.

Protestan #Productores de #Café contra la empresa #Nestlé.

En #Tapachula cerca de 400 #Cafeticultores se manifiestan frente al palacio municipal contra la empresa global #NESCAFÉ exigiendo mejores precios al producto que le venden.

Les están comprando por debajo del precio de producción. #Chiapas — Gabriela Coutiño (@GabyCoutino) November 23, 2026

“We harvest the coffee, tend to it all year round, and we get paid 43 pesos (US $2.20) per kilogram. That same coffee sells for 580 pesos ($29) in the supermarket,” the protesters pointed out.

The farmers are demanding a fair price of at least 60 pesos ($3) per kg.

Meanwhile, farmer Eduardo Camarena told the newspaper La Jornada that the discontent extends throughout at least twenty municipalities and that the issue affects 165,000 families.

He noted that the gap between the price Nestlé pays farmers and the coffee’s retail price does not result in higher earnings for producers.

Camarena added that although farmers have held talks with the company, Nestlé has refused to adjust prices in response to the cost increases producers have faced. Moreover, he accused the company of centralizing the coffee market in the border region.

Protesters requested the intervention of the Chiapas state government to facilitate negotiations with Nestlé to agree on what they consider a fair price for their coffee.

“The cost of production, plus a decent profit for the producer — that is what we are asking for; it’s only fair,” he stressed.

Figures from the Agriculture and Rural Development Ministry (Sader) revealed that in Mexico, approximately 701,735 hectares across 10 states are dedicated to growing coffee beans, with national production expected to exceed one million tonnes by the end of 2026.

Production is spearheaded by Chiapas, with a contribution of 392,000 tonnes of beans per year, followed by Veracruz, with 256,000 and Puebla, with 225,000.

With reports from La Jornada and Diario de Chiapas

World.title: Mexico attracts record US $43.1B in FDI through September, but new investment plunges 42%
World.content:
Listen to this article

Mexico received a record-high US $43.09 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI) in the first nine months of 2026, a 5.3% year-on-year increase, the federal Economy Ministry (SE) reported Tuesday.

The figure exceeds the total FDI Mexico attracted in 2025 — $40.87 billion — but new investment declined 42.1% compared to the January-September period of last year.

The SE said in a press release that the FDI result “reflects the strength of the country’s macroeconomic and institutional foundations, as well as the momentum of Plan México, and reaffirms Mexico’s status as one of the world’s most attractive destinations for foreign investment.”

FDI in Mexico has increased in recent years amid the nearshoring trend, although some analysts argue that the country has yet to fully capitalize on the opportunity.

The Economy Ministry highlighted that Mexico was the world’s sixth-largest recipient of FDI in the first half of 2026, behind the United States, China, the Netherlands, Brazil and the Czech Republic, according to OECD data.

Mexico received $23.591 billion in FDI in the first quarter of 2026 and an additional $11.377 billion in the second quarter to bring the six-month total to $34.968 billion. The third quarter total was $8.122 billion.

The lion’s share of FDI came from the reinvestment of profits

According to the SE, foreign companies already operating in Mexico reinvested $34.975 billion in profits between January and September. Thus, 81.2% of Mexico’s FDI total came from the reinvestment of profits.

The dollar total increased 26% year over year to reach a record high, reflecting “foreign investors’ confidence in continuing to bet on our country over the medium and long term,” according to the SE.

The second-largest share of FDI came from the transfer of funds between companies within the same corporate group. Those transfers totaled $4.315 billion between January and September, representing 10% of the FDI total.

The dollar value of transfers between companies declined 34.6% compared to the same period of last year.

Finally, new investment in Mexico accounted for 8.8% of the FDI total in the first nine months of the year, down from a 16% share in the same period of last year. New FDI totaled $3.8 billion, down 42.1% from $6.563 billion in the first nine months of 2025.

The SE didn’t mention the year-over-year decline in overall new investment, but highlighted that new investment in Mexico’s manufacturing sector increased 58.8% to reach $1.124 billion.

The ministry reported that new foreign investment in the transport equipment sector, which includes automotive, aerospace and train production, surged 999.3% annually, while new FDI in the computer/electronic components sector increased 605.2%.

“This reflects the strength of domestic production chains and foreign investors’ confidence in Mexico as a high value-added manufacturing hub,” the SE said.

The think tank México ¿Cómo Vamos? has set a target for Mexico to attract $10 billion annually in new foreign investment. With cumulative new investment at just $3.8 billion through the first three quarters of the year, the think tank gives Mexico a yellow light — the middle rating in its three-color economic traffic-light system.

Over three-quarters of FDI came from just 5 countries

In the first nine months of 2026, the United States retained its position as the leading source of FDI in Mexico. U.S. companies invested $19.334 billion in Mexico in the period, accounting for 44.9% of the total.

The next largest sources of FDI in Mexico were:

Spain: $6.208 billion (14.4% of the FDI total between January and September)

Germany: $2.895 billion (6.7%)

The United Kingdom: $2.586 billion (6%)

Canada: $2.447 billion (5.7%)

The five top sources of FDI in Mexico accounted for 77.7% of total foreign direct investment in the country in the first nine months of the year. The SE also highlighted that 50.5% of FDI came from the United States and Canada, reflecting what it described as “the deep integration of North American value chains.”

The SE data indicates that 22.3% of FDI in Mexico between January and September came from countries outside the top five investors. Chinese investment in Mexico has increased in recent years, but the East Asian nation was not among the top 10 investors in the country in the first half of the year. The SE didn’t report an investment total for China in the first nine months of 2026.

Mexico City was easily the top FDI recipient

The SE reported that Mexico City — where many large foreign companies have offices — remained the leading destination for FDI in the first nine months of 2026. The capital received $19.602 billion during the period, accounting for 45.5% of total FDI.

The next biggest recipients of FDI were:

Nuevo León: $4.431 billion (10.3% of the FDI total)

Jalisco: $2.707 billion (6.3%)

Baja California: $2.362 billion (5.5%)

Puebla: $1.753 billion (4.1%)

The five top recipients of FDI in Mexico received 71.7% of total foreign direct investment in the country in the first nine months of the year.

Twenty-seven states shared the remaining 28.3% in FDI, which totaled $12.236 billion.

Almost 45% of FDI went to Mexico’s manufacturing sector

Mexico’s large manufacturing industry was the top recipient of FDI between January and September, receiving $19.231 billion, representing 44.6% of the total. FDI in the manufacturing sector increased 26.6% compared to the same period of last year.

The SE reported that the increase in FDI in the manufacturing industry was mainly driven by higher investment in the production of computer/communications equipment and electronic components ($1.814 billion); beverages and tobacco ($1.804 billion); food ($1.309 billion); and chemicals ($1.271 billion).

Mexico’s exports of computer equipment, including AI servers, have surged this year, fueled by growing demand amid the AI boom in the United States.

The financial services and insurance sector was the second-largest recipient of FDI, after manufacturing. The sector received $10.635 billion in FDI between January and September, representing 24.7% of the total. Foreign investment in the financial services and insurance sector grew 3.7% year over year.

The next largest recipients of FDI in the first nine months of 2026 were:

The transport, postal services and storage sector: $3.099 billion (7.2% of the FDI total). Foreign investment in this sector increased 59.3% year over year.

The construction sector: $2.481 billion (5.8%)

The temporary accommodation sector: $1.826 billion (4.2%)

The remaining 13.5% of FDI totaling $5.818 billion went to other sectors of Mexico’s economy.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: It’s official! Mexico will co-host the 2031 FIFA Women’s World Cup
World.content:
As expected, Mexico will serve as co-host of the FIFA Women’s World Cup in 2031, an assignment that the Claudia Sheinbaum administration said “reaffirms Mexico’s organizational capacity and its position as a great host of international sporting events.”

“After the international exposure and excellent image that Mexico offered to the world as host of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, this new designation confirms that our country has the infrastructure, experience, human talent and organizational capacity to host competitions of global scope,” the government said in a press release.

¡EL SUEÑO DE JUGAR UN MUNDIAL EN CASA SERÁ UNA REALIDAD!🥹🇲🇽 Las futbolistas mexicanas no ocultaron su emoción después de la confirmación de México como anfitrión de la Copa Mundial Femenina de 2031. Una noticia que ilusiona a las nuevas generaciones y representa una oportunidad histórica para seguir impulsando el futbol femenil en nuestro país. — Claro Sports (@ClaroSports) November 23, 2026

As the lone proposal for the 2031 “Mundial,” the joint Mexico-U.S.-Costa Rica-Jamaica bid was approved by FIFA on Monday. The four North American nations will play host to a newly expanded 48-team tournament, up from the 32 participants in next year’s Cup in Brazil.

This will be the first time Mexico stages the Women’s World Cup and national soccer federation officials are lobbying to have a significant presence, offering to host the final, the opening match and the tournament draw.

In the men’s World Cup (which Mexico co-hosted alongside the United States and Canada), Mexico hosted the inaugural match (and only 13 of 104 total games), while the final and the draw were held in the United States.

Presently, there are no binding commitments from host cities or stadiums. FIFA’s bid evaluation report listed four primary Mexican host cities — Mexico City, Guadalajara, Monterrey and Torreón (Coahuila) — while Mexican officials proposed additional candidate cities.

FIFA announced that 42 stadiums across the four countries have signed Memorandums of Understanding, demonstrating “each stakeholder’s motivation to participate in the organization of the tournament.”

Mexico’s National Commission for Physical Culture and Sport described the hosting opportunity as “a platform to inspire new generations, expand opportunities for participation, and demonstrate that Mexican girls and young women can find in sport a path to develop, compete and achieve their dreams.”

Looking beyond the tournament, the government said it hopes “to leverage its legacy so that women’s soccer reaches more schools, neighborhoods and communities; so that more and more girls have access to decent and safe sports spaces, and so that talent finds opportunities to develop.”

With reports from Record, El Universal, The Athletic, ESPN and Milenio

World.title: Nearly half of Mexican firms report that US tariffs impact their cost structure
World.content:
U.S. tariffs have had an impact on the cost structure of 45% of companies in Mexico, a global survey conducted by HSBC revealed, with most businesses (68%) believing that the resulting high costs will continue through the next few years.

According to the survey, conducted among 500 companies in Mexico, tariff costs affected expenses more than supplier issues (40%) and raw material prices (38%).

Which of the following have impacted your cost base over the past 6 months?

Nevertheless, 90% of Mexican business owners plan to expand their international business in the next two years. Such optimism about bilateral trade despite the tariffs has actually strengthened since last year’s HSBC survey, when 86% of Mexican businesses foresaw a rise in the international exchange of goods,

Maximiliano Rossi, regional director of Global Trade Solutions at HSBC Mexico and Latin America, told Imagen Radio that the survey’s offsetting findings (tariff impact and trade expansion) are notable, particularly in light of “the uncertainty surrounding [U.S.-Mexico trade] negotiations and the issue of tariffs.”

Rossi said companies established in Mexico have “modified operating processes and supply networks to mitigate the financial impact of trade barriers and maintain competitiveness in international markets.”

In this regard, global trade has begun to abandon the indiscriminate opening and outsourcing scheme toward Asia of the 1980s and 1990s and regional blocs are now playing a more important role.

As such, 83% of companies indicated that the changes made to respond to trade uncertainty and disruptions have been effective.

Survey respondents confirmed that the changes are reshaping suppliers, energy security, inventory and production footprints. “With further action planned, the redesign of trade networks remains an ongoing process rather than a one-off response to disruption,” the HSBC report says.

Rossi went further, saying that “supply chains are adapting, and Mexico has a unique, unparalleled situation.”

AI adoption as tariff adaptation

Furthermore, as businesses “expand internationally through the transformation of supply chains, the adoption of digital channels and the use of digital intelligence (AI) tools” are becoming increasingly important.

Of note, the HSBC survey found that AI adoption is accelerating faster than AI oversight.

While 85% have already deployed AI in at least one trade-related function, 76% have implemented fewer than five of the 10 AI safeguards assessed in the survey.

In other findings, 73% said changes made to their supply chains have improved their cash flow and working capital, and 49% of firms said they have optimized their trade networks.

With reports from Expansión and Imagen Radio

World.title: MND Local Puerto Vallarta: All-ages activities for family visits to Vallarta
World.content:
Living on the Nayarit coast on Banderas Bay for more than 11 years, with family and friends who like to visit often, we’re always on the lookout for events and activities everyone would enjoy — from kids to grandparents. As high season kicks off in Puerto Vallarta and more families and friends are coming together, here are some of our favorite all-ages activities, plus what’s on our list to check out.

Make your own chocolate

Did you know the chocolate you love today has its origins in Mexico? The Mokaya in Chiapas were the first to turn cacao into chocolate, circa 1900 B.C. Subsequent civilizations such as the Olmecs, Maya and Mexica (also known as the Aztecs) further expanded the production and uses of cacao, from fermented drinks to currency.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Mente Cacao (@mentecacao)

As a national heritage food, today cacao is used and celebrated all over Mexico, from spicy moles and sweet treats to hot beverages and ceremonies. For a chocoholic like me, Mexico is the place to be.

My parents are also chocolate lovers, so when they visited last year, we booked a chocolate-making workshop at ChocoMuseo in downtown Vallarta. Our workshop leader was knowledgeable and entertaining, sharing the history of chocolate in Mexico and teaching us the intricacies of chocolate making. We came away with more than a dozen uniquely flavored chocolates apiece, which we made from scratch starting with grinding cacao beans.

ChocoMuseo is one of several local chocolate shops and cultivators that offer chocolate-making workshops in Vallarta, including Xocodiva, Mente Cacao in Nuevo Vallarta (which makes the best chocolate ice cream I’ve ever tasted, and I’ve eaten a lot of chocolate ice cream in my 54 years) and Planeta Cacao.

Explore nature without breaking a sweat

Banderas Bay and the rivers and mountains that surround it are brimming with beautiful, bold and curious wildlife, from brightly colored macaws and noisy chachalacas to lumbering crocodiles and iguanas the size of large dogs. The area is also home to unique plant life and pollinators that are becoming harder to see as development encroaches on their native habitats.

But you don’t have to hike through the jungle to view nature’s treasures, thanks to gardens and sanctuaries that make getting up close and personal with local wildlife and plants possible and the experience more accessible for all ages. These include the Vallarta Botanical Gardens (which also has a lovely restaurant), Santuario de Guacamayas (a conservation center for the Mexican green macaws) and El Cora Crocodile Sanctuary in Nuevo Vallarta. Or just take a walk alongside the Marina Golf Course and you’ll likely happen upon a few crocodiles wading or lounging at the ponds’ edges, or giant iguanas sunbathing in the middle of the afternoon.

And of course, el rey of the bay — humpback whales — start making their appearance in December when ocean temperatures cool down. The official start of whale-watching season this year is Dec. 8, and several outfitters can take the family out for a viewing trip, a must-do for anyone coming to Vallarta this time of year.

Go see a show

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Movie Picnic | Cine al aire libre (@moviepicnic)

Vallarta has tons of entertainment options, from outdoor movies to musical revues and simple community theater to high-production shows. Most are open to all ages (for some shows, children under 18 must be accompanied by an adult) and cater to a variety of tastes and budgets.

From Nov. 12 to May 27, Puerto de Luna Hotel hosts Movie + Picnic outdoor cinema in its garden area with family-friendly movies on Thursdays, Fridays and Saturdays. This week (Nov. 26-28), the movies are “Top Gun: Maverick,” “Billy Elliot” and “Klaus.” Also, now through Dec. 6, Teatro Sin Borders, the only English-language theater in Vallarta, is presenting the crime comedy “Laughs in Spanish.” If your family speaks Spanish, Cerka, a community theater in Nuevo Vallarta, has performances throughout the year (as well as acting and singing classes).

For those looking for something extra spectacular, LUDÕ, an underwater acrobatics show from Cirque du Soleil at VidantaWorld, is bound to take your breath away (and make you wonder how the acrobats hold their breath so long!). The amphitheater where the production takes place is equally impressive. Audiences sit inside a 360-degree aquarium where acrobats perform on stage and in the water behind the aquarium walls. The show recently received the Thea Award for Outstanding Achievement from the Themed Entertainment Association. This one’s on our list to check out as a possible holiday gift for the family.

Make your own art

Visiting Mexico will definitely inspire your inner artist. If your family likes to create, Puerto Vallarta has many artist spaces and classes throughout the year. A few include the Artist Hour at the Living Room Bookstore and Cafe in the Marina, where local artists teach classes such as painting, ceramics and more on Thursday afternoons. Also, Arte Vallarta Museo in the Romantic Zone and The Annex Studio and Gallery, a community art space near Playa Camarones, offer classes in printing, painting, ceramics, mosaic, folk art, weaving and more.

What are your favorite family-friendly activities and events in Vallarta? Drop your recommendations in the comments section below.

Debbie Slobe is a writer and communications strategist based in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco. She blogs at Mexpatmama.com and is a senior program director at Resource Media. Find her on Instagram and Facebook.

World.title: Inflation rises to nearly 4% in first half of November
World.content:
Annual headline inflation in Mexico ticked up to 3.96% in the first half of November, the highest rate since early May, fueled in part by a 20% year-over-year surge in fruit and vegetable prices.

Reported by the national statistics agency INEGI on Tuesday, the headline rate came in slightly above the 3.92% median forecast of economists surveyed by Reuters.

It is 0.21 percentage points higher than the 3.75% reading for October. The last time Mexico’s annual headline rate was higher was in the first half of May, at 4.11%.

The annual headline rate has now risen in five consecutive quincenas (15-day-periods) between the first half of September and the first half of November. It appears likely that headline inflation will rise for a fourth consecutive month in November after declining every month between April and July.

INEGI also reported on Tuesday that Mexico’s annual core inflation rate — which excludes volatile food and energy prices — was 3.68% in the first half of November, down from 3.80% across October. That was lower than the 3.88% forecast of economists surveyed by Reuters. The annual core rate — which is watched closely by economists and policymakers — was the lowest since the first quincena of March.

INEGI also reported that consumer prices increased 0.54% in the first half of November compared to the second half of October.

The publication of the latest inflation data comes almost three weeks after the Bank of Mexico board voted in favor of lowering the central bank’s benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 6.25%. Three of five board members voted in favor of the cut, despite recent increases in Mexico’s headline inflation rate. The board is expected to vote in favor of maintaining the central bank’s key rate at 6.25% at its final monetary policy meeting for 2026 on Dec. 17.

The Bank of Mexico targets an annual headline rate of 3%, with a tolerance range of 2%-4%.

Inflation data in detail

INEGI’s data shows that fruit and vegetable prices were 20.05% higher in the first half of November than a year earlier. Those prices are sensitive to adverse weather conditions, which can disrupt production and reduce supply.

Compared to the second half of October, prices for green tomatoes surged 39.31% in the first half of November, while regular tomatoes were 28.95% more expensive and poblano chiles were 26.97% dearer.

Annual inflation rates in the first half of November for other categories monitored by INEGI were as follows.

4.66% for processed food, beverages and tobacco

1.86% for non-food goods.

4.17% for services.

3.53% for energy, including electricity and gasoline.

Meat prices fell 2.15% on a year-over-year basis. Annual inflation for agricultural products (fruit, vegetables and meat) was 6.65% in the first half of November.

With reports from La Jornada and Reuters

World.title: Aeroméxico now offers 7-day Mexico City stopovers as tourism to the capital surges
World.content:
Mexico City’s government wants travelers who change planes in the capital to stay a while.

The city’s Tourism Ministry and the airline Aeroméxico announced on Nov. 18 a “stopover” program that lets connecting passengers stay more than 24 hours and up to seven days before continuing to their final destination. Travelers can take advantage of the offer from both the Mexico City International Airport (AICM) and the Felipe Ángeles International Airport (AIFA), and can use it on the outbound trip, the return or both.

The goal, according to a press release, is to lengthen visits and increase tourist spending. The program is meant to showcase the capital’s culture, food, entertainment, hotels, attractions and shopping.

“In Mexico City, there are 3,000 activities per day, so a stopover is a wonderful way for visitors and tourists to easily extend their stay,” said Tourism Minister Alejandra Frausto Guerrero during the program’s announcement.

For Aeroméxico, it’s a chance to make use of its main hub and strengthen the capital’s role as a gateway for domestic and international travelers.

Jennie Shrem Serur, director general of the city’s Tourism Promotion Institute, said the agency is working with the airline on a broader strategy that includes developing experiences, routes and tours to be offered through Aeroméxico’s platform. The aim, she said, is for travelers to see the capital as a reason to pause, not merely a stop on the way elsewhere.

The program applies in every market where Aeroméxico operates, as long as the itinerary connects in Mexico City. It is offered in all cabins and fare classes, with costs, conditions and baggage allowances varying by fare. When scheduling a flight online, select the option for “stopover;” round-trip flights will permit travelers to make two stopovers in Mexico City: one on their way out and one on the way back.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Daura Emir Suspended Over Assault Claim
World.content:
A tourist’s smart-glasses video has put a traditional ruler’s conduct under official review in northern Nigeria, while the allegation remains unproven and disputed.

Nigeria: Katsina State

Katsina State in north-west Nigeria has barred the Emir of Daura, Alhaji Faruk Umar Faruk, from all official engagements and travel after a foreign tourist alleged that he sexually assaulted her at his palace. The state government announced the step on Tuesday 24 November 2026 and set up a committee to investigate.

She told Tribune Online it was the only sexual harassment she met on the whole tour, and that she might not have been the first woman to experience such conduct but could have been the first to record it.

Premium Times, an Abuja-based investigative newspaper, reported on 22 November that it examined a 60-second copy of the video, which shows a close-range encounter but whose camera angles do not conclusively establish the alleged touching. The newspaper added that the copy has not been independently authenticated against the original recording.

Blueprint, a Nigerian newspaper, reported on 23 November that Instagram removed the original post. Mirka says she did not delete it, believes mass reporting triggered an algorithm and has asked for human review, while Meta, Instagram’s parent company, had not explained.

An unnamed palace source told the Lagos daily Punch as Premium Times reported on 22 November, that her account was fabricated, though the source acknowledged she visited. That denial rests on one anonymous person, and the emir had not personally issued a detailed response by 24 November.

Ibrahim Usman Murtala, spokesman of the Daura Emirate Council, the emirate’s governing body, confirmed by phone on Monday 23 November that the emirate knew of the video and had begun a review to establish whether it was authentic or altered. He said the council would issue an official statement afterwards.

The Katsina government statement, issued by Commissioner for Information and Culture Dr Bala Salisu Zango, said Governor Dikko Umaru Radda directed a committee to investigate the allegation and advise the government on what to do. It suspended all official engagements and travels of the emir, and Blueprint reported that the bar stays pending the outcome of the investigation.

The government assured the public that justice would be served and said the committee’s findings and recommendations would be fully implemented. It urged residents to stay calm and law-abiding, but published no committee members, terms of reference or deadline.

Amnesty International Nigeria, the national branch of the human-rights group, urged the police and the Katsina government on Sunday 22 November to investigate effectively, through due process and a fair trial. Blueprint reported on 24 November that Amnesty also condemned reported death threats and abusive messages against Mirka, who reportedly received hundreds, and asked police to protect her.

Blueprint reported on 23 November that the Katsina Police Command said it had received no formal complaint. Nothing in the public record shows a criminal complaint.

Blueprint reported that Col. Abubakar Dangiwa Umar (retd), a former military governor of Kaduna State, wrote an open letter to Governor Radda asking for the emir’s suspension pending investigation, and said it should not be read as a declaration of guilt. Pulse Nigeria, an online news site, noted that the emir has not been found guilty of any offence.

Premium Times noted that the case comes less than five months after Radda pledged stronger enforcement against sexual and gender-based violence on 1 July 2026. Premium Times said open questions include whether police will investigate and whether investigators will seek the original recording.

The emir remains on the throne but out of public duties, and the allegation has not been tested by any court or committee. The government has set no date for the committee’s findings.

Frequently Asked Questions

Has the Emir of Daura been removed or charged?

No. He is barred from official engagements and travel pending the committee’s work, he remains emir, and no charge appears in the public record.

Has the video been proven authentic?

Not yet. Premium Times said its copy had not been authenticated against the original, and the Daura Emirate Council says it is reviewing whether the footage is real or altered.

What happens next?

The state committee investigates and advises the government. The government has given no deadline.

World.title: CSN Drops 6.22% as Steel Stocks Slide | Steel Wrap, Nov 24
World.content:
Brazil's CSN fell 6.22% to a six-month low on 24 November 2026, while the SLX steel fund lost 1.73% and Ternium slipped 1.25% as metals sold off.

Steel — the daily wrap.

Key Facts CSN, a Brazilian steelmaker, fell 6.22% to US$0.5064 in New York, a six-month low.

a six-month low. SLX, a fund of steel producers, fell 1.73% to US$89.23, 12.13% lower over 20 sessions.

12.13% lower over 20 sessions. Ternium, the Mexican producer, fell 1.25% to US$47.32; Gerdau was unchanged at US$4.27.

Gerdau was unchanged at US$4.27. Copper and gold both sold off, and steel followed metals lower.

and steel followed metals lower. Brazil’s steel association expects steel imports to fall 15% in 2026 but calls the problem structural.

Today’s Focus Steel shares across Latin America fell on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, and Brazil’s CSN fell hardest. Its New York shares ended at their lowest close in at least six months, and they are down 41.79% over 20 sessions. The main cause was a broad retreat from metals. Copper and gold both fell, and investors sold the sectors most tied to economic growth. Beneath that sits a slower problem: cheap Chinese steel that Brazilian and Mexican mills say squeezes their prices. Governments in both countries have answered with duties, but the shares show the relief has not arrived yet. Latin American steel had a poor Tuesday, and CSN had a dreadful one. The Brazilian group’s New York shares fell -6.22% to US$0.5064, their lowest close in at least six months.

The SLX fund, which holds steel producers from around the world, lost -1.73% to US$89.23. Ternium, the Mexican maker, slipped -1.25% to US$47.32, while Gerdau held still.

Behind the day sits a long grievance. Brazilian and Mexican mills say they cannot match the price of steel arriving from China and other parts of Asia.

Assessment — Sector slump, CSN in a rout MEDIUM The sector move fits a market-wide fall in metals, and the shares are in a continuing downtrend rather than a fresh shock. CSN’s collapse is out of proportion to its peers and points to something specific to the company, which reporting has not yet explained. The variable to watch is whether metals stabilise, because steel shares are unlikely to recover while copper and gold keep falling.

03 Why it moved

First and heaviest, investors fled metals. Copper lost its rebound from earlier in the week, and the gold fund fell 2.27% in the session and 7.67% over five sessions. The S&P 500 slipped 0.50% and the VIX fear gauge, which measures expected market swings, stood at 26.36. Confidence: high.

Second, the usual helpers failed. The dollar index eased 0.45% to 103.85 and the 10-year US Treasury yield dipped 2 basis points to 4.93%, which normally supports metals. The best reading is that fear of a growth scare, and of a policy error by the US Federal Reserve, outweighed the relief. Confidence: medium.

Third, Chinese imports keep capping what mills can charge. Aço Brasil, the industry association, expects rolled-steel imports to fall 15% in 2026 to about 4.9 million tons,. Its president calls the problem structural. We found no fresh data on Brazilian construction or car output, so demand is a background worry, not a measured cause.

CSN’s fall is the least explained. Trade policy is unlikely to be the trigger. The best-supported reading is company-specific stress amplified by a nervous market, with low confidence.

04 The trend behind it

SLX has fallen 4.83% over five sessions, 12.13% over 20 and 17.4% over 60. It sits 21.4% below its 12-month high of 113.57 on 2 June, and 14.4% above its low of 77.97 on 24 November 2025.

CSN’s slide is steeper: down 19.62% over five sessions and 51.3% over 60. This is a continuation of a downtrend, not a new phase, though CSN’s speed is unusual.

Our own history since 2007 offers a cautious guide. After 43 earlier SLX falls of this size, the fund was higher 20 sessions later in 22 cases (51%), with a median move of +0.4% and a worst case of -35.0%. For CSN, the 7 earlier cases split 3 higher and 4 lower, with a median of -2.8%. History is not a forecast, but it says a deep fall is no guarantee of a bounce.

05 What it means for Latin America

In Brazil, the 2026 anti-dumping duties on Chinese cold-rolled and coated steel, running up to five years, should help local mills. Even so, shares have not responded.

In Mexico, Ternium’s chief executive, Máximo Vedoya, said in November that the firm would ‘very likely’ file more anti-dumping cases, mainly against Asian steel.

Ternium’s exposure to US tariffs is limited, Vedoya said, because it has cut exports from Mexico to the US sharply. Its priorities in the review of the USMCA trade deal between the US, Mexico and Canada are tighter rules of origin and easier US steel tariffs under Section 232, a national-security trade law.

06 The names to watch

CSN is the one to watch: the lowest close of the year leaves no chart support, and any explanation from the company would matter. Gerdau’s flat day hides a 31.0% gain above its 3.26 low of 20 March, which shows how far it has already climbed.

Ternium has a catalyst of its own. Near-term shares will follow trade news.

07 What would end it

For SLX, the levels are the 77.97 low as support and 113.57 as the ceiling. For Gerdau, 3.26 is support and 5.24 resistance, while CSN has no 12-month floor below today’s close.

The turn needs two things: a stabilisation in copper and gold, and clearer trade protection for mills in Brazil and Mexico. No dates are set for either.

So the honest answer is that the slide ends when metals stop falling. Duties help the mills over years, not days.

08 What to watch

Copper and gold: Both fell on Tuesday; steel has followed metals down, so a stable day in either would be the first sign of relief.

Both fell on Tuesday; steel has followed metals down, so a stable day in either would be the first sign of relief. Trade protection: Duties on Asian steel shape mill profits over years, not days.

Duties on Asian steel shape mill profits over years, not days. USMCA review: Ternium wants tighter rules of origin and easier US steel tariffs; outcomes shape Mexican mills.

Ternium wants tighter rules of origin and easier US steel tariffs; outcomes shape Mexican mills. CSN’s next disclosure: Any statement explaining the fall would end the guessing around a 51.3% drop in 60 sessions.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did CSN fall so much?

Reporting has not confirmed a cause. The best-supported reading is company-specific stress made worse by a broad sell-off in metals, with low confidence.

Are Chinese imports still the problem?

Aço Brasil expects imports to fall 15% in 2026 to about 4.9 million tons, but calls the problem structural, so mills still feel the pressure.

Is SLX a steel price?

No. SLX is a fund holding steel-producing companies, so it tracks company shares, not the price of steel itself.

Will the slide continue?

In 22 of 43 earlier falls of this size, SLX was higher 20 sessions later. That is close to a coin toss, and not a forecast.
