World.title: China launches Shenzhou-24 to Tiangong station
World.content:
A new Chinese crew is on its way to the Tiangong station after a launch that China called a complete success. This includes a Pakistani pilot, who is making a brief visit.

The Shenzhou-24 spacecraft lifted off on a Long March-2F rocket at 8:18 am local time (0018 GMT) from the Jiuquan launch center in the Gobi Desert.

The China Manned Space Agency reported that the capsule separated from the rocket about 10 minutes later and entered orbit, and called the launch a "complete success".

State broadcaster CCTV showed the three crew members leafing through a manual minutes after liftoff and reported that they were in good condition.

What do we know about the crew?

Tang Hongbo is making his third trip to space. CCTV said he will become the first astronaut to board Tiangong three times. Wu Yi is on his first flight, as is Pakistani pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first foreigner to fly on a Chinese crewed mission.

"I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis," Ali told a news conference on Tuesday, switching between Urdu, Mandarin and English.

China-Pakistan space ties To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The handover on the station will be unusual. Shenzhou-23 commander Zhu Yangzhu will remain on board for a year, while the rest of his crew — Lai Ka-ying, Hong Kong's first astronaut, and Zhang Zhiyuan — return to Earth with Ali.

Zhu's stay is reportedly China's first full-year spell in space. Reuters said it will be the longest single stay by a Chinese astronaut. It has been described as a test of how the human body copes, ahead of planned Moon missions and possibly a journey to Mars.

What is on the agenda?

The crew will carry out more than 90 experiments and technology tests, Xinhua reported. At a news conference on Tuesday, Tang said differences in language, culture and psychology had made teamwork harder, but that both sides' efforts were paying off.

Ali, speaking in Mandarin, told reporters: "It's like my daily training. Day after day, reaching new heights."

China's 2030 target for a crewed Moon landing is unchanged despite the delay to its Chang'e-7 lunar mission. The United States is aiming for 2028.

World.title: US jury convicts Huawei of violating sanctions, stealing trade secrets
World.content:
Huawei was found guilty of 10 out of 12 charges levelled against it. The company said it plans to appeal the verdict.

A US jury convicted Chinese tech giant Huawei on a slew of charges on Tuesday including stealing trade secrets and violating sanctions.

The jury in the Brooklyn federal court found the company guilty on 10 of the 12 criminal counts that it faced, which also included bank fraud and wire fraud.

"For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft," US Attorney General Todd Blanche said after the verdict.

However, the jury acquitted Huawei on two charges of racketeering and conspiring to obstruct justice.

The verdict is the latest blow to the Chinese tech giant which has for years been banned from selling networking devices to telecom carries in the US and other Western countries. However, its consumer electronics business has continued to grow as its networking business in other countries.

Stolen source code, antenna technology and robot tech

Prosecutors detailed a number of ways Huawei stole trade secrets from competitors in order to undercut them in the market.

In once instance, a Huawei employee slipped into a competitor's booth at a Chicago trade fair in order to photograph circuitboards inside another company's networking divice.

Huawei was also found to have once sold routers containing source code from a rival company.

How the China-US AI arms race is escalating To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Prosecutors also said a Huawei employee once removed a robotic arm from a competitor's lab so it could be photographed and measured.

According to court records, the victim companies included Cisco Systems, Motorola Solutions, T-Mobile, Quintel USA and Fujitsu.

"The misappropriated intellectual property included trade secret information and copyrighted works, such as source code and user manuals for internet routers, antenna technology, and robot testing technology," the Department of Justice said.

False statenments about Iran operations

Prosecutors also alleged that Huawei did business in countries subject to US sanctions including Iran and North Korea.

Huawei then made false statements to both US government officials and banks in order to hide this activity, prosecutors said.

"Few crimes are as serious as Huawei's decades-long pattern of endangering US national security, violating the sanctity of US commerce, and impeding the ‌enforcement of ​US laws," US Attorney Joseph Nocella said.

Lawyer Brian Heberlig represented Huawei in court Image: Jane Rosenberg/REUTERS

Huawei to appeal verdict

Huawei continued to deny the allegations even after the verdict on Tuesday.

"We believe the government's remaining charges are equally without legal or factual merit," the company said in a statement.

"The five trade secret-related disputes cited by the government were all civil matters that were resolved over the past two decades. No court ever found Huawei liable for willful intellectual property misappropriation, and the company was never ordered to pay damages for trade secret misappropriation."

The company's lawyer, Brian Heberlig, said: "We fully expect to appeal."

Huawei is set to be sentenced next September and could face billions of dollars in penalties.

World.title: Scientists discover quasar formed 630 million years after the Big Bang
World.content:
Scientists are seeing the quasar as it was 13.1 billion years ago — when the universe was less than 5% of its current age.

ESA's Euclid telescope revealed the most distant known quasar, formed within 630 million years of the universe-forming Big Bang.

That's considered a very early development in the 13.8 billion-year history of the cosmos, and it smashes previous records.

The light carries valuable information about the early history of the universe.

Researchers at the European Space Agency on Tuesday announced the discovery of the most distant, and therefore oldest, quasar ever observed.

The discovery, made by a German astronomer and his team, was published in the journal Astronomy and Astrophysics.

A quasar refers to an extremely bright core of an active galaxy powered by gas falling into a supermassive black hole.

Quasars represent a brief phase in a galaxy's life, during which the nucleus can outshine the rest of the system.

"As enormous amounts of gas, dust and matter fall toward the black hole, they form a swirling accretion disk that heats up to extreme temperatures and radiates tremendous amounts of energy, outshining the entire rest of the galaxy by factors of hundreds or even thousands," said astronomer and study co-author Silvia Belladitta of ​the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy in Germany and the INAF Bologna Observatory of Astrophysics and Space Science in Italy.

"This makes quasars visible across billions of light-years, allowing us to observe ​them from the very early universe. Studying quasars helps astronomers understand how the first galaxies formed and evolved, and how the supermassive black holes at their hearts grew to such enormous sizes," Belladitta said.

More evidence that black holes were extremely massive very early on

The newly discovered object, formally known as J1504+6252, is nicknamed Dún Aonghas.

The red dot in the image below corresponds to seeing the universe as it was roughly 13.1 billion years ago — just 5% of its current age.

"I think it adds to the evidence that some objects in the early universe developed remarkably ​quickly. Just 630 million years after the Big Bang, this black hole had already grown to about 360 million times the mass of the sun and was shining as ​a quasar," said astronomer Julien Wolf of the European Southern Observatory in Germany, lead author of the research.

The discovery then supports the scenario in which supermassive black holes form through the direct collapse of large gas clouds and subsequently accumulate additional matter.

Dún Aonghas was first detected by the European Space Agency's Euclid telescope, with images having been characterized using a combination of ground- and space-based telescopes.

The ESA's orbiting telescope is meant for missions that uncover the mysteries of dark matter, which is the invisible glue lumping galaxies together, and dark energy, the force that pushes them apart.

World.title: European court finds states can turn back migrants in some cases
World.content:
Europe's top human rights court ruled that member states can turn back migrants unless they've been identified as people who were at risk of suffering.

The European Court of Human Rights on Tuesday ruled that states belonging to the Council of Europe group have a right to control foreign arrivals.

But the court ruling said all 46 member states of the group — that includes all EU and some non-EU countries and promotes democracy and human rights on the continent — must ensure and uphold human rights of people even in hostile environments.

The European court ruling is a complicated one since it deals with a case concerning the entry of nationals of Afghanistan, Iraq and Cuba into EU member countries Poland, Latvia and Lithuania between 2021 and 2022.

That was a time when a border standoff was playing out between Belarus and the EU's eastern member states, with Belarus having been accused of entirely manufacturing a migration crisis to put pressure on the EU.

Belarus arranged for people from various third countries to enter their state and then pointed them to the EU's frontiers.

Europe's human rights court says countries can turn back migrants with duty of care

Europe's most important human rights court on Tuesday ruled that states have a right to control the entry of foreign nationals into their territory even when migration has been weaponized.

The court calls Belarus' hostile actions of 2021 as having been an instance of "instrumentalization of migration."

But the court said that states must still ensure that migrants are protected against inhumane or degrading treatment.

In the context of a surge in migration, for example, national authorities were still to identify people who were particularly at risk of suffering or enduring ill treatment.

The migrants in the case brought before the European court said that they had been violently prevented from crossing into the EU without their asylum applications having been examined and that their human rights had been violated.

"In a context of instrumentalization of migration, the removal of a foreign national to the instrumentalizing state would not, as such, constitute a violation of Article 3 (prohibition of torture and inhuman and degrading treatment)," the court press release said.

The court ordered Poland, Latvia and Lithuania to pay compensation for their treatment of migrants at the EU's external borders with Belarus.

Five EU countries announce plan with Rwanda to establish 'return hub'

Five EU countries also last week announced a plan with Rwanda to establish a so-called return hub in the African nation.

The hub will host rejected asylum seekers waiting to return to their countries of origin.

But there are many concerns about the project since Rwanda ranks low on human rights measures and there are questions about whether people's rights will be sufficiently protected.

World.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy and Hungary's Magyar meet amid thaw in ties
World.content:
Hungary's Prime Minister Peter Magyar has arrived in Ukraine for meetings with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and ethnic Hungarians. Both leaders say they want better relations after a change of leadership in Budapest.

Hungary's new Prime Minister Peter Magyar arrived in Ukraine on Tuesday afternoon for meetings with President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as well as with ethnic Hungarians living in the west of the country.

The meeting comes as both say they want better relations after a change of leadership in Budapest — no doubt a welcome change for Kyiv after years of Viktor Orban obstructing funding for its self-defense against full-scaler Russian invasion.

Ukraine's Zelenskyy posted his thanks for the meeting with a photo on X, writing: "A visit that is sure to bring positive results. We already have agreements in the areas of politics, energy, and infrastructure. Thank you!"

The Ukrainian president said agreements had been reached and teams had been tasked with implementing them.

Despite his softer approach, Magyar has said Hungary will not be sending arms to Kyiv while at the same time vowing, "we stand with Ukraine against the Russian aggressor."

Rights of ethnic Hungarians tied to war support and EU accession talks

Magyar has insisted that the rights of tens of thousands of ethnic Hungarians in the Transcarpathia — a region that was part of Austria-Hungary until the end of World War I and situated at the borders of Ukraine, Hungary, Poland, Romania and Slovakia — be resolved before Budapest can wholeheartedly back Ukraine and its possible accession to the European Union.

Relations deteriorated significantly over the issue in 2017, when Kyiv passed a law making Ukrainian the official language of all secondary education in Ukraine, something Budapest viewed as discriminatory toward ethnic Hungarians.

Last month, Ukrainian lawmakers passed legislation allowing ethnic minorities in the country expanded rights regarding the teaching and use of their native languages. The move was welcomed by Budapest and Hungary dropped its opposition to Brussels opening accession talks with Ukraine.

Magyar pitched this week's trip — the first to Transcarpathia by a Hungarian prime minister since 2015 — in April, after defeating Orban.

Before departing for Ukraine, the Hungarian leader said: "I hope these talks will be successful. I think this is a historic day and a good opportunity to put Ukrainian-Hungarian relations on a new footing and to rebuild trust as we did with our other neighbors."

World.title: Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remains controversial
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

It took a while for the video call to connect. When Volodymyr Zelenskyy finally greeted the delegates in Berlin, applause broke out. The Ukrainian president appealed to the gathered parliamentarians from 32 NATO member states to keep supporting his country, especially against the massive aerial bombardment from Russia.

"Dear friends, winter is now ahead of us. And of course, our number one priority is air defense," Zelenskyy told the delegates. His country urgently needs more Patriot and other comprehensive anti-air attack systems. "And your countries have them. Missiles that can stop Russian ballistic missiles should not be sitting in warehouses collecting dust. And we say this openly. Please help us with this."

Western allies boost Ukraine's defenses but clash over deep strikes To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Ukraine seeks to join NATO

Zelenskyy renewed his call for his country to join the NATO military alliance. That issue is not for the NATO Parliamentary Assembly, which was gathered for its 72nd annual meeting in Berlin, to decide. But it was important to the Ukrainian president to reiterate his request.

After the war ends, Ukraine needs strong security guarantees and NATO could ensure those. "Wouldn't it be more effective to simply bring Ukraine into NATO?" Zelenskyy asked, arguing: "Wouldn't that be better for all of us, for everyone? Cheaper to put in place? And more reliable when it comes to actually protecting security?"

There is conflict among NATO members about the possibility of admitting Ukraine. The alliance has affirmed multiple times that the path to membership stands open to Ukraine — however, in the long term rather than the near future. This is primarily because of the ongoing war and the possible assistance obligations of other NATO countries for Ukraine, which was attacked by Russia.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte rejected the Ukrainian demands at the summit, which for the first time in 26 years was held in Berlin. Ukraine had entry prospects; however, NATO members currently lack unanimity on this issue. NATO alone decides who becomes a member. "There is total clarity on that within the alliance," Rutte said.

If Russia attacked NATO, would Germany be prepared? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Merz: Denying Ukraine NATO membership in 2008 'was a mistake'

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz advocated for Ukraine to receive security guarantees similar to what NATO members have, in the instance of a possible ceasefire. In retrospect, it was clear "what a mistake it was not to follow the American suggestion back in 2008 at the NATO summit in Bucharest to admit Ukraine as a member," Merz said at a joint press conference following a meeting with Rutte.

Whether or not a NATO entry for Ukraine could be part of negotiations with Russia is another question, according to Rutte. He approved of current US efforts to bring about peace talks, and how Europe was closely consulting with Ukraine and the US for a unified position. "But it is also to test now whether Putin is willing to play ball, and then these issues might come up again."

The Russian invasion of Ukraine has led to NATO arming itself on a massive scale. Members have committed to raising their countries' defense spending to 5% of their gross domestic product (GDP) by 2035.

Rutte warned that all the allies needed a credible path to get there, "and ideally, they get there sooner than 2035." In addition, he said weapons production among member states needed to further increase because "right now, demand still far exceeds the supply."

Why Germany's military ambitions face a battle at home To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Germany's military budget has had a massive increase

The contribution by Germany's Bundeswehr armed forces to NATO was explained by Carsten Breuer, Germany's highest-ranking soldier. For example, the massive increase in military spending: "Our defense budget has tripled since 2021. The goal is to achieve the 5% target, which was set at the summit in The Hague, well before 2035." In the coming year, Germany's defense budget has risen to more than €139 billion ($151 billion).

The Bundeswehr was further developing into a "constantly modernized, effective and innovative army, Breuer said. Also, a much larger one than before. "To reach our current capability goals we are expanding the Bundeswehr to a total of 460,000 soldiers by the mid-2030s," the German chief of defense said. Of those, 200,000 are to be reservists. "This is like walking a tightrope because we must find the right balance between growth and operational readiness."

Following his speech, Breuer answered questions from the delegates who showed keen interest in the developments. The discussion was a preview of Breuer's new post: He has been voted in as the new chair of the NATO Military Committee and will move to the alliance's headquarters in Brussels mid-next year. Then he will become the principal military advisor to NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. "I take this election as a sign of recognition that Germany has now accepted its responsibility as well as its role in security policy," Breuer said.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: HIV infections could rise amid aid cuts, UN warns
World.content:
The impact of United States government funding cuts has been dramatic for many HIV programs, UNAIDS warned. The agency expects that 2027 data to show an increase in new infections after being on the cusp of ending AIDS.

New HIV infections could rise next year for the first time in years, reversing a historic decline amid funding cuts and anti-rights campaigns, the United Nations (UN) warned on Tuesday.

"The world has moved closer towards controlling the HIV pandemic, but changes in funding and resulting service disruptions jeopardize this progress," the UNAIDS agency said in its annual global update.

AIDS-related death numbers has fallen to its lowest in more than two decades. According to the organization, this was made possible by broader access to treatment and improvements in the quality of care programs.

The virus claimed roughly 570,000 lives globally in 2025. This means almost 1,600 people died everyday. In comparison, this figure was 600,000 in 2024 and 1.3 million in 2010.

Based on data from 172 countries, the agency estimated that 41 million people worldwide were living with HIV in 2025, of whom 32.1 million were receiving antiretroviral treatment.

The wider use of antiretroviral medication also reduces the risk of HIV transmission, the organization said. It estimates that 1.2 million people contracted HIV in 2025, down from 1.3 million the year before. The peak in 1994 saw 3.5 million.

UNAIDS said Lenacapavir, an injection administered just twice a year, has marked another turning point in HIV prevention [FILE: July 2024] Image: Nardus Engelbrecht/AP/picture alliance

"HIV, which was once a death sentence, has become a manageable health condition for millions of people thanks to life-saving HIV medicines," said UNAIDS.

'Dramatic impacts' of US aid cuts

Despite the encouraging data so far, cuts to international funding have hampered efforts to fight HIV, the agency warned.

HIV programs faced an 18-percent decrease in international financing over the past year, said UNAIDS.

"Funding losses have destabilized HIV programs worldwide, coinciding with a wider contraction in official development assistance over the years," it said.

Although the United States remains the largest international donor for HIV programs, its contributions dropped by 26% between 2024 and 2025.

How USAID cuts could result in higher HIV transmission To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

After dismantling USAID, the world's largest foreign aid agency, last year, the Donald Trump administration has sought to replace decades of aid with new bilateral deals.

"The impact of the United States government funding cuts has been especially dramatic given the reliance of many countries on its support for core HIV programs," said UNAIDS.

Meanwhile disbursements from the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria dropped by 13% in 2025.

Next year's data may show rising infections

"We are on the cusp of ending AIDS – this has been the greatest story of global ​health – and just when we should finish it, cuts and the rolling back of human rights is ​threatening to take away our gains," Winnie Byanyima, executive director of UNAIDS, told ​Reuters.

"We haven't ‌got the data yet, but we see the signs. We see all the signs of reversals," she added.

Byanyima predicted that data released in 2027 would begin to reflect a rise in new HIV infections.

In 2015, the UN set a goal to end AIDS by 2030.

World.title: Pope Francis diaries recount spiritual crisis, him seeing the 'Devil'
World.content:
Extracts of the late Pope Francis' diaries have been published, the first release of its kind since the 1960s. They discuss his struggles with his role in the Vatican and visions of the devil and the gates of hell.

The late Pope Francis suffered a spiritual crisis during his papacy when he struggled with how to lead the Catholic Church and believed he saw and heard the devil on several occasions, according to an annotated collection of his private diaries published on Tuesday.

Francis was pope for 12 years until his death last April.

Cardinal Victor Fernandez, a compatriot and close collaborator of Francis', collated the diary entries and provides accompanying commentary, in the first set of papal diaries to be published posthumously since those of John XXIII, who died in 1963.

The 160-page sample of Francis' diaries is the first release of its kind in more than 50 years Image: Gregorio Borgia/AP Photo/picture alliance

What does the book say about Francis' difficulties as pope?

The diary entries speak of the Argentine-born pontiff not wanting to be someone "who uses others like puppets," according to the accompanying commentary.

"It was all mixed with governance issues, pressure regarding decisions to make, and aridity and desolation," a December 2022 entry from Francis said.

Although the book does not make clear exactly who Francis worried he was using like puppets or the nature of the internal pressures, Francis encountered stern resistance from more conservative forces within the Church as he urged the staid institution to modernize.

Cardinal Fernandez wrote that Francis "ultimately recognized it was the worst trial that had toremented him ... and that he felt that he was in a continual battle not to fall into this demonic seduction."

Various world leaders attended Francis' funeral last April [FILE: April 2025] Image: IPA/ABACAPRESS/IMAGO

What does the book say about Francis' religious visions and dreams?

The 160-page selection of excerpts — starting in 1992 when he was still known as Jorge Mario Bergoglio and running until a few months before his death — are arranged by theme and pay closer attention to Francis' internal spiritual experiences than Vatican politics.

But one of the three occasions listed where the late pope believed he had seen the Devil was during a meeting with Vatican officials in January 2021 early in what he termed a spiritual crisis. In that instance he even believed to have heard the figure speak.

"I can't forget the powerful raspiness of his voice," Francis wrote in an entry. "The Lord granted me an opportunity to leave that meeting, and thus he freed me."

Other entries detail how Francis believed that God spoke to him in his dreams, and one from 2018 stated: "Last night I saw the entrance to Hell. I peeked in to look a little, and it terrified me."

Pope Francis' life and legacy To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What else features in the diary excerpts?

The papers show Francis to be self-critical at times, chastizing himself for "feelings of disdain, envy, pride" or for ignoring a drunken man who approached him "because I wanted to have a serene walk."

At one point in a 2022 entry he refers to himself as the "proud, self-sufficient, cynical, self-deceptive Jorge."

They also show how in later years he felt anxious to make the most of his remaining years, and regretful about some of his deicsions earlier in his life.

"I want to do good during the little time I have left, desiring to be good," he wrote in 1996 on turning 60. "How much time I've used badly! How much badly done!"

The accounts also list his regret after a visit to Chile in 2018 when he faced stern criticism for initially dismissing allegations of sexual abuse and cover-up against a bishop there before later apologizing.

"It was hard for me to admit what happened in Chile; I didn't think it was so serious," a "devastated" pontiff wrote three years later.

Fernandez also recounts comments from Francis on some senior officials in the Vatican including his successor, US Cardinal Robert Prevost, now Pope Leo XIV. According to Fernandez, Francis called him "a great pastor, a generous missionary, and an irreproachable man."

World.title: Llega el apagón de encuestas: ¿Qué dice el promedio con las últimas?
World.content:
Esta es la última actualización del promedio de EL PAÍS, del 23 de noviembre. Además, construye tu propio promedio

Se publican decenas de encuestas en una campaña. Son el mejor instrumento para predecir unas elecciones, sobre todo cuando las miramos juntas: eso hace nuestro promedio. Combina todos los estudios dando más peso a las encuestadoras que más aciertan. En su última actualización, ese promedio sitúa al PP con el 31,5% de los votos, unos 2,5 puntos por delante del PSOE (29%), y con Vox alrededor del 18%.

En el gráfico puedes elegir entre tres promedios. El “medio” es el que usamos habitualmente; los otros dos sirven para comparar: “agresivo” (que reacciona antes a los cambios pero tiene más ruido), y otro “cauto” (que se mueve menos).

Los sondeos se han movido desde la convocatoria del 6 de octubre. El cambio más claro es la subida del PSOE, que estrecha la ventaja del PP: era de 6 puntos y ahora es de menos de 2,5, y bajando. Nuestros cálculos dicen que el PSOE tiene al menos un 25% de probabilidad de ser primero.

Algo que también ha cambiado es la izquierda del PSOE. Las últimas encuestas estiman un 6,8% de voto para lo que hemos llamado Frentes (Frente Amplio y las coaliciones con Podemos, Compromís, Ara Més o Unidad del Pueblo Canario) y un 1,1% para Podemos en solitario. Juntos rondan el 8% de voto, lejos del 12,3% que logró Sumar en 2023.

La suma de izquierdas y derechas

El número clave de las elecciones es el resultado por bloques. Al cierre, la derecha suma el 51,2% de los votos (PP, Vox y SALF) y la izquierda, el 38,7% (PSOE, Frentes, Podemos y Adelante Andalucía). Son 12,5 puntos de distancia, cuando en las generales de 2023 casi empataron, con 45,6% y 44% respectivamente. La suma de PP y Vox tendrá seguramente la mayoría si supera el 47% de votos.

La ventaja de la derecha creció entre 2024 y el verano de 2025, cuando sus votos pasaron del 48% al 52%. Pero en campaña se ha reducido unos tres puntos. Se ha cumplido nuestra hipótesis inicial: la izquierda, que partía desmovilizada, ha recuperado terreno con la convocatoria electoral, aunque siga por detrás.

El promedio también constata que las encuestadoras discrepan. Casi todas ponen al PP primero, pero con ventajas distintas: desde menos de un punto, según 40dB. o Ipsos, hasta los casi siete de Hamalgama. Solo SW Demoscopia y Cluster17 sitúan al PSOE por delante, además del CIS. Pero el dato de este último es poco informativo porque el centro sobrestima a la izquierda desde 2018.

¿Y si corregimos los llamados sesgos? Algunas encuestadoras se desvían hacia la derecha o hacia la izquierda. Nuestro promedio no lo corrige por un motivo: esas desviaciones cambian de una elección a otra y casi nunca son sistemáticas. Pero podemos ver qué pasaría si lo hiciéramos: el siguiente gráfico permite corregir cada encuesta con el sesgo histórico de su casa.

El resultado depende de qué elecciones miramos. Con los errores de todas las elecciones desde 2018, generales y autonómicas, la ventaja del PP sobre el PSOE sube de 2,5 a 3,5 puntos: en conjunto las encuestas se han quedado cortas con la derecha. Pero en las generales ha pasado lo contrario: subestimaron a la izquierda. El caso más recordado es 2023: las últimas encuestas daban a la derecha 5,4 puntos de ventaja, y en las urnas sacó solo 1,6. Si ajustamos las encuestas con sus sesgos solo en las tres generales desde 2018, la ventaja del PP baja a un punto, aunque la suma de derechas sigue claramente por delante.

Todos estos números son tentativos. Primero, porque las encuestas son una aproximación. Y segundo, porque entre las últimas encuestas y el 29-N hay seis días. La izquierda venía recortando distancia. Esa tendencia podrá seguir o no, pero ya no podremos contarlo aquí con sondeos públicos: la ley impide publicarlos en los cinco días previos a la votación.

¿Cómo funciona el promedio?

Un promedio de encuestas suele ser más preciso que cualquier encuesta aislada: suma la muestra de todas y compensa en parte sus errores, porque mezcla la “cocina” de cada encuestadora. El nuestro funciona así:

1) Todas las encuestas. Usamos las de voto al Congreso publicadas desde las generales de 2023, salvo las encargadas por partidos y las que no tienen trabajo de campo propio. La mayoría las tomamos de Wikipedia.

2) Con distinto peso. Cada encuesta importa según su encuestadora, su muestra y su antigüedad. La nota de cada casa sale de nuestro comparador, que valora su error, su sesgo y si publica sus microdatos (las mejores pesan el doble que una casa normal). El peso de una encuesta se reduce a la mitad cada diez días y desaparece a los 30.

3) Cada casa cuenta una vez. De cada encuestadora pesa su último sondeo, para que no mande quien publica más.

4) Mira hacia atrás. El promedio de cada día solo usa las encuestas con el trabajo de campo terminado hasta entonces. Si una se publica con retraso, la línea de esos días se corrige un poco.

5) Tres ritmos. El promedio central y dos para comparar: el agresivo reduce el peso a la mitad cada 8 días y corta a los 14; el cauto, cada 30 y a los 60.

6) Las listas del 29N. Desde el 14 de octubre medimos las candidaturas nuevas, y las encuestas anteriores se traducen a ellas. SALF y Adelante Andalucía entran en el promedio poco a poco, a medida que las publican las encuestadoras.

7) El sesgo, aparte. La corrección del interactivo usa el error de cada casa en la ventaja entre bloques desde 2018, entero: enseña qué pasaría si las casas volvieran a fallar como de media.

8) El promedio es sólido, pero no infalible. Lo hemos probado con 41 elecciones desde 2018: cinco días antes de votar, falla 1,5 puntos por partido de media. Cambiar la ventana o los pesos lo mejora una décima como mucho. Cuando falla es porque fallan todas las encuestas a la vez, algo que ningún promedio puede corregir: por eso nuestro modelo añade esa incertidumbre.

Todas las encuestas

World.title: ¿Se ha movido el voto útil? Las opciones de izquierda y derecha en cada provincia con las últimas encuestas
World.content:
El modelo de EL PAÍS dice que hay 40 escaños en el aire. Consulta a qué partido le sirve más tu voto

Las encuestas tratan de predecir los votos del próximo 29-N, pero el modelo electoral que publicamos en EL PAÍS desde hace una década va más allá: estima los escaños en cada provincia, les asigna probabilidades, e incluso señala el llamado voto útil. A continuación mostramos sus pronósticos actualizados con las encuestas del 20 de noviembre, incluido el sondeo posterior al debate de 40dB.

En el primer interactivo puedes ver los escaños seguros (99% de opciones), probables (75%-99%) y en juego (25%-75%) de cada partido. En total hay 175 seguros, 135 probables y 83 en juego (suman más de 350 porque varios partidos se disputan los escaños). También puedes elegir una provincia y ver nuestra estimación allí.

Voto útil: ¿qué voto ayuda a tu bloque?

Muchas personas votan para maximizar las opciones de un gobierno de izquierdas o de derechas. Quizás tienen un partido favorito, pero se hacen otra pregunta: ¿a qué partido de su bloque le sirve más su voto? Es lo que se llama voto táctico o estratégico. La respuesta cambia en cada provincia: por el método D’Hondt, un voto al PP y otro a Vox no valen lo mismo en escaños, porque uno de los dos suele estar más cerca de ganar el último diputado. Y lo mismo pasa con PSOE, Frente Amplio o BNG.

¿Cuál es el voto táctico en tu provincia? Puedes verlo en el mapa. Primero elige un bloque. Entonces el mapa mostrará, para cada provincia, el partido de ese espectro que tiene más probabilidades de ganar (o salvar) un escaño para su bloque.

Para un votante de derecha, existe voto táctico en 34 provincias. Hay 18 donde le conviene votar al PP (probablemente) y 16 donde le conviene hacerlo por Vox. A veces la diferencia es grande: en Gipuzkoa, Lugo y Ourense, un voto a Vox casi nunca decide un escaño, mientras que el PP se disputa el último con Bildu o el BNG. En Álava o Melilla, un voto al PP vale más de cinco veces lo que uno a Vox. Pero hay territorios donde un votante indiferente entre PP y Vox maximiza sus opciones eligiendo al partido de extrema derecha. Es lo que pasa en La Rioja, por ejemplo.

En la izquierda, el voto táctico favorece al PSOE en 35 de las 52 provincias. En 19 provincias es el único del bloque que mueve escaños en nuestras simulaciones, porque los Frentes y Podemos tienen números débiles en los sondeos. Hay excepciones en territorios con fuerzas locales: por ejemplo, en Lugo y Ourense parece que un voto al BNG es mejor para los intereses del bloque. Y ocurre algo parecido con Adelante Andalucía en Córdoba y con la Unidad del Pueblo Canario en Santa Cruz de Tenerife.

En las provincias grandes, en cambio, el voto táctico apenas existe. En Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia o Sevilla da casi igual votar a un partido u otro del bloque: las fuerzas principales tienen todas opciones de lograr representación.

Nuestra simulación también muestra otra cosa: mover un escaño es mucho más barato en las provincias más pequeñas. La probabilidad de que justo tu papeleta sea la decisiva es siempre minúscula (un voto cualquiera tiene una posibilidad entre 117.000 de decidir un escaño). Pero no es siempre igual de minúscula. En Lleida un voto al PP pesa seis veces más que la media: una posibilidad entre 19.000. Y en Ávila o La Rioja, uno al PSOE pesa unas cinco veces más. En el otro extremo, un voto al PP o a Vox en Madrid vale la mitad de lo normal, en parte porque allí cada escaño cuesta más votos: hay unos 94.000 votantes por diputado, frente a 25.000 en Soria.

Una advertencia: esto no es una recomendación de voto. Es la aritmética de los escaños según las encuestas de hoy, que todavía pueden moverse y que son siempre una aproximación. Además, el voto táctico solo mide la probabilidad de mover un escaño, pero un voto puede tener utilidad para apoyar unas ideas o una formación incluso cuando no se traduzca en asiento del Congreso.

¿Cómo funciona el modelo?

El modelo parte de nuestro promedio de sondeos, lo proyecta a cada provincia con su historia y microdatos del CIS, y le añade la incertidumbre de las encuestas en el pasado. Después simulamos las elecciones 20.000 veces y contamos cuántas veces gana cada partido cada escaño. Así podemos clasificarlos en tres grupos: seguros, probables y en juego.

El siguiente gráfico muestra qué significan estas probabilidades. Puedes simular las elecciones una, dos, tres o cien veces para hacerte una idea intuitiva de cuántas veces se gana un escaño de cada tipo.

El modelo es sólido. Cada pieza la hemos puesto a prueba con otras elecciones generales. Por ejemplo, hemos probado varias formas de repartir el voto entre provincias, siguiendo técnicas habituales, y nos quedamos con la más precisa en votos y escaños.

El modelo es cauteloso. Y lo es por diseño: predecir cada provincia es difícil porque las encuestas pierden precisión a escala provincial. Un sondeo de 2.000 o 5.000 entrevistas no basta para estimar directamente el voto de Soria, Pontevedra o Castellón. Por eso no lo intentamos: lo que hacemos es usar el voto histórico de cada partido en cada provincia y lo que dicen en cada comunidad los microdatos del CIS, que acumulan decenas de miles de entrevistas. Además, las fuerzas locales no siempre salen en las encuestas y pueden sorprender al final: Teruel Existe gana escaño en una de cada cinco simulaciones. Y pasa algo similar con partidos pequeños en las provincias grandes: Podemos consigue un diputado por Madrid en el 60% de las simulaciones, y SALF, en el 24%. Si detectas cualquier omisión, escríbenos.

Y el modelo es confiable. Estas predicciones las hemos hecho muchas veces. Por eso sabemos que el modelo funciona y está bien calibrado. En 2023 dimos 189 escaños como seguros y se cumplieron todos, igual que en las dos elecciones de 2019 (156 y 153). Los que dimos como probables se cumplieron el 94% de las veces (365 de 388), en la parte alta del 75%-99% que prometíamos. Los errores de cada provincia se compensan en parte al sumarlos, así que el total es más fiable que cada provincia por separado. El modelo también acierta en el total nacional: en las generales de 2016 a 2023, los escaños de cada partido grande cayeron dentro de nuestra horquilla del 80% en 19 de 20 casos, más de lo prometido: es la cautela de la que hablábamos.

Si quieres seguir todas las encuestas del 29-N, apúntate el nuevo pódcast de Kiko Llaneras, en Spotify, YouTube, Apple Podcasts o iVoox.

Metodología

Las predicciones las produce un modelo estadístico basado en sondeos y en su precisión histórica. Es una versión renovada del que hemos usado en unas 40 elecciones desde 2016: en Andalucía, Castilla y León, Aragón, Extremadura, las europeas, las generales de abril y noviembre de 2019 y de 2023, y otras en México, Francia o el Reino Unido.

Funciona en cuatro pasos. 1) Un promedio de encuestas que pondera cada sondeo por su tamaño, su fecha y la precisión histórica de su encuestadora, según nuestro comparador. 2) Una proyección del voto a cada provincia con un modelo logístico, que parte de las generales de 2023 —y, para los partidos nuevos o que ahora concurren por separado, de las europeas de 2024 y las andaluzas de 2026— y se alimenta también con microdatos del CIS de cada comunidad. 3) La incertidumbre de las encuestas, calibrada con los errores de 44 elecciones en España desde 1986 y con una base internacional de miles de sondeos, según el tamaño de cada partido y los días que faltan para votar. Usamos distribuciones t de Student, con colas más anchas que una normal, y errores correlacionados entre partidos. Esos errores tienen una parte común a toda España, porque las encuestas suelen fallar en la misma dirección en todas partes, y otra propia de cada provincia. 4) 20.000 simulaciones de las elecciones, repartiendo los escaños según D’Hondt con barrera del 3% en cada circunscripción.

Un escaño es seguro si un partido lo gana en más del 99% de las simulaciones; probable, entre el 75% y el 99%, y en juego, entre el 25% y el 75%. En nuestras pruebas con las generales de 2016 a 2023, esas probabilidades están muy bien afinadas: los escaños en juego se cumplieron 202 veces, frente a las 195 que predecía el modelo.

Para calcular el voto táctico usamos las mismas 20.000 simulaciones. En cada una añadimos (o quitamos) un puñado de votos a cada partido en cada provincia, y miramos si su bloque gana (o pierde) un escaño. Solo contamos cuando el escaño cambia de bloque. El resultado es la probabilidad de que un voto decida un asiento para su bloque ideológico. Los bloques son derecha (PP, Vox y SALF), e izquierda (PSOE, Frente Amplio, Podemos, ERC, EH Bildu, BNG y Adelante Andalucía). PNV, Junts y CC quedan fuera.

En los gráficos nacionales agrupamos como Izquierdas a Frente Amplio, Podemos y las coaliciones Compromís-Front Valencià, Unidad del Pueblo Canario y Ara Més-Front Ampli; en cada provincia aparecen por separado.

Si quieres seguir todas las encuestas del 29-N, apúntate al nuevo pódcast de Kiko Llaneras, en Spotify, YouTube, Apple Podcasts o iVoox.
