World.title: El Gobierno reivindica su traca final de medidas sociales previas al 29-N: “Cumplimos con nuestro deber”
World.content:
La coalición evita cualquier tensión y muestra sintonía en la presentación de un paquete millonario de políticas como el impuesto a la banca, la rebaja de autónomos y el permiso por fallecimiento

El Gobierno aprovecha a fondo el último Consejo de Ministros antes de las elecciones —la ministra portavoz confirmó que no habrá ninguno más extraordinario este viernes— con una traca final con mucho contenido político y económico. El Ejecutivo ha aprobado medidas que afectan a millones de personas, con otras que suponen una guerra cultural también con la Comunidad de Madrid en cuestiones sensibles como el aborto, con prórroga del impuesto a la banca, simplificaciones y reducciones para millones de autónomos, una gran ampliación de 2 a 10 días de la baja por fallecimiento que afectará a todos los trabajadores que sufran una situación así, la ampliación a 20 semanas del permiso por nacimiento, o la prórroga de las ayudas al transporte público. Un paquete que en condiciones normales daría para varios consejos y esta vez se acumuló en uno y precisamente el último antes de votar. El Ejecutivo ha dejado sin aprobar, eso sí, el indulto al fiscal general del Estado, que previsiblemente se hará ya en funciones.

La supervisión permanente de la Junta Electoral Central, que ha sancionado a varios ministros, ha evitado que el Ejecutivo lanzara las campanas al vuelo, pero los cuatro miembros del Gobierno que han comparecido, tres del PSOE y una de Sumar, Yolanda Díaz, han reivindicado esta decisión de llenar de contenido el último Consejo de Ministros antes de los comicios ante las críticas de electoralismo.

La semana pasada hubo alguna tensión amable entre los ministros de la coalición, que compiten electoralmente, pero esta vez todo fue armonía y se ofreció una imagen de sintonía similar a la que se vivió en el debate a ocho del lunes en TVE, donde no hubo ataques importantes entre el PSOE y el Frente Amplio, que sí reivindica como propias algunas de las medidas más exitosas del Ejecutivo.

Yolanda Díaz y Elma Saiz, este martes en la rueda de prensa posterior al Consejo de Ministros. Víctor Sainz

“Cumplimos con nuestro deber”, ha explicado la vicepresidenta Díaz. “Estamos en plena legislatura y estamos gobernando con un instrumento democrático y legal como la Diputación Permanente”, ha insistido la portavoz, Elma Sáiz. “Cada medida tiene una generación de crédito con normalidad y dentro de normativa presupuestaria”, se ha justificado el ministro de Hacienda, Arcadi España, cuando le han preguntado por cómo se financian todos estos anuncios si el Gobierno sigue con los Presupuestos de 2023 prorrogados.

El Gobierno explica que ninguna de las medidas aprobadas este martes es un invento electoralista de última hora. Todas llevaban meses en estudio, algunas incluso estaban comprometidas desde hace un año, como el aumento de las bajas por fallecimiento, pero las enormes dificultades políticas de esta legislatura las han ido retrasando y el riesgo de que Junts las tumbara las fue dejando hasta que finalmente se acaba la legislatura y hoy era el último día para sacarlas adelante. En la Diputación Permanente, Junts es irrelevante, así que todo este paquete se puede sacar adelante siempre que lo apoye el PNV.

Aunque no pudieran decirlo así para evitar la condena de la Junta Electoral, es evidente que el Gobierno quería lanzar un mensaje político muy claro con esta traca final: si se renueva el Ejecutivo progresista, habrá más medidas como estas, que, según Díaz, son “coherentes” con lo que se ha hecho en años anteriores, pero si suman PP y Vox, se dará la vuelta y muchas incluso podrían ser rápidamente derogadas.

El Gobierno no solo aprueba medidas claramente progresistas para el voto de izquierdas, sino que también busca votantes más moderados, por ejemplo, con la reducción de impuestos y simplificación —de cuatro liquidaciones de IVA al año a una— para casi tres millones de autónomos, un sector en el que la derecha tiene mucha ventaja, según los sondeos. Esta rebaja de impuestos a los autónomos era reclamada hace tiempo por el colectivo.

Arcadi España, este martes en la rueda de prensa posterior al Consejo de Ministros, en La Moncloa. Víctor Sainz

Los ministros han hecho justificaciones muy políticas de sus medidas, siempre tratando de evitar exhibir logros del Ejecutivo porque eso es lo que prohíbe la Junta Electoral Central desde la rueda de prensa tras el Consejo de Ministros. “El año pasado la banca española tuvo 35.000 millones de euros beneficios, este año ya va por 30.000″, ha explicado el ministro de Hacienda, que ha añadido que el dinero recaudado, 1.400 millones para 2027, se destinará a construir vivienda pública. “Es importante que los bancos compartan parte de sus beneficios con la sociedad para hacer políticas de vivienda”, ha insistido después de recordar que se han recaudado 5.700 millones desde que se implantó en 2023 el impuesto. Serán las autonomías, sin embargo, las que gastarán ese dinero en vivienda, y el Gobierno no dejó muy claro cómo se garantizará que lo hagan. España ha explicado además que 2,6 millones de autónomos se verán beneficiados por una bajada de impuesto que se ha aprobado este martes y que supone 465 millones de euros de rebaja. España ha señalado que otras medidas, como la prórroga de la ayuda para carburantes, se estudiarán a finales de año cuando se conozca el IPC y se tomarán si la legislación permite hacerlo en funciones.

La ministra de Igualdad, Ana Redondo, ha sido la encargada de abrir paso a la batalla política con Isabel Díaz Ayuso, porque el Gobierno recurre al Tribunal Constitucional su ley del concebido no nacido, porque cree que se arroga unas competencias que no tiene. Redondo, en tono también buscadamente neutro por temor a la Junta Electoral Central, ha recordado además que, mientras en Galicia, gobernada por el PP, el 77% de los abortos se hacen en centros públicos, en Madrid o Andalucía, controladas por el mismo partido, no llegan al 1%.

La ministra de Igualdad, Ana Redondo, durante la rueda de prensa posterior al Consejo de Ministros. Víctor Sainz

Sáiz ha sido la encargada de justificar que no son medidas electoralistas. “Esta es nuestra hoja de ruta, es pura coherencia. Son medidas que se dirigen al 100% de la ciudadanía. Muchas de ellas tienen que ver con las fechas, como las prórrogas que hay que hacer porque llega el final del año, y todas están aprobadas en tiempo y forma. Vienen después de una madurez, de un trabajo largo”, ha insistido. También la vicepresidenta Díaz ha rematado esa idea: “Estas medidas no surgen ahora, se han trabajado en el seno del Gobierno. Esta norma [la ampliación del permiso por fallecimiento] viene del derecho europeo, estamos trasponiendo una directiva, pero además nos colocamos muy por encima del conjunto de países de nuestro entorno”, ha reivindicado.

La portavoz del Ejecutivo ha aprovechado para criticar al PP y Vox por alentar la idea de un posible pucherazo. “En democracia hay que saber ganar y hay que saber perder. Es intolerable que se cuestione el sistema electoral, que es uno de los mejores del mundo. Exijo respeto”, ha expresado. El Gobierno lanza así la idea de que la oposición teme no sumar como en 2023, a pesar de que casi todos los sondeos dicen que sí lo hará. En La Moncloa creen que las cosas están cambiando mucho en los últimos días e incluso defienden que Sánchez acertó con su estrategia en el debate, y confían en que el encuentro a cuatro del jueves sirva para rematar una tendencia que ven muy positiva de movilización de la izquierda, pero también de votantes del PSOE más moderados que ahora tenían dudas o estaban pensando pasar al bloque de la derecha. El Gobierno y sobre todo el presidente, Pedro Sánchez, mantienen el optimismo hasta el final y confían en la remontada, y esta traca final en el Consejo de Ministros está pensada para empujarla.

World.title: Feijóo: “En España no habrá sitio para quien no respete a las mujeres ni a las personas LGTBI”
World.content:
A pocas horas de que dé comienzo el Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra la Mujer, el PP vuelca su mensaje de campaña en las mujeres y en la violencia machista. Los populares también cargan contra el Ejecutivo de Pedro Sánchez por su “hipocresía”, ha defendido Alberto Núñez Feijóo, al reivindicar sus políticas feministas mientras La Moncloa infunde “machismo, inseguridad y corrupción”. “En España no habrá sitio para quien no respete a las mujeres ni a las personas LGTBI. Y me preocupa mucho que este discurso no sea capaz de hacerlo la izquierda en nuestro país”, ha proclamado el líder del PP en la tarde de este martes, en una intervención en la que ha prometido “expulsar a los extranjeros que cometan delitos contra la libertad sexual”, una de las medidas que contempla su programa para el 29-N. “¿Cómo es posible que aceptemos que se persiga a un homosexual? Yo quiero que vosotras, las mujeres de este país, estéis seguras y sobre todo que seáis libres", ha añadido Feijóo durante un mitin en Alicante, la cuarta provincia más poblada de España, ante unos 1.500 cargos y simpatizantes. Y a quienes ha pedido “no confiarse” y movilizarse “hasta el último instante”.

El acto en Alicante tiene lugar un día antes de que una delegación del Partido Popular participe en la manifestación convocada por el Movimiento Feminista de Madrid y el Foro de Madrid con motivo del 25-N. En paralelo, su socio en los gobiernos autonómicos y que puede completar su mayoría para formar Gobierno tras las próximas elecciones camina en dirección contraria. Vox pide poner fin al “fracasado” sistema de protección de las víctimas de violencia machista y acabar con la red de asociaciones que reciben ayudas públicas para atenderlas.

El PP utilizará este miércoles los casos de corrupción que afectan a antiguos cargos del PSOE para atacar al candidato socialista, aprovechando la coincidencia en campaña con el Día Internacional de la Eliminación de la Violencia contra la Mujer. El Partido Popular tiene agenda con actos electorales protagonizados por mujeres de su ejecutiva en distintos escenarios. La vicesecretaria Alma Ezcurra hará declaraciones en el parador de Teruel y la diputada Cayetana Álvarez de Toledo comparecerá frente al edificio de la Plaza de España de Madrid en el que residió Jéssica, expareja del exministro José Luis Ábalos.

Génova publicará además a primera hora del 25-N un manifiesto para renovar “su compromiso con las mujeres que sufren violencia machista”, una promesa que reiteran en los últimos días para reforzar la idea de que esta es una línea roja frente a Vox. En la Comunidad Valenciana, el PP obvió el concepto de “violencia machista” y calificó de “violencia intrafamiliar” la que sufren las mujeres a manos de sus parejas y exparejas en el acuerdo de Gobierno suscrito por el expresident Carlos Mazón con Vox en junio de 2023. Un Ejecutivo que saltó por los aires junto al resto de coaliciones un año después. En Alicante, Feijóo ha reiterado la medida de su programa que busca expulsar a los migrantes que cometan agresiones sexuales.

La cuarta provincia

Feijóo ha pisado este martes la Comunidad Valenciana solo tres días después del gran acto celebrado en la plaza de toros de Valencia. Eso, cuando hay otras autonomías en las que no ha recalado ni lo hará, ni en precampaña ni en campaña. ¿Por qué? Fuentes del PP justifican el doblete por distintos motivos. Primero, porque la plaza de toros de Valencia representa por sí misma un lugar emblemático, símbolo de victorias electorales del PP, que buscaba una imagen de fuerza. Segundo, porque la provincia de Alicante es la cuarta más poblada de España y la quinta en aportación al PIB nacional. “La Comunitat ha sido clave siempre en las victorias del Partido Popular”, ha proclamado el líder del PP en Alicante, provocando los aplausos de los presentes y los gritos de “¡se nota, se siente, Feijóo presidente!”. “Tienen toda la razón, es gente bien formada gracias a las políticas de educación de la Generalitat”, les ha respondido el candidato popular.

Según los sondeos del PP valenciano, el partido tiene asegurados los cinco escaños de 2023, pero hay uno que podría perder Sumar (hoy Frente Amplio) y que se llevaría Vox (ganaría uno más). En el terreno sostienen que la formación de Santiago Abascal gana a ddeptos por la cuestión de la gestión del agua en una tierra con una fuerte actividad agrícola. Hoy, Feijóo ha reiterado su promesa de promover un gran “pacto del agua” si es investido presidente. El problema es que tiene que aunar las sensibilidades de distintos territorios gobernados por el Partido Popular con intereses encontrados. El presidente de la Comunidad, Juan Francisco Pérez Llorca, se ha lanzado también contra el Gobierno y el PSOE por la misma cuestión. “Nos han cortado el trasvase Tajo Segura mientras los agricultores alicatinos pagan un millón de euros al mes”, ha criticado.

World.title: Pedro Sánchez: “Cataluña no va a fallar y va a liderar la gran victoria progresista”
World.content:
Serrat y Loles León apoyan al líder socialista en el mitin más multitudinario de los últimos años en Barcelona. El presidente anuncia una nueva ley para evitar que España entre en una guerra ilegal

El PSC ha celebrado este martes en Barcelona su mitin más multitudinario de los últimos tiempos con el objetivo de llevar a Pedro Sánchez en volandas a la victoria. Con un aforo desbordado, colas en el exterior y conatos de avalanchas, el recinto de la Fira de Barcelona, en la avenida Maria Cristina, se ha quedado pequeño. Acompañado del president y primer secretario del PSC Salvador Illa, Pedro Sánchez ha llegado a las puertas del pabellón y ha cogido un micrófono bajo una fina lluvia, ha dicho a los concentrados que no han podido acceder: “Cataluña no va a fallar el 29-N y va a liderar la gran victoria progresista”. La organización calcula que se han movilizado el acto 10.000 personas entre las que han entrado al pabellón y las que se han quedado fuera siguiendo el mitin a través de una pantalla gigante. La actriz Loles León, en la tribuna, y el cantautor Joan Manuel Serrat, este a través de un video, han participado en el acto.

Enfundados en camisetas rojas con el lema La força de la gent, el PSC ha movilizado a toda la militancia posible después de haber organizado la campaña en actos de pequeño formato. “Gracias de corazón por esta movilización en toda España y particularmente en Cataluña”, ha dicho Sánchez, que se ha hecho una infinidad de selfies hasta el escenario. Su discurso en el exterior ha sido el preludio de su intervención final en el que ha lucido simbólicamente dos camisetas: primero, una blanca en la que se se leía Más que un mitin y otra roja con esta frase en catalán: “Si votem, els aturem· (“Si votamos, los paramos”). “Tenemos una cita con la historia. No vamos a fallar. Va haber una movilización historia, remontada épica y victoria del partido socialista. Queremos el 75% y una mayoría absoluta de 176 escaños”, ha vuelto a mencionar este martes, como en varios de sus últimos mítines.

El presidente del Gobierno y candidato socialista, Pedro Sánchez, ondea una senyera en un momento del mitin. Massimiliano Minocri

El aumento hasta 20 semanas del permiso de paternidad, los 10 días de permiso por fallecimiento de un familiar, la reducción de los gravámenes a los autónomos o el nuevo impuesto a la banca. El presidente ha reivindicado las mejoras sociales aprobadas este martes en el Consejo de Ministros y anunciado que si revalida el cargo una nueva ley de Defensa nacional que requería disponer de mayoria absoluta para evitar que España pueda entrar en “guerras ilegales”, ha dicho, con la inclusión en el ordenamiento jurídico de la renuncia expresa a participar en una guerra como forma de agresión o presión diplomática.

Con objetivo de aumentar la participación, Pedro Sánchez ha reivindicado que este 29-N puede decantarse por la fuerza de la gente y ha recordado a cuatro personas con nombres propios que fueron catalizadores de cambios legales: Nevenka Fernandez (ley de igualdad), Ana Orantes (ley de violencia de género), Ramona Maneiro (ley de eutanasia) y Pedro Zerolo (ley de la protección del colectivo LGTBI). “Que los ciudadanos piensen en el país que quieren los próximos cuatro años. La historia no la escriben los hombres poderosos, la escribe la gente de a pie”, ha insistido.

Cataluña es el principal granero de votos socialistas y el PSC, convencido de la magnitud del reto, ha tirado de épica, echado el resto y ha etiquetado el acto como el mitin de la victoria. Ninguna encuesta, salvo la del CIS, se la adjudica a la izquierda pero el PSC considera que la remontada es posible si la participación se supera el 75%. No quieren pensar en otro escenario que en Cataluña sería particularmente complicado para una Generalitat dirigida por socialistas.

El presidente del Gobierno y candidato socialista, Pedro Sánchez, participa en un mitin en Barcelona por las elecciones generales del 29-N. En primer plano, a la izquierda, el 'president' catalán, Salvador Illa. Massimiliano Minocri

El mitin ha estado enfocado a movilizar a los votantes de izquierda indecisos. Y para ello el PSC ha recurrido también a la actriz Loles León, que ha contagiado su hilaridad, y a Serrat, que ha enviado un mensaje en vídeo. “¡Hay que movilizar a quien no vea todo lo que no se nos viene encima! Somos las mujeres de los años 70, con las tetas bien puestas“, ha exclamado León, que ha afirmado que Pedro Sánchez no insulta porque está lleno de amor a Begoña, su esposa. El cantautor ha sido más austero y ha sintetizado que votar no es solo un derecho que costó mucho ganar sino también un deber. ”Si vamos todos, ganamos”.

Tras defender que Pedro Sánchez, a diferencia Alberto Núñez Feijóo, sí que entiende Cataluña, Salvador Illa ha alertado del “peligro” de la abstención y ha reclamado el voto de todos los catalanistas. “Nos jugamos mucho. ¡Es un gran tipo y un político inmenso!”, ha dicho el president. El PSC desde el minuto uno se ha tapado los oídos e ignorado las recriminaciones a su izquierda de ERC y Frente Amplio y ha evitado entrar en el cuerpo a cuerpo con ellos. El alcalde Jaume Collboni ha reclamado el voto —“Estamos aquí para que Pedro siga siendo presidente de la nación”— y el ministro de Industria, Jordi Hereu, cabeza de lista, ha alertado del peligro de Vox. “Atacan la lengua, la cultura de Cataluña, todo lo que queremos”, ha advertido. “Será una gran victoria histórica. Pedro, aquí se te quiere y se te admira mucho. Te vamos a dar la victoria de la España progresista con el calor y los votos de Cataluña. A ti te han quemado muchas veces por la convivencia en Cataluña. Por eso te han quemado los fascistas”, ha zanjado.

Asistentes al mitin del PSOE, este martes en Barcelona.

Nadie duda en el PSC de que volverá a revalidar su victoria en estas elecciones. En 2023, el partido dirigido por Illa aportó a la bancada socialista 19 escaños, el segundo mejor resultado de su historia. Su objetivo siempre ha sido agrandar la distancia con el PP —ahora de 13 escaños—, pero ahora la derecha tiene dos cabezas y ha emergido con fuerza Vox en todos los sondeos. Sin ambages, el PSC ha reclamado desde el primer día una movilización histórica y la concentración del voto para derrotar a la derecha y la extrema derecha. El domingo, en Girona Hereu pidió un voto masivo para lograr el tercer escaño y para que no fuera a Vox. El pronóstico da idea de la irrupción de la extrema derecha: desde hace 15 años, es decir, el PP no logra tener representación en esa provincia.

World.title: Un centenar de veteranos socialistas sevillanos muestran su apoyo a Sánchez en respuesta al voto en blanco de Felipe González
World.content:
A menos de una semana para las generales del 29-N, 87 veteranos militantes socialistas de Sevilla han firmado un manifiesto de apoyo a Pedro Sánchez. “En estos momentos, de verdadero peligro de que las opciones de derecha radical puedan gobernar España, nos parece más necesario que nunca concentrar el voto de izquierda en el Partido Socialista. Es mucho lo que nos jugamos”, sostienen en el mensaje, que llega un día después de que el expresidente Felipe González sostuviera en Badajoz que, si confesara las razones por las que va a votar en blanco, el PSOE “perdería millones de votos más”. “[El manifiesto] estaba escrito ya, pero sus declaraciones generan una sinrazón entre la militancia”, explica a este diario Pepe Romero, un referente sindical en la capital andaluza y muy cercano en su juventud al antiguo secretario general, que fue su abogado cuando fue detenido durante el franquismo.

Como Romero, entre el casi centenar de firmantes figuran otros estrechos colaboradores de González, como Pepe Caballo o Luis Yáñez, desencantados con la deriva del expresidente. “Una cosa es la posición interna democrática de cada uno de nosotros, pero de cara a una convocatoria electoral tan complicada como la que estamos viviendo, este tipo de manifestaciones no se entienden”, abunda Romero. La trascendencia de estas elecciones es, precisamente, lo que quieren subrayar los suscriptores del manifiesto. “Una involución antidemocrática podría eliminar las conquistas sociales arduamente conseguidas por la clase trabajadora y devolvernos a una sociedad oscurantista, como la que ya conocimos y padecimos en cuarenta años de dictadura. Es obligación de todos los que creemos en el socialismo democrático alertar a la ciudadanía de lo que puede ocurrir”, sostienen.

No es el único veterano socialista molesto con las palabras de González. El primer presidente de la Junta de Andalucía, Rafael Escuredo, ha definido en X al exlíder del PSOE como un “viejo gruñón, incapaz de entender que su tiempo pasó”. “Lo mejor que puede hacer es callarse”, abunda.

No es la primera vez que Escuredo reacciona a las declaraciones de González. En febrero ya le pidió al histórico dirigente socialista: “Por qué no te retiras y nos dejas en paz”. “Se está quedando solo”, se lamenta Romero, que cree que González se ha alejado de la militancia, con la consecuente pérdida de ascendencia sobre los simpatizantes del partido.

El manifiesto de los socialistas veteranos de Sevilla pretende también llamar a la movilización de las bases en una provincia que podría caer, por primera vez en la historia de la democracia, del lado del PP en unas elecciones generales. Esta circunscripción es un bastión socialista que siempre ha votado al PSOE en las citas para el Congreso, pero que se ha teñido de azul en el resto de convocatorias electorales de los próximos años. El líder del PP andaluz y presidente de la Junta, Juan Manuel Moreno, se ha marcado como objetivo fundamental conseguir dar el vuelco histórico en este territorio.

World.title: Appeal court rejects state bid to pause Bonaire climate ruling
World.content:
The Netherlands has to draft binding national targets, the Court of Appeal in The Hague has ruled, after the state requested a suspension of its obligation.

The ruling is another step in the Bonaire climate case, which was taken to court by Greenpeace on behalf of the residents of the Dutch island in the Caribbean, where climate change is destroying the coral reef.

That case was won in January, and the court found that the government in The Hague had acted in a discriminatory manner to its people there.

Part of the ruling was that the Netherlands must set binding emissions targets for the whole economy in law by July 28, 2027, as well as draw up an adaptation plan for Bonaire that can be implemented by 2030. The ruling must be carried out even while an appeal is under way.

The government appealed the ruling in April, requesting a suspension. The Court of Appeal has largely rejected that request, but said international air and maritime transport can be left out of the targets but the government must move otherwise forward.

Marieke Vellekoop, director of Greenpeace Netherlands, said in a reaction: “The state has once again been reminded of its responsibility. Executing the judgment is not a non-binding ambition, but an obligation.”

Vellekoop said it was “incomprehensible that the state is doing everything it can to delay climate action,” while the consequences of the climate crisis are becoming increasingly severe. “On Bonaire, but also here in Europe. The cabinet must stop delaying and get to work now.”

World.title: Erasmus MC head of intensive care steps down over safety report
World.content:
The head of intensive care at Rotterdam’s Erasmus Medical Centre, Diederik Gommers, has stepped down in the wake of a damning report into a “culture of fear” that potentially compromised the safety of staff and patients.

The healthcare inspectorate IGJ said the situation in the department, the largest in the Netherlands, amounted to “a serious threat to the safety of patients or care”.

Gommers, who became one of the public faces of the Netherlands’ coronavirus response in 2020 when he was a member of the government’s Outbreak Management Team, quit his post with immediate effect when the findings became known this week.

The department’s board of directors has been placed under heightened supervision after the report said the psychological safety of staff was compromised by a management that did not accept being challenged or criticised.

The Erasmus MC hospital said in a statement on its website that it accepted it should have recognised the warning signs and taken action sooner.

“We are sorry that some colleagues did not feel safe enough to voice their concerns. Everyone should feel free to express their views, challenge each other and share signs.”

The hospital added that there was no suggestion patients had received substandard care as a result of the problems in the department.

18-month investigation

Inspectors began investigating the ICU 18 months ago after a whistleblower raised concerns about the workplace culture.

NOS late-night news show Nieuwsuur and regional news channel Rijnmond said they had seen hundreds of internal emails and documents going back five years and spoken to 26 current and former staff about the situation.

Doctors said “tensions” between medical specialists deterred staff from speaking out if they were critical of or worried about their colleagues’ decisions.

Jan Maarten van den Berg, a former healthcare inspector who specialised in intensive care, told Nieuwsuur: “These conclusions are very severe. There needs to be a breakthrough in the situation at Erasmus for the sake of the patients.”

Nieuwsuur earlier reported that Gommers did not have the legally required qualifications to carry out medical research on patients. The hospital said Gommers had not done any clinical research since 2023 and had started studying to obtain his certificates.

World.title: Juice and milk bottles to join deposit scheme in 2027
World.content:
Dutch packaging trade association Verpact has announced it will begin a deposit return system for plastic juice and dairy bottles on its own initiative, according to broadcaster NOS.

Plastic juice and dairy bottles of up to three litres will carry a deposit (statiegeld) from next year. Verpact said it is preparing a phased rollout in 2027. Labels, return machines, IT systems and logistics will all have to be adjusted.

The move follows pressure from climate and green growth minister Stientje van Veldhoven, who wants 90% of plastic bottles sold in the Netherlands to be collected by January 1, 2028. According to NOS, that target cannot be met without juice and dairy bottles.

In September, Van Veldhoven proposed making deposits compulsory on all plastic bottles up to three litres and banning the sale of bottles and cans without a deposit.

Dairy bottles have so far been exempt because producers say they are hard to clean, and the minister has made hygiene measures a condition. Many juice producers already charge a deposit voluntarily.

World.title: Cold comfort: Dutch skater smashes one-hour natural ice record
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Marathon skater Judith Krabbenborg has taken advantage of the early cold snap to smash the world one-hour record for skating on natural ice.

The 29-year-old took to the ice in Winterswijk, Gelderland, at 8.30am on Tuesday and covered a distance of 34 kilometres 878 metres, beating the previous women’s record by 2.6 kilometres.

“I could feel my legs and my back hurting at the end, but there were so many people standing on the sidelines that it gave me energy,” she told NOS.

The previous record, set four years ago by Femke Mossinkoff, also in Winterswijk, was the first official time for the hour by a woman on natural ice. On the same day Bart Vreugdenhil set the current men’s record of 36 kilometers 717 metres.

Most skating records are set on artificial ice, but Winterswijk is one of three arenas where the local club has been able to create a natural arena for early-morning skaters during the recent cold weather.

The all-time women’s record is 40 kilometres 569 metres, set by another Dutch skater, Carien Kleibeuker, in Inzell, Austria, in 2015.

The rink at Winterswijk closed a few hours after Krabbenborg’s record-breaking skate as the ice started to melt, but it is expected to be available again on Wednesday morning.

World.title: Dutch police seek witnesses to Suriname massacre, 40 years on
World.content:
The Dutch police unit for war crimes, TIM, is helping prosecutors in Suriname search for witnesses of the notorious 1986 Moiwana massacre in which at least 39 civilians were murdered by the Surinamese army.

It is believed likely that people with evidence or testimony are living in the Netherlands. The TIM put out a call for witnesses on Opsporing Verzocht, a police appeals programme, on Monday night.

The massacre occurred during Suriname’s so-called Interior War (1986-1992), a conflict between the military regime of Desi Bouterse, who seized power in a 1980 coup, and rebels led by his former bodyguard Ronnie Brunswijk. Around a third of the country’s entire population moved to the Netherlands in the years around independence in 1975.

With the massacre’s 40-year commemoration coming up, Surinamese prosecutors have asked the TIM to help revive a hunt for evidence and hold those responsible to account.

Soldiers of the army led by Desi Bouterse attacked Moiwana, which is a Maroon village close to the border with French Guiana. They were supposedly hunting Ronnie Brunswijk, a militant regime opponent who was said to be hiding in the village, though survivors say he was not there and the soldiers opened fire anyway.

The case has been stalled for decades. The police inspector leading the investigation into the incident was assassinated in 1990, and though the Inter-American Court of Human Rights ruled in favour of the survivors in 2005 and ordered reparations and apologies, no one has been prosecuted.

Bouterse himself became president of Suriname from 2010 to 2020. He died in 2024. Brunswijk became vice-president from 2020 to 2025. The Surinamese prosecution service reopened an inquiry in 2023 and preliminary judicial investigation began in 2025.

The 40-year commemoration will be held this coming weekend on November 29. TIM is urging anyone with information to come forward.

World.title: New HPV vaccine could save nearly 13,000 cancer diagnoses a year
World.content:
Nearly 13,000 people could avoid a cancer diagnosis later in life if the Netherlands raises its HPV vaccination rate, new medical research has found.

Children aged 10 are given two doses of the vaccine, which protects against a virus that causes cervical cancer in women.

A new version introduced in September covers a wider range of cancers that affect both sexes, such as vaginal and penile cancers.

Around 80% of people in the Netherlands contract the human papillomavirus, mainly though sexual activity.

Most people who are infected have no symptoms, but persistent infection is responsible for around 99.7% of all cases of cervical cancer, one of the most common types in women. Every year 1,100 women and 400 men are diagnosed with a form cancer linked to HPV, most of whom are under the age of 45.

Researchers at Erasmus Medical Centre in Rotterdam and the Dutch cancer centre IKNL said 12,800 diagnoses could be saved if the new vaccine is given to all children who reach the age of 10 in future.

The Netherlands currently has a vaccination rate of 61% for the HPV vaccine, well below the World Health Organisation’s advisory rate of 90% for girls. Around 60% of boys have had the jab as well since the public health agency RIVM added it to their vaccine schedule in 2022.

Gynaecologist and oncologist Luc van Lonkhuijsen, of Amsterdam’s university medical centre, said many parents were anxious about side effects or dismissed it as unimportant.

“We have been vaccinating for 15 years and the number of side-effects we see is really very limited,” he told NOS.

World.title: No evidence of mental illness in suspect of Lisa’s murderer
World.content:
Experts have found no evidence of mental disorder in the man accused of murdering Lisa from Abcoude, the 17-year-old girl whose killing last year sparked a nationwide uprising against femicide and public safety.

The public prosecution service (OM) had ordered an investigation into the mental state of the man, who calls himself Chris Jude, after he claimed he had heard voices telling him to commit rape and murder.

The findings were released in the fifth preliminary hearing of the case at Amsterdam district court on Tuesday.

He’d previously denied remembering anything about the incident, but then admitted to the crimes and said he’d been hearing voices.

On August 20 last year, Lisa phoned the police while cycling back to her parents house after a night out. She was feeling threatened by a man following her on a path through Duivendrecht.

By the time the police arrived, it was too late and her body was found. A manhunt led to Jude’s capture several days later. He was also charged with the rape and attempted rape of two other woman in Amsterdam days before murdering Lisa.

World.title: Erkens claims wolves can be culled despite EU protected status
World.content:
Junior agriculture minister Silvio Erkens has moved a step closer to allowing provinces to shoot wolves for population control.

Erkens said in a letter to parliament that the Netherlands could comply with EU conservation rules with 11 wolf packs, three fewer than the current number, after studying a report commissioned by his predecessor, Jean Rummenie of the farmers’ party BBB.

Experts have warned that the report by Italian independent researcher Marco Appollonio was flawed and likely to face legal challenges if he went ahead with measures based on its findings.

Rummenie ordered Appollonio to study the Dutch wolf population after rejecting an earlier analysis by Wageningen University & Research, the Netherlands’ leading agricultural college, which concluded that the Netherlands could sustainably support between 23 and 56 wolf packs.

Appolonio concluded that the wolf population in the Netherlands is “genetically healthy” and the country met the European Union’s criteria for maintaining a standing population of wolves, Erkens said.

“This confirmation that conditions in the Netherlands are favourable for a maintained population make it possible to manage wolves in the Netherlands, and that is the decision I am taking in principle,” the junior minister wrote.

Wolf-free zones

EU rules require member states to identify how many wolves they can support and recognise their place in the ecosystem as apex predators. Wolves contribute to biodiversity by controlling populations of species such as wild boar and deer and forcing them to disperse, which protects the plants they feed on.

Erkens said he wants to create wolf-free zones by asking provinces to identify areas that are suitable for wolves to roam, where they should be confined.

This would help reduce the number of confrontations with people and their pets and mean less damage caused by wolves feeding on livestock, he argued.

But ecologists say the study is likely to fall foul of EU rules because Rummenie asked Appolonio to take into account the economic impact of wolves, something the EU explicitly forbids.

The European Court of Justice said in a recent ruling against Austria that preventing loss of livestock was not a valid reason on its own for culling wolves, after a farmer was allowed to kill a wolf that had killed 20 of his sheep.

Problem wolf

Arie Trouwborst, professor of nature conservation law at Tilburg University, told NOS: “That binding report by the court has been completely ignored in the Italian report. The report from Wageningen showed that a minimum of 23 packs are needed to fulfil the [EU] criteria.”

In the Netherlands a so-called “problem wolf” was shot dead under licence last year after it attacked walkers in the near Utrecht, but only after a protracted court battle between the provincial government and conservation group Faunabescherming.

Erkens has called a national wolf summit in February where provincial and local government, vets and representatives of the tourism and recreation industry will discuss the government’s strategy.

He also plans to work more closely with Germany, Belgium and Luxembourg to draw up a common policy on wolf populations and press the EU to recognise the interests of “very small densely populated countries such as the Benelux countries.”

World.title: Poland and US sign defence technology cooperation agreement

Poland and the United States have signed an agreement on defence research, development, testing and evaluation, concluding 17 years of negotiations and opening the way for deeper technological cooperation. The agreement establishes a framework for joint defence projects, as well as the exchange of technical data and expertise, giving Poland – which is already a major importer of US arms – a formal role in the development of American defence technologies for the first time. Under Secretary Emil Michael (@USWREMichael) and Mr. Cezary Tomczyk, Poland’s Secretary of State at the Ministry of National Defence, signed the Agreement Between the Government of the United States of America and the Government of the Republic of Poland for Defense Research,… pic.twitter.com/7EAgK3nD2i — Department of War CTO (@DoWCTO) November 23, 2026 The agreement was signed at the Pentagon by Poland’s deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk and US under secretary of war for research and engineering Emil Michael. According to the Department of War, the deal will help “turn research and development into validated military capabilities to jointly support US and Polish warfighters”. Tomczyk said the agreement would allow Polish universities, research institutes and companies to participate in joint research and development work on defence technology with US partners and would enable such technologies to be tailored more closely to the requirements of the Polish armed forces. During a briefing in Washington, Tomczyk admitted that the agreement had been negotiated for what he described as a “probably record-breaking” 17 years, but he noted a “significant acceleration in relations” between the US and Poland over the last six months. General Marcin Górka, who oversees innovation in the Polish armed forces and accompanied Tomczyk to the United States, likewise welcomed the agreement, which he said would “open the doors to American military laboratories for our scientists and engineers”. Górka also said the agreement would enable Poland and the United States to jointly develop anti-drone systems and advanced drones, with testing taking place in both countries. Poland is a major importer of US military hardware. Between 2021 and 2025, it was the biggest overall importer of arms in NATO, with around 44% of that equipment coming from the US, including F-35 fighter jets, Abrams tanks, Patriot air defence systems and HIMARS rocket launchers. But Poland has recently sought to move from being a client of the US defence industry to more of a partner. Earlier this month, Polish defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth signed a declaration on expanding bilateral defence-industrial cooperation Poland and the US have signed a statement of intent on strengthening defence industry cooperation. Polish defence minister @KosiniakKamysz said his country would be "the US ambassador in the EU", including seeking EU funds for jointly produced equipment https://t.co/SKHrxTEKIW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 11, 2026 Last month, Poland was chosen as the location for a planned Patriot missile maintenance and servicing facility, the first of its kind outside the United States. In May, an agreement was signed to establish a centre in Poland for servicing the engines of Abrams tanks. This year, Polish state defence group PGZ was chosen as the first European producer of American Barracuda-500M cruise missiles, while US defence giant Northrop Grumman and Polish arms manufacturer Niewiadów-PGM announced plans to jointly produce artillery shells in Poland. Poland is also seeking to host a new permanent US military base, with Tomczyk reiterating during his Washington visit that a decision is expected from the Trump administration in early December. NATO has approved the deployment of an Airborne Warning and Control System to Poland in response to three Russian missiles striking Polish territory last week. Hours after the decision was announced, Poland’s airspace was again violated by a Russian drone https://t.co/gudQJsPlQ5 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 24, 2026 The new agreement on defence technology was signed amid heightened tensions with Russia. On Friday, three Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles struck separate locations in southeastern Poland, near the Ukrainian border. Tomczyk said the Polish delegation had briefed Pentagon officials on the missile strikes, which he described as a “provocation” by Russia. The Polish minister was also asked about US President Donald Trump last week calling Russia’s Vladimir Putin his “friend”. “One thing is certain: Vladimir Putin is not our friend; he is a threat to us,” replied Tomczyk. “This is the most important message that should come from Poland and resonate with the people of the United States.” Subsequently, on Monday night, a Russian drone entered Polish airspace from Ukraine for a few minutes before turning back. World.title: Poland, Lithuania and Latvia violated rights of migrants sent back to Belarus, finds European court

Poland, Lithuania and Latvia violated the human rights of migrants from Afghanistan, Iraq and Cuba who entered their countries illegally from Belarus in 2021 and 2022, the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR) has ruled. However, the ECHR did also recognise that states have the right to prevent the entry of migrants who have been “instrumentalised” by Belarus in order to create a crisis on the European Union’s eastern borders. That latter finding prompted Poland’s deputy interior minister with oversight of migration policy to hail today’s rulings as a victory and endorsement of the government’s tough border policies. It was also described as a groundbreaking moment by a leading human rights organisation. 📽️ Watch a video explainer on the Grand Chamber cases concerning instrumentalisation of migration. 📽️ Regardez la vidéo explicative sur les affaires de Grande Chambre sur l'instrumentalisation de la migration. pic.twitter.com/ZhXqZ6lIur — ECHR CEDH (@ECHR_CEDH) November 24, 2026 In 2021, Belarus began encouraging, assisting and, in some cases, forcing tens of thousands of migrants – mainly from Asia and Africa – to irregularly cross into the neighbouring EU states of Poland, Lithuania and Latvia. Belarus engineered the migration crisis as part of the various “hybrid actions” undertaken alongside its ally Russia with the intention of destabilising countries they regard as hostile. In response, Poland, Lithuania and Latvia took a variety of measures intended to prevent the entry of irregular migrants from Belarus. In many cases, they carried out so-called “pushbacks”, sending migrants who had crossed the border back into Belarus. On Tuesday, the ECHR announced three sets of rulings on cases brought against Poland, Lithuania and Latvia in relation to actions they had taken against specific migrants who had entered from Belarus. The European court noted that the migrants had “entered unlawfully” as part of Belarus’s “instrumentalisation of migration”, which it described as a “hostile action” that had “the intention of destabilising the respondent states or the wider region”. This “represented a deliberate threat to the state” and “was liable to put at risk its essential functions, including the maintenance of law and order and the safeguarding of its national security”. Poland wants the European Union to deny the right to asylum for migrants who cross EU borders in organised, aggressive groups, just as Poland has itself done on its border with Belarus https://t.co/7Gbsvs6I1e — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 7, 2026 The court found that states do have the right to control entry, and even fully close their borders, as well as to “remove a foreign national to the instrumentalising state”, without it automatically being a violation of the human rights convention. However, the ECHR also deemed that, “before removing an individual in such circumstances, national authorities had an obligation to detect those individuals who would be particularly at risk of suffering or enduring ill-treatment”. That included those who had personal vulnerabilities (such as old age, ill health or a disability) or who would face a threat to their life or serious risk of mistreatment by being returned to Belarus. In the cases of Poland and Latvia, the ECHR found that they had breached the obligation to undertake such an assessment before returning certain migrants. A court has found that Poland's border guard violated the law when sending two Afghan and Ethiopian men back to Belarus after they injured themselves crossing the anti-migrant border fence. One of them had made clear his wish to claim asylum in Poland https://t.co/42yOuGEgns — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 18, 2024 For Poland, the case concerned an unnamed Afghan national who had been part of a group that had crossed back and forth over the Polish-Belarusian border multiple times, as often happened in the early stages of the crisis. The ECHR noted that it had, at the time, issued an interim measure requiring that the Afghan man not be returned to Belarus. However, the Polish authorities did not take this into account, and sent him back to Belarus on 20 October 2021, thereby demonstrating they had not complied with their obligation to properly assess his need for protection, found the ECHR. The court also ruled that, in the case of that applicant as well as a fellow Afghan national, Poland had violated their rights by preventing lawyers from having access to them. It ordered Poland to pay the two men €20,000 (89,000 zloty) and €5,000 respectively as compensation. Two Afghan asylum seekers who crossed from Belarus into Poland have been awarded compensation for their mistreatment by Polish border guards. They were detained and driven back towards the border by officers, who did not accept their asylum applications https://t.co/M9bSHakS5j — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 18, 2025 In Latvia’s case, the ECHR ruled that the country had violated its obligations by sending Iraqi Kurdish children, some of whom were infants, back into Belarus, “disregarding the[ir] evident vulnerability”. At the same time, the European court dismissed further complaints by adult migrants against Latvia and Lithuania, finding that they had not demonstrated any vulnerability or risk. However, it did find that Lithuania had violated some Cuban migrants’ rights by failing to properly inform them of the reasons they were being held in a detention camp and thereby also of their right to legally challenge their detention. It also ruled that Latvia had violated the rights of migrants on its territory due to the poor conditions they found themselves in when camped out on Latvian territory, with no access to sanitary facilities and insufficient protection from rain and cold nighttime temperatures. ⚖️ Grand Chamber cases ➡️ Responding to realities of instrumentalisation of migration at Belarus border, European Court safeguards essential rights and reiterates limits of Convention protections. 🔗 Press release: https://t.co/nflEyCWKb1 — ECHR CEDH (@ECHR_CEDH) November 24, 2026 In response to today’s ruling on Poland, the deputy interior minister with oversight of migration policy, Maciej Duszczyk, hailed it as “very important and favourable for us”. He said that the ECHR’s findings regarding states’ rights to defend their borders from instrumentalised migration effectively endorsed Poland’s policies. The Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights (HFPC), a Warsaw-based NGO, also noted that the ECHR’s Grand Chamber had, for the first time, defined the scope of states’ obligations when another state has instrumentalised migration “In the ECHR’s view, when migration is instrumentalised, states are not obliged to assess whether people being returned to the state instrumentalising migration will have access to an adequate asylum procedure there,” noted HFPC. Bardzo ważny i dobry dla nas wyrok Europejskiego Trybunału Praw Człowieka. Niezakwestionowano naszego modelu walki z nielegalną migracją. Trybunał odniósł się do instrumentalizacji jako sprzecznej z Konwencją i podkreślił prawo państ do obrony i ochrony swoich granic. — Maciek Duszczyk (@MaciekDuszczyk) November 24, 2026 A number of Polish courts have also found that the authorities violated the rights of migrants on the Belarus border. Last year, two Afghan asylum seekers were awarded 5,000 zloty compensation for their mistreatment by Polish border guards. In 2024, another court found that the border guard violated the law when sending Afghan and Ethiopian migrants back to Belarus after they had injured themselves while crossing the border. Last year, Poland’s government effectively formalised pushbacks by introducing a ban on asylum claims by people crossing the border irregularly from Belarus, who are now sent back without their applications being accepted. The measure has been criticised by human rights groups – including the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and Poland’s own human rights commissioner – as a violation of international law and Poland’s constitution. The number of attempted illegal crossings by migrants from Belarus to Poland fell from 15,500 in the first half of 2025 to 235 this year – a drop of over 98% Poland also now claims a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally https://t.co/RFZkd7CeIk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 20, 2026 Poland has also implemented a number of other tough policies, including easing rules for the use of firearms by uniformed officers protecting the border from illegal migration. This year has seen the migration crisis abate significantly, with Poland reporting a 98% decline in attempted illegal crossings from Belarus, as well as a 100% success rate in apprehending those who do cross. World.title: NATO to send surveillance aircraft to Poland after Russian missile strikes
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. NATO has approved the deployment of an Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) to Poland in response to last week’s incident in which three Russian missiles struck Polish territory. Shortly after the decision was announced, Poland’s airspace was again violated by a Russian drone that entered from Ukraine. However, although the military was given authorisation to shoot the object down, they did not do so after the drone began to move back into Ukraine. Today, NATO Ambassadors met in the North Atlantic Council to discuss last week’s violations of Polish airspace. This was a dangerous incident and Russia bears full responsibility. NATO and Allied assets reacted quickly to the airspace violations, and the Supreme Allied Commander… — NATO Spokesperson (@NATOpress) November 23, 2026 On Friday morning last week, three objects struck at different locations in southeast Poland, not far from the Ukrainian border. The incidents took place amid large-scale Russian attacks on Ukraine, and on Sunday Poland confirmed that all three were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles. The missiles were in Polish airspace for around three minutes before striking the ground. Two Swedish Gripen fighter jets, which were patrolling Polish skies as part of a NATO air policing mission, received authorisation from NATO’s Combined Air Operations Centre to fire upon the objects if certain conditions were met. However, the pilots were unable to confirm their identity in time due to poor weather conditions. On Monday, an extraordinary meeting of the North Atlantic Council, NATO’s main decision-making body, took place to discuss the incident. Afterwards, deputy defence minister Paweł Zalewski, who represented Poland at the meeting, announced that NATO had agreed to place an AWACS “at Poland’s disposal”. Later, NATO’s spokeswoman, Allison Hart, confirmed that “the Supreme Allied Commander Europe has authorised the forward deployment of a NATO AWACS aircraft” and is also “examining the deployment of additional assets as he continues to assess our deterrence and defence posture in Poland and elsewhere”. Poland has confirmed that the three objects which struck its territory last Friday were all Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles. Preliminary findings indicate the missiles were recently manufactured at a plant in Dubna, Russia https://t.co/4N6k3eBUGN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 23, 2026 “This is a very serious capability that gives us enhanced situational awareness,” said Zalewski, quoted by news website Wirtualna Polska. “This is an immediate NATO response, and we are very happy about it.” “What I heard today is a great demonstration of the alliance’s unity with Poland in the face of Russian attacks,” he added. “It’s safe to say that the Russians have moved up the escalation ladder in their relations with NATO.This means…the need for an appropriate response.” Zalewski emphasised that “we’re not talking about offensive actions in any way, but about the ability to defend against all the attacks Russia is launching against NATO countries”. The aim is “not to escalate, but to…discourage Russia from attacks”. Wiceminister @ZalewskiPawel w Kwaterze Głównej #NATO: Do dyspozycji Polski będzie jeden samolot szybkiego ostrzegania #AWACS. To jest bardzo poważna zdolność, która daje nam pogłębioną świadomość sytuacyjną. I to jest natychmiastowa reakcja NATO. — Ministerstwo Obrony Narodowej 🇵🇱 (@MON_GOV_PL) November 23, 2026 On Monday night, after NATO had made its decision, Poland’s airspace was again violated, this time by a Russian drone that crossed the border from Ukraine. The operational command of Poland’s armed forces announced shortly before midnight that it had continuously tracked the object and granted authorisation to shoot it down. However, after the drone changed course and began to head east, back towards the border, a decision was made to refrain from engaging it, “taking into account the potential threat to civilians and the possible consequences of shooting down the object”, said operational command. W trakcie nocnego ataku Federacji Rosyjskiej na cele w zachodniej części Ukrainy, prowadzonego z wykorzystaniem środków napadu powietrznego, doszło do krótkotrwałego naruszenia polskiej przestrzeni powietrznej przez rosyjski bezzałogowy statek powietrzny. W odpowiedzi na… pic.twitter.com/BhJN7UYg7m — Dowództwo Operacyjne RSZ (@DowOperSZ) November 23, 2026 According to a report by broadcaster RMF, based on unnamed sources, the vehicle was a jet-powered drone that flew 20 km into Poland and remained in Polish airspace for around nine minutes. Speaking to RMF on Tuesday morning, Zalewski said that “it is difficult to imagine that this was an accident; we assume it was an intentional action”. Russia has so far not commented on either its missiles hitting Poland last Friday nor the latest drone incursion. They are the latest in a series of airspace violations. In September this year, a Russian helicopter briefly crossed the border from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. In September 2025, around 20 Russian drones crossed Poland’s eastern borders in an unprecedented violation that prompted Poland to trigger NATO’s Article 4. The Netherlands will become the latest country to purchase Poland’s Piorun man-portable air-defence systems, which have been increasingly in demand following their successful use during Ukraine’s defence against Russia. On Monday, their Polish manufacturer, Mesko, which is part of state-owned defence group PGZ, signed an agreement adding the Netherlands to a list of countries that will buy Pioruns with funds from the European Union’s SAFE mechanism for financing defence spending. 🇵🇱🇳🇱⚡ HOLANDIA DOŁĄCZA DO DRUŻYNY PIORUNA! W @PGZ_MESKO_SA w Skarżysku-Kamiennej podpisano aneks do umowy ramowej, umożliwiający Holandii dołączenie do wspólnych zamówień zestawów PIORUN. ✍️ Dokument podpisali gen. dyw. Artur Kuptel, Szef @AgencjaUzbr, oraz Krzysztof Marwicki… pic.twitter.com/lVH0QgdD0t — Polska Grupa Zbrojeniowa🇵🇱 (@PGZ_pl) November 23, 2026 Piorun (meaning “thunderbolt” in Polish) is a shoulder-mounted system that fires air-defence missiles capable of destroying aerial vehicles, such as helicopters, drones and low-flying planes, at short range. In 2022, Pioruns were among the large quantities of military equipment that Poland provided to Ukraine to help its eastern neighbour defend itself from Russia’s full-scale invasion. The systems have been successfully used to take down Russian aircraft. Since then, they have been in high demand, with Mesko receiving orders from the United States, Norway, Belgium and Sweden, as well as Ukraine itself. In August this year, Mesko signed an 8 billion zloty (€1.8 billion) agreement to supply further Piorun systems to Poland, Norway, Lithuania and Latvia, with the deal financed through SAFE funds. Precise details were not revealed. However, the agreement was said to involve the supply of “several hundred” launchers and “several thousand” missiles, with over 80% of the equipment going to Poland’s own armed forces. Now Mesko has signed an addendum to that deal, adding the Netherlands to the list of countries that are jointly ordering Pioruns. Deputy defence minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka, who has overseen Poland’s participation in the SAFE programme, said after attending Monday’s signing ceremony that the Netherlands would not be the last country to join the procurement of Pioruns. “We promised that the list of Mesko’s buyers from all over Europe would grow, and today we have living proof of that,” said Sobkowiak-Czarnecka. “And I can reveal a secret: it’s not over yet.” She noted that Mesko has stepped up its production volumes in response to demand. Last year, it could produce “several hundred” systems annually; that has now risen to 1,500, and is set to grow even further. Last week, PGZ and the state assets ministry signed an agreement to support Mesko’s expansion with around 370 million zloty from the state Capital Investment Fund (FIK). It will help bring production capacity to around 2,500 per year. 🗣️ "Obiecywaliśmy, że lista kupujących z całej Europy będzie się powiększać i mamy tego żywy dowód. A mogę zdradzić sekret, że to jeszcze nie koniec. Dzisiejsza umowa to umowa w ramach zakupów w mechanizmie SAFE"@magdasobkowiak o zestawach Piorun dla Holandii ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/sTxG5SwnbZ — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) November 23, 2026 Growing demand for Pioruns resulted in Mesko last year posting the best financial results in its 100-year history. The firm’s revenues of 2.3 billion zloty in 2025 were up 33% year-on-year. The EU’s SAFE programme is providing a total of €150 billion in loans at preferential rates for member states to use on defence-related spending. Poland, with around €44 billion, is the largest single recipient. While most SAFE purchases are conducted individually by member states, some are also carried out jointly. Such joint procurement can also involve certain non-EU countries, such as Norway. World.title: Public astronomical observatory opens in Warsaw
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Warsaw’s first astronomical observatory open to the public and run by a local municipal institution launched on Sunday. Its organisers say the facility, with two telescopes allowing safe observation of the Sun and photography of the cosmos, is aimed at astronomy enthusiasts as well as children and young people, who will be able to watch the night sky and participate in recording data without needing their own equipment. The new observatory, which is located on the roof of the Gocław Culture Terminal in the Praga-South of Poland’s capital, was created in response to growing public interest in astronomy, science and new technologies, says city hall. “Under the three-metre-high dome, specialised equipment awaits, allowing for observation of the sky, including safe viewing of the Sun,” said mayor Rafał Trzaskowski, who visited the facility last week ahead of its official opening. “Anyone who is interested can come here and learn about space through observation, photographing the sky and hands-on activities,” he added. The observatory will be free to use but only accessible during organised events, owing to limited space and the expensive equipment it contains, reports newspaper Super Express. “The dome houses very expensive equipment. For most of the year, it will function as a broadcasting station, and images from the telescopes will be projected onto screens in the main hall of the terminal,” Jacek Białek, head of Gocław Culture Terminal, told the newspaper. “We will invite people inside the dome as part of programs, the dates of which will be published on the cultural centre’s website,” he added. Participants in workshops and events will also be able to help collect and analyse data, with Białek noting that the centre will be working closely with scientists from the University of Warsaw The new facility cost around 500,000 zloty (€111,000), most of which was covered from the district budget, with contributions from private donations as well as grants from the state-owned military optoelectronic equipment company PCO and the national lottery foundation. The core of the new facility is a 14″ DO-GSO (Ritchey-Chrétien) telescope with a mirror diameter of approximately 35 cm and a focal length of approximately 2,850 mm, placed on an EQ8-RH equatorial mount with automatic sky tracking. This setup, along with a QHY268M Pro monochrome camera, a filter wheel and an electronic focuser, will be used for astrophotography and targeted photometric measurements, producing images suited to Warsaw’s atmospheric conditions. The observatory also boasts a specialist Sky-Watcher Heliostar 100 H-Alpha telescope, which is used for safe and detailed observation and astrophotography of the Sun, allowing viewers to see structures in the solar atmosphere invisible through an ordinary telescope. The telescope allows solar prominences – large, bright features extending out from the Sun’s surface – to be observed and compared with images produced on other days. The telescope is protected by a three-metre dome that automatically opens and rotates. Warsaw has been chosen as the location for a new European Space Agency security centre, as Poland takes another step in its ambitions to become a bigger player in the space sector The facility will be the @esa's first outside its 11 founding member states https://t.co/WnHIbrW3ze — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 13, 2026 The observatory also features a computer coordinating its measurements, a camera showing almost the entire sky, and a weather monitoring system. Observations will depend on atmospheric conditions and visibility. “Examples of how this telescope might be used include photographing the cosmos and conducting simple research, such as measuring changes in the brightness of stars and producing graphs illustrating these changes,” explained Ewa Konarzewska from Gocław Culture Terminal. Poland has placed great emphasis on developing its space industry in recent years, with the aim of becoming a major European player in the sector. Last year, the country launched its first national military satellite. A Polish firm, Creotech Instruments, signed Poland’s largest-ever contract with the European Space Agency, a €52 million deal to build and launch a constellation of Earth observation satellites. Meanwhile, 2025 also saw astronaut Sławosz Uznański-Wiśniewski become the second-ever Pole to travel into space, as part of an ESA mission to the International Space Station. Earlier this year, Warsaw was chosen as the location for a new ESA centre focused on civil security and resilience, with the agency’s head declaring that “Poland has rapidly become one of the driving forces in Europe’s space sector”. We cannot do what we do without your support. Prosecutors investigating three objects that landed in Poland last Friday morning have confirmed that they were all Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles. They added that preliminary findings indicate the missiles were recently manufactured at a plant in Dubna, Russia. The objects struck at three different locations in southeastern Poland – Nowy Lipowiec, Rudnik and Mołodycz – not far from the Ukrainian border. The incidents took place amid large-scale Russian attacks on Ukraine. No injuries or damage to infrastructure was reported as a result of the strikes on Poland. Prokuratorzy wojskowi oraz Żandarmeria Wojskowa ustalili, że w Nowym Lipowcu, Rudniku i Mołodyczu spadły rosyjskie pociski manewrujące Ch-101. Wyprodukowano je w IV kwartale 2026 r. w zakładach w Dubnej pod Moskwą. W dwóch miejscach oględziny już się zakończyły. Dziś rano,… https://t.co/nNfkvx4FAq — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 23, 2026 Initially, on Friday, Poland’s defence minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, identified one of the objects as a Kh-101 cruise missile – the same type as one that entered Polish airspace and exploded in eastern Poland in July this year. He said another was also likely a missile while the third was probably a jet-powered drone. However, in a statement issued on Sunday, the district prosecutor’s office in Lublin, which is leading the investigation, confirmed that all three objects were Kh-101 cruise missiles. Analysis is still underway, but “preliminary findings indicate that all the missiles were manufactured in the fourth quarter of 2026 at a plant in Dubna (Moscow Oblast, Russian Federation)”, said the prosecutors. Dubna is home to MKB Raduga, the Russian aerospace firm that produces Kh-101 missiles. “Kremlin trolls will once again try to convince Poles that these are not Russian missiles,” wrote Waldemar Żurek, the justice minister and prosecutor general, “but the evidence nips those lies in the bud.” Ireneusz Nowak, the operational commander of the Polish armed forces, revealed on Friday that the three missiles were in Polish airspace for around three minutes before hitting the ground. Two Swedish Gripen fighter jets, which are helping patrol Polish skies as part of a NATO air policing mission, had attempted to intercept the missiles. They received authorisation from NATO’s Combined Air Operations Centre to fire upon the objects if certain conditions were met. However, the pilots were unable to confirm the identity of the objects in time, largely because of “extremely difficult weather conditions”, said Nowak, quoted by the Rzeczpospolita daily. Komunikat szwedzkich Sił Zbrojnych w związku z naruszeniem polskiej przestrzeni powietrznej: "Szwedzkie myśliwce JAS Gripen w misji obrony powietrznej nad Polską Szwedzkie Siły Powietrzne uczestniczyły minionej nocy w operacji obrony powietrznej z wykorzystaniem samolotów JAS… pic.twitter.com/oq9WXW3vXO — Ambasada Szwecji (@AmbSzweWarszawa) November 20, 2026 Poland’s NATO allies have expressed support for and solidarity with Poland in the wake of Friday’s incident. “I can guarantee that NATO will defend every ​inch of Polish territory,” said the alliance’s secretary general, Mark Rutte, on a visit to Warsaw on Saturday. Later that day, Kosiniak-Kamysz announced that, “in the near future, we will receive strong support from our NATO allies to strengthen the protection of our eastern border”. He revealed that an extraordinary meeting of the North Atlantic Council, NATO’s main decision-making body, would take place on Monday, at which Poland will present specific proposals for action. It remains unconfirmed whether they were deliberately directed into Polish airspace or veered off course during the large-scale attacks on Ukraine. However, in recent months, the Polish government has warned of intelligence suggesting the likelihood of “provocations” by Russia, including airspace and border violations. World.title: FedEx-led consortium completes €7.8bn takeover of Polish delivery giant InPost
World.content: Why are you now seeing adverts on our website for the first time? Click here to learn more. Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A consortium led by FedEx has completed its €7.8 billion (34.5 billion zloty) takeover of Polish delivery giant InPost. The deal will see InPost remain headquartered in Poland, with founder and CEO Rafał Brzoska staying at the helm. Friday’s announcement brings to a close a process that was first announced in February and received European Commission approval in August. InPost’s shares have now been delisted from the stock exchange. The takeover follows years of rapid growth for InPost, which pioneered the use of parcel delivery lockers in Poland before spreading rapidly in major western European markets, including France, Spain and the UK. A consortium of Advent, FedEx, A&R Investments and PPF has completed its takeover of Poland's InPost, which is now private. InPost has delisted from Euronext Amsterdam. Founder Rafał Brzoska stays on as CEO, and the company remains headquartered in Poland. pic.twitter.com/HWigKVPC3w — IPO Newsroom (@IPONewsroom_) November 20, 2026 Under the deal, FedEx and Advent, an American private equity firm, each hold 37% of InPost. A&R Investments, Brzoska’s own investment vehicle, has 16% and PPF, a Czech investment fund founded by the late billionaire Petr Kellner, 10%. PPF, A&R and Advent were previously already stakeholders. The consortium acquired InPost at a price of €15.60 per share, valuing the company at approximately €7.8 billion. In a statement published on Friday, Advent confirmed that InPost would retain its name, branding, Polish headquarters and operational independence following the takeover. Brzoska, who founded his business in 1999, will continue as CEO alongside the existing management team. “InPost’s home market of Poland will remain the blueprint for new innovations, which will then be scaled across InPost’s wider European network,” said Advent. They added that the new consortium would now “accelerate investment” in InPost’s operations, helping the firm “extend its reach further”. FedEx and InPost would also “explore opportunities” to cooperate with one another. “InPost has built a leading position in Europe’s out-of-home delivery segment,” said FedEx’s CEO and president, Raj Subramaniam. “Connecting our global network…with InPost’s last-mile capabilities gives both businesses a potential springboard for profitable growth.” Brzoska, who is one of Poland’s wealthiest individuals, said that the new partnership would “deliver the long-term capital, global reach and deep technology expertise we require to build on what we have already achieved together as a leading European e-commerce enabler”. President Macron has thanked Polish delivery giant InPost for its latest investment in France The firm, which already operates over 9,000 parcel lockers in France through its subsidiary Mondial Relay, will now spend a further €500m to expand its presence https://t.co/caOGNQemfm — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 2, 2026 InPost is the largest operator of parcel lockers in Europe, with around 70,000 across the continent. That includes roughly 30,000 in Poland and 16,000 in the UK, including in branches of the British Post Office, with over 23,000 more in the seven Eurozone countries where InPost operates. In the second quarter of 2026, InPost had revenue of 4.18 billion zloty (€970 million), up 18.2% year on year, while its number of parcels handled rose 16% to 380.9 million. The strongest revenue growth came in the eurozone, where sales increased 37.9%, followed by Poland, with 12.7% growth. Revenue in the UK and Ireland rose 9.8%. Poland recently managed to prevent a planned Russian “false-flag operation” at the border that, if it had not been stopped, could have “ended tragically”, says a retired general who acts as an advisor to the defence minister. His statement follows a report earlier this week by a leading newspaper, based on statements by unnamed senior officials, that Poland had foiled an attempt by Russia to carry out a major “provocation” on the border with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad.
