World.title: Coalition targets ‘operational capabilities’ at Hodeidah port as diplomats condemn Houthis
World.content:
RIYADH: The Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen carried out strikes at Hodeidah’s port early on Wednesday, as top diplomats condemned the Houthis for targeting a civilian building in Riyadh.

Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Maliki, the coalition’s spokesperson, said that operational capabilities at the port on Yemen’s west coast were targeted.

He said a number of other targets in Saada and Amran governorates were also destroyed.

The coalition earlier told civilians in Hodeidah to avoid the city’s port, with Al-Maliki posting a notice to social media containing a map showing the evacuation zone.

On Tuesday, eleven people were hurt after a tower in Riyadh’s King Abdullah Financial District was targeted by a Houthi drone.

Two Saudis, two Indians, three Nepalese, and four Egyptians were injured in the attack.

Al-Maliki said “the deliberate targeting of civilians and civilian objects by the terrorist Houthi militia will be met with a firm response.”

The coalition also said on Wednesday that it had intercepted and destroyed several drones over the Kingdom’s Eastern Province.

Meanwhile, Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan held separate calls with his Bahraini, Egyptian and US counterparts.

The diplomats condemned attacks by the Iran-backed group on civilian and civilian infrastructure in the Kingdom.

Last week, one of the towers at King Abdullah Financial District was targeted.

The attack resulted in material damage to several floors of the tower and neighboring buildings. There were no injuries in that attack.

The coalition is supporting the internationally recognized government against the Houthi rebels who seized the Yemeni capital Sanaa in 2014.

World.title: China’s Shenzhou-24 space flight takes off with Pakistani national as first foreign astronaut
World.content:
JIUQUAN, China: China’s Shenzhou-24 space flight launched successfully on ​Wednesday morning, with its three-man crew including a Pakistani national, who will be the first foreign astronaut to board the Tiangong space station.

Using a Long March-2F rocket, the spacecraft took ‌off at 8:18 a.m. (0018 ‌GMT) from ​the ‌Jiuquan ⁠Satellite ​Launch Center ⁠in northwest China.

Zeeshan Ali, a 40-year-old pilot who will become the first Pakistani in orbit, will work as a payload specialist and is set to stay at ⁠the station for 5 to ‌10 ‌days, conducting experiments.

He is ​accompanied by Chinese ‌commander Tang Hongbo and flight ‌engineer Wu Yi.

China is promoting Tiangong as a hub for international cooperation while the NASA-led International Space Station ‌faces possible retirement by 2030.

To prepare for the flight, Ali ⁠trained ⁠for seven months in Beijing, during which he underwent intensive Chinese-language classes, learning Chinese songs and reading Chinese poetry. He also practiced calligraphy and played table tennis.

“I’m not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder,” Ali told ​reporters on ​Tuesday.

World.title: WHO chief says staff evacuated from DR Congo hospital
World.content:
GENEVA, Switzerland: The head of the World Health Organization said Tuesday that health staff had been evacuated from a hospital in Democratic Republic of Congo after they spent three days sheltering there from fierce fighting.

Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said staff from the World Health Organization, the DR Congo’s health ministry and other staff had left the hospital in Akwe in Ituri — the province at the epicenter of the DRC’s deadly Ebola outbreak.

They had taken refuge there “amid fierce conflict for over three days” and have been evacuated “under very challenging circumstances.”

The UN health agency chief said that due to the increased insecurity, an Ebola team of WHO staff and partners had been temporarily relocated “until the situation calms.”

A total of 5,775 deaths out of 11,762 cases have been confirmed in the vast central African country’s worst-ever Ebola outbreak, according to the WHO.

The virus has spread across swathes of the DRC’s east and northeast, which have been plagued by violence for more than 30 years.

Tedros said Sunday that the frequency of attacks had increased since the end of October, seriously affecting the Ebola response.

There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo strain of Ebola behind the explosive outbreak declared in May.

Two Bundibugyo-specific candidate vaccines are set to enter clinical trials in Ituri.

One is ChAdOx1, an adenoviral vector jab developed by the University of Oxford with the Serum Institute of India (SII).

The other, mRNA-1469, was developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid-19 pandemic.

Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, announced Tuesday it had signed an advance purchase commitment with the SII and Serum Life Sciences to secure access to up to 1.5 million doses of ChAdOx1.

The doses would be procured if the clinical trials prove successful and the shot receives regulatory approval.

World.title: Groups sue Trump administration after changes made to Philadelphia slavery exhibit
World.content:
PHILADELPHIA: A Philadelphia-based history preservation group has filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration over what it claims is a “whitewashed depiction” of slavery following changes made to an exhibit at the site of President George Washington’s home.

The lawsuit, filed Monday in federal court in Pennsylvania, names the Interior Department and Secretary Doug Burgum, and the National Park Service and Acting Director Jessica Bowron.

Avenging the Ancestors Coalition says the changes made earlier this year to the President’s House/Slavery Memorial violate the Equal Protection component under the Fifth Amendment and the Administrative Procedure Act, which, in part, authorizes the court to set aside agency action that is arbitrary, capricious, an abuse of discretion or doesn’t follow the law.

Panels put in place in 2010 at the exhibit originally told the story of how nine slaves lived in the home along with George and Martha Washington in the 1790s, when Philadelphia was briefly the nation’s capital.

The Trump administration began removing those panels earlier this year. Philadelphia filed a lawsuit and a lower court forced the federal government in February to stop while the city appealed the changes. A federal Appeals Court panel reversed that and ruled July 3 that the work could continue.

The Park Service later began installing interpretive panels for a new exhibit at the President’s House site, according to the lawsuit.

The new panels “dilute and de-emphasize” the original meaning of the exhibit, the complaint said. The original exhibit also featured descriptions of the hardships faced by the nine slaves, including physical and sexual violence, which the lawsuit claims were watered down or completely omitted in the new exhibit.

“Moreover, the original glass panels that were removed have not been replaced or restored, and the motion-activated videos remain turned off.”

Since the start of President Donald Trump’s second term, his administration has been targeting diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives throughout the federal government, in historic and cultural institutions, education, medicine and in private businesses.

An executive order signed by Trump in 2025 called for federally owned or controlled historic sites to not display information to “disparage Americans past or living” and to focus on the “greatness of the achievements and progress of the American people.”

The Black Journey: African American Walking Tour of Philadelphia, another plaintiff in the latest lawsuit, asks the federal court to return the memorial to its original condition and to permanently restrain the Trump administration from enforcing or implementing the orders that led to the changes made this year.

The National Park Service and the Interior Department did not immediately respond Tuesday to requests for comment.

The Interior Department said in a statement this summer that the new “panels are full of historical context and highlight the momentous events that took place in the President’s House and the other sites at Independence National Historical Park.”

“They acknowledge the evils of slavery, including its injustices and hypocrisies, and, by telling the stories of the nine slaves that Washington kept in the President’s House, remind us of their essential humanity,” the statement said.

World.title: Bellingham wondergoal helps Real thump PSV, Arsenal and Man City held
World.content:
Jude Bellingham came off the bench to score a spectacular goal as Real Madrid maintained their perfect Champions League start with a 5-1 comeback victory over PSV Eindhoven on Tuesday, while Arsenal ​were held 1-1 at home by Borussia Dortmund and Manchester City drew 2-2 with Napoli.

Real Madrid looked in real trouble at home to PSV, going in at the break behind to Ivan Perisic’s penalty, before they roared back through a goal from Federico Valverde and Bellingham’s stunning strike.

Having seen an acrobatic volley blocked minutes earlier, the England midfielder controlled Kylian Mbappe’s pass with two touches in the air and curled a superb shot into the far corner from well outside the area.

Mbappe netted twice to put Real out of sight before Vinicius Jr got in on the act with a late ‌goal having struck ‌the post twice earlier in the game.

Real moved top of the ​standings ‌on ⁠15 points, ​three ⁠ahead of Paris St. Germain who host AS Roma on Wednesday. Como, 1-0 winners over AEK Athens, and Real Betis, who beat Slovan Bratislava 2-0, also have 12 points, one more than Arsenal.

The Premier League leaders’ clash with their Bundesliga counterparts ended all square after a second-half goal from Dortmund’s Maximilian Beier canceled out Viktor Gyokeres’ strike in the 10th minute.

Manchester City had to come from behind twice after a scoreless opening half. Ayyoub Bouaddi equalized following Rasmus Hojlund’s opener for Napoli and Rayan Cherki scored four minutes from ⁠time to rescue a point for City after Noa Lang put Napoli ‌back in front.

BELLINGHAM BEAUTY

Jose Mourinho won the Champions League with Porto ‌and Inter Milan, but fell at the semifinal stage in ​each of his three seasons during his previous ‌spell in charge at Real. He opted to leave Bellingham on the bench for the visit ‌of PSV, and it almost went horribly wrong.

PSV took a deserved lead in the 32nd minute, with 37-year-old captain Perisic showing all his experience, ignoring the whistles ringing out around the Bernabeu before sending Thibaut Courtois the wrong way from the spot.

They almost doubled their lead before the break as the unmarked Kodai Sano glanced a header ‌off target as the visitors continued to cause Real serious problems.

Arsenal's Viktor Gyokeres in action with Borussia Dortmund's Joey Veerman during the UEFA Champions League match at Emirates Stadium, London on November 24, 2026. (Reuters)

Mourinho responded with three changes at the interval, including the introduction of Bellingham.

“We were ⁠struggling to keep possession ⁠but, when Jude came on, he gave us that peace of mind and we could play much better,” Valverde told Movistar.

Real equalized five minutes after the break, thanks to Arda Guler’s quick-thinking, with the Turkish midfielder flicking a backheeled pass to Valverde in the area, who steered his first-time shot into the bottom corner.

Real’s fans were on their feet 10 minutes later, scarcely believing what they had seen, while Bellingham’s teammates looked similarly shell-shocked.

Marc Cucurella walked away with his head in his hands in wonder while the other Real players rushed to congratulate the scorer.

Manchester City's Rayan Cherki celebrates after scoring his side's second goal during the Champions League opening phase soccer match between Manchester City and Napoli in Manchester, England, Tuesday, Nov. 24, 2026. (AP)

Real took command after Bellingham’s goal and punished a loose pass in the PSV defense, Guler finding the unmarked Mbappe to extend the France forward’s scoring run to seven successive Champions League appearances.

Mbappe added his second before Vinicius rounded off a ​resounding victory from Bellingham’s pass, underlining the Spanish ​side’s credentials as serious contenders to take PSG’s crown.

Elsewhere, Porto claimed a 1-0 win at Feyenoord, RB Leipzig defeated Lens 3-1, Galatasaray beat Aston Villa 1-0 and Bodo/Glimt beat LASK by the same scoreline.

World.title: Israeli left-wing party halts coalition talks with Eisenkot
World.content:
JERUSALEM: Israel’s left-leaning Democrats party announced Tuesday that it was halting coalition talks with Yashar, the party of Gadi Eisenkot, who has been tasked with attempting to form a new government.

Neither Eisenkot nor outgoing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu obtained a clear majority following last month’s vote.

In recent days, Yashar and Netanyahu’s Likud have held three round of talks to discuss a possible coalition, even though no breakthroughs have ostensibly been reached.

“Against the backdrop of progress in negotiations to form a unity government with Netanyahu... and a parallel deadlock in negotiations to form a change government, the Democrats party announces that it is suspending talks with the Yashar party,” the Democrats wrote on X on Tuesday evening.

The party, led by former army major general Yair Golan, has been pushing Eisenkot for a coalition with two Arab-majority lists that achieved an unprecedented seat haul in the vote, in a bid to unseat Netanyahu.

But another partner in the anti-Netanyahu bloc, the right-wing Israel Beiteinu party of Avigdor Liberman, has reiterated its opposition to a government supported by Arab parties.

Eisenkot and Liberman met on Tuesday evening and announced they “agreed to sign a coalition agreement,” Yashar said in a statement.

Likud sneered at tensions inside the anti-Netanyahu bloc. “They’re falling apart” the party wrote on its Telegram channel, commenting on the Democrats’s stepping out of coalition talks.

Eisenkot was tapped on November 8th to form a new government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension.

World.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky, Hungary’s Magyar hail new era in post-Orban ties
World.content:
BEREHOVE, Ukraine: Ukraine’s Volodymyr Zelensky and Hungary’s Peter Magyar held talks in west Ukraine Tuesday, with both hailing a new era in ties after years of tension between the neighbors under Budapest’s previous Kremlin-friendly ruler Viktor Orban.

Magyar, a pro-EU conservative who took office in May and ended the long Orban era in the country, crossed into Ukraine to meet Zelensky in the war-torn country’s westernmost region Transcarpathia — which is also home to a Hungarian ethnic minority.

The Hungarian prime minister met Zelensky in the city of Uzhgorod, where they laid wreaths in a local cemetery and held talks, before holding a media briefing in the border town of Berehove.

“This is an important moment and it is .. very sensitive,” Zelensky said in a press conference alongside Magyar, calling their conversation “positive.”

“It is in the interests of all neighbors to maintain good relations with one another... I am very grateful that you have been able to achieve this; let us begin to build trust — better late than never,” Magyar said.

The pair played a symbolic volleyball match in a school in Transcarpathia.

Under nationalist Orban, Kyiv’s ties with Hungary — a neighboring EU and NATO country — were essentially frozen, with the former prime minister traveling to Moscow during Russia’s invasion.

Relations improved significantly after Kyiv recently passed legislation addressing Budapest’s longstanding concerns over the rights of Ukraine’s Hungarian minority.

Following the vote, Hungary agreed to allow the European Union to open new sections of EU membership negotiations with Ukraine.

Magyar said he met with local ethnic Hungarians who welcomed the change in tone.

“They’re very pleased that the two countries have finally started to move closer to one another, that we’ve finally put a stop to this completely unnecessary and inexplicable political escalation,” he said.

He said the pair discussed “symbolic” projects, such as the reconstruction of Hungarian high school in Berehove, which turns 125 next year.

Entering another winter, Moscow’s full-scale offensive against Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands and displaced millions.

‘Friendship with Putin leads to nowhere’

Zelensky said Ukraine was now counting on the support of post-Orban Hungary, including in its aspirations to join the EU.

In order to end the war, “solidarity with Ukraine is essential, whilst friendship with Putin leads to nowhere,” Zelensky said in an apparent jibe to Orban.

He also said he had an “absolutely honest” conversation with Magyar on Kyiv’s EU aspirations, who has expressed skepticism on Ukraine joining the EU quickly.

“I said quite frankly today, Prime Minister, that for us this is an irreversible path,” Zelensky said, adding that Ukraine will not go “back to Russia” and that this was “the choice of our people.”

Ukrainians had in 2014 held a pro-EU revolution that overthrew a Moscow-backed leader.

Magyar had earlier condemned Russia’s invasion, highlighting his break from Orban’s stance.

“I would like you to know that the Hungarian people deeply condemn this appalling Russian aggression,” he said.

Energy, transport

Zelensky also said the pair had discussed energy and the prospect of bringing Hungarian diesel into Ukraine — for Budapest to help Kyiv with its exports during wartime.

“There is a shortage of electricity and so on, and our people are defending themselves, our communities are defending themselves... We are counting on Hungary’s support as well,” Zelensky said.

Magyar said he was bringing humanitarian aid worth around $2.9 million, including medicine and energy equipment.

Ukraine and Hungary share a short border, with Transcarpathia forming the westernmost part of the country and Uzhgorod lying on the border with nearby Slovakia.

World.title: How Israel’s political uncertainty is shaping the debate over Iran and the West Bank
World.content:
LONDON: On any other day, perhaps, the deployment of Israeli troops into villages, towns and refugee camps in the occupied West Bank on Monday might have attracted greater attention on Israeli news sites.

The military operation in Al-Amari refugee camp in particular, during which tear gas and stun grenades were fired and dozens of Palestinians were held for interrogation, drew the attention of international media.

But across much of the Israeli press, from the left-leaning Haaretz to the conservative Jerusalem Post, the latest incursion into Palestinian territory and its potential implications for the viability of a future Palestinian state received little attention.

Instead, the Israeli media were preoccupied with Benjamin Netanyahu’s efforts to form a government and return to office as Israel’s next prime minister, and the measures he appears prepared to consider to achieve that.

The Israeli military generally describes such raids as preventive counterterrorism operations aimed at dismantling Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad cells, seizing weapons and disrupting attack plots, including in areas where Palestinian Authority security forces exercise limited control.

However, for a prime minister who has long made national security central to his political platform, some observers suggest the raids in Al-Amari and Netanyahu’s reported attempts to persuade the US to resume bombing Iran may reflect overlapping political and strategic considerations.

“Both seem to be true,” Sarah Yerkes, acting co-director of the Middle East Program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, told Arab News.

An Israeli soldier gestures toward a Palestinian man during a protest. Across across much of the Israeli press the latest incursion into Palestinian territory and its potential implications for the viability of a future Palestinian state received little attention. (REUTERS file)

“Netanyahu’s political future is hanging by a thread and he needs to do everything he can right now to convince the right-wing parties who are in the midst of coalition building that they need him to stick around.

“But this also reflects the Netanyahu government’s longstanding policy of annexation by stealth. They are once again ‘creating facts on the ground’ that make it much harder to undo during any future negotiation process.”

It is almost exactly nine months since Israel and the US launched their joint surprise attack on Iran, triggering a regional conflict that saw Tehran retaliate by attacking America’s Gulf allies and disrupting the global economy by effectively closing the Strait of Hormuz.

Against the backdrop of the stalled conflict with Iran, the subsequent Israeli invasion and occupation of a “buffer zone” in Lebanon, and the ongoing violence in Gaza, Netanyahu has failed to secure a renewed electoral mandate to govern.

Israel’s election on Oct. 27 ended with the Netanyahu bloc holding 53 seats in the Knesset — eight short of the majority needed to form a government. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc has 48 seats but, with the backing of Arab parties, has been invited by President Isaac Herzog to build a coalition and form the next government.

Intensive negotiations are now underway and, with his political future uncertain, Netanyahu, long known as “Mr. Security,” has again placed national security concerns at the forefront of the political debate.

“Netanyahu, especially since the election, has become an agent of chaos,” Ahron Bregman, a senior teaching fellow in the Department of War Studies at King’s College London and a former major in the Israeli army, told Arab News.

“His primary goal is to prevent the opposition from forming a coalition without him. One method he employs is to create a sense of urgency and emphasise external threats, whether real or imagined.”

Reports emerged last week that Netanyahu has been pressing US President Donald Trump to renew attacks on Iran, citing claims that Tehran has advanced chemical and biological weapons programs.

Such claims are particularly sensitive in a region where the US-led invasion of Iraq in 2003 was justified in part by subsequently discredited allegations concerning weapons of mass destruction.

On Nov. 18, The New York Times, citing US and Israeli officials, reported that Netanyahu was “pressing hard for the US to join his country in a four- to seven-day campaign of airstrikes against Iran.”

It added that Roman Gofman, the director of Israel’s intelligence agency Mossad, had held talks in Washington with his counterpart at the CIA, and that “other top Israeli officials, including Shlomi Binder, the director of military intelligence, have advocated a resumption of operations in discussions with American counterparts.”

Netanyahu and his allies, however, maintain that the urgency of their calls for renewed military action is driven by intelligence assessments rather than domestic political considerations.

According to Israeli and Western officials cited by CBS News, the prime minister’s office has raised concerns about the pace at which Tehran is rebuilding its ballistic missile production capabilities and fortifying underground nuclear sites, including Mount Pickaxe.

Israeli officials reportedly fear that the window of opportunity to target these facilities could soon close.

Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot and other officials pose for a family photo. Netanyahu rejected suggestions that he was manufacturing a crisis, accusing rivals of downplaying security threats for political gain. (REUTERS file)

Speaking at a Likud faction meeting on Monday, Netanyahu rejected suggestions that he was manufacturing a crisis, accusing political rivals of minimizing genuine security threats for partisan gain.

However, also on Monday, The Times of Israel reported that researchers within Mossad had assessed that there was “no immediate need for military action against Iran,” a position echoed by Netanyahu’s rival Eisenkot and the Israeli military’s chief of staff.

In an editorial on Nov. 24, Haaretz concluded that, despite the continuing threat posed to Israel by Iran’s missiles and nuclear program, Israel currently “has no justification for another war with Iran.”

It continued: “One cannot sever the defense-related debate from the political reality or ignore the possibility that political considerations are influencing Netanyahu’s decisions.”

Even before the election, “there was concern that military moves against Iran were meant to provoke an Iranian response that would create an emergency allowing the election to be postponed.

“Now, we cannot rule out the possibility — an idea also noted by leaders of the change bloc — that the motive for going to war would be an attempt to impose ‘unity.’ Everything so as not to lose power.”

It remains unclear whether Trump will agree to Netanyahu’s reported request. The US president is said to be undecided.

Netanyahu, Bregman said, “prefers to act on Iran, which, for sure, will stop the process of forming a new government. But to do that, he depends on Trump’s shifting moods.

“In contrast, when it comes to the West Bank, he is less reliant on Trump. His inaction regarding the ongoing situation there — including the harassment of innocent Palestinians — suggests that he is complicit in it, and this is his way of creating a sense of urgency.”

On Nov. 24, The Jerusalem Post reported that, according to previously undisclosed internal Israeli military data, “nationalist crime” by settlers in the West Bank had increased by approximately 42 percent in 2026 so far compared with the whole of 2025, “while politicians watch from the sidelines.”

The increase in violence against Palestinians is also reflected in figures released on Nov. 20 by the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, which said the number of attacks on Palestinian olive farms this year “exceeds that recorded in any previous olive harvest season.”

More than 400 Israeli settler attacks linked to the Palestinian olive harvest had resulted in casualties or property damage, including damage to more than 4,000 trees and saplings.

Settler violence, OCHA added, “has extended to Areas A and B, where Palestinians faced fewer such attacks in previous years,” while “solidarity activists, journalists and diplomats have also been attacked, and over 25,000 kilograms of produce have been vandalized or stolen.”

The “Elimination Project,” run by B’Tselem, the Israeli Information Center for Human Rights in the Occupied Territories, documents what the organization describes as “Israel’s systematic dismantling of Palestinian collective life in the West Bank … as part of a comprehensive mechanism of elimination that works to dismantle the conditions for continued Palestinian existence in the West Bank, while deepening Jewish control and supremacy in an irreversible manner.”

Israeli soldiers detain a Palestinian man during a raid in Al-Amari refugee camp in Ramallah. B’Tselem said the operation should be seen in the context of Israeli policy aimed at dismantling Palestinian collective life in the West Bank. (REUTERS file)

A series of charts compiled by B’Tselem documents increases in Palestinian deaths, settler violence, the establishment of outposts, home demolitions, the displacement of communities and the number of “movement obstacles” in the West Bank — including checkpoints, permanent gates and earth mounds.

“What we are witnessing on the ground is an escalation in settler attacks across the West Bank, backed by the Israeli military and the state, alongside widespread demolitions of Palestinian homes by Israeli authorities throughout the West Bank,” Yair Dvir, spokesperson for B’Tselem, told Arab News.

“The military operation in Al-Amari refugee camp should also be understood in the broader context of Israeli policy aimed at dismantling Palestinian collective life in the West Bank and deepening Israeli control and Jewish-Israeli presence throughout the territory.”

Israel, said Bregman, “is actively implementing ethnic cleansing in the West Bank and is pursuing the annexation of this land.

“It is naive to think that only a small group of young individuals, No’ar HaGva’ot, or Hilltop Youth, as these thugs are known, are responsible for the horrific events we witness in the West Bank. In reality, the military, backed by the government, plays a significant role in the ethnic cleansing.

“The civilized world must impose apartheid-style sanctions on Israel to stop these war crimes. It is beyond belief that we see horrific attacks on Palestinians, including such ‘military operations’ as in the Al-Amari refugee camp, while the world remains silent.”

World.title: Baghdad to manage oilfields under Kurdish security control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Tuesday the federal Ministry of Oil to manage oilfields under Kurdish security control, triggering an immediate rejection from the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) and escalating a broader campaign to centralize state power.

Al-Zaidi’s directives follow an investigation into massive crude oil smuggling at the state-run North Oil Company.

The federal Oil Ministry in Baghdad must take over Kurdish-secured fields in four northern provinces—Kirkuk, Nineveh, Diyala, and Salah al-Din.

Erbil is prohibited from approving crude or refined product exports without federal ministry sign-off.

Iraq’s Border Ports Authority is instructed to take over all official border crossings in the Kurdistan region of Iraq, while security forces close informal crossings and unpaved roads connecting Iraqi Kurdistan to neighboring provinces.

The Iraqi prime minister suspended top executives at the North Oil Company and dismissed the head of the border authority pending further probes.

Last week, Baghdad threatened military action to enter the Iran-backed armed group Kataib Hezbollah’s stronghold in Jurf al-Sakhar after investigators linked the militia and senior officials to a multi-hundred-million-dollar oil smuggling network.

According to reports, al-Zaidi is attempting to curb non-state armed groups and rein in regional autonomy to stabilize Iraq for foreign investment.

World.title: Iraqi security seizes two drone launchers in Maysan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security forces seized on Tuesday two drone launchers and drone engine components hidden in an agricultural area in the southeastern province of Maysan.

The operation was announced by Iraq’s Security Media Cell and carried out by a specialized intelligence and technical team supervised by the director of Maysan Intelligence and Counterterrorism.

Following intelligence reports, security forces deployed to cordon off and search the farmland, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

Alongside the two concealed launch platforms, authorities recovered scattered remnants and components of a drone engine.

Authorities have seized the equipment and initiated legal and technical procedures. Officials have not yet identified who placed the launchers or confirmed whether they had been used in previous attacks.

After a drone attack targeted a pipeline in Saudi Arabia in September, which Riyadh and Baghdad said was launched from Iraqi territory, Iraqi security forces have discovered drone launchers near the border with Iran.

World.title: Iraqi political blocs name nominees to replace Communications and Transport Ministers
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Political factions within Iraq’s Coordination Framework have finalized their nominees to replace key cabinet members in an upcoming ministerial reshuffle led by Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi, including the portfolios of Communications, Transport, and Oil, according to a coalition source speaking on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

The source disclosed that the Islamic Supreme Council of Iraq (ISCI), headed by Humam Hamoudi, has put forward several candidates—prominently Ahmed Abdul-Jabbar and former Health Minister Saleh Al-Hasnawi—to assume the Ministry of Communications in place of incumbent Minister Mustafa Jabbar Sanad.

Meanwhile, the Badr Organization, led by Hadi Al-Amiri, has selected Mohammed Al-Zubaidi as its nominee for the Ministry of Transport to succeed current Minister Wahab Al-Hassani.

The nominations follow revelations by a government source on Monday, November 23, confirming a political and executive agreement to carry out a phased cabinet reshuffle immediately after Parliament settles the federal general budget bill. Driven by formal performance evaluations and consultations with nominating blocs, the first phase is expected to target three portfolios for distinct reasons:

Ministry of Transport: The planned replacement of Minister Wahab Al-Hassani is attributed to health reasons.

Ministry of Oil: Prime Minister Al-Zaidi is weighing the dismissal of Oil Minister Bassem Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi due to operational shortcomings across multiple files and recent revelations of crude oil theft and smuggling networks across several Iraqi cities. Alongside naming new ministers, the government is considering merging the Ministries of Oil and Electricity into a unified “Ministry of Energy”, potentially placing both portfolios under the current Electricity Minister.

Ministry of Communications: Coalition sources confirmed the move to replace Mustafa Sanad, though specific official grounds for the change have not yet been detailed.

The impending shakeup comes roughly six months after the Council of Representatives granted confidence to Al-Zaidi’s cabinet on May 14, 2026, and just over a month after the government completed its 25-ministry lineup on October 15.

World.title: Baghdad to take over border crossings in Iraqi Kurdistan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered federal authorities on Tuesday to take control of all border crossings in Iraqi Kurdistan and directed the Oil Ministry to manage oilfields under Kurdish security control in Diyala, Kirkuk, Salah al-Din, and Nineveh provinces as part of a crackdown on oil smuggling.

The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) was instructed to approve crude oil and petroleum product exports only through the federal Oil Ministry.

Baghdad also announced plans to monitor oilfields with cameras and deploy Oil Ministry personnel at checkpoints leading into the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

Al-Zaidi directed the federal border crossings authority to assume control of all crossings in the Kurdistan region of Iraq. He also instructed the Border Forces Command to close unofficial international border crossings and ordered the shutdown of seasonal roads and unpaved routes connecting the four provinces and Iraqi Kurdistan.

The prime minister removed the head of the border crossings authority, suspended the director general of the state-owned North Oil Company and his deputies pending investigation, and dismissed several security officials in Kirkuk.

The directives followed an investigation into smuggling at the state-run North Oil Company and a wider campaign against illicit oil networks—including alleged smuggling in Jurf al-Sakhar linked to the Iran-backed Kataib Hezbollah group, which denied the accusation.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets Egyptian businessmen in Cairo
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi affirmed on Monday that Iraq has a promising investment environment and opportunities in several sectors.

Al-Zaidi’s remarks took place during his meeting with a group of Egyptian businessmen in the Egyptian capital, Cairo, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The meeting is part of the Iraqi government’s efforts to strengthen the economic partnership between the two countries and expand investment cooperation.

The Iraqi government is striving to increase the presence of the private sector, recognizing its critical role in bolstering the country’s economy and attaining progress, according to al-Zaidi.

The Iraqi prime minister noted that the Iraqi investment law offers investors benefits and protection, including tax and customs exemptions.

Al-Zaidi listened to the views, recommendations, and suggestions put forward by Egyptian business leaders to increase investments in Iraq.

Egyptian business leaders conveyed their gratitude for the incentives that Iraq provides to investors as well as their interest in the available investment prospects.

World.title: Iraq, Egypt sign several memoranda of understanding
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Egyptian Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly oversaw a ceremony held to sign 10 bilateral cooperation documents and memoranda of understanding (MoUs) on Monday in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital.

The ceremony followed the fourth session of the Egyptian-Iraqi Joint Higher Committee, co-chaired by both leaders during Al-Zaidi’s first official visit to Egypt since taking office.

The two countries signed a treaty to prevent tax evasion and eliminate double taxation on income and capital.

Health and trade officials finalized a MoU covering medical supplies and pharmaceuticals.

Regulators inked deals for radio and TV broadcasting cooperation alongside nuclear and radiation oversight.

Additionally, both sides signed five other documents establishing joint programs in fisheries, scientific research, national planning, youth, and sports.

Prior to the ceremony, al-Zaidi met President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to expand economic cooperation and coordinate diplomatic efforts on regional security.

World.title: US exports to Iraq reach $727 million in first nine months of 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – U.S. exports to Iraq surpassed $700 million during the first nine months of 2026, reaching a cumulative total of $727 million across the first three quarters of the year, according to U.S. Census Bureau figures published via the International Trade Centre’s (ITC) Trade Map platform on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

Quarterly data shows that bilateral shipments held steady through the first half of the year before gaining momentum in the third quarter:

Q1 2026: $238 million

Q2 2026: $238 million

Q3 2026: $251 million

Nine-Month Cumulative Total: $727 million

The $727 million export volume spans a diverse range of industrial, energy, agricultural, and healthcare goods shipped to the Iraqi market.

Primary export categories include pharmaceuticals and medical products, heavy industrial equipment, gas turbines, machinery and appliances, petroleum derivatives, and agricultural staples such as rice.

World.title: US dollar holds near 169,500 dinars across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar hovered just shy of the 170,000-dinar threshold across major domestic parallel markets on Tuesday morning, November 24, 2026, with purchasing bids settling near 169,000 IQD per $100 in key commercial hubs.

According to morning monitoring figures, physical banknote rates opened across Baghdad, Erbil, and Basra with minor regional variations.

In Baghdad, currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 169,500 IQD against buying offers of 169,000 IQD per $100.

In Erbil, currency desks matched Baghdad’s 169,500 IQD retail selling quote while offering slightly lower purchasing bids at 168,750 IQD per $100.

In Basra, foreign exchange offices recorded marginally softer retail selling rates at 169,250 IQD alongside buying offers of 168,750 IQD per $100.

Overall, parallel cash rates continue to trade at a spread of 17,250 to 17,500 dinars above the Central Bank of Iraq’s (CBI) official cash rate of 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

World.title: Passport has discrepancies in place of birth: CJP's Saurav Das rendered ineligible for foreign travel
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A notice served to CJP activist

on Monday evening by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai, asking him to explain alleged discrepancies in his documents relating to place of birth, had rendered his passport ineligible for foreign travel till the response was received and matter resolved.

Sources in the govt said the mismatch in birth particulars across different set of documents like aadhaar, passport and birth certificate was flagged in inputs received over the last couple of months, prompting RPO to initiate a fresh verification of documents and information recorded in his passport application file. The passport was issued to him on Aug 21, 2019.

While police verification is done either before or after issue of passport (in case of âtatkalâ passport), if any adverse or incorrect information comes to light during validity of the passport, a re-verification can be ordered by the RPO by issuing a show-cause notice to the citizen, asking why the passport should not be impounded.



A notice was sent to Das by e-mail on Monday evening, asking him to respond within 7 days to the alleged âmaterial suppression of factsâ relating to his place of birth. He was asked to clarify the âincorrectâ particulars with supporting documents, failing which he could face impounding of his passport under Section 10(b) of the Passports Act, 1967. The notice explicitly advised him not to use his passport till he had filed his response.





âAs per rules, if a show-cause notice is issued to the passport holder on why his passport should not be impounded in view of furnishing of incorrect particulars, and a reply is awaited, the respondent cannot travel abroad on that passport till the matter is disposed of,â an officer told TOI. âDas was well-aware that the pending RPO notice would be flagged in the immigration systems, preventing his clearance for boarding the flight to London.

Yet, he chose to travel to the airport, possibly so he could play the victim after being stopped at immigration,â said the officer.

Das, as per reports, however claims he did not see the email, which landed hours before his flight, till he checked his inbox at the immigration counter.

World.title: 1st privately built PSLV set for launch early next year: Isro chief
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The first privately built Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV-N1) is ready for a maiden launch in the "first quarter of next year",

chairman V Narayanan said on Tuesday. He also said govt is fast-tracking satellite launches in collaboration with startups "in a big way" as Isro currently has only 56 space assets in orbit.

Talking about foreign collaboration, the Isro chairman said, "India is collaborating with 64 countries... At least 434 satellites for 34 countries have lifted off from Indian soil during the last 12 years."

Gaganyaan in final phase, says Isro chief

Speaking on the sidelines of the 5th India International Space Conference in Delhi, Isro chief V Narayanan said, âEarlier, it was only Isro that built PSLV with the support of industry. Now, an L&T and HAL consortium has been given five PSLVs (to build).



So, the first rocket PSLV-N1 is getting ready and we are targeting to launch it by the first quarter of next year.â Isroâs arm NSIL signed a contract with the consortium in Sept 2022 for Rs 860 crore for five PSLV rockets.

Narayanan said, âWe need to build a lot of space assets for communication, navigation and earth observation. This canât be done by govt sector (alone). Isro and INSPACe are hand-holding private companies and you will see its benefit five years from now.

Vikram-32 chip has come out, and we are going to induct it.â

World.title: Rajiv Gandhi's security withdrawn to get him killed, says Rahul
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress politician

said the security of his father,

, was removed deliberately to get him killed, making a sensational charge years after the former PM was assassinated by a suicide bomber in Tamil Nadu.

In a video interaction with his mother

and sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Rahul said, "Papa's security was removed so that he got killed. Papa's security removal was not an accident. It was done on purpose so that he got killed." "An atmosphere was created for him to get killed. It was obvious what was going on. I told papa and mom, and had an argument about it with my father," he said.

Act passed by Rajiv government offered SPG cover only to PM, not former PMs

Rahul Tuesday posted a video featuring the family discussing Sonia Gandhiâs recently released book âBelongingâ, in which his charge came just after his mother spoke about the lax security arrangements during Rajiv Gandhiâs visit to Bihar as leader of the opposition, where he faced stone pelting.



Rahul had accompanied his father on his Bihar visit.

Even though Rahul alleged there was an âintentionâ behind withdrawing his fatherâs security in 1988, the Special Protection Group Act, passed in 1988 by the then Rajiv government, restricted SPG cover strictly to the PM and not to former PMs. Thus, Rajiv lost the protection after being voted out in 1989. V P Singh replaced him as PM. When Rajiv was assassinated at a rally in Tamil Nadu on May 21, 1991, the Chandra Shekhar government was in office.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





Following the assassination, the PV Narasimha Rao government amended the Act, extending protection to former PMs and their immediate family members for five years after leaving office. This brought Sonia, Rahul and Priyanka under its cover. It was further amended in 1994 to prolong the duration to 10 years.

Rahul also said Sonia has not written about how she was treated by some people. He said she was âhumiliated, abusedâ in politics, adding he may talk about it someday.

World.title: 6 years after split, Akalis & BJP tie up for Punjab assembly polls
World.content:
NEW DELHI: After six years of separation marked by AAP's rise in Punjab,

and

on Tuesday renewed their alliance ahead of assembly polls, with home minister

recognising the regional party as the "big brother" in the tie-up and claimant to the chief minister's chair in case NDA returns to office after a decade.

Shah was joined by SAD president

Sukhbir Singh Badal

and BJP chief Nitin Nabin at the announcement, timed to coincide with Guru Nanak's birth anniversary, exuding confidence in their victory and the governing AAP's wipeout in the polls to be held early next year.

The Akalis had broken away from NDA over the now-scrapped farm laws.

The revival of the alliance after a period which saw SAD's fortunes nosedive and BJP achieve limited success in expanding its base outside its influence in urban areas brings NDA right back into the reckoning in a state where AAP and Congress were being seen as the main election contenders.



BJP and SAD are banking on the revival of the social compact between the former's base among Hindus and the latter's once-formidable farmer constituency. Much will depend on whether their renewed chemistry will enthuse their traditional voters in a crowded battlefield.

Amit Shah: BJP-SAD pact not merely political, itâs an emotional bond

PM Modi, whose meeting with Badal in Parliament complex on Aug 7 was the first clear indication of the tie-up, was emphatic in his endorsement of what he called a "natural alliance".





"Putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first. I am extremely delighted that Shiromani Akali Dal returns to NDA family and that too on the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji. Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress," home minister Amit Shah said. Modi will be in Moga on Dec 8 to attend a rally to mark Parkash Singh Badal's birth anniversary.

Shah said, "The alliance between BJP and SAD is not merely political; it is an emotional bond rooted in mutual trust and Punjab's history. NDA is now complete with Akali Dal's return."

"A tidal wave has started today," SAD's Sukhbir Singh Badal said, claiming the alliance would bag 100 seats in the 117-member assembly.

Shah was quick to emphasise the alliance's emotive symbolism of Hindu-Sikh brotherhood in the border state with a history of social tensions and spells of militancy; Nabin too described it as a "natural alliance", and Badal invoked his father's description of their ties as "nau-maas da rishta" (together like nail and flesh).

Jana Sangh, BJP's political predecessor, had allied with Akalis too. Shah's announcement that SAD will be the senior partner - Badal being the obvious CM face even though no such announcement was made - despite its shrinking base, underscores BJP's recognition that its Sikh ally should lead the alliance and look like a credible contender for office.

The BJP, however, is expected to contest a bigger number of seats than the 23 it used to in the alliance.

Akali's 10-year stint in office, with BJP as junior partner, ended in 2017 with their massive defeat at the hands of Congress as a big chunk of its core voters revolted over the government's alleged mishandling of sacrilege incidents and issues of drug abuse and corruption, creating a fertile ground for AAP's rise and its subsequent sweep in 2022.

Congress general secretary in-charge of Punjab Sachin Pilot said, "It's a compromised alliance, a desperate alliance. BJP and SAD have not revealed why they parted ways six years ago, what were the reasons that SAD and BJP left each other. Have the GoI and BJP given any assurance to the country on MSP, have they apologised for the three black farm laws, and what is the SAD view on the hundreds of protesters who died on the Delhi border in the farmers' protest? Both parties had no political space left in the state, and they have chosen to join hands.

"

World.title: Amit Shah: Kartarpur corridor to open after review
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union home minister

said Tuesday that the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor, which allows pilgrims to travel visa-free to a holy site associated with Guru Nanak across the border in Pakistan, will be opened as soon as national security concerns are resolved.

Responding to a media query at a news briefing, where he announced the BJP-Shiromani Akali Dal alliance ahead of the Punjab polls, he said national security should not be politicised, noting that it is the Modi government which built it.

Government had closed the corridor after Operation Sindoor over security concerns. Shah said Kartarpur went to Pakistan after India's partition due to Congress' carelessness.

"As soon as this (national security) issue is completely resolved, we will immediately reopen Kartarpur Sahib with full honour," he added.

World.title: ICMR: Over 50 per cent of women of reproductive age anaemic
World.content:
NEW DELHI: More than half of women of reproductive age (15-49 years) in India are anaemic, while nearly two-thirds of adolescent girls and boys are deficient in vitamin B12, pointing to a wider nutritional challenge that goes beyond iron deficiency, a new national survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) has found.

The findings fill a key data gap in the NFHS-6 fact sheets released earlier this year, which did not include anaemia estimates. Government had subsequently said these would be drawn from an independent ICMR survey based on venous blood samples.

The ICMR-National Institute of Nutrition's SAMPADA survey for 2023-25 found anaemia in 55.9 per cent of non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49 years. NFHS-5 reported a prevalence of 57 per cent among women in the same age group.



The figures, however, are not directly comparable because the surveys covered different groups of women and used different testing methods.

State-wise estimates showed sharp regional disparities, with Andaman and Nicobar recording the highest prevalence at 81.2 per cent among non-pregnant, non-lactating women aged 15-49 years.

The burden was also high in other groups. Anaemia affected 46.3 per cent of adolescent girls and 22.8 per cent of adolescent boys aged 10-19 years.





Among children, 41.8 per cent of those aged 12-59 months and 31.3 per cent of those aged 5-9 years were anaemic. The prevalence was 43.6 per cent among pregnant women and 58.1 per cent among lactating women. Among adult men aged 20-59 years, it stood at 22 per cent.

B12 deficiency was more widespread among adolescents, affecting 65.4 per cent of girls and 66.1 per cent of boys. It was found in 57.4 per cent of women of reproductive age and 60.4 per cent of adult men aged 20-59 years.

The prevalence stood at 63.1 per cent among pregnant women and 51.8 per cent among lactating women.

Iron deficiency accompanied anaemia in only 27 per cent of adolescent girls and women of reproductive age, despite anaemia affecting 46.3 per cent and 55.9 per cent of these groups, respectively. Iron deficiency itself remained common, affecting 36.3 per cent of adolescent girls, 34.1 per cent of women of reproductive age, 29.6 per cent of pregnant women and 23 per cent of children aged 12-59 months, compared with 10 per cent for adolescent boys.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"Not all anaemia is caused by nutritional deficiencies such as iron, vitamin B12 or folate deficiency. Conditions such as thalassaemia, sickle cell disease, aplastic anaemia, chronic kidney disease, tuberculosis and cancer can also cause anaemia. Iron supplements alone will not help these patients," said Dr Tulika Seth, professor of haematology, AIIMS.

"We have been working with the Anaemia Mukt Bharat programme to develop simple algorithms to identify such cases," Seth added.

The survey covered more than two lakh people across 183 districts in 35 states and union territories, drawing data from over 81,000 households and analysing over 1.7 lakh blood samples.

World.title: From ghat to gallery, Banaras set for brush with art
World.content:
Despite its noisy, crowded lanes and walls with their own artwork of paan stains, the city is more than the Instagram reels of Ganga aarti and sunset boat rides suggest.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

To linger in Banaras is to linger in another era, an era which one cannot quite date by century," wrote Harvard scholar Diana L Eck in 'Banaras: City of Light'. The inaugural CII Banaras Biennale, which opens on Nov 27 and is on view till Dec 31, gives art lovers a new excuse to linger in one of India's oldest cities.Despite its noisy, crowded lanes and walls with their own artwork of paan stains, the city is more than the Instagram reels of Ganga aarti and sunset boat rides suggest. Aptly themed 'Kashi/Light; City as Sensorium', the biennale seeks to put Banaras on the cultural map, but without treating it as a mere backdrop. "The biennale is envisioned as a long-term commitment to positioning Banaras as a global capital of living culture," says Madhav Singhania, chairman of the steering committee of CII Banaras Biennale 2026. The Biennale spans visual art, textiles, craft, music, performance and scholarship, with events spread across ghats and galleries.That approach is rooted in the idea that the city's past and present need not be kept apart. At the centre of the exhibition is Bharatiya Kala Bhavan (BKB) inside the Banaras Hindu University campus, where lead curator Gayatri Sinha has chosen to place contemporary work among the museum's extensive collection of more than one lakh objects."Can we make the ancient and the contemporary conversational?" she asks.The question is the aesthetic thread that ties the biennale together. There is a more literal dhaga, too - of silk and zari. Pramod Kumar KG, who is curating the textile and craft section, is looking to connect Banaras's mastery of the loom with contemporary fashion and design.BKB's collection began with art historian Rai Krishna Das, who started collecting in 1920. Its present building was inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1962. The main gallery houses Sinha's exhibition, 'The Cycle of Life: Samsara', which looks at life, death, livelihood and renunciation in Banaras. "If you visit Varanasi, sooner or later, this integration between life and death, between life, livelihood and renunciation, between the appropriation of a certain sensibility and the letting go of your human education becomes very important. "Sinha draws from BKB's impressive collection of terracotta sculptures, miniature paintings, textiles and coins, and makes connections with contemporary art. Terracotta heads, some nearly 2,000 years old, are shown alongside a contemporary work in the medium by Ravinder Reddy. Manu Parekh, whose artistic practice has repeatedly returned to Banaras, also features in the exhibition. An 11ft-by-11ft tapestry based on his work, woven by Karishma Swali's Chanakya School of Craft, evokes the city at night.Biennales in India have usually been led by artists, curators or foundations, but this one brings industry and cultural institutions such as the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art and Sunil Munjal's Serendipity Arts together. "This is sort of curatorially led, but industry-driven," says Tarana Sawhney, chairperson of the CII Art & Culture Committee.The intention is not simply to parachute a festival into the city and leave. "We didn't want to create a festival that just went in, kind of engaged with the city and left," Sawhney says. Skilling and textile development initiatives are part of a larger effort that will continue after visitors have gone. For Sinha, the work is ultimately about bringing objects, histories and artistic practices together without erasing their differences. In Banaras, where the old and the everyday share the same streets, that conversation is already part of the city.

World.title: Govt plans multi-year motor insurance for cars, bikes; no insurance, no fuel pilot at 10 petrol pumps in NCR
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Road transport ministry is proposing a series of measures to address the problem of uninsured vehicles on roads, including introducing a single premium for four- and six-year insurance policies for cars and two-wheelers, respectively.

Separately, the Supreme Court Committee on Road Safety has asked road transport and petroleum ministries to launch a pilot of the âno insurance, no fuelâ initiative at five petrol pumps each in Haryana and Uttar Pradesh which have automated number plate recognition (ANPR) cameras that can identify vehicles and help verify their insurance status.

TOI has learnt that the road transport ministry is also working on the plan to link premiums to traffic offences recorded against vehicle owners in the previous year.



The proposed changes are aimed at encouraging more vehicle owners to maintain valid insurance coverage and improving compliance with the Motor Vehicles Act. Under the proposal, insurance premiums could increase based on specific traffic violations recorded against a vehicle in the preceding year, making repeated offenders pay more for insurance.

The ministry is also examining options to revise the base insurance rates for specified vehicle categories, including electric vehicles, as part of a broader review of the existing premium structure.





Insurance data show that nearly 25 crore active vehicles have valid insurance, which is around 81% of the vehicles that are currently running across the country. While over 90% of heavy commercial vehicles have valid insurance, itâs around 88% in the case of cars. The compliance is least at around 57% in case of three-wheelers and itâs around 80% in case of two-wheelers.

Supreme Court had earlier issued directions to govt to examine measures to ensure that vehicles plying on roads have valid insurance coverage. Third-party motor insurance is mandatory under the Motor Vehicles Act. Vehicles without valid insurance pose a serious risk in case of crashes, leaving accident victims and their families vulnerable to inadequate compensation.

World.title: Israeli Defence Minister says Iran is developing chemical weapons
World.content:
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) that Iran is developing chemical weapons and vowed to stop Tehran from obtaining them.

"Iran is in the process of developing chemical weapons but has not yet reached the capability to attack Israel with them," said Mr. Katz in a statement published by his Likud party on Telegram.

"We must not allow this to proceed," he added.

Last week CNN, citing U.S. intelligence, reported that Iran has been developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb in Washington.

The report quoted anonymous sources characterising Iran's plans as "an effort to give itself options rather than an indicator of an imminent attack".

A dirty bomb is a conventional explosive laced with chemical or radioactive materials.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed the report, calling it "Iraq War-style propaganda" with "Israeli fingerprints all over it".

"Nobody is buying it," Mr. Araghchi wrote on X.

In a briefing to Israeli reporters on Tuesday (November 24), Mr. Katz floated the possibility of a preemptive strike against Tehran if necessary.

"If we recognise that the Iranians intend to attack Israel, can't we tell the army to attack earlier and thwart the threat?" he said, according to a transcript from Israel's Channel 12. "If the Iranians attack us first, it will be a failure."

Israel held a general election last month in which neither caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main opponent Gadi Eisenkot obtained a clear majority.

Mr. Eisenkot has been tasked by President Isaac Herzog with attempting to form a government, and Mr. Netanyahu has talked up the threat from Tehran as he insists on the need for a unity government that includes his Likud party.

He has also reportedly urged U.S. President Donald Trump to resume war on Iran, following two rounds of fighting last year and earlier this year.

But Mr. Katz said Mr. Netanyahu had dissuaded Mr. Trump from an attack before the Israeli vote last month.

"Trump was the one who considered attacking before the (Israeli) elections. The prime minister told him: I don't want to attack beforehand," he wrote in his statement on Tuesday (Novmber 24).

On Monday (November 23), Mr. Eisenkot said he saw no immediate reason to attack Iran.

During a press briefing at Israel's parliament in Jerusalem on Monday (November 23), Mr. Eisenkot said the "Iranian threat is the most serious threat to the State of Israel".

"But at this moment I do not see a direct and immediate threat to the State of Israel that would require action before a government is formed," he added.

World.title: Why has the FSSAI sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri? | Explained
World.content:
The story so far: On November 22, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), the country’s apex food-safety regulator, sanctioned prosecution against packaged drinking water manufacturer Bisleri International Pvt. Ltd. after a sample of its water was found to be non-compliant with prescribed safety standards, with the regulator declaring it unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

The public-health stakes are significant. In 2023, bottled water was the principal source of drinking water for 15% of urban and 6% of rural households, as per Data For India. For consumers buying it at railway stations, airports, highway eateries and neighbourhood shops, a sealed bottle is often taken as an assurance of safety. Yet, the data submitted in Parliament in February 2025 revealed that 333 of 1,300 enforcement samples of packaged drinking water tested in 2023-24 failed to meet prescribed standards. Similarly, in 2022-23, 650 of 1,776 samples had been found non-compliant.

According to the FSSAI, a sample of packaged drinking water (other than mineral water) collected from Bisleri’s premises was found to be non-compliant with the prescribed limits for “bromate” and was declared unsafe under the 2006 Act. Following an appeal by the food business operator (FBO), the sample was referred to a Referral Food Laboratory for further examination, which also declared the sample unsafe, citing the detection of “polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons” (PAHs).

In its response, Bisleri has maintained that its water is safe for consumption, saying the matter concerned a batch manufactured at its Goa facility in September 2025, one of 143 manufacturing plants in its network. In a statement issued on November 23, the company said the FSSAI had collected six samples from its Goa facility on September 30, 2025. While five samples met the prescribed standards, the sixth recorded a “bromate” level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre. Further, Bisleri said it appealed on November 22, 2025, following which the sample was sent to a referral laboratory for retesting. The laboratory, as claimed, found the bromate level within the prescribed limit but separately detected PAHs. Citing the divergent test findings, the company reportedly arranged an independent examination of the same sample at an FSSAI-approved laboratory, which, according to Bisleri, also found the bromate level within limits. The company said it submitted these results to FSSAI’s Western Regional Office on February 2, 2026, but received no further communication and understood that the matter had been closed.

Water is essential for digestion, blood circulation, temperature regulation and kidney function, but its safety cannot be judged by its appearance, taste, odour or sealed packaging alone. Contamination may be microbiological, causing illnesses such as diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid, or chemical, with some substances posing risks through prolonged exposure. In India, packaged water broadly falls into two categories: (1) “packaged drinking water”, which may be sourced from surface water, groundwater or seawater and treated through processes such as filtration, decantation, reverse osmosis (RO) and disinfection; and (2) “natural mineral water”, drawn from protected underground sources and characterised by a relatively stable mineral composition. Both must meet prescribed chemical and microbiological safety standards.

World.title: Thomas Markle charged in U.S. on second count of possessing child sexual abuse material
World.content:
Thomas Markle, the estranged father of Britain’s Duchess of Sussex, ⁠Meghan Markle, and father-in-law of Britain’s Prince Harry, was indicted on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) in U.S. federal court on two counts of possessing child sexual abuse material.

The indictment doubles the number of federal ‌charges currently lodged in Los Angeles against the 82-year-old Markle in a case that grew out of an investigation initiated last month in the ‌Philippines, where he previously resided.

The elder Markle was originally charged on ‌November ⁠5 in a criminal complaint with a single felony count of ⁠possessing child sexual abuse images.

According to an FBI affidavit filed with the complaint, the material in question was found in two Los Angeles storage units and included two explicit photos of Markle posed with ​a naked underage girl and other ‌images of him with children in various stages of undress.

One of the photos showed a naked girl in a room that appeared to be part of a motel chain in the Philippines, the affidavit said.

Philippine police said last ‌week criminal complaints had been filed against Markle in the country’s Cebu ​province, where he once lived, accusing him of violating local laws against online sexual abuse and exploitation of children.

Markle has denied the ⁠allegations, telling the Daily Mail the claims were untrue and describing them as “sick lies.”

He was arrested on November 6 at a Florida assisted-living facility where he has been ‌a patient, and is expected to be transferred to California in the coming weeks to be arraigned in US District Court in Los Angeles on the two-count grand jury indictment returned on Tuesday (November 24).

Following a court-ordered psychiatric evaluation of Markle, a U.S. magistrate judge in Tampa, Florida, last week ruled that he was mentally competent to stand trial, meaning that he understood the proceedings against him and could ‌assist in his own defense.

Each count of possession of child sexual abuse material, an offence referred to ​in the US criminal code as possession of child pornography, is punishable by up to 20 years in prison if he is convicted, ⁠the U.S. attorney’s statement said.

Meghan Markle, an American actor, has been estranged from her ⁠father since the run-up to her marriage to King Charles’ younger son, Harry, in 2018, when the duchess has said she first became aware ‌of allegations against her father. She has said she was “deeply distressed” over the matter, which led her to cut off contact between her father and ​her two children, Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5.

World.title: U.S. set to slap tariffs on China, EU and others after probe on excess industrial capacity: report
World.content:
The Trump administration is poised ​to imminently release the findings of a probe aimed at countering alleged excess industrial capacity in 16 ⁠major U.S. trading partners, three people with knowledge of the matter said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), with new import duties on a wide range of goods expected.

The results of the investigation are expected as soon, these people said. The U.S. Trade Representative’s office is expected to propose ‌new duties that would stack on top of previous tariffs already imposed during President Donald Trump’s second term.

The duties would partly replace tariffs struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February. The administration’s tariffs have in part ‌contributed to higher prices on consumer goods in the United States, and a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll following November’s midterm elections ‌showed ⁠62% of respondents would support efforts to repeal the tariffs.

Tailored tariff rates

It is unclear what tariff rates ⁠would be proposed. One of the people said that the duties would be specifically tailored to each country, with goods from Mexico and Norway unlikely to see any immediate levies.

USTR has been investigating most of the US’s largest trading partners under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 over what it called ​evidence of excess industrial capacity.

The White House is ‌expected to honor capped tariff rates that were included in finalized US trade deals with partner countries, this person said. These include duty caps of 15% on goods from the EU, Japan and South Korea and 19% for Malaysia.

The U.S. also is expected to honor the 20% cap on Trump’s second-term tariffs on goods from China, as long as a ‌trade truce due to expire on January 10 is extended. If it expires, the Chinese excess capacity rate would ​rise to a higher level.

The U.S. Trade Representative’s office and the White House did not respond to Reuters queries about the pending announcement.

Ryan Majerus, a former senior Commerce Department trade official, said he ⁠expects a lengthy report that could include differentiated tariff remedies for each of the 16 trading partners.

Majerus, a partner with King & Spalding, said the administration could propose high tariff rates of 15% to 25% on imports from countries deemed to have excess capacity in various sectors. ‌Those levies would stack on top of existing tariffs of 10% or 12.5% imposed under a separate investigation into lax enforcement of anti-forced labor laws.

However, he said the administration could also propose lower tariff rates with escalation clauses that would ratchet rates higher over time unless countries take steps to reduce excess production capacity.

Replacement tariffs

The countries included in the probe are China, India, Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Vietnam, Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, Switzerland, Norway, Singapore, Bangladesh and Cambodia, along with the European Union.

The Wall Street Journal reported earlier that the probe’s results could be unveiled as soon as this week.

USTR launched the excess capacity probe in March, along ‌with a separate probe into weak or lax enforcement of anti-forced labor laws in 59 countries and the European Union. Together, the duties are meant to ​rebuild Trump’s global “Liberation Day” tariffs that were struck down by the U.S. Supreme Court in February.

The Trump administration has singled out China as the biggest source of excess industrial capacity, which it says is flooding global ⁠markets with steel, aluminum, electric vehicles, appliances, solar products and other goods. China has rejected the accusations, saying its exports reflect competitive advantages.

The probe ⁠is also partly directed at Chinese investment into countries in Southeast Asia, including Vietnam, Indonesia and Cambodia, to manufacture goods for the US market and avoid prior US tariffs.

Under a U.S.-China trade truce due to expire on January ‌10, the Trump administration has capped second-term tariffs on Chinese goods at 20%, in addition to duties of about 25% imposed during Mr. Trump’s first term. The US has already imposed a 12.5% anti-forced labor duty on all Chinese imports, leaving only ​7.5% to reach the 20% cap.

The U.S. and China also are working to cut tariffs on $30 billion of non-strategic imports from each side.

World.title: No power can harm India as long as it reveres Sikh Gurus, says U.P. CM Adityanath
World.content:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) said that no power in the world will be able to harm India as long as it continues to hold Sikh Gurus in reverence and respect.

“The sacrifice, penance, martyrdom, and spiritual consciousness of the Sikh Gurus are invaluable treasures of India’s national unity, social harmony, and cultural pride,” Mr. Adityanath said, addressing a program organised on the occasion of the 557th Prakash Parv of Sahib Shri Guru Nanak Dev Ji in Lucknow .

“Through ‘Ek Onkar’, Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj gave the message of uniting all humanity. His teachings remain as relevant today as they were then. We must not confine these teachings to events and celebrations alone, but imbibe them in our lives and continuously familiarize the younger generation with them as well,” he added.

Referring to the spiritual and religious significance of Kartik Purnima, the U.P. Chief Minister said, “Today is an extremely sacred day for entire state. Since 4 am, I have been receiving updates on the number of devotees and arrangements at various religious sites across the state. At Shukratal in Muzaffarnagar, lakhs of devotees are taking a holy dip in the Ganga.

At Garhmukteshwar in Hapur, approximately 15 lakh devotees took a holy dip on Tuesday. Meanhwhile, more than 15 lakh devotees took a dip of faith in the Ganga at Tigri in Amroha. A large number of devotees also arrived in Prayagraj and Farrukhabad, while lakhs of them visited the Ganga in Ayodhya and Kashi,”.

Referring to the journeys undertaken by Guru Nanak Dev Ji and social conditions prevailing during his time, Mr. Adityanath said, “When he conveyed the message of unity to humanity, society was grappling with numerous social evils and divisions. Society was fragmented in the name of caste, untouchability and discrimination.

At the same time, he said foreign invasions and external attacks posed challenges. During such difficult times, Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj united all humanity through the mantra of ‘Ek Onkar’. His clear message was that God is one and we are all His children. Therefore, every human being deserves equal respect. This mantra, given by him, became a great force for uniting society at that time, and it remains relevant even today. Despite limited means and resources, Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj traveled to various places and spread the message of humanity, equality and spiritual consciousness among the masses,”.

Explaining the three principal teachings of Guru Nanak Dev Ji Maharaj, ‘Naam Japo, Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako’, the U.P. CM added, “Remembering God, performing kirtan and embracing the spirit of togetherness generate positive feelings within human beings. This dispels ignorance and awakens the strength of unity in society,”..

World.title: Tiruchi colleges train faculty and students to adapt to AI, ML in classroom
World.content:
Higher education institutions in Tiruchi have begun integrating emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML), by not just including them in their syllabi, but also creating capacity building programmes for teachers and students in recent years.

ML is a branch of AI that uses algorithms to learn patterns from data and make predictions, classifications, or decisions without explicit hard-coded instructions.

A growing number of institutes are opting for faculty development programmes (FDPs) that focus on how to integrate AI and ML in the pedagogy as well.

“Though there is a buzz over the entry of AI into the classroom at present, it not actually a new phenomenon. It has existed in multiple forms before, and is still developing newer versions. The best results are mainly down to prompting the machine. If one learns how to give an AI prompt [an input such as a question, description or command to an AI model to get a response], one can create product successfully, and personalise it as well,” Anantha Ganesh, founder and director, Bodhi Multiverse UK, told The Hindu.

The Tiruchi-based tech company has conducted six AI-related faculty development programmes for city colleges this year, and is in the process of creating an e-commerce platform for women’s self-help groups in the Tiruchi district.

“The rapid increase in the number of AI tools and software can be frustrating for users and creators, but we expect this to stabilise in the coming years,” said Mr. Ganesh.

Capacity building programmes for educational institutions in Tiruchi typically cost upwards of ₹850 per person depending on the course and duration.

In the classroom

Though many institutions offer degree programmes in emerging technologies, there is a shortage of faculty qualified to teach them.

“The syllabus has not been updated to cater to the new subjects, which has created problems for both students and teachers. It would be better for students to start industrial internships in the first year of their course, so that they can get exposure to the technologies in real time,” said Kevin Giftson, founder, CEO, Aske AI, a company that conducts tech learning modules for colleges, developers, and healthcare professionals.

At National College, teachers are encouraged to complete at least two modules in emerging technologies every year through Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) offered on government portals.
