The platform says the meeting, which took place on 19 November, does not continue the informal dialogue with Russia that existed previously. Instead, it creates a new, direct high-level political channel that could undermine the Geneva International Discussions.

What does the platform’s statement say?

The platform points out that the meeting took place in an official setting, with the two countries’ national flags on display.

It says the Russian side presented the meeting as an official contact between the foreign ministries of the two countries, and the Georgian side did not object.

“This raises the question: are the authorities laying the groundwork for normalising Russian-Georgian relations in a way that no longer makes de-occupation a precondition?” the statement says.

The Anti-Annexation Platform is a non-partisan civic association founded in Georgia on 27 August 2026. It aims to oppose Russia’s occupation and annexation policies and defend Georgia’s territorial integrity and sovereignty.

Its founders include politicians, former military personnel, diplomats, security experts and journalists.

The Anti-Annexation Platform also focuses on the location of the meeting and the issues discussed.

It says Minsk was not chosen by chance: Russia openly stated in 2024 that it wanted to move the Geneva International Discussions to Minsk.

The platform therefore warns of a risk that Minsk could become the centre of a political channel running parallel to the Geneva format.

The statement stresses that the Geneva International Discussions remain the only active international negotiating format involving the European Union, the United Nations and the OSCE. The talks address the situation in the occupied territories, Russia’s responsibility, security and humanitarian issues.

The platform believes that moving these issues into a bilateral format with Russia would weaken international involvement and Georgia’s negotiating position.

19 ноября в вечернем эфире проправительственного грузинского телеканала «Имеди» министр On 19 November, Georgian Foreign Minister Maka Bochorishvili said on the evening news programme of the pro-government Imedi TV channel that “there is nothing wrong with dialogue with Russia”.

“In recent years, whenever it comes to our relations with Russia or our attitude towards it, there have been attempts to instil fear of dialogue and talks, and to reject them outright. This is the country with which we have the most problems, and they are the biggest ones. We cannot resolve any problems without talks and dialogue if our goal is to find solutions or settle disputes,” the minister said.

The Anti-Annexation Platform says Bochorishvili’s remarks the previous day about fear of talking to Russia miss the point:

“Georgian society is not afraid of dialogue. The key question is on what terms this dialogue takes place, what agenda it follows and whose interests it serves.”

The Anti-Annexation Platform has called on the authorities to answer the following questions:

Why did the Georgian side agree to hold the meeting in Minsk?

Why did it not explore the possibility of holding a meeting under the new format in Geneva rather than Minsk?

What do the “practical arrangements” mentioned by Russia involve?

How will the authorities distinguish this new format from the Geneva International Discussions?

What guarantees are there that this process will not undermine the Geneva format and lead to the normalisation of diplomatic relations without de-occupation?

The meeting and its political context

According to statements by the Georgian government and the Russian Foreign Ministry, the two sides discussed trade and economic cooperation, cultural and humanitarian ties, regional security and the importance of the Geneva International Discussions.

Both sides said they had reached certain practical arrangements and agreed to maintain contact. However, they did not disclose the details of these arrangements.

This was the first meeting of its kind since Zurabashvili became the prime minister’s special representative. His mandate covers not only trade, economic and humanitarian issues but also the peaceful settlement of the conflict with Russia.

Since 2012, direct dialogue with Russia had taken place under the so-called Karasin-Abashidze format. The meetings were held mainly in Prague and focused on trade, transport and humanitarian issues.

The new format, the choice of Minsk as the venue and Zurabashvili’s broader mandate have prompted criticism in Tbilisi.

Former diplomats and experts have expressed concern that the meeting could mark a step towards direct political dialogue with Russia and the restoration of diplomatic relations.

World.title: Tajikistan's mining output declines 3.4% in ten months
World.content:
Photo: The press office of the Tajik President

BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 25. Tajikistan's mining output decreased by 3.4% year-on-year in January–October 2026, reaching 15.27 billion somoni ($1.65 billion), according to Trend's calculations based on data from the Agency on Statistics under the President of the Republic of Tajikistan.

In October 2026 alone, mining output amounted to 1.57 billion somoni ($170 million), representing a 1.9% increase compared with October 2025.

The sector's cumulative performance marked a sharp reversal from the previous year's expansion. In January–October 2025, mining output had increased 1.5 times year-on-year, equivalent to approximately 50% growth, meaning the annual growth rate dropped by 53.4 percentage points in the reporting period.

The year-on-year growth rate in October also slowed by 3.9 percentage points, from 5.8% in October 2025 to 1.9% in October 2026.

For comparison, total industrial output in Tajikistan reached 59.82 billion somoni ($6.48 billion) in January–October 2026, up 13.5% year-on-year, following a 22.8% expansion in the same period of 2025. In October 2026, overall industrial production stood at 6.65 billion somoni ($720 million), increasing by 6.2% year-on-year after growing 10.2% in October 2025.

Mining accounted for approximately 25.5% of Tajikistan's total industrial output in January–October 2026, and 23.6% in October 2026.

Tajikistan’s mining and quarrying sector—which encompasses the extraction of gold, silver, antimony, lead, zinc, coal, and non-metallic construction materials—was a major contributor to the country's industrial growth in 2025.

According to official statistics, mining output surged by 36.2% in full-year 2025 to reach 20.53 billion somoni ($2.22 billion), accounting for nearly 31% of Tajikistan's total industrial production. The moderation in 2026 reflects both a high statistical base from the previous year's rapid expansion and ongoing shifts in global metal prices and external demand.

World.title: US government may acquire stake in Nvidia - Trump
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 25. US President Donald Trump has not ruled out the possibility of the American government acquiring a stake in technology giant Nvidia.

"I’ve thought about it. I’ve said that perhaps I should do it. But I haven’t discussed it yet. Maybe it’s not too late," Trump said.

He emphasized Nvidia’s importance to the development of artificial intelligence in the United States, recalling that in 2025, the US government acquired a 10% stake in Intel.

However, Trump did not specify the terms under which the government might acquire an equity stake in Nvidia.

The US president also raised the possibility of pardoning Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, although he said he did not believe such a step would be necessary.

Trump noted that appointing an unsuitable candidate to a leadership position could have serious consequences for the United States. He also said he had helped facilitate Huang’s return to a leadership role at the company.

Meanwhile, the White House expressed hope that Huang would provide truthful testimony at upcoming hearings before the US Senate Banking Committee.

US authorities suspect that Nvidia's AI chips are being illegally supplied to China.

According to the information provided, Huang stepped down as Nvidia's CEO and president on November 12, following reports of his alleged ties to a woman suspected of spying for China. The Chinese Foreign Ministry dismissed the allegations as slanderous.

On November 23, Nvidia's board of directors unanimously voted to reinstate Huang as CEO and president. According to the company, U.S. authorities had provided assurances that his return to the position would not pose a threat to American national security.

World.title: Solar power plants generate 1.9 billion kWh in Kazakhstan in nine months
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 25. Solar power plants in Kazakhstan generated 1.9 billion kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electricity in January-September 2026, according to the Ministry of Energy's latest data on renewable energy generation.

Meanwhile, total electricity output from renewable energy facilities reached 7.8 billion kWh during the reporting period. According to Trend's calculations, solar power plants accounted for approximately 24.4% of this volume, or nearly one-quarter.

Kazakhstan’s solar power sector consists of both large utility-scale photovoltaic plants and smaller generation facilities operating across several regions. As of the second quarter of 2026, the country had 52 solar power plants with a combined installed capacity of 1,375.2 MW, accounting for around 36.7% of the total installed renewable energy capacity of 3,749.6 MW. Wind power remains the largest renewable energy source by installed capacity, with 2,058.9 MW. According to the Kazakhstan Electricity Grid Operating Company (KEGOC), solar power plants accounted for 1,353 MW of Kazakhstan’s total installed electricity generation capacity of 26,807 MW as of January 1, 2026.

The country’s solar generation facilities are spread across several regions, with major projects including the 100 MW Nurgisa solar power plant in the Almaty Region, the 100 MW Shu-100 plant in the Zhambyl Region, the 100 MW Saran plant in the Karaganda Region and the 100 MW Nura plant in the Akmola Region. Another major project is the Burnoye solar power plant in the Zhambyl Region, developed in two stages and commissioned in 2015 and 2018. The project was implemented through a partnership between Samruk-Kazyna Invest and British company UG Energy Limited.

World.title: Iran's Shanol gas field produces 10 million cubic meters per day
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 25. Iran's Shanol gas field currently produces 10 million cubic meters of natural gas per day, according to Saeed Momtazan, an official at the South Zagros Oil and Gas Production Company, the Ministry of Petroleum reported.

"Currently, 19 wells are operational at the Shanol gas field. The gas produced from these wells is transported to the gathering center through an 8-inch pipeline. It is then sent to the separation center through a 24-inch pipeline," he noted.

Momtazan said that major maintenance work had been carried out at the Shanol gathering center over approximately one month to ensure gas supplies during the winter months. During the maintenance, all wells, facilities, and equipment were inspected, and the necessary measures were taken.

The company official added that, due to restrictions resulting from sanctions imposed against the country, most maintenance work is carried out in cooperation with local and startup companies.

Momtazan said that operations at the Shanol gas gathering center had become particularly difficult during the 12-day war in June last year and the 40-day war this year, as there were concerns that the facility could also be targeted.

The Shanol gas field was commissioned in 2006. According to the source, 19 wells are operating at the field.

According to information from Iran's South Zagros Oil Fields Company, gas is produced at four fields in the Parsian operating area: Tabnak, Homa, Shanol, and Varavi. The area has a total production capacity of 76 million cubic meters of gas and 25,600 barrels of gas condensate per day.

World.title: US plans to raise import tariffs on China and dozens of other countries
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 25. The administration of US President Donald Trump is preparing to increase import tariffs on goods from China and dozens of other countries.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is expected to announce the findings of an investigation this week into industrial subsidies and excess production capacity in China, the European Union, and 14 other countries.

According to preliminary information, the United States may raise tariffs on imports from China, Japan, South Korea, and all 27 EU member states. The measures could affect most categories of imported goods.

The final tariff rates have not yet been determined. However, representatives of the US administration have repeatedly stated their intention to restore the tariff levels introduced by Donald Trump last year.

As previously reported, in October, China's Ministry of Commerce announced retaliatory measures in response to what it described as U.S. attempts to disrupt global supply chains under the pretext of addressing "overcapacity."

World.title: Kazakhstan plans to add 8.4 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2035
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 25. Kazakhstan plans to commission at least 8.4 GW of new renewable energy capacity by the end of 2035, including around 1.8 GW of solar power, the country's Ministry of Energy said.

The planned expansion covers solar, wind and other renewable energy facilities. According to Trend's calculations, solar power will account for approximately 21.4% of the planned new capacity, or more than one-fifth of the total.

The ministry also reported that Kazakhstan is developing a portfolio of prospective solar power projects with a combined capacity of around 900 MW.

These include a 300 MW solar power plant planned by China Energy and projects by Tumar Commerce with a combined capacity of up to 1,5 GW.

China Energy Engineering Corporation (Energy China), one of China's major energy and infrastructure engineering companies, is involved in the construction of a solar power plant in Kazakhstan's southern Turkistan Region. The project is being implemented in partnership with Kazakhstan's Samruk-Energy and includes an energy storage system with a capacity of 90 MW and 360 MWh. Total investment exceeds $200 million, while annual electricity generation is expected to surpass 600 million kWh.

According to Samruk-Energy, around 70% of the photovoltaic modules had been installed by October 2026. The plant is expected to begin supplying electricity in December 2026, with full commissioning scheduled for the first quarter of 2027.

Meanwhile, Tumar Commerce is developing renewable energy projects with a combined capacity of up to 1 GW, including solar power plants in the Turkistan, Zhambyl and Kyzylorda regions. According to Samruk-Energy, the projects were scheduled for implementation between 2023 and 2028. Preparatory work included feasibility studies and design, negotiations with banks and financial institutions on financing, and the selection of equipment suppliers and contractors. However, the available information does not confirm that construction of these projects has begun.

World.title: Tajikistan's industrial output increases 13.5% in January–October 2026
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 25. Tajikistan's industrial output increased by 13.5% year-on-year in January–October 2026, reaching 59.82 billion somoni ($6.48 billion), according to Trend's calculations based on data from the Agency on Statistics under the President of the Republic of Tajikistan.

In October 2026 alone, the country's industrial production amounted to 6.65 billion somoni ($720.5 million), representing a 6.2% increase compared with the same month of 2025.

However, Trend's calculations show that the pace of industrial expansion slowed noticeably compared with the previous year. In January–October 2025, industrial output had risen by 22.8% year-on-year, meaning that the growth rate in the corresponding period of 2026 decelerated by 9.3 percentage points.

A similar moderation in growth was recorded on a monthly basis in October. Industrial output had expanded by 10.2% year-on-year in October 2025, compared with 6.2% in October 2026, marking a slowdown of 4 percentage points in the annual growth rate.

Tajikistan’s industrial sector is wrapping up the 2022–2026 "Years of Industrial Development" and transitioning into the new Accelerated Industrialisation Programme for 2026–2030, which targets at least 25% annual industrial growth and aims to raise industry's share of GDP to 30%. In full-year 2025, total industrial output rose 22.1% year-on-year to 66.73 billion somoni ($7.23 billion) — driven largely by a 36.2% surge in mining and quarrying — before moderating to 14.1% growth in the first half of 2026 and 13.7% in January–September 2026.

World.title: Poland and UK sign agreement on joint development of new medium-range missile
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, November 25. The governments of Poland and the United Kingdom have signed an agreement on joint funding and cooperation in the research and development of a new medium-range missile, the CAMM-MR/FCM.

The document sets out the key areas of cooperation between the two countries in developing the new missile system and reaffirms their strategic partnership in the field of air defense.

The project will involve companies belonging to the Polish Armaments Group (PGZ), enterprises from Poland's defense industry, as well as research and development organizations.

Participation in the program is expected to enable Poland's defense industry to make significant technological advances and expand its production capabilities in the field of advanced missile systems.

The agreement provides for the implementation of the project at its initial concept development stage.

The CAMM-MR/FCM (Future Common Missile / Medium-Range) is a next-generation surface-to-air missile with an operational range of more than 100 kilometers, designed to expand the capabilities of the CAMM missile family.

The new missile is intended for deployment in both ground-based air defense systems and naval platforms. It is designed to intercept aircraft, helicopters, unmanned aerial vehicles, and cruise missiles.

World.title: Ireland lose skipper for Wallabies clash while Suaalii relishing centre role
World.content:
Ireland stand-in skipper Dan Sheehan will miss his side's final Nations Championship match against the Wallabies after being given a two-week suspension following his red card for a croc-roll against South Africa at the weekend.

Sheehan's initial yellow card eight minutes from the end of Saturday's 20-17 win was upgraded to a red after the match.

The 28-year-old has captained Ireland in the absence of injured Caelan Doris.

Sheehan, usually a hooker, played at number eight for the first time in his international career against the Springboks as the side were grappling with an injury crisis at the back of the scrum.

Ireland are already without at least three number eights through injury, with Jack Conan and Sean Jansen missing, as well as Doris.

Given the Wallabies' strength at the back of the scrum, the absentees will be cause for concern for the Irish.

Ulster's 23-year-old giant, James McNabney, should be fit to return after missing the Springboks clash after he was knocked out on debut against Fiji, although his Ulster teammate, backrow utility forward Nick Timoney, will likely start.

Ireland, which finished third in the Northern Hemisphere section, will face Australia at Twickenham in a play-off to decide fifth and sixth place.

Meanwhile, Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii said he enjoyed the combination at centre with the experienced Len Ikitau as the debate over his best position for the Wallabies continued.

Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii says he enjoyed playing centre. (Getty Images: Michael Steele)

Suaalii played at centre in his first 22 starts for Australia, following his high-profile defection from rugby league, but new Wallabies coach Les Kiss moved him to wing for the 42-38 victory over South Africa in Perth in September and the first Bledisloe Cup clash against New Zealand last month.

The absent Hunter Paisami may be expected to challenge him for that outside centre spot, while Ikitau could benefit from a move to 13, with Carter Gordon at 12.

In the Nations Championship this month, he was picked on the wing against England but returned to the midfield against Scotland and last weekend's 29-26 win over Wales.

"I just love playing rugby and, being able to play 13, you get to be both sides of the ball. You can defend and attack and you're in the front line," he said in London.

"Playing alongside Lenny, he's great with his comms. He's quiet off the field but once he goes on the field, he helps you quite a bit."

The 23-year-old Suaalii has also been a regular fullback for the New South Wales Waratahs in Super Rugby but has not been picked at number 15 for Australia.

With the hosting of the World Cup now less than a year away, and where home hopes will rest heavily on his shoulders, where best to use Suaalii's powerful presence has stirred plenty of debate among Aussie pundits.

"I think my biggest thing is just, I'm still learning the game. I'm still trying to get better each week," he added.

"It doesn't matter what number I have on my back; I'm just trying to use the skill sets I have … defence, aerial attacking, ball in hand, breakdown.

"I see myself just growing my game in all that sense: the attack, defence, breakdown, transition. I'm really just focusing on putting my energy towards trying to get better in that sense and then position-wise, it's just up to the coach.

"I've always said that. I'm happy to play anywhere, just always just trusting what the coach is going to do and, at the end of the day, I'm playing for my country, so I'm always grateful for that."

Reuters/ABC

World.title: Breaking: Regional council charged over 5yo boy's death
World.content:
Western Australia's workplace safety watchdog is prosecuting one of the state's most significant regional councils over the death of a five-year-old boy at the local museum.

Sammy suffered fatal injuries when he was crushed by an old parking meter on display at the Bunbury Heritage Museum in January last year.

WorkSafe alleges the City of Bunbury breached safety regulations at the museum.

"The boy, who was attending school holiday activities at the museum, entered the museum courtyard area where a decommissioned parking meter was being stored," a WorkSafe spokesperson said.

Sammy passed away after he was critically injured at the Bunbury Heritage Museum. (Supplied: WA Police Media)

"The parking meter became unstable and fell on him, causing fatal crush injuries."

The boy died in hospital after being rushed there for treatment.

The City of Bunbury has been charged with failing to ensure, as far as was reasonably practicable, that the workplace was without risks to the health and safety of any person and, by that failure, causing the death of the boy.

City representatives will face the Bunbury Magistrates Court next month.

World.title: Man charged after ram raid at Canberra home
World.content:
ACT police have charged a 38-year-old man after a ram raid at a home in Denman Prospect.

Police say four men arrived at the home in Canberra's west about 10:50am on Tuesday morning in a beige Mazda 3.

The group allegedly rammed the vehicle into the home's roller door, and then entered the property, smashing windows and a fish tank.

Police say they located the Mazda 3 a short time later, travelling with a silver Volkswagen Tiguan in Lyons.

It is alleged both cars failed to stop when directed by officers before crossing over to the wrong side of the road and driving through a school zone.

Following this, officers set up a police cordon at a home in Chifley believed to be known to the man.

After negotiations with specialist police, the 38-year-old surrendered and was arrested.

He was charged with aggravated burglary with intent to damage property and joint commission of damage to property.

The man, who was subject to a good behaviour order, faced the ACT Magistrates Court today.

He did not apply for bail, and the case is expected to be back in court in January.

Police are asking anyone who witnessed the ram raid or has dashcam footage of either the beige-coloured Mazda 3 or silver Volkswagen Tiguan driving in the Denman Prospect or Lyons areas yesterday to come forward.

World.title: Northern Territory government working on 'castle law'
World.content:
The Northern Territory government has confirmed it is working to introduce "castle law" in the NT.

The principle, also known as castle doctrine, removes the duty of residents to retreat from an intruder within their own home.

Instead, it provides the basis for occupants to use force — including lethal force in some instances — to defend themselves and their property.

Under the current NT Criminal Code, a person is not criminally responsible for an offence involving the use of lethal force if they believe it is necessary to defend themselves or another person, where their actions are "a reasonable response in the circumstances as he or she perceives them".

The defence also applies where the person uses force to protect property or remove a trespasser, unless the force "involves the intentional infliction of death or serious harm".

In a Facebook comment posted on Monday, NT Education Minister Jo Hersey confirmed the government was working on introducing castle law in the NT.

Lia Finocchiaro says they want Territorians to be able to defend themselves. (ABC News: Pete Garnish)

Ms Hersey's comment echoes similar remarks made by Chief Minister Lia Finocchiaro in recent weeks.

"We recognise people want the opportunity protect themselves," she said.

" We are looking at castle law options, that is still on the table. "

If introduced and passed, the Northern Territory would be the first state or territory to explicitly legislate castle law in Australia.

Castle law has gained significant traction across the country recently, with Katter's Australia Party launching petitions to legislate the doctrine in Queensland.

The principle also formed a key part of the Libertarian Party's platform at the Victorian election in November this year.

While Country Liberal Party insiders have confirmed work has been done on legislating the principle, a date for legislation has not been specified.

World.title: Flinders Island sergeant shot on duty 'still has long way to go', family says
World.content:
The brother of a police officer shot while on duty on Flinders Island said he was humbled by the community support being shown to his family.

Tasmanian Police Sergeant Michael Preshaw sustained serious injuries in what police believe was a targeted shooting outside the Whitemark police station on Saturday night.

He remains in a serious but stable condition at the Royal Hobart Hospital after surgery.

Special Operations Group officers have been assisting local police efforts. (ABC News: Kelsey Reid)

Nicholas Preshaw, a fellow police officer who is understood to be Sergeant Michael Preshaw's twin brother, posted on social media this morning to thank those who had reached out.

"The number of text messages, phone calls, offers of support, coffees, meals and acts of kindness has been truly overwhelming, to say the least," he said.

"Our family … has been humbled by the support shown over the past few days.

" Michael still has a long way to go, but if the way he has handled this so far is any indication, he will get through it. "

'Hope he gets to read this' brother posts

Police believe Sergeant Preshaw was shot in the side and arm by a man in his mid-20s, who was known to police, with a stolen 12-gauge shotgun just after 9.40pm.

It is alleged Sergeant Preshaw returned fire. The body of the alleged shooter was found in nearby Walker Street with what is believed to be a gunshot wound to his torso.

Nicholas Preshaw went on to praise his brother in a post, saying he "hopes he gets to read this when he wakes up".

"I just want to say that he is the only bloke I know who could have saved his own life the way he did," he said.

"That is not to take anything away from the remarkable people who stepped in after the event and did everything they could to keep him alive before he made it to the Royal Hobart Hospital."

Tillie Preshaw, who is understood to be Sergeant Preshaw's daughter, also posted on Facebook today, thanking the community for its "love and support".

"From the bottom of my heart, thank you to everyone who has been there for us and, most importantly, to those who helped keep Dad here with us," she wrote.

"Dad, when you wake up, I hope you know just how loved you are, how many people are in your corner and how incredibly proud we all are of you.

" You have always been my biggest inspiration, my role model and my hero, long before any of this. "

Tasmania Police is yet to reveal the identity of the man involved in the shooting.

A coronial investigation and professional standards investigation are also underway.

World.title: Probe finds Chevron methane plumes deliberately released
World.content:
Chevron's Gorgon gas project vented massive methane plumes to ease pressure on its troubled carbon capture and storage (CCS) system, investigators say.

The finding was prompted by a United Nations alert sent in August, when huge clouds of the greenhouse gas were detected soaring above the $81 billion facility off Western Australia's Pilbara coast.

Five consecutive satellite observations between November 2025 and August 2026 estimated methane emissions averaging 4.9 tonnes an hour — nearly five times the reported rate at Gorgon over the past two years.

But the WA's Department of Water and Environment Regulation (DWER) says August's emissions event was planned, based on information from Chevron and gathered during a site inspection earlier this month.

"DWER concluded that the emissions were associated with venting of reservoir carbon dioxide through approved facility infrastructure during periods where constraints affected operation of the CCS system," Environment Minister Matthew Swinbourn said in a statement.

"DWER has found no evidence that the emissions detected on 29 August 2026 were associated with an uncontrolled leak, upset condition, incident, or unauthorised emissions source."

Matthew Swinbourn says the emissions were part of the venting of reservoir carbon dioxide. (ABC News: Lauren Smith)

Located on Barrow Island, about 60 kilometres from the West Australian mainland, the Gorgon complex remains the country's most expensive resources venture.

A Chevron spokesperson told the ABC the company had worked "constructively" with DWER and was committed to responsibly managing its emissions, including methane.

"Gorgon operates within some of Australia's most rigorous environmental and regulatory frameworks, with extensive requirements governing how emissions are managed, monitored and reported," the spokesperson said.

WA regulator actively investigating methane cloud at Chevron The WA government has confirmed it is now investigated the repeated large methane emissions from Chevron's Gorgon gas complex.

Whistleblower: Emissions 'deliberate'

In claims tabled by WA Greens MLC Sophie McNeill before state parliament overnight, a whistleblower working on Barrow Island accused Chevron of "deliberately releasing" the methane rather than slowing down production.

The three-point statement made to Ms McNeill reiterated that the emissions had not been a leak and blamed Chevron's CCS.

Reporting by Chevron shows its production of liquefied natural gas (LNG) at Gorgon has regularly outstripped its stated 15.6 million tonne per annum design capacity.

According to the multinational's own compliance reports to DWER, it has surpassed 15.6 million tonnes by close to 8 per cent each year since 2021.

Sophie McNeill tabled the whistleblower statement in parliament. (ABC News: Courtney Withers)

Global LNG prices sit near multi-year highs following attacks on Qatari suppliers and shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Ms McNeill said the emissions amounted to a violation of Gorgon's environmental approvals, which stipulated there might be "no routine venting or flaring policy" except where normal operations were unavailable.

"It is a commercial choice by Chevron to do this," she said.

Carbon capture scrutiny

The revelations coincide with new data calculating the shortfalls of Gorgon's CCS.

Chevron and its joint venture partners are obligated to sequester 80 per cent of the carbon dioxide (CO2) released by Gorgon's particularly carbon-rich gas fields.

But engineering issues ensured the CCS system did not operate for the first three years of gas exports, and it has lagged behind the 80 per cent benchmark in the time since.

Technicians working on Gorgon's CCS system. (Supplied: Chevron)

The alert-triggering methane plumes appear to originate near the plant's three acid gas removal units, which strip unprocessed natural gas of CO2 and other impurities.

When operating as intended, the CO2 is then piped to a separate facility for injection into Barrow Island's sandstone underlayer.

A Chevron spokesperson acknowledged that challenges had "constrained injection rates".

"We're progressing projects to optimise the system, with work well underway," the spokesperson said.

Chevron documents published this month say that about 5.54 million tonnes of reservoir CO2 was separated and only 1.45 million tonnes (26 per cent) was buried during the past financial year.

Energy researcher Tim Baxter said it was the smallest share since Gorgon's CCS began, meaning more than 4 million tonnes of CO2 had been vented into the atmosphere and required offsets.

Tim Baxter was critical of Chevron's forays in CCS. (Supplied)

It is not clear why methane, the main component of natural gas, is also being released, but Mr Baxter said DWER's conclusion demonstrated "downstream impacts" affecting Gorgon's environmental performance.

"What we have from there is a cascading series of failures," Mr Baxter said.

World.title: Concern 'big money' is flowing into Victoria's election despite donation cap
World.content:
Tens of thousands of dollars in election donations from companies linked to property developers, the construction and investment advisory industries have flowed to a Victorian political party, despite a new cap aimed at keeping "big money out of elections".

Victoria brought in a cap on what any one person or "related bodies corporate" could donate to a single political party or independent candidate earlier this year, with then-premier Jacinta Allan pledging "Victoria's elections should be decided by Victorians — not by who has the deepest pockets".

The new law capped donations at $5,030 between April 15 and November 28 — the day of the election. After this, the cap rises to $7,500 over the following four years.

Analysis by the ABC has found donations from linked companies totalling well above the relevant period's cap, including one case where 20 entities linked to two property developers donated $98,000 in one week.

Victoria election 2026 live updates: For all the latest news from the campaign trail, read our blog.

The transactions appear to comply with the new rules because they do not meet the strict definition of "related bodies corporate" in the Corporations Act.

Transparency International Australia chief executive Clancy Moore said the rules created a "loophole … [that] clearly goes against the intention of the reforms" and that large donations risked eroding public trust in democracy.

"We're seeing in Victoria and other states trust in our democracy and political parties at all-time lows," Mr Moore said.

"Voters see property developers, data centre companies, rich individuals donate thousands of dollars to candidates and political parties … there's a perception that these entities are getting a quid pro quo, and you know, potentially getting something in return for their donations."

Ex-footballer turned developer kicks in $20,000

In one case in late August, three companies wholly-owned and directed by former AFL star-turned major property development player Fraser Brown donated $5,000 each, totalling $15,000, to the Victorian branch of the Liberal Party.

The companies, called GPH No.1, GPH No.4 and GPH Plant, are all registered at the same address as Brown Property Group in Hawthorn.

Mr Brown also donated $5,000 in his own name on that same day, as did two family members.

Three companies owned by Fraser Brown donated $5,000 each to the Victorian Liberals, totalling $15,000. (brownpropertygroup.com.au)

Brown Property has in recent years snapped up tightly contested land across the city, reportedly paying $250 million last year for a kale farm in Clyde North.

The group lists eight active house and land planned communities with a self-assessed development value of at least $1.7 billion.

Mr Brown did not respond to the ABC's requests for comment.

In a separate case in early September, five firms linked to two directors of a major construction services company, Checkpoint, each made a donation of $5,000 to the Victorian Liberal Party, totalling $25,000.

Four of the companies, which all include the term "CBS" in the title, are jointly majority owned, via another company, by Checkpoint directors Gavin Casey and Clement Giambattista, while the fifth is majority owned by companies of which they are directors.

Mr Giambattista and Mr Casey did not respond to the ABC's requests for comment.

Companies linked to construction businessmen Clem Giambattista (left) and Gavin Casey made donations totalling $25,000. (check-point.com.au)

In another case in mid-May, three companies — Ketom 2, Ketom 3 and Ketom Pty Ltd — jointly owned by investment advisory specialist Ronn Bechler and Maxine Bechler, made three donations of $5,000 each to the Victorian Liberal Party.

Mr Bechler told the ABC he did not wish to discuss political donations.

Three companies owned co-owned by Ronn Bechler made three separate donations of $5,000. (LinkedIn)

Developers pledge almost $100,000 in one week

Meanwhile it's emerged donations by a group of companies linked to three other wealthy property developers were far higher than initially reported in the media.

The Age in September reported that between late April and early May a dozen businesses with variations on the name "Mensch", made a total of $58,800 donations to the Victorian arm of the Liberal Party.

Three men were linked to all firms either via shareholdings or directorships.

They were David Scalzo, the scion of a food import and distribution empire, Califam Constructions managing director Anthony Caligiuri and Eli Goldfinger, who runs a corporate advisory consultancy specialising in property development, compliance and succession planning.

David Scalzo is linked to businesses which donated tens of thousands of dollars to the Victorian Liberal Party. (Perri Group)

Analysis by the ABC has revealed the total figure of donations linked to two of these men — Mr Caligiuri and Mr Goldfinger — is in fact higher.

A further eight firms of which Mr Goldfinger and Mr Caliguiri are directors also made donations over the same period of $4,900 each.

In total, the ABC has identified 20 firms with links to Mr Goldfinger and Mr Caliguiri which donated a total of $98,000 over a one-week period to the Liberal Party's Victorian branch.

A spokesman for this group of 20 entities, which includes Mensch Investments, thanked the ABC for acknowledging that separate company donations were lawful.

Anthony Caligiuri is linked to 20 firms which donated a total of $98,000. (califam.com)

He said each company acted with integrity and full disclosure.

"Each donation was reported to the Victorian Electoral Commission in the manner prescribed by the VEC on its website, subjecting each donation to VEC vetting," the spokesman said.

"We encourage anyone else wishing to exercise their democratic right of donating to also act lawfully and to disclose and report donations to the VEC.

"We assume the government has thoughtfully designed donation laws, especially after having the advantage of High Court scrutiny of donation laws earlier this year.

"Over many years we have supported productive and visionary members of parliament across the political spectrum at both a state and federal level."

The Victorian Electoral Commission said it did not comment on specific cases.

It said related bodies corporate were defined as when one company was a holding company of the other, one is a subsidiary of the other, or one is a subsidiary of a holding company of the other.

"Common ownership by a single individual does not mean, by itself, that companies are related bodies corporate," the spokesperson said.

"We expect parties and other donation recipients to have processes and procedures in place to identify donations made or received from related entities."

Laws changed in wake of High Court ruling

Victoria's donation laws were overhauled after a High Court decision handed down on April 15 struck out an entire section of the existing Act dealing with caps on political donations.

The existing laws were challenged by two independent candidates — Paul Hopper and Melissa Lowe — who argued the donations cap was unfair and risked allowing established political parties to benefit from wealthy donors where new and independent candidates could not.

The High Court decision left the state without any regulation of political donations in the lead-up to the November poll.

Victoria's parliament then scrambled to pass new laws in June that restored caps on donations and reinstated public disclosure requirements and public funding.

The new legislation was applied retrospectively to any donations received between April 15 and November 28, where any donations received above the $5,190 cap were to be returned to donors.

Victoria's new donation laws were passed after the High Court struck down the previous laws. (ABC News: Gregory Nelson)

The ABC asked the Victorian Liberal Party, which were the recipients of all four cases identified, whether they had examined any of those transactions, or returned any donations from any source after the new laws were introduced.

A Victorian Liberal Party spokesperson replied that "the Liberal Party operates in compliance with the requirements of the Electoral Act".

Companies are not required to publicly reveal their ownership or directorship structure when disclosing donations, which means the ABC cannot say whether there are more examples of these kinds of companies making donations across the political spectrum.

Transparency International Australia's Clancy Moore said the ABC's investigation showed the need for greater beneficial ownership transparency.

Victoria's new laws have an in-built review by an expert panel, which will form after the election and hand down its findings late next year.

Mr Moore said he hoped the review would look at the "loophole" present in the laws, which he said were rushed through parliament without proper scrutiny.

"Because it's really not the intent of the government's law to have corporate entities donating up to $100,000 in the lead up to an election," Mr Moore said.

He also urged the panel to consider banning donations from "high risk" industries, such as property developers.

"It's particularly risky, there's clearly a risk of poor governance and even a risk of corruption when you have private interests involved in planning, in construction, in those economic sectors that are regulated by government but also have key decisions like an approval process or a tendering process, where you have those entities donating large amounts of money, because it could either knowingly or unknowingly influence government decision-makers," Mr Moore said.

"It absolutely feeds into a perception of the system being rigged, and, you know, governments favouring private interests against the interests of citizens."

World.title: ACT police crack down on 'prolific' repeat youth offenders
World.content:
ACT Policing has launched an operation cracking down on repeat youth offenders amid concerns that a small group of juveniles are responsible for a significant amount of crime across the territory.

Police said Operation Tectona would focus on disrupting youth crime and anti-social behaviour by targeting "prolific recidivist youth offenders", their "associates", and crime hotspots.

As part of the operation, police said they would conduct high-visibility patrols at shopping centres, schools, and other places where young people gathered.

Authorities said the crackdown aimed to prevent and disrupt targeted attacks, organised fights, retail crime, and the possession of offensive weapons.

Australian Bureau of Statistics data — released in March — indicated that the ACT's youth offender rate was relatively low compared to other states and territories.

Scott Lee says police intelligence has identified individuals, associates, and locations linked to some of the most concerning recent incidents. (ABC News: Donal Sheil)

But Chief Police Officer Scott Lee told ABC Radio Canberra there was a small number of offenders — estimated to be fewer than 50 individuals — that were targeting the territory.

He said the offenders were around 16-17-years-old, and some of them were young adults, adding they had been "influencing other young people".

Police intelligence has identified individuals, "associates", and locations linked to some of the recent incidents across the territory, he said.

The chief police officer said that while police were committed to addressing the causes of youth offending, "there also needs to be accountability for those who continue to commit serious or repeated offences."

ACT police said officers apprehended 326 people aged 14 to 17 in 2025-26, down slightly from 334 the previous year.

Crime in the capital

Canberrans have voiced their concerns about crime in the territory in recent weeks.

Earlier this month, the Liberal Party hosted a community forum to discuss crime after multiple violent incidents in the city's south.

About 100 locals attended the meeting and aired their personal experiences, with some people adding that they did not feel safe.

A community forum was held in November on the state of crime in Canberra. (ABC News: Niddal Mustafa)

The meeting followed multiple violent incidents in the area, including the stabbing of a student outside Lake Tuggeranong College.

In an interview on ABC Radio Canberra, the chief police officer said young people had been carrying knives for "defensive purposes".

"We don't want any knives in our community, but once they're being carried by people, obviously the consequences are serious," he said.

Opposition Leader Mark Parton has welcomed the operation, adding the community had forced the issue onto the agenda.

Canberra Liberals leader Mark Parton says the operation shows the community's concerns were real. (ABC News: David Sciasci)

"Canberrans turned up, spoke out and refused to be told everything was fine," he said.

"ACT Labor wouldn't listen, so we did. This operation shows those concerns were real.

" Parents shouldn't have to worry about knives at the school gate. "

Recent events 'understandably caused concern': minister

Police Minister Marisa Paterson said "recent events in our community have understandably caused concern for many Canberrans".

ACT Police Minister Marisa Paterson says safety is a priority. (ABC News: Callum Flinn)

She said she wanted to "reassure the community that their safety remains a priority".

World.content:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has touted the government’s new pact with the Solomon Islands in front of the largest ever visiting delegation to Parliament.

Albanese said the agreement, which includes banning China from building military bases in the Pacific Island nation, marked a great day for the region and made Australia the Solomon Islands’ primary security partner.

Prime Minister of the Solomon Islands Matthew Wale (right) and his delegation during question time. Dominic Lorrimer

“This relationship and this agreement brings us a new chapter of friendship, advancing our shared interest and the interests of our region,” Albanese said.

“Australia’s prosperity and security is simply inseparable from our Pacific family. When our neighbours are stronger, Australia is stronger as well.”

Albanese personally welcomed his Solomon Islands counterpart Matthew Wale, and said he had probably also set a record. “I doubt whether 17 members of the cabinet of any government apart from Australia’s, have been present here on the floor of the parliament”.

Speaker Milton Dick confirmed: “This is the largest parliamentary delegation ever to sit on the floor of the House of Representatives”.

World.title: ‘Multiple queens’: More fire ants detected as Sydney nest part of rare colony
World.content:
Updated PoliticsNSWBiosecurity ‘Multiple queens’: More fire ants detected as Sydney nest part of rare colony Jessica McSweeney Updated November 25, 2026 — 2:24pm ,first published 12:25pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

A discovery of red imported fire ants in Sydney’s west has been identified as a rare colony with multiple queens never detected before in NSW. The NSW government has established a specialised taskforce after further surveillance of the Auburn site discovered a larger and more complex infestation than first realised, with more alive ants detected after the site was treated on the weekend. The fire ant nest at Auburn has been identified as a rare colony with multiple queens. NSW Government Unlike nests with one queen, the colony discovered in Auburn contains multiple queens which can support a higher concentration of ants and nests in a smaller area. The type of colony is rare in Australia. Imported materials are believed to be the source of both the Enfield discovery two months ago and the Auburn nest, although the two locations are not believed to be connected. The government is yet to identify the country of origin of both incursions.



A new taskforce will trace high-risk products transiting through the businesses around the Auburn site, which mostly includes shipments from Asia, Agriculture Minister Tara Moriarty said. “I was able to check it out myself yesterday, and even though the area is not geographically big, the types of ants that we have here do spread in a different way … we’ve not seen ants spread in this way ever like this in NSW before,” Moriarty said. More than 900 members of the public have called the fire ant hotline, but no ants have been detected at other sites. Fire ants are one of the worst invasive species to reach Australia. Invasive Species Council A Biosecurity Control Order will be in place on Friday to formally limit the transport of high-risk materials from the area, including mulch, soil and building materials.



The fire ants found in Auburn are believed to have been there for about 12 months before it was reported by a member of the public. “At this stage, we’ve found all of these queens in this one particular zone, but the tracing will help us to determine if other colonies have set up elsewhere,” Moriarty said. Related Article Updated

Biosecurity New fire ants’ nest found near Sydney importers may have been there for a year Known as polygyne fire ant colonies, these groups of ants can establish new nests when a queen and workers move away from the existing colony in a process known as budding. The ants are native to South America but have spread internationally, particularly into the United States, thanks to freight shipping.



Their painful bites cause burning sensations that can last for an hour, and kill pets, native wildlife and humans sensitive to insect bites. Red imported fire ant nests appear as small mounds of dirt with no obvious exit holes. Suspected sightings should be reported on 1800 680 244 or via an online form. World.title: Why boom Blues draftee thinks he could have played AFL this season
World.content:
SportAFLAFL 2027 Why boom Blues draftee thinks he could have played AFL this season Jon Pierik November 25, 2026 — 2:16pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Prized Carlton draftee Cody Walker has declared he is all but a “ready-made” AFL player and has his mind set on a round one debut against Richmond – the club which also bid for him. Walker, the No.3 overall selection in the national draft, and his fellow influx of draftees – Harvey Spawton-Guy, Jackson Watkins, Ethan Herbert and Marcus Prasad, the latter the shortest listed player in the AFL – are dealing with their first week of pre-season training along with other first-to-fourth-year players. Stepping up: Prized Carlton draftee Cody Walker believes he is ready to play AFL senior football. Getty Images On a warm Wednesday morning, Walker sparkled when working with fellow midfielders, including young star Jagga Smith and George Hewett, the veteran opting to return a week ahead of schedule. Walker, whose father Andrew played 202 games for the Blues, has had the benefit of spending much of the past 18 months at the club. He has been likened to Patrick Dangerfield for his power and speed out of stoppages, and even suggested he could have been ready for the big league last season.



Related Article Draft AFL draft, all the picks: Pandemonium at year 12 graduation as three schoolmates drafted on same night “I definitely would have liked to have, you know, challenged myself to do that [to have played AFL football in 2026], and I see myself as a pretty ready-made player,” Walker said. “And that’s all thanks to the Carlton footy club as well for giving me a gym program for so many years, and then also getting me training with AFL players for … a year and a half now. So, I think I definitely would have liked to have challenged myself, but I am ready this year.” Walker spent time in the VFL last year on a wing and at half-forward, but his long-term future is likely more as an inside midfielder. The Echuca product, who played senior football for his home club aged 16, keen fisherman and former Bendigo Pioneer said his game differed to his father’s more high-flying and outside running role.



What is clear is that Walker was a wanted man. The Tigers made a strong pitch to recruit Walker, who was tied to the club’s next-generation academy. They also bid for him on draft night, but the Blues matched. Walker has embraced life as a professional player for some time, and already considers himself a leader among his rookie teammates, some of whom are still settling in after shifting from interstate. Father and son: Cody Walker is presented with his guernsey by his dad Andrew, who played 202 games for the Blues. The Age He said it had been a touching moment when his father presented him with the No.1 guernsey he used to wear. “It’s pretty special, to be honest,” Walker said. “When I got handed it the other day, when Dad presented it to me, I didn’t actually know I was getting it until Dad said turn around, and I saw it. And yeah, it was a little bit emotional to me and Dad.



“It’s a pretty cool number as well. The first locker in the change room.” Related Article AFL 2026 More than 60 players were picked in the AFL draft. Here’s who your club selected, and what they said about it Walker said his father had offered a simple piece of advice heading into his first pre-season campaign. “Just attack my first year like this is my 13th … don’t really hold back. At the end of the day, that’s your team now, and yeah, just really attack it,” Walker said. It’s been a week of adjustment for the new crew. Spawton-Guy, a West Australian key forward who had Nick Riewoldt as his idol, fell asleep at the cinema watching a movie with teammates on Monday night, so exhausted was he after a demanding first day of training.



Prasad, taken in the rookie draft, has modelled his game on Hawthorn star Nick Watson – and for good reason. Prasad is listed at 167cm, shorter than Fremantle’s Isaiah Dudley (168cm), Watson (170cm), with whom he shares the same management team, and North Melbourne’s Caleb Daniel (171cm). World.title: Baking bad: Political brawl erupts over tradwife social media videos
World.content:
PoliticsFederalSocial media Baking bad: Political brawl erupts over tradwife social media videos Brittany Busch Updated November 25, 2026 — 2:04pm ,first published 11:56am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Close Share A A A

Shadow Attorney-General Michaelia Cash has attacked a Labor senator’s claim that women should be shielded from tradwife content online, as the Coalition shapes up to follow One Nation and promise to repeal the government’s digital duty of care. The opposition frontbencher wielded WA senator Ellie Whiteaker’s recent comments on social media linking tradwife content – which promotes traditional family values – to subservience to men, and clashed with Housing Minister Clare O’Neil on Wednesday morning, who rejected the claim that Labor wanted to ban baking videos. Senior Labor and Liberal frontbenchers have clashed over whether tradwife content will be captured by the digital duty of care laws. Marija Ercegovac In the social media clip in question, Whiteaker points to a video of a woman baking a “spicy snack” for her husband as leading to content in which a woman says her husband and God are her bosses. Whiteaker said a conversation needed to be had about what women were seeing online: “Being told to give up their independence, to submit to a man, to obey their husbands – things that women just shouldn’t be exposed to online in 2026.”



The Labor senator went on to say: “Our digital duty of care bill puts responsibility on the platforms. It holds them accountable for what you see in your feeds, and it makes sense. They make money off it. They should be accountable for it. “It also gives the power back to you to decide whether you want the algorithm or not. And if you do, great, you can keep it. But if you don’t, you can switch it off.” Loading Appearing on Seven’s Sunrise on Wednesday morning, Cash said: “Since when did a woman choosing to bake for her husband ... choosing to stay at home, or a traditional view of marriage, become a problem for the Labor Party?” O’Neil responded that “of course there’s nothing wrong with baking”.



“That is completely made up, and the type of content that Michaelia is talking about, of course it doesn’t create harms,” she said. The stoush erupted after Labor struck a deal with the Greens to legislate the next pillar of its online safety agenda, which the opposition has branded as censorship. The laws passed the Senate on Wednesday. Conservatives have seized on Whiteaker’s comments as evidence for their argument. Opposition communications spokeswomen Sarah Henderson described the remarks as an insight into the government’s “insidious” online agenda in a social media post last week. O’Neil insisted on Wednesday that tradwife content would not be banned and challenged Cash to justify voting against reforms that would prevent children from terrorism and eating disorder content. “Michaelia and her colleagues are howling at the moon trying to come up with any way that they can think of to oppose this legislation,” she said, as she and Cash shouted over each other. “I just can’t fathom it … how can you defend your position?”



Related Article Social media Tech giants to face billion-dollar fines for breaching Labor’s digital duty of care laws Asked what her concerns were given O’Neil’s response, Cash said the prime minister had a track record of lying. “Labor have made it very, very clear the type of content they believe should be included,” she said. “The minister and the regulator under this bill ... have sweeping powers to define what harm is. Take that section out of the act. For God’s sake, Clare – read your own legislation.” O’Neil replied: “No … you read the legislation, Michaela, and you go back to Western Australia and you explain to the people who elected you to parliament why you are voting against a bill that actively protects Australian children.”



Labor removed a controversial power in the laws that would have allowed the communications minister to designate new harms, but concerns remain around how the harms identified in the legislation will be defined. The digital duty of care lists content deemed harmful to children, including pornography, promoting eating disorders and bullying. But other definitions of harm have been criticised as too broad and open to interpretation, particularly encouraging “hostile attitudes towards women or gender equality” and “any other material or conduct, or combination of material and conduct, that may cause serious harm to children”. Constitutional law expert Anne Twomey has also raised concerns that the bill is too vague because in practice it means removing content that could be harmful to children from all publicly available platforms that children can access. “Is this what is intended, or have I missed something?” she asked in a submission to a parliamentary inquiry into the digital duty of care.



Coalition frontbencher Andrew Hastie said on Wednesday morning the digital duty of care was “heavy-handed censorship”, and “our instinct and our posture will be to repeal it”. Communications Minister Anika Wells dismissed censorship concerns on Wednesday, including from the newly appointed United States ambassador who attacked the laws and said protecting free speech was a US priority. View post on X “Vaguely defined ‘harms’, backed by penalties of up to 5 per cent of global revenue, will push platforms to censor lawful speech,” David Brat said in a post on X. “As Australia’s largest foreign investor, the US is concerned with regulations that impose disproportionate compliance burdens on American companies relative to competitors.”



Asked whether Australia expected retaliation from the Trump administration, Wells told Radio National: “It’s not for me to hypothesise what another nation and nations administration might want to do.” She said she had a useful first meeting with Brat on Tuesday, and that each party understood that position of the other. “We’re ironing out where there are points of difference,” she said. “We won’t take a backward step from protecting Australian kids and helping Australian parents, and they won’t take a backward step from their position.” Cut through the noise of federal politics with news, views and expert analysis. World.title: Golden Dragon hits 27g/t gold as WA discovery deepens
World.content:
Sponsored BusinessCompaniesBulls N' Bears Golden Dragon hits 27g/t gold as WA discovery deepens Brought to you by BULLS N’ BEARS Andrew Todd November 25, 2026 — 2:01pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. Golden Dragon Mining has struck the deepest gold yet at its Coodardy prospect in Western Australia’s Murchison region, with a 4-metre hit grading 7.84 grams per tonne (g/t) gold from 70m downhole, confirming gold continues into the fresh rock at depth and requires deeper probing. The company says the latest 17-hole, 1871m reverse circulation (RC) drilling program has confirmed the key northeast-trending mineralised structure now extends for more than 500m of strike and, importantly, remains open to the north, south and northeast. Drilling crews on site at Golden Dragon’s Coodardy prospect in WA’s Murchison region. The latest results from Coodardy arrive as exploration activity gathers pace across the white-hot Murchison region, with several explorers, including Golden Dragon, looking to ramp up drilling assaults across new targets to take advantage of the region’s hungry existing processing infrastructure and historically high-grade gold operations. Golden Dragon says its latest standout hit at Coodardy came from the northernmost drill line tested to date and represents the company’s deepest high-grade intersection into fresh rock. The result suggests the mineralisation is not simply a shallow, weathered feature, but continues at depth into the Murchison greenstones.



‘(This) represents another important step towards our longer-term objective of advancing Coodardy towards resource development.’ Golden Dragon Mining managing director Simon Buswell-Smith It joins a growing list of solid intercepts at the prospect, including a previously reported 8m at 10.82g/t gold from just 25m and another hit of 11m at 6.42g/t gold, containing a spectacular one-metre section at 59.20g/t. Geological interpretation indicates a shallow, east-dipping mineralised system where gold is hosted within quartz veining, altered dolerites and chlorite schists. The company believes higher-grade zones occur within stacked quartz vein arrays, forming structurally controlled shoots that could point to a much larger, stacked system. Golden Dragon Mining managing director Simon Buswell-Smith said: “This is an excellent result for Golden Dragon and represents another important step towards our longer-term objective of advancing Coodardy towards resource development.” Coodardy lies within the broader Cue project outside of Meekatharra, where Golden Dragon has been busy consolidating a prolific gold acreage. The strategy recently attracted a significant vote of confidence from Shanghai-listed heavyweight Chengtun Mining Group, with the gold miner tipping in $2.2 million at a premium for a cornerstone 19.9 per cent stake in the company.



Once all of its new applications are granted, Golden Dragon will control a dominant landholding of roughly 619 square kilometres in the same region that hosts Westgold’s 2.3-million-ounce Big Bell gold mine. To keep the exploration ball rolling, the company recently launched into a major aircore assault at Cue to test two sizeable anomalies in its gold corridor that stretch for more than three kilometres. The program, totalling 6000 to 9000 metres, will probe gold-in-soil targets around the Coodardy-Behring Bore area, where recent surface work has suggested the company’s known gold footprint could be considerably bigger than previously thought. If successful, the program could effectively link Golden Dragon’s Curtis Find, Behring Bore, Coodardy and Piston prospects into a single, big mineralised system rather than a series of isolated targets, a substantial prize for any major looking to muscle into the Westgold, Ramelius-dominated terrain. With deeper drilling set to resume in early December and the northern extensions still wide open, Golden Dragon has plenty of room to chase more high-grade ounces. The pieces look to be falling into place at Coodardy, with the next campaign set to test whether the growing discovery can deliver the scale needed for a maiden resource. World.content:
NationalQueenslandTragedy US father drowns while saving children at popular Gold Coast swimming spot Courtney Kruk November 25, 2026 — 1:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month. An American influencer has shared a candid video of her despair after a family “trip of a lifetime” turned to tragedy when her husband drowned saving their children on the Gold Coast. Patrick Rohde, 41, was unresponsive when he was pulled from the water at Tallebudgera Beach about 1.15pm on Monday. He was declared dead at the scene by attending emergency services. Thais Rohde (right) says her husband Patrick (left) died saving their two children from drowning. BookTok creator Thais Rohde, known online as “ChaptersWithThais”, posted a tearful video on social media on Tuesday. She said he died saving their two children, aged seven and eight, after they were swept away in a current.



“My husband died, less than 12 hours ago, and I don’t know what to do,” she said. “We are in Australia, for a trip – me, him and the kids. And he drowned, at the beach … holding my kids. “I am lost … how am I going to survive the rest of our lives?” Rohde said the family would return to Pennsylvania this week, but her husband’s body would remain in Australia for now.



“My kids are devastated [and] traumatised. “I am in a foreign country, and I just have so much that I need to do. “This was supposed to be a trip of a lifetime and a dream to come to Australia, and my husband is dead. What do I do?” Rohde later updated a fundraiser launched to support the family and return Patrick’s body to the United States, and said she had been overwhelmed by the response to her candid video, intended to “share heartbreaking news with my small community”.



“I never imagined that video would reach millions of people and I am truly humbled and overwhelmed by the outpouring of love, prayers and messages from strangers all over the world,” she wrote. “Thank you for holding us in your hearts during the hardest moment of our lives.” A spokesperson for City of Gold Coast confirmed lifeguards were on patrol at Tallebudgera Creek on Monday and were among the first responders, performing CPR until paramedics arrived. “Our thoughts are with the family at this time, and we are also providing support to our lifeguards,” the spokesperson said. “During the warmer months (September to May), Tallebudgera Creek is patrolled every day, with city lifeguards on duty Monday to Friday, and volunteer surf lifesavers on weekends and public holidays.



“The city regularly reviews the areas we patrol to ensure patrols are conducted in the right locations and are appropriately staffed based on visitation, incident data, a location’s risk profile and conditions.” A report was being prepared for the coroner. World.title: ‘We’re interested in him’: Bennett confirms Munster is on Souths’ radar
World.content:
SportNRLNRL 2026 ‘We’re interested in him’: Bennett confirms Munster is on Souths’ radar Adrian Proszenko November 25, 2026 — 1:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. South Sydney coach Wayne Bennett has confirmed the club’s interest in Cameron Munster, but has no intention of turning the Melbourne playmaker into a halfback. Speculation that next year could be Munster’s last at the Storm has ramped up after this masthead revealed he had knocked back their latest offer, an increase from $750,000 to $850,000 per season. That figure is well below the $1.1 million contract he is on, at a time when the salary cap is increasing and there are new teams jockeying the signatures of marquee men. Loading For the first time in his career, the 32-year-old is seriously considering a move to Sydney, just as the Rabbitohs have flagged their interest. “We will meet up with him in the future,” Bennett said. “He’s coming off contract and we’re interested.



“He doesn’t look like he’s staying in Melbourne. That’s his decision, whether he makes the decision to stay in Melbourne … We’re talking 2028, not 2027. We’ve got our squad for 2027 … “He’s a quality football player, that’s what I will say.” Wayne Bennett and Cameron Munster. Aresna Villanueva Bennett’s pursuit of Munster is an indication there is no bad blood after the Kangaroos five-eighth knocked back an approach to work with him at the Dolphins. They worked together for Queensland in the 2020 State of Origin series: the Maroons won it 2-1 and Munster earned the Wally Lewis medal as the player of the series. Souths have also met with out-of-favour Rooster Sam Walker, in a sign they are chasing an elite playmaker. Cody Walker has re-signed for 2027 – the club has an option on his services for the following year – while Ashton Ward, Bud Sullivan and Jonah Glover are South Sydney’s other halves options.



Asked about chasing Munster while also being in the hunt for Walker, Bennett said: “It’s nothing to do with anyone else. If we approached Cameron Munster, it means we want him to play with us. “There’s an opportunity to do that, if we get to that stage. I certainly haven’t met with him, no one at the club has met with him at this stage … “We’re happy with what we’ve got for a seven. It will all be played out with who is coming and going over the next 12 months.” Munster began his career as a fullback before transitioning into the five-eighth role. Bennett has no intention of turning him into a halfback. “He’s a six, he won’t be playing seven at this stage of his career,” Bennett said.



On Tuesday, Munster said he was open to all offers after feeling he had been lowballed by Melbourne. “I’m not saying I’m going to leave Melbourne, just, obviously, with the terms and conditions that they put out to me was probably something I was a little disappointed in,” Munster said. “But I guess it’s a business.” Storm veteran Cameron Munster. Getty Images It is a testing time for the Storm, given they have yet to name a replacement for coach Craig Bellamy when he finishes up at the end of next year and a host of other superstars – including Harry Grant and Stefano Utoikamanu – are weighing up big offers to sign elsewhere. The Rabbitohs have their own rostering issues to work through, including whether to retain Latrell Mitchell. This masthead reported that some club powerbrokers were happy to let him go, while Bennett has long been a supporter.



Related Article Updated

NRL 2026 Munster to tour Sydney clubs despite Storm’s improved contract offer “Nothing has changed,” Bennett said. “There will be talk about Latrell, but he knows where he stands with us, and where we stand with him. “We would love Latrell to finish his career with us. That’s what we’re intending to do.” Bennett said the current off-season was the messiest yet from a player movement perspective.



“We just need to have a look at it, our transfer system and player movement system,” he said. “We need to look at it a bit harder, that’s what we need to do.” News, results and expert analysis from the weekend of sport sent every Friday.

World.title: Shaun Tan could win a Booker Prize. Four children will help decide
World.content:
CultureBooksLiterature Shaun Tan could win a Booker Prize. Four children will help decide Melanie Kembrey November 25, 2026 — 1:15pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Gift icon Gift Gift icon 0 / 3 No gift articles left You've used all of your gift articles. 3 more will become available on the 1st of every month.
